“This is going to be a good one, obviously, for the confidence to go into the postseason. But either way, it’s not make or break. I just want him to pitch well and feel good going into October.”
A Potential October Preview
Roberts acknowledged that the Dodgers are paying close attention to the Padres during this final regular-season series, recognizing that the two clubs could meet again in the playoffs.
He mentioned gathering information on Robbie Ray, Michael King and San Diego’s bullpen, with Nick Pivetta scheduled to pitch Thursday.
The Dodgers are also keeping an eye on the Braves, whose result against Cincinnati could affect Los Angeles’ opportunity to clinch the bye.
But Roberts said a favorable result on the out-of-town scoreboard wouldn’t change his approach in the middle of Thursday’s game.
“We’re playing to win, and I don’t think if the scoreboard reads that they’re winning or they lost, it would change anything.”
“I want to win tonight.”
Four Million Reasons to Celebrate Dodger Baseball
Thursday’s home finale also comes with a significant milestone, as the Dodgers are expected to surpass four million in attendance for the second consecutive season.
Roberts praised the organization’s ability to draw fans from around the world and the atmosphere they create at Dodger Stadium.
“The amazing thing is that it’s not just localized, clearly. It’s not just domestic. It’s international. You look at everyone, everyone looks different in Dodger Stadium. It’s spectacular, and our players certainly feed off of it.”
“It’s not taken for granted. I think opponents feel it, certainly in the later innings, when they see the third deck full and the speakers are blaring.”
Roberts credited the organization’s ownership and front office for consistently putting a star-studded team on the field.
“Los Angeles loves stars, and they want to see superstars, and we have a lot of superstars, which draws people. And I think our product is very consistent.”
For a team preparing for its 14th consecutive postseason appearance, Thursday offers another opportunity to reward those fans with something worth celebrating.
The Dodgers have already clinched the NL West. Now they can secure the first-round bye, give their pitching staff some much-needed rest and head into October with their biggest stars appearing to find their form at precisely the right time.

title: Cam Schlittler Ends Season Tying Historic Sandy Koufax Record
author: Joey Haverford
body:
The historic MLB regular season of Cam Schlittler ended after the New York Yankees pulled him following 3 innings on Thursday night. Schlittler gave up two runs to the Tampa Bay Rays, but one of them was unearned due a throwing error impacting one run. This allowed Schlittler to hit a specific mark that was needed to tie one of the most impressive pitching records.
Schlittler tied iconic pitcher Sandy Koufax with 25 total starts giving up one or fewer earned runs in a single season. The stat not having an innings limit or demanding a quality start of 6 innings meant the Yankees could have pulled him at any point to keep the record. Schlittler is the strong favorite to win the American League Cy Young Award and ended the season with the historic accomplishment.
Aaron Boone decided to pull Schlittler after 70 pitches and the third inning scare of Tampa Bay scoring a few runs. The one earned run outing also allowed Schlittler to end his season with the mark of an ERA under 2.00. Schlittler had the most dominant season for a Yankees starting pitcher since the 1980s. Yankees fans can celebrate each accolade knowing they have a superstar ace for many years now.
How Cam Schlittler Became Unexpected Ace
Last season’s call up in the latter half of the season showed Schlittler as a dominant starting pitcher from day one. Schlittler had an electric performance in Game 3 of the Wild Card series vs the Boston Red Sox to get the Yankees to the playoffs and became a beloved hero thanks to it.
The great early introduction last season made Schlittler more motivated to have one of the greatest first full seasons in MLB history. A blistering fastball is Schlittler’s biggest weapon, and it allows him to lead a staff with legends Gerrit Cole and Max Fried behind him.
Schlittler did what worked for him last season and became a dominant force who helped the team stay afloat. Injuries to Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton would have doomed the Yankees in past seasons. However, Schlittler anchored a tremendous pitching staff to lead the team to wins via that strength over hitting.
Cam Schlittler’s Wild Card Status Scaring Yankees Fans
Boone has claimed that Fried and Schlittler will start the first two games vs Boston in the Wild Card Series next week, but it could go either way. Cole and Carlos Rodon will be saved for a potential Game 3 or for the following ALDS if the Yankees advance.
Most Yankees fans badly want Schlittler to start Game 1 since he is the most trusted pitcher, and it would help get him on the found faster for a potential ALDS series vs the Tampa Bay Rays. Fried’s experience and extra days off are making him a viable choice.
Regardless, it is a great sign for Schlittler that the Yankees’ fan base already trusts him more than three proven winners in the rotation. The playoff run will see Schlittler having the chance to continue winning over Yankees fans as the ace every series.

title: Top Prospect Josue De Paula Could Still Play a Role for the Dodgers in 2026
author: Justin Binkowski
body:
Outfielder Josue De Paula's first stint with the Los Angeles Dodgers has officially come to a close. But that doesn't necessarily mean he won't wear a Dodgers uniform again this year.
De Paula, MLB Pipeline's No. 6 overall prospect for 2026, was optioned to Triple-A on Wednesday as the Dodgers activated two-way star Shohei Ohtani from the injured list. The 21-year-old made his MLB debut on Sept. 11 and appeared in 11 games for Los Angeles, hitting .323 (10-for-31) with one home run, seven RBIs, seven runs scored, and 11 walks.
Most notably, De Paula was promoted to the big leagues straight from Double-A. So, with this recent roster move, the young prospect made his Triple-A debut on Wednesday in the Oklahoma City Comets' playoff game. The 6-foot-3 outfielder went 0-for-3 with two walks and a run scored in Oklahoma City's 7-2 postseason victory over the Las Vegas Aviators, the Athletics' Triple-A affiliate. But this might not be the only taste of playoff baseball the lefty-swinging slugger gets in 2026.
Will the Dodgers actually consider putting Josue De Paula on their playoff roster?
Although De Paula was optioned on Wednesday, he's still eligible for the Dodgers' National League Division Series roster, according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya. Ardaya said the young outfielder could "be given heavy consideration" for a spot on the postseason team, but it remains to be seen whether Los Angeles will go down that route.
While his first stint in the majors was brief, De Paula regularly showcased his offensive skill set and ability to get on base. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts even called him a "special hitter," according to Ardaya. But Los Angeles mostly used the 21-year-old as a designated hitter, limiting him to two games in the big-league outfield. And now that Ohtani is back, the Dodgers don't have an immediate need for a DH.
As things stand, it's unclear if De Paula will be on Los Angeles' postseason roster. If he is included, it'll most likely be in a pinch-hit role, unless an injury pops up. Either way, the talented prospect has quickly shown that he can make an impact for the Dodgers now and in the future.
Justin Binkowski is a lifelong baseball fan returning to cover the sport he loves after spending nearly a decade writing about video games. Before his time as managing editor at Dot Esports, Binkowski attended King's College in Wilkes-Barre, PA, where he was also a relief pitcher on the school's baseball team. While in college, Binkowski was a media relations intern for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders during the 2014 season.

title: Lakers transition from ‘LeBron Era’ to a Luka Doncic-led squad
author: Benjamin Royer
body:
EL SEGUNDO — So much had changed since Rob Pelinka last publicly spoke with the media.
More than half the Lakers’ roster is new. Pelinka made Austin Reaves a max level-contract player as the permanent partner to Luka Doncic. Lakers ownership is set to change hands for the second time in two seasons – in a $12.5 billion acquisition from Mark Walter to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner that is still awaiting approval from the NBA. Lakers governor Jeanie Buss is battling her siblings to try and halt the sale of their minority ownership and dissipation of the Buss Family’s involvement with the franchise.
And as Pelinka, entering his ninth full season with the Lakers and his sixth as the team’s president of basketball operations, reminded the world – moments after conducting a moment of silence for longtime public address announcer Lawrence Tanter, who died Wednesday at 76 – LeBron James is gone.
“I thought it would be appropriate at the front to express gratitude for the LeBron Era here,” Pelinka said Thursday afternoon during his annual preseason press conference with head coach JJ Redick. “Clearly, new team and new players, and that’s what we’re going to talk about today, but we as an organization are still grateful for the run that we had with him here.”
Marked by a transformative offseason in which Pelinka said the team added 15-plus people to the front office staff, as well as nine players – highlighted by the blockbuster trade addition of former Utah Jazz center Walker Kessler as the team’s franchise center – the Lakers will be playing on a different plane of franchise identity heading into the 2026-27 regular season.
Doncic, Reaves and Kessler. Pelinka built his star trio, with all of them on multi-year contracts as the focal point of the Lakers’ future. Pelinka stressed three fundamental pillars for their offseason goals: retain Austin Reaves, acquire a franchise center and “develop a roster of JJ Redick dribble-pass-shoot players that were younger and add depth to our roster.”
Pelinka said Thursday he believes he’s accomplished all three.
Former Lakers guard Marcus Smart told the Houston Chronicle on Wednesday that he felt disrespected by the Lakers’ offer to him in free agency. When asked about the lack of continuity on the roster, instead opting to sign new players to fill out the team (Austin Reaves was the only free agent who the Lakers re-signed), Pelinka pointed to their thesis: rounding out a team in a similar age to Reaves and Doncic.
The average age of the Lakers’ roster is 25.5 years old as currently constructed.
As of Thursday, the Lakers are one spot over the league maximum of fully-guaranteed players allowed on a team at any given time. Pelinka said competition through training camp and the preseason will determine the final 15 players ahead of the Opening Night roster cut deadline, adding that he wouldn’t rule out a two-for-one trade to finalize the roster.
Redick said for the first time in three seasons, he has a roster full of players in fully defined roles. He said he has six or seven wings at his disposal and that the team should be naturally deeper and able make better use of its bench players.
“I feel like the pieces actually fit together, and so those roles probably get even more crystallized,” Redick said. “I’ll give you the wings, like there’s a very clear ask for you to be able to play, and if you don’t do those things, then you’re not going to play. That’s just the reality. We’ve already had some of those conversations this week with our players. We have high, high confidence in these guys that they’re going to buy into that.”
Insisting that starting spots are still up for grabs, Redick said he is confident in the trio of Doncic, Reaves and Kessler – who Pelinka said was “fully healthy, fully cleared” – leading the way.
“I’m pretty confident in three of the spots,” Redick said. “The other two spots will not be two white guys. Those are the two things that’s not changing.”
Both Pelinka and Redick credited the offseason camaraderie built through a pair of player minicamps – one in Las Vegas during the NBA Summer League, and the other through an all-expenses-paid trip for the Lakers’ roster to Ljubljana, Slovenia for five days in August.
“Part of the reason we’re so excited is because we know they’re gonna connect on a human level,” Redick said. “That’s only gonna help them on the court.”
After the team returned from Slovenia, Pelinka said he was having a conversation with new wing Matisse Thybulle at the team’s practice facility about the power of the “handwritten note.”
Thybulle replied with a story.
“At one point (guard) Collin Sexton stood up and was like, ‘Look at where we are. Like, there are a lot of people that never get to come overseas and experience. … This is amazing, and someone’s treating us to it,’” Pelinka said. “And then I guess at the end of the trip, each player took the time to write a handwritten note and then present it to Luka to thank him.”
On the ownership front, Pelinka said introductory meetings with Iger and Kushner have been “excellent” but added that he can’t say more than that the tone was “positive” because the transaction is pending.
While he said he was grateful for what he’s learned from working with Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, Pelinka also said he wasn’t able to speak further on the relationship between the L.A. sports teams (Walter still owns the Dodgers) due to the pending sale.
Pelinka said the front office additions were primarily in the strategy and analytics department. They hired two assistant general managers – Eric Amsler and Rohan Ramadas – and “rebuilt our player experience and player development arm.”
“With that comes new equipment, new recovery and modalities,” Pelinka said. “We’ve worked with our training department to do that. Just changed everything everywhere, but I think the goal, as the Lakers brand, is not just to be at the same level as all the other 29 teams in those areas, but to be the leader. That’s just what’s required here.”
Thursday was just the start of the Lakers cementing the tone with media day scheduled for Monday and training camp to follow.
A trek, a journey.
Or as Pelinka opined as the team’s theme for the season ahead: “The Odyssey.”
“Every season is a little bit like ‘The Odyssey,’ if anyone has seen the movie,” Pelinka said. “You launch a season, and there’s things that happen throughout that you can’t predict, but you have to stay together as a group and stay strong.”

title: 【ＭＬＢ】大谷翔平〝50ー50〟の異常性 カブス・PCAの偉業で浮き彫り「とんでもない」（東スポWEB） - Yahoo!ニュース
body:
カブスのPCAことピート・クローアームストロング外野手（24）が24日（日本時間25日）、本拠地最終戦となったマーリンズ戦で今季40盗塁目を記録し、史上7人目の「40―40」の快挙を達成した。 【動画】本拠地最終戦で今季40盗塁目を決めたカブス・PCA 初回先頭の打席に立ったPCAは四球を選んで出塁すると、続く鈴木の打席で二塁を陥れて大台に到達。すでに放っていた45本塁打と合わせ、2024年に大谷翔平投手（32＝ドジャース）が成し遂げて以来の大記録を打ち立てた。今季の大ブレークで大谷の4年連続となるリーグMVP受賞を阻み、自身初の栄冠を手にする可能性が一段と高まった。 チームは1点を追う5回に鈴木が値千金の26号ソロで同点に追いつき、6回の無死三塁のチャンスでホーナーが決勝の左前適時打を放って2―1で勝利。2年連続23度目のポストシーズン（PS）進出を決めた。 この日、村上が出場し、同じくPS進出を確定させたホワイトソックス戦を中継した「NHK BS」で解説を務めた新井宏昌氏は「40―40も素晴らしいんですけども、大谷選手が50―50って…。これ、とんでもないですね」とポツリ。 PCAの快進撃もすさまじいが、大谷が54本塁打、59盗塁で記録した前人未到の「50―50」ははるか先…。今季の大谷は左ヒザや右上腕などの負傷に見舞われて負傷者リストにも入ったが、PCAの偉業によって大谷が残した異常な記録が際立つ格好となっている。

title: Dave Roberts Announces Dalton Rushing News Ahead of Dodgers vs Padres Series Finale
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will give Dalton Rushing three games — and that likely means, at most, three at-bats — to prove he's worth a spot on the team's postseason roster.
Manager Dave Roberts announced before Thursday's series finale with the San Diego Padres that Rushing will be activated off the injured list ahead of Friday's game against the San Francisco Giants.
With that activation, Rushing will have just three games to play in before the season ends. Since he's unable to catch, he's merely a pinch-hit option off the bench, which is the role he'd play for the team in October.
While Rushing could theoretically be the Dodgers' designated hitter, they just got Shohei Ohtani back, and want him to get as many at-bats as possible before the postseason begins.
Thus, Rushing will likely have a maximum of three plate appearances as a pinch hitter over the final three games of the season to make his case.
It appears Rushing is battling with top prospect Josue De Paula — who was optioned on Wednesday but remains eligible to return before the National League Division Series — for a spot on the postseason roster.
Roberts admitted earlier this week that Rushing likely has the tougher path to winning the spot.
“Hitting off the bench is very difficult and so you're just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance," Roberts said. “To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed, and to kind of think that you have three games to get back in the playoff form, which is tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. but it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue.
“We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
Roberts said on Thursday that the team wanted to give Rushing one more opportunity after everything he did for the team this year. He stepped into a starting role amid Will Smith's extended absence, and hit .249 across 78 games with 12 home runs, 36 RBIs and an OPS of .798.
Rushing said to the LA Times that he's hoping to be able to impact the team in any way come October.
“Just showing them that I can swing it, and it’s an option,” Rushing said. “I know that you kind of tie [the team’s] hands up when you can’t play defense. So, I’m not expecting anything… just continue to take at-bats and see where we go from there.”

Noah Camras graduated from the University of Southern California in 2022 with a B.A. in Journalism and a minor in sports media studies. He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. Noah is the publisher of Dodgers on SI after contributing as a writer and editor over the last three years.

title: Dodgers' Yoshinobu Yamamoto Sends Message To Fans Before Postseason Begins
author: Aaliyan Mohammed
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have punched their ticket to the postseason and will be looking to three-peat.
Last postseason, Yoshinobu Yamamoto had a run for the ages, throwing two complete games, working 28 2/3 innings and closing out the World Series on zero days of rest after throwing six innings the day before. He won World Series MVP and will once again be looking to deliver in October.
Yamamoto was an All-Star once again this year, posting a 2.53 ERA. However, he let Dodgers fans know after his final start of the regular season that he plans to play his best baseball in the postseason.
"Now we're getting into October, so I'd like to live up to the high expectations," Yamamoto said after Wednesday's game.
The Dodgers' postseason rotation this year will feature Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. It's very possible that Yamamoto is not even the Dodgers' No. 2 starter in October. The Dodgers have yet to reveal how they will line up their starters in October, but it's very likely they will have a bye and will have their pick.
If Yamamoto delivers as he did in last year's postseason, the Dodgers will have no problem winning the National League once again.
More MLB: Rays Announce Two-Time All-Star Not Available For ALDS

title: How much should Dodgers fans buy into Edwin Diaz’s success since coming off the IL?
author: Evan Roberts
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not mince his words when talking about Edwin Díaz during his mid-September rehab assignment. "He needs to pitch better. It hasn't been good," said Roberts.
Diaz, who has the highest average annual value in MLB relief pitcher history ($23M), struggled in the first four appearances of his rehab assignment. He had thrown just 40 of 86 pitches for strikes in his first four games with Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Diaz's fourth appearance was especially worrying. He threw 30 pitches — just 13 of them for strikes — walked three batters and allowed five runs. Diaz rehab came in the Pacific Coast League, which is notorious for being the most hitter-friendly league in all of baseball. That atrocious outing came in Sugar Land, however, which is the most pitcher-friendly venue in the PCL.
When the Dodgers activated Diaz from the injured list, Roberts revealed he'd be used in low-leverage situations. Well, he has been perfectly fine in his three low-leverage outings since September 18, which has assuaged some of the Dodgers fans panic levels.
Should Dodgers fans buy into Edwin Diaz’s success?
Diaz has only allowed one hit since returning from the IL. The Dodgers, however, had a run margin of +19 in those three games.
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” said Roberts after the Dodgers 7-0 win over the Padres on September 22.
The Dodgers will almost certainly give Diaz another opportunity against the San Diego Padres on Thursday. The current home series against the Friars will be Diaz's last opportunity to pitch against a playoff team before the postseason begins.
The Dodgers are currently without Emmet Sheehan, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, and Eric Lauer. Outside of Alex Vesia, the rest of the bullpen is incredibly shaky. Tanner Scott has a 5.40 ERA so far this month, Justin Wrobleski has not improved since being moved to the bullpen, and who knows what Blake Treinen has left in the tank?
Dodgers fans should get accustomed to seeing Diaz the rest of the season. He's quite possibly the linchpin to this team going deep in the playoffs with the way this bullpen looks right now. Dodgers fans have the right to remain skeptical that Diaz will return to the optimal version of himself,

title: Dodgers Lineup vs Padres: Will Smith Out, Shohei Ohtani Leading Off
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres are facing off in the rubber match of their three-game series on Thursday night with plenty at stake for both teams.
The Dodgers, who have already won the National League West division, can clinch a first-round bye with a win or Atlanta Braves loss over the season's final four games.
They're also still chasing the Milwaukee Brewers for the No. 1 seed, but will need some help to secure home-field advantage throughout the postseason.
As for the Padres, they're looking to clinch a postseason spot, with their magic number currently sitting at 1.
Thus, the winner of Thursday's game will be celebrating in some capacity. If it's the Padres, they'll be making a champagne and beer mess in the visitor's clubhouse at Dodger Stadium. If it's the Dodgers, they'll be shaking hands and looking forward to their five-day layoff beginning next week.
Dodgers vs Padres Pitching Matchup on Thursday
Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the mound for the Dodgers in his final tune-up before the postseason.
Glasnow has been shaky since coming off the injured list at the end of August, sporting a 4.50 ERA over 28 innings with 38 strikeouts to 10 walks. Overall this season, he's 5-1 with a 3.46 ERA and 87 strikeouts across 67.2 innings (12 starts).
Glasnow is expected to be the team's No. 4 starter in the playoffs behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell.
Opposite Glasnow will be Padres right-hander Nick Pivetta, who missed nearly five months this season with an elbow injury but has been incredibly sharp since returning.
In his three starts since coming off the IL, Pivetta has allowed just three runs over 14 innings for a 1.93 ERA. He has 11 strikeouts to one walk in that time.
Dodgers Starting Lineup
- Shohei Ohtani, DH
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Teoscar Hernández, LF
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Max Muncy, 3B
- Andy Pages, CF

- Tommy Edman, 2B

First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. San Diego Padres on Thursday, Sept. 24 is 7:10 p.m. PT/10:10 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and in the MLB app.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).

title: Dodgers Considering Edwin Diaz for Postseason Closer Despite Disastrous Season
author: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have countless questions to address before the postseason as their quest to win three consecutive championships continues, but one of the biggest uncertainties on the roster is relief pitcher Edwin Díaz.
Díaz is a three-time All-Star and has an impressive reputation on the mound. He and his 253 saves through his first nine seasons in MLB earned a massive three-year, $69 million contract to help the Dodgers towards their ultimate goal.
The start to his Dodgers career was far from ideal to say the least, pushing a 10.50 ERA through his first seven appearances (six innings). Towards the end of April, he was placed on the injured list as he underwent a procedure to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
Upon his return in late-July, it was unforunately more of the same with 11 earned runs in nine appearances. After heading back to the injured list for a month with neck inflammation, he has appeared to make significant strides with just one hit and walk allowed to go along with six strikeouts in his last three outings.
Manager Dave Roberts knows that the timing couldn't be worse given the imminent postseason and Díaz needing more reps, but at least for the moment, the skipper sees someone who can pitch in October in Díaz.
“I think it’s one of those things where if you’re one of the 12 pitchers on a postseason roster, you’re in the ‘trust tree’” Roberts said. “He’s put himself right smack in that conversation. Given all that he’s had to go through this year to right the ship is a big credit to him.”
Roberts also admitted that reasons beyond Díaz's control may seem to have influenced his poor play to start his Dodgers tenure, but perhaps these are all in the rear-view for the reliever.
“I think he’s in as good a spot as he’s been in all year, mentally, physically. The ball is coming out well,” Roberts said. “Yeah, I think that swagger is starting to come back, and I like the way that the energy that he’s exuding, it’s real. It’s something for us to build on.”
Roberts still couldn't put a label on who will have the 'closer' role come the postseason, but detailed a plan for a different pitcher who saw immense struggles to start the Dodgers chapter of his career (Tanner Scott) and how the two can work in tandem down the stretch.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”

He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

After heading back to the injured list for a month with neck inflammation, he has appeared to make significant strides with just one hit and walk allowed to go along with six strikeouts in his last three outings.
Manager Dave Roberts knows that the timing couldn't be worse given the imminent postseason and Díaz needing more reps, but at least for the moment, the skipper sees someone who can pitch in October in Díaz.
“I think it’s one of those things where if you’re one of the 12 pitchers on a postseason roster, you’re in the ‘trust tree’” Roberts said. “He’s put himself right smack in that conversation. Given all that he’s had to go through this year to right the ship is a big credit to him.”
Roberts also admitted that reasons beyond Díaz's control may seem to have influenced his poor play to start his Dodgers tenure, but perhaps these are all in the rear-view for the reliever.
“I think he’s in as good a spot as he’s been in all year, mentally, physically. The ball is coming out well,” Roberts said. “Yeah, I think that swagger is starting to come back, and I like the way that the energy that he’s exuding, it’s real. It’s something for us to build on.”
Roberts still couldn't put a label on who will have the 'closer' role come the postseason, but detailed a plan for a different pitcher who saw immense struggles to start the Dodgers chapter of his career (Tanner Scott) and how the two can work in tandem down the stretch.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”

title: Alexander: Wouldn’t another Dodgers-Padres playoff series be fun?
author: Jim Alexander
body:
LOS ANGELES — If there are any messages being sent this week, they’re subtle ones.
The Dodgers and Padres have become quite the rivalry in recent years. The Padres’ stars, particularly Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado, get on the nerves of Dodger fans. San Diegans, with their tendency to dislike all things associated with the metropolis to the north – except for that segment of folks who still can’t totally let go of the Chargers – relish the opportunity to, well, beat L.A.
Consider: When the Padres finally slew the dragon from the north as the late Peter Seidler, then owner, memorably predicted, they did everything but push back closing time in the Gaslamp Quarter. The roar that accompanied that 2022 National League Division Series victory might still be echoing in Petco Park all these years later, so hungry were Padres fans to take down the Dodgers, especially after L.A. had beaten them on neutral ground in the 2020 COVID-19-influenced postseason.
It’s also fairly obvious that the Dodgers’ 2022 failure, followed by a 2023 NLDS sweep by the Arizona Diamondbacks, helped create the monster in Chavez Ravine that is currently terrorizing all of baseball, including the segment of ownership that is willing to push the game to the brink in its zeal for a salary cap that labor has no intention of ever accepting.
You think Andrew Friedman and the rest of the Dodgers’ front office didn’t redouble their efforts following those two playoff flameouts? The mere possibility of a three-peat now should be proof of how much those losses stung. And the hype video in Dodger Stadium these nights is a pretty accurate representation of the state of mind here, the feeling that the Dodgers and their fans not only don’t care that they’ve become baseball’s villains, they relish it.
As the voiceover narrator puts it, “What’s wrong with being the bad guy? If being the best makes you bad, so be it. … If we’re being honest, sometimes it’s fun to root for the bad guy. … You need teams like us so you can point your finger and say, ‘That’s the bad guy.’”
The villainy works both ways, of course. Witness the first inning of the first game of this current series on Tuesday night.
Machado provokes strong reactions in L.A. because (a) he spent the final months of the 2018 season with the Dodgers, (b) his style of play was, shall we say, overly energy efficient – or, as he put it, “I’m not the type of player that’s going to be ‘Johnny Hustle’” – and (c) after that season he signed a 10-year, $300 million free agent contract with San Diego.
So, in Game 1 on Tuesday night, Brock Stewart’s first pitch to Machado knocked him down. The crowd jeered, loudly, and Machado took the moment to sit there and nod his head as if to say, “Yeah, it’s on.”
There were no further dust-ups in the first two games of this series, a 7-0 Dodgers victory on Tuesday night and a 5-1 Padres victory on Wednesday.
This wasn’t quite on the order of the series in June 2025, when then-Padres manager Mike Shildt and Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages exchanged words on the first night after Pages was hit by a pitch, Tatis and Shohei Ohtani were both plunked and Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was eventually ejected the second night, and Roberts and Shildt exchanged words at home plate after Tatis was hit again in Game 3.
Actually, the teams have been comparatively sedate in 2026. As for their fans on social media … ah, we’ll leave that alone.
But a Dodgers-Padres postseason series would almost certainly bring all of the emotions to the surface. Remember, the Padres not only knocked the Dodgers off in 2022 but had them on the ropes in 2024, one game away from another early elimination, before an 8-0 victory in a Game 4 bullpen game in San Diego reversed the momentum.
Also, keep in mind that after the Padres had knocked out Clayton Kershaw in an early season game in San Diego in 2023, a “Crying Kershaw” meme was posted on the Petco Park scoreboard. Consider, too, that the Dodgers gave fans replica Kershaw World Series rings before the first game of this series.
Coincidence? I think not.
And so here we are again. Los Angeles and San Diego split the first two games of their series this week, and while it might not be a major topic of conversation in either clubhouse this week you can bet these teams are casting wary eyes at each other, aware that fate could throw them together in yet another best-of-five (or maybe even best-of-seven) classic.
First things first. After Wednesday night’s game the Dodgers were still one victory or one Atlanta defeat away from clinching the No. 2 spot among division winners and the right to skip the best-of-three Wild Card round. The Padres’ magic number for clinching a wild card berth, likewise, was one.
Will Smith wasn’t about to look ahead. “We’re still approaching it as trying to win some ballgames,” he said. “I don’t think we’ve clinched the bye yet, so we’re still trying to do that.”
But Roberts acknowledged that it was in the back of his mind.
“Yeah, yeah, it’s in there,” he said.
“We’re pretty familiar with these guys. But yeah, absolutely. You know, we’re gathering information on Robbie Ray (Wednesday night’s starter), and, you know, there are guys in the ’pen and (Michael) King (Monday) and we’ll see (Nick) Pivetta (Thursday). So, certainly.”
And, Roberts noted before Wednesday night’s game in response to a question from San Diego Union-Tribune columnist Tom Krasovic, “They’re a thorn in our side and great competition.”
The feeling, I’m sure, is mutual. And while it might wear both teams out, don’t you wish these teams went back to facing each other 18 times during the regular season instead of 13, as they did this season?
Come to think of it, a five-game playoff series … nah, let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves.
jalexander@scng.com

title: Dodgers' weak effort vs. Padres in first game without Josue De Paula was frustratingly ironic
author: Katrina Stebbins
body:
On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Dodgers reactived Shohei Ohtani from the 15-day IL and optioned Josue De Paula, which was just about the most unpopular decision they could've made.
No one can really complain about having Ohtani back, but De Paula had captured the hearts and attentions of Dodgers fans so quickly that we would've preferred the team make a more drastic measure, like cutting Alex Call, than sending De Paula away for the time being.
There is still a distinct chance that the Dodgers enter a petition with the Commissioner's Office to carry De Paula on their postseason rosters, but fans want every second of the No. 1 prospect they can get.
The Dodgers took the field for the second game of three against the San Diego Padres without their electric rookie, and they certainly played like they'd lost a spark.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto is no stranger to getting little-to-no run support from his team. In the fifth, with the Padres already up 2-0 thanks to a Manny Machado homer, Yamamoto gave up back-to-back singles before a Dustin Harris laid down a bunt. Yamamoto fielded and tried to throw to third to get the lead runner, but it sailed into foul territory, allowing a run to score.
The Dodgers offense, meanwhile, only scored a single run on a Tommy Edman sac fly.
Dodgers clearly already missing their sparkplug after Josue De Paula option, loss to Padres
The Dodgers' loss and an Atlanta Braves win kept LA from clinching the first-round bye that escaped them last year. The Padres' win allowed them to pull away from the rest of the crowded NL Wild Card pack. Going into Wednesday's game, the Padres, Chicago Cubs, and Philadelphia Phillies were all tied with the same 87-70 record. The Phillies also lost, which allowed the Padres to pull away by a game in the standings.
Although the Dodgers clinching is still all but inevitable, fans are getting antsier the further we come down to the wire.
There are still some big questions to be answered when the Dodgers get to October, the De Paula vs. Dalton Rushing debate being one of them. Dave Roberts already admitted that it would be an uphill battle for Rushing, given how well and how immediately De Paula established himself.
The offense's lifeless showing against the Padres on Wednesday might've been an indirect plus in De Paula's column. Look what they turned into without him.

title: Meeting the Padres in the last home game before the playoffs
author: Estevão Maximo
body:
After this matchup, the next time the Dodgers play at home, it will likely be hosting the winner of the WC series between the third- and sixth-place teams, and the theme of this game against the Friars is one. Having split the first two games of this series, the Dodgers are still one win away from that second seed in the National League, and for the Padres, it’s one win away from clinching a playoff berth—even though they currently occupy the fourth seed, one game up on the Phillies and Cubs.
The contrast between the importance of securing that one win in this specific game could not be bigger. For the Dodgers, visiting the lowly Giants at the end of the season, whatever happens here, only a travesty could prevent them from sitting out the Wild Card round. It’d take a travesty for the Padres too, but it’s a more real possibility given they host the Diamondbacks in the final series of the year. A sweep there isn’t particularly likely, but ideally, San Diego would like to play that series with the playoff spot locked up.
Carrying on the similarities, you have a pitching matchup with two names that could be defined as the X factors for these teams and their respective goals in postseason baseball. Nick Pivetta and Tyler Glasnow are both coming off injury-filled campaigns, with the pair combined falling short of 20 starts. All things considered, though, at least Glasnow has been fully built up for some time, while Pivetta has yet to crack 80 pitches in his three starts back, slowly working his way up.
Thursday game info
- Teams: Dodgers vs. Padres
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium
- Start time: 7:10 p.m.
- TV: SportsNet LA, MLB Network (out of market)
- Radio: AM 570 (English), KTNQ 1020 AM (Spanish)

title: Dodgers Star Hopeful He'll Avoid Major Offseason Surgery
author: Jason Fray; Unknown
body:
Dalton Rushing’s breakout season has not exactly gone to plan for himself or the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The upstart catcher got his first taste of extended play in the wake of Will Smith spending much of the first half of the season on the injured list.
Rushing impressively has clubbed 12 homers in only 250 plate appearances. As his confidence grew, the Dodgers faced the reality that Rushing needed to play multiple times a week — even if that meant mixing in starts at first base along with his duties behind the plate.
Unfortunately for Rushing, his season became derailed on Aug. 3. Reports initially focused around a partially torn UCL in his elbow. However, as Rushing recently told Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times, that had been a preexisting injury he had been playing through since 2022.
Instead, it’s actually a flexor strain which has sidelined the catcher. Rushing is hoping that he can still be an impact player for the ballclub with the postseason right around the corner.
He's also hoping to avoid offseason surgery.
“I’m pretty confident I can still avoid surgery after the shot,” Rushing said. “Obviously, when I re-injured it the second time, I was almost 70-30, thinking that I was for sure going to need surgery. But after I got the shot and it ran its course, I feel as close to healthy in my arm as I have in a pretty long time.”
Rushing is projected to be activated at some point this week. With only a few games remaining on the schedule, the Dodgers will determine whether he can be a threat off the bench solely as a hitter.
With Miguel Rojas and Kiké Hernandez occupying two of the team’s bench spots on a hypothetical roster, the need for a left-handed bat is there.
At this point, Rushing is likely battling with phenom Josue De Paula for a spot on the roster for the first round. De Paula was fantastic in his brief stint in the big leagues — before being sent down on Wednesday — hitting .323 with a whopping 11 walks to just five strikeouts.
Where Rushing has the obvious edge is in collective experience. He likely won’t be able to catch even in an emergency role, though.
Having said that, as someone that can provide pop from the left side, the Dodgers will have to weigh whether experience wins out over a very young yet gifted rookie with less than 50 at-bats at the major league level.

title: Dodgers news: What Dave Roberts said about Shohei Ohtani's 1st game back from IL
author: Abdullah Imran; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: What Dave Roberts said about Shohei Ohtani's 1st game back from IL appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani returned to the lineup Wednesday after spending two weeks on the injured list.
Ohtani was activated before Los Angeles' 5-1 loss to the San Diego Padres after missing time because of left knee soreness and right biceps discomfort. It was his first game since Sept. 7, and he was inserted into the No. 2 spot against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.
The 32-year-old finished 1-for-4 with a walk and two strikeouts. His first at-bat ended with a 99 mph single to right field, and he later hit a 384-foot flyout to center. His biggest missed opportunity came in the fourth inning, when he struck out with the bases loaded during the Dodgers' best scoring chance.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Despite the result, manager Dave Roberts came away encouraged by what he saw from Ohtani.
"He looked good. I thought the at-bat quality was good," said Roberts. "There wasn't any chase. I thought he hit the ball hardest in his first at-bat. It's been a while since he's played in a game, but it just felt like he wasn't sped up at all."
In his final games before landing on the IL, Ohtani had appeared physically compromised at the plate, including moments when he shook out his arm and winced. Los Angeles placed him on the injured list on Sept. 9 after trying to manage the lingering issues while keeping him available.
Ohtani had begun his hitting program about a week before Wednesday's return and had recently faced simulated pitching. He had entered his last game before the IL stint batting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs, 89 runs and 80 walks through 134 games.
Roberts said Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Thursday for the series finale. The Dodgers are also still evaluating their batting order against left-handed pitching for the postseason. Against right-handers, Roberts said he would likely put Ohtani back in the leadoff spot and move Mookie Betts to No. 2.
Betts had occupied the leadoff role while Ohtani was away and was batting .366 with six homers, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs in 18 September games.
Ohtani won't take the mound in the playoffs, making his health at the plate all the more important as October approaches.
Related: Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal set to return to Dodgers

title: Giving back to LA schools ‘the right thing to do’ for Roberto Clemente Award nominee Smith
author: Sonja Chen
body:
Back when Will Smith's wife, Cara, taught first grade at a Title I school in Kentucky, she saw firsthand how many of her students did not have access to the resources they needed for success, whether at home or at school. Through her, it opened Smith's eyes to an area where he could one day make a difference.
In 2021, Cara and Will Smith founded the Catching Hope Foundation, which has been a presence in the Los Angeles community ever since. In recognition of the foundation's work, Will Smith was the Dodgers' nominee for the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award.
"It's a huge honor," Smith said. "I think Roberto's legacy is incredible. Obviously incredible baseball career, but more importantly, the stuff he did off the field. You know, he's 1A in that regard, doing things for other people and making other people's lives better."
The Roberto Clemente Award is one of Major League Baseball's highest honors, given annually to the player who best represents the game through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanthropy and positive contributions on and off the field.
One player from each team is nominated for the award, and the overall winner is determined by a blue-ribbon panel that includes a fan vote, which is open until Sunday. The winner will be honored during the 2026 World Series.
Mookie Betts won last year's Roberto Clemente Award, joining Justin Turner (2022), Clayton Kershaw (2012) and Steve Garvey (1981) as the fourth Dodger to win the league-wide honor. Smith could become the fifth, but for him, being able to use his platform for good is reward enough.
"We really enjoy brightening kids' days and helping them out and getting them on their feet, or just giving them opportunities that they probably wouldn't have had unless we step in and provide it," Smith said. "It's super important to us just because we feel like it's the right thing to do. We have an opportunity to help people and just enjoy it."
The Catching Hope Foundation states that its mission is "to help underprivileged children with critical skills needed for leadership, self-advocacy, and self-sufficiency." The aim is to allocate resources to students in need that will help them develop valuable tools for success.
To that end, the Catching Hope Foundation has entered into longer-term partnerships with multiple schools, beginning with Clifford Elementary School in 2024. The relationship began with an L.A. Reads Storytime event and continued across two school years, ending with the installation of a permanent outdoor literacy space as part of a 2024 World Series Legacy Initiative in partnership with the Dodgers and MLB.
In 2025, the Catching Hope Foundation partnered with two additional schools -- Manhattan Place Elementary School in South L.A. and Langdon Elementary School in the San Fernando Valley -- which also received outdoor literacy areas. As the relationships with each school blossomed, Smith and his foundation have gained a deeper understanding into how to best serve each community.
The Smiths work with school districts to identify which schools have the greatest needs, whether they be related to funding, student performance or external circumstances. Following the devastating 2025 Southern California wildfires, they partnered with the Los Angeles Unified School District Foundation and the Pasadena Unified School District Foundation to auction off the 2024 World Series final out ball, donating $180,000 in proceeds to the districts.
In April of this year, the Catching Hope Foundation visited one of the impacted LAUSD schools, Marquez Charter Elementary School, which burned down in the Palisades Fire but has since reopened. Students from Marquez Charter were later invited to Dodger Stadium for the Catching Hope Community Clinic, an annual event that hosts a different elementary school each year.
"We like trying to build a relationship with the schools and really get to know them and what they need and what's truly going to help the kids," Smith said. "Not, we're offering one thing to the school that might not need it. It's, no, what do you really need for the school that's really going to help encourage kids to show up and learn and be happy and just enjoy school and learning, and to set them up the rest of their lives?"
As a catcher, Smith builds relationships with the members of his pitching staff on a daily basis. That ability plays a big role in his work with the community, too.

title: Dodgers exec confirms Shohei Ohtani suspicions as injuries potentially impact playoff impact
author: Jack Harris
body:
In hindsight, Andrew Friedman made the Dodgers’ handling of Shohei Ohtani’s injury-plagued season this year sound rather simple.
Throughout Ohtani’s return to a full-time two-way role, the team’s president of baseball operations said, the Dodgers checked in with the superstar “on a daily basis, a weekly basis” to monitor how he was feeling as he handled both pitching and hitting duties.
That process intensified once Ohtani began battling left knee and right arm injuries in the middle of the season, leading both to the decision to remove Ohtani from the starting rotation in early July –– but also to let him continue playing through his ailments as the team’s everyday DH while attempting to ramp back up with a pitching program, as well.
It all reached a tipping point two weeks ago, when a clearly diminished Ohtani was finally placed on the injured list amid a 6-for-52 batting slump, and had any plans of returning to the mound this season scuttled for good.
And now, continuing such dialogue will be crucial over the rest of the campaign, with Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday for a postseason push that he and the team hopes will see the 32-year-old slugger rediscover his typical productivity at the plate.
“The most important thing is how much better he feels,” Friedman said, speaking to reporters before Ohtani’s 1-for-4 performance in a loss to the San Diego Padres. “Now, it’s about continuing that as he takes game-intensity at-bats.”
How Ohtani and the Dodgers reached this point, of course, has been the subject of much speculation and criticism over recent weeks.
From the start of the year, the club’s No. 1 priority was having Ohtani at full strength as a hitter entering the playoffs.
That they failed in that endeavour –– even Friedman acknowledged Wednesday that Ohtani probably isn’t back to 100% physically, though also insisted that “Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great” –– will be the source of significant retrospection within the organization.
Especially if a compromised Ohtani prevents the Dodgers from winning a third-consecutive World Series this fall.
“There’s no question [the injuries] affected him,” Friedman said. “I think the fact that he feels as good as he does right now is certainly encouraging. Now it’s about making sure that holds.”
Friedman didn’t assign blame for why Ohtani’s season went so wrong. He didn’t second-guess the team’s decision to let him play with his injuries for as long as they did, nor Ohtani’s insistence on trying to try and push through his physical problems.
Every time the sides met to discuss Ohtani’s usage, Friedman said, “his answer has been whatever it takes to help the team win. It legitimately has been that single time.”
The one dynamic Friedman did emphasize upon reflection, however, was whether Ohtani was honest enough with himself about how much his health had deteriorated.
“He’s not always the best reporter of how he feels,” Friedman said. “Freddie [Freeman is] the same way. Clayton Kershaw. I’ve been around a lot of these guys that feel like their job is to be out there to help the team however they can, and sometimes will downplay some things that are bothering them.”
In a vacuum, that isn’t necessarily a bad thing.
Friedman said he had “respect” for Ohtani’s dedication to post as often as possible. He recognized that, “in his mind, he thought the best way to help the team was to go out and play.”
At this point, though, it’s hard not to wonder whether Ohtani pushed himself too hard –– and that the team wasn’t proactive enough in stopping him from doing so.
“I think in his mind, he just thought that what he was dealing with was more minor,” Friedman said, while cutting Ohtani some slack by noting he never received more significant diagnoses than inflammation in both his knee and arm.
“Again, the communication back and forth has been awesome,” Friedman added. “The fully sharing exactly how he’s feeling, maybe not as awesome.”
It has certainly left the Dodgers in a less-than-awesome spot now, uncertain of exactly what version of Ohtani they will get over a grueling October trek.
This week, Friedman said the Dodgers want to get Ohtani “as many at-bats as we can” so he can build “some rhythm and timing” with his swing. However, he also didn’t commit to Ohtani playing all five of the team’s remaining games, wanting to see how he handles his return to action first (Wednesday’s performance, at least, offered some signs of progress).
It means, in the coming weeks, more daily check-ins will continue between Ohtani and the Dodgers.
At this point, it’s the best they can do to manage his health entering the playoffs.
As for the past?
“He was in a good enough spot to help us win,” Friedman said, “and we agreed with that.”

Throughout Ohtani’s return to a full-time two-way role, the team’s president of baseball operations said, the Dodgers checked in with the superstar “on a daily basis, a weekly basis” to monitor how he was feeling as he handled both pitching and hitting duties.
That process intensified once Ohtani began battling left knee and right arm injuries in the middle of the season, leading both to the decision to remove Ohtani from the starting rotation in early July –– but also to let him continue playing through his ailments as the team’s everyday DH while attempting to ramp back up with a pitching program, as well.
It all reached a tipping point two weeks ago, when a clearly diminished Ohtani was finally placed on the injured list amid a 6-for-52 batting slump, and had any plans of returning to the mound this season scuttled for good.
And now, continuing such dialogue will be crucial over the rest of the campaign, with Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday for a postseason push that he and the team hopes will see the 32-year-old slugger rediscover his typical productivity at the plate.
“The most important thing is how much better he feels,” Friedman said, speaking to reporters before Ohtani’s 1-for-4 performance in a loss to the San Diego Padres. “Now, it’s about continuing that as he takes game-intensity at-bats.”
How Ohtani and the Dodgers reached this point, of course, has been the subject of much speculation and criticism over recent weeks.
From the start of the year, the club’s No. 1 priority was having Ohtani at full strength as a hitter entering the playoffs.
That they failed in that endeavour –– even Friedman acknowledged Wednesday that Ohtani probably isn’t back to 100% physically, though also insisted that “Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great” –– will be the source of significant retrospection within the organization.
Especially if a compromised Ohtani prevents the Dodgers from winning a third-consecutive World Series this fall.
“There’s no question [the injuries] affected him,” Friedman said. “I think the fact that he feels as good as he does right now is certainly encouraging. Now it’s about making sure that holds.”
Friedman didn’t assign blame for why Ohtani’s season went so wrong. He didn’t second-guess the team’s decision to let him play with his injuries for as long as they did, nor Ohtani’s insistence on trying to try and push through his physical problems.
Every time the sides met to discuss Ohtani’s usage, Friedman said, “his answer has been whatever it takes to help the team win. It legitimately has been that single time.”
The one dynamic Friedman did emphasize upon reflection, however, was whether Ohtani was honest enough with himself about how much his health had deteriorated.
“He’s not always the best reporter of how he feels,” Friedman said. “Freddie [Freeman is] the same way. Clayton Kershaw. I’ve been around a lot of these guys that feel like their job is to be out there to help the team however they can, and sometimes will downplay some things that are bothering them.”
In a vacuum, that isn’t necessarily a bad thing.
Friedman said he had “respect” for Ohtani’s dedication to post as often as possible. He recognized that, “in his mind, he thought the best way to help the team was to go out and play.”
At this point, though, it’s hard not to wonder whether Ohtani pushed himself too hard –– and that the team wasn’t proactive enough in stopping him from doing so.
“I think in his mind, he just thought that what he was dealing with was more minor,” Friedman said, while cutting Ohtani some slack by noting he never received more significant diagnoses than inflammation in both his knee and arm.
“Again, the communication back and forth has been awesome,” Friedman added. “The fully sharing exactly how he’s feeling, maybe not as awesome.”
It has certainly left the Dodgers in a less-than-awesome spot now, uncertain of exactly what version of Ohtani they will get over a grueling October trek.
This week, Friedman said the Dodgers want to get Ohtani “as many at-bats as we can” so he can build “some rhythm and timing” with his swing. However, he also didn’t commit to Ohtani playing all five of the team’s remaining games, wanting to see how he handles his return to action first (Wednesday’s performance, at least, offered some signs of progress).
It means, in the coming weeks, more daily check-ins will continue between Ohtani and the Dodgers.
At this point, it’s the best they can do to manage his health entering the playoffs.
As for the past?
“He was in a good enough spot to help us win,” Friedman said, “and we agreed with that.”

title: 山本由伸 大谷復帰に「うれしい」自身は９敗目もＭＬＢトップ２２度目ＱＳ/デイリースポーツ online
author: デイリースポーツ編集部
body:
山本由伸 大谷復帰に「うれしい」自身は９敗目もＭＬＢトップ２２度目ＱＳ
「ドジャース１－５パドレス」（２３日、ロサンゼルス）
ドジャースの山本由伸投手（２８）は６回４失点で９敗目を喫した。それでも自責点２で、ＭＬＢ単独トップとなる２２度目のクオリティースタート（６回以上、自責点３以下）を達成。「うれしく思いますし、またそういうことができるように頑張ります」と、力を込めた。
大谷の復帰についても言及。一緒にゲームに出場したことで「同じ試合に出られてうれしいし、チームメートも同じだと思います。何よりファンの方がうれしいと思いますし、とにかくよかった」と語った。
今回がレギュラーシーズン最後の登板となり、今後はポストシーズンに向け調整する。昨季のワールドシリーズは獅子奮迅の活躍でＭＶＰを獲得。３連覇に向け「今も去年も調子よくシーズンを終われた。体の調子も良くてしっかり準備できると思う」と語っていた。

title: Los Angeles Dodgers' Mookie Betts Signs With 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment
author: Loree Seitz
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts has signed with 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment for personal representation.
Under the new representation structure, the firms will spearhead the four-time World Series champion’s personal endorsements, brand partnerships and business development.
The partnership comes as the eight-time MLB All-Star and entrepreneur hopes to expand his business footprint off the field, with both 3 Arts Sports and SSE focused on his personal branding and business endeavors. It marks a shift in Betts’ career as he focuses on long-term creative ownership and global brand expansion.
“Mookie Betts is a generational talent on the field and an incredibly forward-thinking entrepreneur off it. We are thrilled to collaborate across sports and entertainment to build a comprehensive strategy for one of baseball’s most enduring icons,” 3 Arts Entertainment co-CEO Brian Weinstein and SSE founder and president Doug Sanders said in a joint statement. “This partnership aligns with Mookie’s ambitious vision by tapping into our respective teams’ expertise and industry relationships.”
Betts joins the 3 Arts Sports roster alongside sports stars that have shaken up the pop culture scene, including Travis Kelce, the WNBA’s Sophie Cunningham and NFL star Jayden Daniels.
“I’ve always believed in surrounding myself with people who understand my vision and bring expertise in areas where I can continue to grow,” Betts said. “As the opportunities around me have continued to evolve, it felt important to build a specialized team that could help me navigate and develop those opportunities the right way. I’m excited to have 3 Arts Sports and SSE alongside me and to have the right people in place to support everything I’m building off the field.”

title: Shohei Ohtani is back — but something doesn’t look right with Dodgers star
author: Dylan Hernandez
body:
Something’s not right.
The Dodgers said so without saying so.
When Shohei Ohtani returned from the 15-day injured list, they batted him second.
This is no knock on Mookie Betts, who led off instead. Betts is an eight-time All-Star who is hitting .317 over his last 42 games, but Ohtani is, well, Ohtani.
Ohtani is the best player in baseball when healthy, or even close to healthy. If the Dodgers believed Ohtani could be that player for them in the postseason, they wouldn’t have moved him out of his customary spot in the order, and it wouldn’t have mattered how anyone else on their team was hitting or whether the opposing pitcher was right- and left-handed.
Presumably, the Dodgers had more insights into his injured right arm and left knee than they shared.
Which is why enthusiasm over Ohtani’s performance on Wednesday should be tempered.
Without question, Ohtani looked better in the 5-1 loss to the San Diego Padres than he did the last time he played.
That didn’t mean he was back to playing like himself – or that he will be at any time during the playoffs.
The return of a Most Valuable Player can have transformative effects on a team, especially if that Most Valuable Player is as healthy as the Dodgers claimed Ohtani was after resting for two-plus weeks, but President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman and manager Dave Roberts both spent time before the game managing expectations.
Asked which version of Ohtani was coming back to the team, Friedman replied, “I mean, these aren’t things there’s a clear answer to.”
Roberts said he wanted to see Ohtani “being controlled, taking good at-bats.”
By that standard, Ohtani’s first game back was a massive triumph.
In the first inning, Ohtani singled off left-hander Robbie Ray on the kind of low pitch he was physically incapable of reaching two or three weeks earlier because of his knee problem.
Ohtani later drove a high 99-mph fastball to the warning track, prompting Dodgers broadcaster Joe Davis to scream: “That is a majestic fly ball!”
“I think if you look back at the last couple weeks when he was active, he wasn’t getting to that pitch,” Roberts said of the four-seamer upstairs from right-hander Bradgley Rodriguez.
For the most part, Ohtani didn’t swing at pitches outside of the strike zone. He worked two-ball counts in each of his first four plate appearances, and drew a walk in the third inning.
The Dodgers would almost certainly take games like this from Ohtani. Regardless of what he actually was and wasn’t able to do, the Padres viewed him as a threat, and that alone made him a presence in the lineup.
Ohtani has acknowledged he was unlikely to be 100% healthy again this season, but maintaining an aura of danger will require him to not return to where he was physically leading up to his IL stint.
“Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start,” Friedman said. “Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. When you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’re done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Or, in this case, to at least be viewed as a threat.
Roberts previously described Ohtani as “pain-free” but acknowledged he was still dealing with “discomfort you can play through.” The Dodgers have already seen what happens when Ohtani plays too many games with his arm and knee problems, and every game he plays theoretically pushes him closer to the stage at which the pain becomes unbearable.
How close is Ohtani to that point?
Was the usually-aggressive Ohtani as patient as he was in the batter’s box because he wanted to protect his arm by limiting his swings?
Did his warning-track drive not clear the outfield wall because he hit the ball with the end of his bat or because he wasn’t at full strength?
What should be made of the two at-bats in which he struck out? With the bases loaded, two outs and the count full in the fourth inning, Ohtani was late on a 98.5-mph sinker by David Morgan. In the ninth, Ohtani looked as if he had no chance against closer Mason Miller, who struck him out on three pitches.
Ohtani wasn’t made available to answer any of these questions. By the time the clubhouse opened to reporters, Ohtani was gone.

“Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start,” Friedman said. “Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. When you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’re done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Or, in this case, to at least be viewed as a threat.
Roberts previously described Ohtani as “pain-free” but acknowledged he was still dealing with “discomfort you can play through.” The Dodgers have already seen what happens when Ohtani plays too many games with his arm and knee problems, and every game he plays theoretically pushes him closer to the stage at which the pain becomes unbearable.
How close is Ohtani to that point?
Was the usually-aggressive Ohtani as patient as he was in the batter’s box because he wanted to protect his arm by limiting his swings?
Did his warning-track drive not clear the outfield wall because he hit the ball with the end of his bat or because he wasn’t at full strength?
What should be made of the two at-bats in which he struck out? With the bases loaded, two outs and the count full in the fourth inning, Ohtani was late on a 98.5-mph sinker by David Morgan. In the ninth, Ohtani looked as if he had no chance against closer Mason Miller, who struck him out on three pitches.
Ohtani wasn’t made available to answer any of these questions. By the time the clubhouse opened to reporters, Ohtani was gone.

title: Josue De Paula Earns Rave Reviews From Dodgers Leadership
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula is no longer on the active roster after getting sent down to Triple-A, but the major league team had nothing but positive things to say.
De Paula played just 11 games with the Dodgers, but he delivered outstanding offensive production and quickly earned the fanbase’s adoration as a young presence at the plate.
However, he was demoted as Shohei Ohtani neared activation from the injured list. Fans who bought into what the 21-year-old showed were disappointed, but the organization seemed just as reluctant to see him go.
What the Dodgers think of De Paula
After the move was announced, manager Dave Roberts said De Paula, as the team’s default designated hitter, was set to lose at-bats now that Ohtani returned.
Still, De Paula earned a postseason look, and the team will factor him into its plans.
“We had a runway to give him, which we gave him, and he performed more than admirably. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night,” Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez.
In terms of skill set, Roberts sees all of De Paul’s traits — the plate approach, swing decision, and vision to deliver in the postseason.
“He’s just a special hitter,” Roberts added. “Hitters don’t see the ball that quickly out of hand; it’s a gift. Just the ability to [limit] chase, I think that lines up in the postseason. And no moment is going to be too big for that kid.”
De Paula’s impressive numbers
Through 11 games in the big leagues, De Paul is hitting .323/.500/.545 with a 1.081 OPS. He is getting on base during half of his plate appearances, and he is really making hitters work.
Andrew Friedman, the president of baseball operations, had been following De Paula closely, and despite the otherworldly production, the Dodgers executive was not surprised.
“It’s what you expect, but you never really know until you see it,” Friedman said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
“But it obviously really stood out, and he’s done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we’re making our postseason roster.”
Meanwhile, Josue De Paula gets the chance to show what he can do defensively in Triple-A while the Dodgers decide.

title: Dodgers' push for first-round bye, favorable playoff schedule means more for Miguel Rojas
author: Katrina Stebbins
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have already punched their ticket to the postseason and rule the NL West once again, but there's a final frontier that eluded them in 2025. They're cusp on clinching a first-round bye in the National League over the Atlanta Braves; a win for the Dodgers or a loss for the Braves on Thursday would lock it up for LA.
The Dodgers would surely love a few days off between the end of the regular season and the start of the NLDS, given how banged up the roster is right now. Shohei Ohtani, Dalton Rushing, and Blake Snell are just a few of their recently injured players who could use a little more time to prepare.
Miguel Rojas would also love to not have to work on October 1, but not because of an injury. According to Bill Plunkett of the Orange County Register, Rojas is scheduled to take his US citizenship test on the same day as a potential Game 3 of the Wild Card series. Rojas is looking to follow in the footsteps of Cincinnati Reds slugger — and fellow Venezuela native — Eugenio Suárez, who passed his citizenship test this season, who passed earlier this month.
The Dodgers would love to have Miguel Rojas for every game of the playoffs
Even if the Dodgers were to fall into the Wild Card, they would host all three of those games at Dodger Stadium, but that could still complicate Rojas' participation in that series. LA could always leave him off the Wild Card roster and bring him back for the NLDS, but he's been on almost every Dodgers postseason roster since he returned to the team in 2023. The only exception was the NLDS in 2024, when he sat with injury.
Rojas has been working in the United States since 2010, when the Reds signed him as an international free agent, but his family still lives in his home country. Earlier this season, he declined a move to the bereavement list after his father passed away in Venezuela, and his wife and children were in Caracas during the devastating earthquakes the country suffered in June.
He's set to retire at the end of the season but has major league coaching and managerial aspirations, so staying in the United States after his playing career makes sense.
Barring disaster, the Dodgers' schedule should be clear to let Rojas take the next step toward US citizenship. Dodgers fans are surely wishing Miggy the best of luck.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Announced Dalton Rushing Update
author: Ben Stinar
body:
On Thursday night, the Los Angeles Dodgers will finish their series with the San Diego Padres (at home).
They are coming off a 5-1 loss on Wednesday night.
Dodgers Announced Dalton Rushing Update
This week, the Dodgers announced the latest update on Dalton Rushing.
He has been out since September 5 with an injury.
MLB.com wrote (on September 22): “Could be activated before the end of the regular season so that the Dodgers can evaluate him as a bench option. He will only be a hitter.”
Before getting hurt, Rushing had been batting .249 with 55 hits, 12 home runs, 36 RBIs and 37 runs in 78 games.
Rushing was picked in the 2nd round of the 2022 MLB Draft.
He is in the middle of his second season in the MLB (all with the Dodgers).
Looking At The Dodgers Right Now
The Dodgers have had another fantastic season.
They are currently 97-61 with a 158 games.

title: L.A. Dodgers Star Mookie Betts Signed By 3 Arts Sports & SSE
author: Anthony D'Alessandro
body:
3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment have partnered to sign Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts for personal representation.
The signing comes at a time when the Dodgers have clinched a playoff spot for a 14th consecutive season. Betts has been playing as shortstop this season. 
Under this new representation structure, 3 Arts Sports and SSE will co-manage personal endorsements, brand partnerships and business development for the four-time World Series champion, eight-time All-Star and former American League MVP.
"Mookie Betts is a generational talent on the field and an incredibly forward-thinking entrepreneur off it. We are thrilled to collaborate across sports and entertainment to build a comprehensive strategy for one of baseball's most enduring icons," said Brian Weinstein, co-CEO of 3 Arts Entertainment, and Doug Sanders, Founder & President of SSE. "This partnership aligns with Mookie's ambitious vision by tapping into our respective teams' expertise and industry relationships."
More from Deadline
"I've always believed in surrounding myself with people who understand my vision and bring expertise in areas where I can continue to grow," said Betts. "As the opportunities around me have continued to evolve, it felt important to build a specialized team that could help me navigate and develop those opportunities the right way. I'm excited to have 3 Arts Sports and SSE alongside me and to have the right people in place to support everything I'm building off the field."
This representation structure marks a unified effort to maximize Betts' impact both as a global athlete and an entrepreneur. 3 Arts Sports and SSE will focus on his personal brand, endorsements and business endeavors.
The Nashville, TN-born Betts was drafted by the Boston Red Sox in 2011 and made his MLB debut in the 2014 season, where he played second base and outfield. He soon became the Red Sox center fielder in 2014 moving to right field in 2016, helping them win the World Series in 2018 when he won the AL MVP award. In 2020, after six seasons with Boston, Betts was traded to the Dodgers and signed a 12-year, $365 million extension with the team through the 2032 season.
Betts counts 22 home runs this season with 68 RBIs.

title: Will Smith Ready to Guide Pitching Staff Into October
author: Steve Webb
body:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Will Smith continued to show encouraging signs at the plate Wednesday night, collecting a single and drawing two walks in the Dodgers’ 5-1 loss to the Padres. The catcher worked lengthy at-bats throughout the evening, something he hopes will carry over into October.
Asked about his approach as the postseason draws closer, Smith emphasized the importance of remaining selective and making opposing pitchers work.
“Just trying to swing at the right pitches, take the right pitches, foul good pitches off,” Smith said. “Just trying to take one good at-bat at a time.”
With San Diego representing a possible postseason opponent, Smith was also asked whether the potential for another October meeting changes how the Dodgers approach their remaining regular-season games.
His answer was straightforward.
“No, we’re still approaching it trying to win ballgames,” he said. “I don’t think we’ve clinched the bye yet, so we’re still trying to do that.”
Wednesday’s loss delayed the Dodgers’ opportunity to secure that coveted first-round bye, but Smith indicated that the team’s confidence remains intact. He emphasized that the players have maintained a consistent outlook throughout the season, recognizing that individual losses are inevitable while keeping their larger objective in mind.
“Just one day at a time,” Smith said. “We’re not going to win every game. We still believe in each other day in and day out to win a ballgame and to reach our goal of winning the World Series again.”
With October approaching, Smith and the Dodgers remain focused on securing their postseason position before turning their attention to defending their championship.

rss_title: Will Smith Ready to Guide Pitching Staff Into October
rss_body:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Will Smith continued to show encouraging signs at the plate Wednesday night, collecting a single and drawing two walks in the Dodgers’ 5-1 loss to the Padres. The catcher worked lengthy at-bats throughout the evening, something he hopes will carry over into October.
Asked about his approach as the postseason draws closer, Smith emphasized the importance of remaining selective and making opposing pitchers work.
“Just trying to swing at the right pitches, take the right pitches, foul good pitches off,” Smith said. “Just trying to take one good at-bat at a time.”
With San Diego representing a possible postseason opponent, Smith was also asked whether the potential for another October meeting changes how the Dodgers approach their remaining regular-season games.
His answer was straightforward.
“No, we’re still approaching it trying to win ballgames,” he said. “I don’t think we’ve clinched the bye yet, so we’re still trying to do that.”
Wednesday’s loss delayed the Dodgers’ opportunity to secure that coveted first-round bye, but Smith indicated that the team’s confidence remains intact. He emphasized that the players have maintained a consistent outlook throughout the season, recognizing that individual losses are inevitable while keeping their larger objective in mind.
“Just one day at a time,” Smith said. “We’re not going to win every game. We still believe in each other day in and day out to win a ballgame and to reach our goal of winning the World Series again.”
With October approaching, Smith and the Dodgers remain focused on securing their postseason position before turning their attention to defending their championship.
