| 11 | Pavin Smith | ARI | 1B | 30% | $4 | 
| 12 | Anthony Volpe | NYY | SS | 30% | $5 | 
AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
Pitchers were the most popular targets, specifically two-steppers, as we chase wins and strikeouts, hoping the Ratio Monster doesn’t eat our leads in ERA and WHIP. JR Ritchie and Daniel Lynch IV were the most added starters who we expect two starts from this week. Ritchie’s MLB debut back in April came with great promise, but walks haunted him greatly, which led to trips back to Triple-A to refine his craft and some bulk inning relief work when he returned to Atlanta in July. Ritchie was recently promoted again, and ran into a juggernaut Cubs offense last week, allowing six runs on seven hits in 4.2 innings. The walk rate (13.7%) isn’t pretty, and he has a good opportunity to end his season on a high note with two reasonable matchups — against the Reds at home and the Marlins on the road. Lynch had served the Royals well as their top southpaw out of the bullpen for most of the season. He moved to the rotation in August and slowly worked his pitch counts upward. Lynch has made it to five innings in each of his last three starts. His latest one (at HOU on September 16) went well — 5 IP – 2 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 3 K. More of that please as he faces the White Sox and Guardians at Kauffman Stadium in the final week. If I could only choose one for the week, it would be Ritchie.
Red Sox pitchers Brayan Bello and Garrett Whitlock were popular buys as the likelihood of roto stars shining bright on them this week is high. Bello is coming off a tremendous outing against the AL-leading Rays on Saturday where he posted an 11:0 K:BB with just one run allowed in eight innings. Those 11 punchies tied his career high. Bello had been the worst starter in the game (6.49 ERA, 1.67 WHIP) through June 4, when he was optioned to Triple-A. Since the All-Star break, mostly out of relief and with two starts, the 27-year-old has been shining. Over those 51.1 innings, he is rocking exemplary ratios (2.28 ERA, 1.01 WHIP) and a 17% K-BB% (22.3% K, 5.3% BB). Bello should make a start against the Cubs next Saturday. The Cubs should be settled into a playoff spot by then, so perhaps they give Pete Crow-Armstrong and some of the other regulars that day off. Boston’s closer Aroldis Chapman has been day-to-day with a lat issue, so perhaps the Red sox have him take it easy and provide Whitlock with some save opportunities. Whitlock has a 7-2 record with a 17.5 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and four saves.
Streaming Diamondbacks is a good idea this week, specifically for their three-game set at Coors Field against the Rockies in the early part of the week. Pavin Smith was a coveted target, coming off a four-day stretch where three of his hits were home runs. Don’t expect Smith to start against lefty Kyle Freeland, but he should be in the lineup for the other two contests against righties. Nolan Arenado was available in one of the 60 Main Event leagues and was acquired for just one dollar.
Better late than never for two punchless Padres who have been quite productive and certainly enjoyed their visit to Coors Field in the first half of last week. Dustin Harris ($10 AWB) and Samad Taylor ($5) have been red hot and playing often over the last 10 days. Though he doesn’t have a home run yet, Harris has been quite productive and helpful to early-bird managers: eight runs, 12 runs batted in and three steals, batting .384 with a 166 wRC+ in 40 plate appearances since September 11. He’s also been batting second against right-handed starters. Taylor has at least one hit in nine of his last 10, including a 3-for-3 effort on Sunday, and has driven in seven in his last seven games.

AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
As always, more reliable starting pitcher depth was available in the 12-team OC pool. Cristian Javier, Anthony Kay, Robert Gasser, Lynch, Yusei Kikuchi, and Max Scherzer were the most added pitchers this week. Javier should pitch twice this week and will hope to put his best foot forward (in this case, his right arm) as the Astros fight for the AL West and a playoff spot. Sutter Health Park is not a fun place to pitch, but the A’s lineup is a watered-down version without Brent Rooker, Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, and Jacob Wilson윌슨. Javier’s first start is in Seattle may not be a picnic with gluten-free granola and Pearl Jam on the Discman.
Milwaukee’s Robert Gasser only draws one start (home vs. STL), but is considered a reliable ratios guy who can score a much-needed win for fantasy managers, as the Brewers will certainly be favorites in that matchup. Gasser earned his fifth win on Saturday, throwing seven scoreless innings against the Orioles. White Sox lefty Anthony Kay has good matchups (at KC on Tuesday and vs. COL on Sunday), though that second start could be pulled away from him. The main problems here is that Kay hasn’t made it to the fifth inning in any of his last five starts. I feel much more comfortable with a single start against the Orioles from Max Scherzer than I do a double (at SEA, at ATH) from wily Yusei Kikuchi. Kikuchi has walked 12 batters in his last three starts.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ryan Johnson | LAA | SP | 50% | 12% | 
| 2 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 18% | 10% | 
| 3 | Jack Perkins | ATH | RP | 26% | 7% | 
| 4 | Dean Kremer | MIN | SP | 45% | 7% | 
| 5 | Ryan Watson | LAA | RP | 10% | 6% |

| 7 | David Peterson | CHC | SP | 56% | 5% | 
| 8 | David Sandlin | CHW | RP | 21% | 5% | 
| 9 | Victor Mesa Jr. | TB | OF | 43% | 4% | 
| 10 | Leo Bernal | STL | C | 35% | 3% | 
| 11 | Javier Sanoja | MIA | 2B,3B,SS,OF | 62% | 3% | 
(+/-) is the % of leagues the player was added to in the previous week
It’s possible that attraction towards Ryan Johnson this weekend relates to dynasty and keeper formats, and not his start in Seattle this week. Johnson has limited run damage over his last nine starts, since August 6, posting a 2.39 ERA, but with an xFIP (5.01) nearly double the mark. Johnson is more of a 4.25-4.50 ERA guy than a sub-3.00 ERA one, as his 90.9% LOB and .229 BABIP portends.
Perhaps a similar mindset applies to folks who scooped up Jack Perkins, who pitched two quality starts on the road against the Rays (6.2 IP – 4 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 8 K) and the Guardians (6 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 0 BB – 4 K), flashing some of his upside and future potential. Perkins has had a difficult season (5.90 ERA, but a 4.16 xFIP, 1.45 WHIP) and will be a tough streamer at home in Sacramento next season, but the strikeouts (25.2%) should always be there.
Andrew Alvarez should have a rotation spot with the Nationals next season. He has been outstanding since the All-Star break, posting a 2.44 ERA (3.30 FIP, 4.02 xFIP) with a 1.10 WHIP and a 22.7% strikeout rate, though he wasn’t able to secure a win in any of those 10 starts. Alvarez won’t be a particularly coveted target in drafts next season, but should have a NFBC ADP somewhere in the 250-325 overall range. He may be a consideration in NL-only keeper leagues with deep benches and five-plus keepers.
Bold Predictions for Week 27
Gavin Williams and Jacob Misiorowski finish the season tied for the MLB lead in strikeouts with 255. Williams punches out 11 and Misiorowski, eight.
JR Ritchie steps up for his two starts and has a Jack Perkins Week 26 type week, helping managers win league titles.
Cade Cavalli twirls a gem in Detroit this week and pulls his 3.02 ERA under 3.00 to end the season. Cavalli will have a top-60 ADP in 2027.
Jo Adell takes advantage of four left-handed starters this week and earns seven RBIs to reach 100, after falling two RBIs short last season.
One of Cristian Javier or Yusei Kikuchi will remind why streaming pitchers in Sutter Health Park, even if part of a two-step, is a mistake.
Miguel Vargas and Colson Montgomery hit three home runs each this week and the White Sox score the most runs in Week 27.
The Houston Astros win the NL West and knock the Texas Rangers out of playoff contention.

original_body:
Every Monday, this column will break down the most popular waiver wire and free agent acquisitions from the weekend. I dig into the top adds on the ever-popular Fantrax and in the NFBC Online Championship (OC), a national mid-stakes contest with 240 total leagues of 12 and a six-figure grand prize. Reviewing player adds between the two should provide us with a well-rounded perspective and barometer of the fantasy baseball marketplace.
Week 26 Overview
Hitters
The San Diego Padres took advantage of their four-game series with the Rockies at Coors Field and a home set with the Marlins, scoring 51 runs, 12 more than any other team. Fernando Tatis Jr. (along with Brandon Lowe and Pete Crow-Armstrong) led the way with a week-high four dingers. Last week’s streamers turned out to be dynamite: Jake Cronenworth (.464-8-2-8-2), Dustin Harris (.379-5-0-7-2) and Samad Taylor (.556-6-1-7-1) really stepped up, particularly Taylor for my competitive Main Event squad that gained two category points in batting average last week. Rake Cronenworth was true to his nickname from several years ago. He led all Major League hitters with 13 hits. The Brewers swiped a league-high 12 bags last week: four each for Jackson Chourio and rookie Cooper Pratt. Tampa’s Chandler Simpson led all runners with five swipes, finally catching Washington’s Nasim Nuñez for the MLB lead with 46. Expect Simpson to finish with 50+ and win the stolen base crown.
Pitchers
Of the 29 two-start pitchers excluding Pirates opener Lake Bachar, three earned two wins: Tarik Skubal, Sean Burke and David Peterson. Houston’s Hunter Brown had an outstanding two-step (10 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 5 K – 20 K) and those 20 punchouts led all pitchers for the week. Gavin Williams punched out 16 in 12 innings and is back atop the AL lead in strikeouts with 244. Dylan Cease (239) may not make his final start of the season and Cam Schlittler (234) is unlikely to catch Williams as both have one start remaining. It’s very possible that Williams catches and passes Jacob Misiorowski (247) for the Major League lead. The Miz pitched three innings in his weekend start and might be limited for his final one.
Tampa’s Bryan Baker was the first reliever to reach 40 saves this season. It’s possible that Cade Smith (39), Riley O’Brien (38) and Mason Miller (37) join Baker. The last time there were three closers with 40 or more saves was in 2019: Edwin Díaz (57), Wade Davis (43), and Craig Kimbrel (42). Shout out to folks who drafted O’Brien late, and/or picked up Baker, Louis Varland or Jacob Latz off waivers and didn’t have to worry about the saves category all season.

It’s the last hurrah for managers with FAB dollars left, hoping to get the best bang for the buck and for variance to lean their way and tip them into league titles. It was odd seeing Shohei Ohtani available in several leagues, and perhaps fortuitous as he should be activated this week and start a few games. Ohtani was acquired in 26 OCs for an AWB of $17. In Main Events, there were 12 shares available and they went for a reasonable $12 a pop. I scooped up a rare Ohtani share in an OC for $2, winning a tiebreaker over the team in 1st place in that league. Andy Pages will be activated on Tuesday, which should push Tommy Edman back to second base. Pages had been out since August 21, but was producing at an exciting clip before the injury — .272 – 72 R – 21 HR – 80 RBI – 12 SB in 550 PA. Managers who acquired him are hoping that he dusts the cobwebs back off and gets right into the swing of things, with all the marbles on the line.

Ritchie’s MLB debut back in April came with great promise, but walks haunted him greatly, which led to trips back to Triple-A to refine his craft and some bulk inning relief work when he returned to Atlanta in July. Ritchie was recently promoted again, and ran into a juggernaut Cubs offense last week, allowing six runs on seven hits in 4.2 innings. The walk rate (13.7%) isn’t pretty, and he has a good opportunity to end his season on a high note with two reasonable matchups — against the Reds at home and the Marlins on the road. Red Sox pitchers Brayan Bello and Garrett Whitlock were popular buys as the likelihood of roto stars shining bright on them this week is high. Bello is coming off a tremendous outing against the AL-leading Rays on Saturday where he posted an 11:0 K:BB with just one run allowed in eight innings. Those 11 punchies tied his career high. Streaming Diamondbacks is a good idea this week, specifically for their three-game set at Coors Field against the Rockies in the early part of the week. Pavin Smith was a coveted target, coming off a four-day stretch where three of his hits were home runs. Don’t expect Smith to start against lefty Kyle Freeland, but he should be in the lineup for the other two contests against righties. Nolan Arenado was available in one of the 60 Main Event leagues and was acquired for just one dollar.

He’s also been batting second against right-handed starters. Taylor has at least one hit in nine of his last 10, including a 3-for-3 effort on Sunday, and has driven in seven in his last seven games.

title: 山本由伸でもベッツでもない…ド軍だけ“異変” 球団の顔が…最新格付けに漂う違和感
author: Full-Count編集部
body:
山本由伸でもベッツでもない…ド軍だけ“異変” 球団の顔が…最新格付けに漂う違和感
MLB公式がチームパワーランキングトップ10を発表した
MLB公式インスタグラムが21日（日本時間22日）、最新の「チームパワーランキング」トップ10を発表した。各球団を代表する主力選手が画像として並ぶなか、2位に入ったドジャースの“顔”として選出されたのは意外な選手だった。
1位のブルワーズにはジャクソン・チョーリオ外野手とウィリアム・コントレラス捕手、3位のレイズにはジュニオール・カミネロ内野手、4位のブレーブスにはロナルド・アクーニャJr.外野手、6位のカブスにはピート・クロウ＝アームストロング外野手ら、各チームで目覚ましい活躍を見せる中心選手たちが大々的にフィーチャーされた。
そのなかで異彩を放ったのが、2位に位置付けられたドジャースだ。球団の顔として掲載されたのは、大谷翔平投手でも、ムーキー・ベッツ内野手でも、山本由伸投手でもなく、期待の若手であるホスエ・デポーラ外野手だった。
他球団が主力級やチームの看板選手を当然のように並べるなか、大物スターがずらりと揃うドジャースにあって、まだメジャーでの実績が極めて少ないデポーラが選ばれたチョイスには、やや違和感を拭えない。
直近の話題性や若手の抜擢という文脈はあるにせよ、圧倒的な存在感を放つスター選手たちを差し置いた画像選定。豪華絢爛なドジャース陣容のなかで浮き彫りとなった“異例の抜擢”は、思わぬ形で注目を集めることとなった。

title: Josué De Paula gana el premio al Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Texas League en AA
author: Juan Mercado
body:
El prospecto dominicano Josué De Paula, el prospecto principal de los Dodgers, se ha convertido en una pieza clave para el equipo de Grandes Ligas durante la recta final de la temporada en la última semana y media. Sin embargo, esto sucedió tras una campaña magnífica en el equipo de Doble-A de Tulsa; el lunes fue nombrado Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Texas League.
Josue De Paula got called up from Double-A to the big leagues at 21 years.
Here are his stats after 10 MLB games and 38 PA.👇
.286 AVG
.474 OBP
.500 SLG
.974 OPS
4 XBH
10 BB
4 K
🔥 pic.twitter.com/DKg7saFAyL
Jugando para los Drillers, De Paula registró una línea ofensiva de .303/.401/.547, con un wRC+ de 145, 27 jonrones, 37 dobles, 106 carreras anotadas, 104 carreras impulsadas y 31 bases robadas en 124 partidos. Estableció marcas personales en todos los rubros, incluyendo más del doble de sus registros anteriores en jonrones (su máximo previo era de 12) y extrabases (66, frente a los 30 anteriores).
Lideró la liga en carreras anotadas, carreras impulsadas, hits y dobles; además, se ubicó entre los cinco mejores de la liga en OPS, porcentaje de slugging, porcentaje de embasado (OBP), promedio de bateo, jonrones, bases robadas, bases totales (274) y extrabases.
También el lunes, Baseball America nombró a De Paula como el Jugador del Año de las ligas menores de los Dodgers.
De Paula no ha dejado de rendir desde su ascenso a las Grandes Ligas; se ha embasado 18 veces en 38 visitas al plato —con 10 bases por bolas que más que duplican sus cuatro ponches— y registra una línea ofensiva de .286/.474/.500, con tres dobles y un jonrón en sus primeros 10 partidos en las mayores.
Los Dodgers contaban con una gran cantidad de prospectos en los jardines este año; de hecho, todos los jardineros seleccionados para el Juego de Estrellas de la Texas League pertenecían a los Tulsa Drillers: Zyhir Hope —traspasado el 2 de agosto a los Detroit Tigers en la operación por Tarik Skubal— y Mike Sirota acompañaron a De Paula. Otros jugadores de Tulsa seleccionados para el Juego de Estrellas fueron el jugador de cuadro Jake Gelof (como bateador designado) y el relevista Nick Robertson.
Eric Wedge fue nombrado Mánager del Año de la Texas League, convirtiéndose en el quinto dirigente de los Tulsa Drillers en obtener este galardón y el primero desde Tim Ireland en 2002, cuando Tulsa era filial de los Texas Rangers. Este reconocimiento llega 19 años después de que Wedge ganara el premio al Mánager del Año de la Liga Americana con Cleveland en 2007.
Hasta ahora, un jugador de ligas menores de los Dodgers ha ganado el premio al Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) en los tres niveles de temporada completa: De Paula se une al jardinero Charles Davalan (Great Lakes, Clase A Avanzada/Midwest League) y al primera base Ontario Easton Shelton (Clase A/California League). Cuando se anuncien los premios de Triple-A, James Tibbs III tendrá buenas posibilidades de ganar el MVP de la Pacific Coast League.

title: Dodgers activate two key players immediately before big Padres series
author: J P Hoornstra
body:
With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres.
Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium—a berth in the postseason for San Diego and a first-round bye for Los Angeles.
Sasaki posted a 3.05 ERA in seven starts after the All-Star break but developed a blister on his throwing hand in August. Pages played in his first All-Star Game in July but fractured a bone in his right hand when he was hit by a 100.2 mph fastball from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler on Aug. 21.
The Dodgers were able to clinch the National League West without the two players, but both figure to play key roles in October for the defending World Series champions.
Postseason roles
The team lost hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez to a back injury earlier this month. For all his second-half success as a starter, the Dodgers need Sasaki more in their bullpen as a right-handed complement to left-handers Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia.
Pages, meanwhile, was excelling at the plate and in the field prior to his injury, which required surgery. He’ll have six games to tune up for the postseason—and a chance at redemption for last October.
The Dodgers won the World Series even though Pages had only four hits in 16 postseason games, managing just an .078 batting average across four playoff rounds.
Without Pages, the Dodgers moved veteran utilityman Tommy Edman to center field. Through week’s end, he was slashing .245/.328/.376 (94 OPS+) in 79 games this season.
The Dodgers are also expecting Shohei Ohtani to return during the Padres series, but he isn’t eligible to be activated from the 15-day injured list before Wednesday.
In corresponding 26-man roster moves, pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

title: Dave Roberts' handling of Roki Sasaki shows why the Dodgers keep winning
author: Jake Elman
body:
If you needed yet another reminder of why Dave Roberts has led the Los Angeles Dodgers to three championships in six years, look no further than his treatment of Roki Sasaki.
Roberts has both built Sasaki up and held the Japanese import accountable through two up-and-down seasons. He hasn’t been stubbornly loyal to the 24-year-old righty, nor has he waved the white flag amid Sasaki’s continued control issues.
As Sasaki nears a return from the IL, Roberts confirmed that Sasaki will start pitching out of the bullpen this week. All signs point to Sasaki serving as a reliever for the second straight postseason.
Sasaki has missed nearly all of September with a hip injury, and he should have some extra time to recover. The Dodgers are closing in one of the NL’s top two playoff seeds, which includes a first-round bye.
Does Roki Sasaki deserve to make the Los Angeles Dodgers’ playoff roster?
Before looking ahead to October, let’s quickly travel back to this past spring. I repeatedly questioned Sasaki’s viability as an MLB starter, largely because of his control and what felt like an inability to handle the pressure associated with pitching Stateside.
Honestly? I really haven’t changed my opinion, though I’ll give Sasaki his flowers. He’s played some of his best baseball in the second half, recording a 3.05 ERA in seven starts. That’s down from 5.33 over 15 first-half outings, though he’s still struggling to make it through five innings.
Most importantly, he’s significantly cut down on his homers, allowing three in 38.1 innings. That’s a fantastic improvement from the 19 long balls he gave up in 81 first-half innings.
So what’s the problem? Walks. I’m old school, so I don’t like young pitchers only working five innings because they can’t hit the strike zone. Sasaki has issued 15 free passes in those 38.1 innings, and it drives up his pitch count.
At the end of the day, Sasaki has completed six innings in just seven of his 22 starts. Now is the perfect time to permanently transition him to a relief role.
But we asked whether Sasaki deserves to be on the playoff roster, and despite my criticism, the answer is an easy “yes.” There’s something to be said about a young player admitting to confidence issues yet powering through and trying to make things work rather than let things spiral.
What’s especially admirable about Sasaki is that he doesn’t complain or make himself out to be a victim. He’s never targeted the media, which has actually had his back for much of the last two years. He’s certainly not teammate Kyle Tucker, whose body language and work ethic have raised red flags dating back to his brief stint with the Cubs.
Maybe Sasaki is the Dodgers’ secret playoff weapon once again. We’d certainly feel more comfortable trusting him in October instead of embattled former closer Edwin Díaz.
Yikes. Imagine reading that on Opening Day.

rss_title: Dave Roberts' handling of Roki Sasaki shows why the Dodgers keep winning
rss_body:
If you needed yet another reminder of why Dave Roberts has led the Los Angeles Dodgers to three championships in six years, look no further than his treatment of Roki Sasaki.
Roberts has both built Sasaki up and held the Japanese import accountable through two up-and-down seasons. He hasn’t been stubbornly loyal to the 24-year-old righty, nor has he waved the white flag amid Sasaki’s continued control issues.
As Sasaki nears a return from the IL, Roberts confirmed that Sasaki will start pitching out of the bullpen this week. All signs point to Sasaki serving as a reliever for the second straight postseason.
Sasaki has missed nearly all of September with a hip injury, and he should have some extra time to recover. The Dodgers are closing in one of the NL’s top two playoff seeds, which includes a first-round bye.
Does Roki Sasaki deserve to make the Los Angeles Dodgers’ playoff roster?
Before looking ahead to October, let’s quickly travel back to this past spring. I repeatedly questioned Sasaki’s viability as an MLB starter, largely because of his control and what felt like an inability to handle the pressure associated with pitching Stateside.
Honestly? I really haven’t changed my opinion, though I’ll give Sasaki his flowers. He’s played some of his best baseball in the second half, recording a 3.05 ERA in seven starts. That’s down from 5.33 over 15 first-half outings, though he’s still struggling to make it through five innings.
Most importantly, he’s significantly cut down on his homers, allowing three in 38.1 innings. That’s a fantastic improvement from the 19 long balls he gave up in 81 first-half innings.

title: 佐々木朗希の配置転換の裏に潜むド軍の思惑 現実味を帯び始める108億守護神の“ロースター外し”「物事は計画通りに進んでない」
body:
佐々木朗希の配置転換の裏に潜むド軍の思惑 現実味を帯び始める108億守護神の“ロースター外し”「物事は計画通りに進んでない」
浮かない表情で球団幹部たちを話し込むディアス(C)Getty Images
米球界はMLBのレギュラーシーズンがいよいよ大詰めを迎え、ポストシーズンに向けた編成の動きも活発化しつつある。現地時間9月20日には、ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は、負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている佐々木朗希を復帰後から救援起用をしていく意向を明らかにした。
今季の佐々木は開幕から23試合すべてで「先発」として投げてきた。しかし、「ポストシーズンに先発は基本的に4人いればいい」と持論を語ったロバーツ監督は、山本由伸、タリク・スクバル、ブレーク・スネル、タイラー・グラスノーを先発ローテーションの軸にする考えを示した。
もっとも、「どんな状況だろうと、ロウキを信頼している」と強調するロバーツ監督をはじめとするドジャース首脳陣の決断には、スター軍団が抱える不安が見え隠れする。それは「絶対的守護神」として君臨するはずだったエドウィン・ディアスのコンディション不良だ。
FAとなった昨オフに3年総額6900万ドル（約108億円＝当時のレート）の大型契約を締結したディアスだったが、開幕直後に右肘の関節遊離体除去手術を受けて離脱。丹念なリハビリを終えて7月9日にようやく復帰を果たすも内容は鳴かず飛ばず。今季ここまで18登板で、防御率10.34、WHIP2.36、被打率.361、与四球率6.32、被OPS1.043とキャリアワーストの水準に落ち込んでいる。

title: Dodgers Get Tyler Glasnow Injury Update After Last Week's Ominous Report
author: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers star pitcher Tyler Glasnow shut down any injury concerns on Friday after a scare last week.
Glasnow looked like his usual self against the San Francisco Giants. He allowed only two runs on three hits and two walks while striking out 10 over six innings to earn his fifth win of the season.
Dodgers skipper Dave Roberts couldn't be more pleased with his outing and, more importantly, loves to see Glasnow healthy heading into the postseason.
“It is just making sure he’s feeling good, he’s healthy, which he is,” Roberts said. “So now it’s just letting him go do what he does and bet on the talent to perform. That’s where I think we all feel good, especially Tyler right now, just knowing the health and where the head’s at, all that stuff. We’re in a good spot.”
Roberts' tone on Friday was different than Glasnow's last outing on Sunday against Miami.
“He’s a big-bodied guy, so there’s a lot of big moving parts,” Roberts said last Sunday. “So sometimes if they get out of whack a little bit, it’s hard to just sync everything up.”
Last week, Glasnow's outing was concerning. Not only did he get the loss against the Miami Marlins, but the 33-year-old was also far from himself.
Roberts said he "didn't feel great" after the fact.
Nonetheless, Glasnow noted that there was nothing to be worried about.
“It wasn’t anything crazy,” Glasnow said. “But I definitely feel better now than I did then."
“Right now, I feel pretty good,” he added. “We worked on some stuff after that last start. Just tried to keep for this start, take it in the next start. And then hopefully everything is feeling good for playoffs.”
Tyler Glasnow Looking to Round Into Form Before Postseason
Glasnow's outing on Friday was his fifth since returning from the 60-day IL.
The 33-year-old dealt with a back injury that held him to seven starts. Before his return in late August, Glasnow last pitched in early May.
Overall, Glasnow has tallied a 3.46 ERA, 87 strikeouts and a 0.96 WHIP in 67.2 innings this season. He'll be relied upon heavily come October as the team's fourth starter.
Glasnow is in his third season in Los Angeles after the Dodgers traded for him in December 2023. In that time, Glasnow has landed on the injured list multiple times but has been stellar when healthy.
In 52 games, Glasnow has a 18-10 record, 361 strikeouts, a 3.39 ERA and a 0.99 WHIP in 292 innings.
He made six appearances (three starts) in last year's postseason, sporting a 1.69 ERA across 21.1 innings with 25 strikeouts. He earned the save in Game 6 of the World Series and took down seven outs in Game 7.

title: Shohei Ohtani y sus jonrones en MLB: cuántos ha conectado en su carrera
author: Alejandro Reza
body:
Shohei Ohtani alcanzó los 310 jonrones en su carrera dentro de las Grandes Ligas, consolidándose como uno de los principales referentes ofensivos del béisbol actual. El japonés continúa ampliando sus registros con los Los Angeles Dodgers.
El japonés superó los 300 cuadrangulares
El pelotero japonés llegó a la histórica cifra de 300 cuadrangulares a principios de julio de 2026, una marca que refleja su impacto desde su llegada a las Grandes Ligas. Desde entonces, Ohtani ha continuado incrementando su cuenta.
Durante la temporada 2026, el jugador de los Dodgers ya suma 30 jonrones, alcanzando nuevamente una cifra que se ha convertido en una constante en su trayectoria dentro de MLB.
Con sus 30 cuadrangulares de 2026, Ohtani consiguió su sexta campaña consecutiva con al menos 30 jonrones. Esta racha comenzó durante su etapa con Los Angeles Angels y se ha mantenido tras su llegada a los Dodgers.
Sus primeros años con Los Angeles
Ohtani conectó 22 jonrones en 2018 y posteriormente registró 18 en 2019. En 2020 sumó siete cuadrangulares, antes de protagonizar una importante explosión ofensiva con 46 jonrones en 2021.
En 2022, el japonés terminó con 34 cuadrangulares, mientras que en 2023 alcanzó los 44. Sus números ofensivos lo mantuvieron como uno de los bateadores más productivos de las Grandes Ligas.
Con Los Angeles Dodgers, Ohtani tuvo campañas de 54 jonrones en 2024 y 55 en 2025, antes de llegar a los 30 cuadrangulares durante 2026. Estos registros explican buena parte de su ascenso hasta los 310 vuelacercas.
El registro histórico de Ohtani
Con los 310 jonrones acumulados hasta agosto de 2026, Shohei Ohtani continúa aumentando su legado en MLB. Su trayectoria incluye temporadas de gran producción tanto con los Angels como con los Dodgers.

El pelotero japonés llegó a la histórica cifra de 300 cuadrangulares a principios de julio de 2026, una marca que refleja su impacto desde su llegada a las Grandes Ligas. Desde entonces, Ohtani ha continuado incrementando su cuenta.
Durante la temporada 2026, el jugador de los Dodgers ya suma 30 jonrones, alcanzando nuevamente una cifra que se ha convertido en una constante en su trayectoria dentro de MLB.
Con sus 30 cuadrangulares de 2026, Ohtani consiguió su sexta campaña consecutiva con al menos 30 jonrones. Esta racha comenzó durante su etapa con Los Angeles Angels y se ha mantenido tras su llegada a los Dodgers.
Sus primeros años con Los Angeles
Ohtani conectó 22 jonrones en 2018 y posteriormente registró 18 en 2019. En 2020 sumó siete cuadrangulares, antes de protagonizar una importante explosión ofensiva con 46 jonrones en 2021.
En 2022, el japonés terminó con 34 cuadrangulares, mientras que en 2023 alcanzó los 44. Sus números ofensivos lo mantuvieron como uno de los bateadores más productivos de las Grandes Ligas.
Con Los Angeles Dodgers, Ohtani tuvo campañas de 54 jonrones en 2024 y 55 en 2025, antes de llegar a los 30 cuadrangulares durante 2026. Estos registros explican buena parte de su ascenso hasta los 310 vuelacercas.
El registro histórico de Ohtani
Con los 310 jonrones acumulados hasta agosto de 2026, Shohei Ohtani continúa aumentando su legado en MLB. Su trayectoria incluye temporadas de gran producción tanto con los Angels como con los Dodgers.

title: Dave Roberts Hints at Possible October Change at Top of Lineup
author: Steve Webb
body:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers still expect Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before October, and Dave Roberts made clear Saturday that his first instinct remains to put Ohtani right back atop the batting order.
But the manager is also preparing for the possibility that things don’t go exactly according to plan.
With Ohtani still sidelined and his return date uncertain, Mookie Betts has moved back into the leadoff spot, a familiar home for the former MVP. After Friday night’s two-homer performance against the Giants, Roberts acknowledged that Betts could become an alternative at the top of the order if the Dodgers need to make an adjustment in October.
“Certainly there is uncertainty with Sho, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever. I just think that Mookie is swinging the bat. He’s hit there many times throughout his career. So it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts certainly looked comfortable there Friday. He reached base four times, homered twice and drove in three runs as the Dodgers beat San Francisco 8-2. Long before Ohtani arrived in Los Angeles, Betts was one of baseball’s premier leadoff hitters, so moving him back there isn’t exactly unfamiliar territory.
Roberts has also been encouraged by the quality of Betts’ at-bats during his recent surge.
“I think with Mookie, results drive kind of his demeanor,” Roberts said. “With the results, I think that he is considerably better. He’s not a chase guy anyway, but he’s cut that down considerably. The quality of contact is considerably higher, and then now you’ve got that attitude, that confidence that we’re used to seeing with Mookie.”
For now, Roberts still expects Ohtani to reclaim the leadoff spot once he returns.
“That’s my first kind of thought,” Roberts said. “But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I’ll kind of potentially redirect, react if it’s a left-right situation, or just supplant him back there in the one.”
That leaves the Dodgers with some flexibility. If Ohtani immediately looks like himself, there may be nothing to discuss. But if he needs time to regain his timing after the layoff, the Dodgers don’t have to force the issue at the top of the lineup. Betts has spent most of his career proving he can handle that job.
The Dodgers are also continuing to work Will Smith back toward a normal workload after his own stint on the injured list. Smith was in the lineup Saturday for a second consecutive game, only the third time he has caught back-to-back games since returning.
“I think he’s come along well,” Roberts said. “I think his swing is in a much better spot, getting better, consistent.”
The Dodgers intentionally scheduled Smith for consecutive games this weekend before giving him two days to recover with Monday’s off day included. Roberts said Smith would then play two or three games in the following series.
“I think it’s a good exercise for him,” Roberts said.
Smith’s return matters well beyond his bat. Roberts also pointed to the growing comfort between Smith and Tarik Skubal after their latest game together, saying the pitcher and catcher finally appeared to reach a point of “mutual trust” regarding the game plan and how Skubal wanted to attack hitters.
That relationship will matter considerably if Skubal is asked to pitch deep into October.
The larger picture is that the Dodgers are beginning to have options again. Smith is rebuilding his workload. Betts is swinging the bat with confidence. Ohtani is expected back. And if Ohtani isn’t immediately ready to carry the leadoff responsibilities, the Dodgers have one of the most accomplished leadoff hitters of his generation waiting right behind him.
There are worse backup plans to have in October.

title: Window tightens for Shohei Ohtani to get ready for playoffs
author: Josh Peter
body:
Window tightens for Shohei Ohtani to get ready for playoffs
Shohei Ohtani’s swing is among the most dangerous in baseball. The Los Angeles Dodgers will have only five games to get it ready for the playoffs, barring any setbacks.
There have been many of them for Ohtani, who’s missed the past 12 games while dealing with issues to his left knee and right biceps. He’s expected to be back in the Dodgers' lineup in the team's upcoming series against the San Diego Padres. There will be only five games left in the regular season.
Because of Ohtani’s lingering knee issues, the Dodgers have shut him down from pitching. But they’d still like him to bat – and a swing that has generated a team-leading 30 home runs this season and 263 over the last six seasons.
In his last 24 games before going on the injured reserve list, however, Ohtani hit .198 (19-for-96) with 34 strikeouts.
It raises a premature, although not outrageous, question involving the four-time MVP: At some point, in some cases, might the Dodgers be better off with Ohtani out of the lineup?
Precious at-bats
The Dodgers haven’t had enough pitchers to throw him live batting practice, and so he’s been hitting off the Trajekt, a machine that simulates real pitchers. And so those final five regular-season games – two against the Padres and three against the San Francisco Giants – because even more critical.
"I do think that when he's activated, it's going to be the best physical place he's been in in quite some time,’’ said Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
So we’ll see if feeling good translates into swinging well for Ohtani.
The Dodgers have managed to win despite missing their MVP designated hitter. Ohtani’s missed 15 of the Dodgers’ last 16 games, and the team has gone 13-3 without him. In six of those games, the Dodgers won by two or fewer runs.
The Dodgers, who clinched a playoff berth by winning the NL West crown, have a four-game lead on the Atlanta Braves to clinch a first-round bye. Los Angeles is two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the No. 1 season and homefield advantage through the NL playoffs.
At-bats figure to become even more precious as the playoffs begin.
Ohtani might have to earn them.

title: Dave Roberts on Shohei Ohtani: "There's a good chance next series we'll see him”
author: Jose Victor Escobar Rodriguez
body:
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Roster Move: Skubal to Bereavement List, Sheehan recalled by Dodgers
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Ohtani ramps up hitting progression: Why Dave Roberts is bullish on star's October return
There is some concern among fans about how much time Shohei Ohtani will need to recover before finally returning to the Los Angeles Dodgers, who have already clinched a playoff spot and are looking to reach their third consecutive World Series.
Fortunately for the Dodgers, the Japanese superstar’s return is getting closer after taking another positive step in his offensive recovery, meaning he could be back as soon as the start of the next series against the San Diego Padres.
What did Dave Roberts say about Shohei Ohtani?
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Ohtani (right biceps and left knee issues) continues to make positive progress and is getting closer to returning to action. The Japanese star could be activated from the 15-day injured list during the Dodgers’ upcoming series.
There's a good chance next series we'll see him
Roberts said after Los Angeles’ 10-4 win over the Giants at Dodger Stadium.
Ohtani was placed on the injured list retroactive to September 8, making him eligible to return Wednesday, in the second game of the Dodgers’ final regular-season home series against the San Diego Padres. His return will only be as a hitter, as the Dodgers have paused his pitching activities for now.
The Japanese star has already begun regaining his timing at the plate. After starting his offensive progression program on Tuesday, Ohtani took the next step by facing pitches from the Trajekt machine, a device that simulates facing real pitchers. According to Roberts, Ohtani felt good after taking 30 to 40 swings on Saturday and also worked on running the bases during batting practice.
A quick recovery before the playoffs
If Ohtani returns on Wednesday, when he becomes eligible to come off the injured list, he will have only five regular-season games to regain his rhythm, find his timing again, and readjust to the intensity of Major League Baseball before the postseason begins.
For that reason, Dave Roberts plans to put him in the lineup for every available game, as the Japanese star needs to accumulate live at-bats to rebuild confidence and be in better shape for the most important part of the year.
Ohtani will also not have a Minor League rehab assignment, as the Triple-A regular season ends Sunday and the Dodgers do not have additional pitchers available to conduct live batting practice sessions.

title: Dodgers activará a Shohei Ohtani para última serie ante Padres
author: Editorial Mediotiempo
body:
¡Regreso estelar! Dodgers recupera a Shohei Ohtani para su última serie ante Padres
Ohtani estaría de regreso en la alineación de los Dodgers con cinco juegos antes de iniciar los playoffs.
La estancia de Shohei Ohtani en la lista de lesionados de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB) podría durar el mínimo posible, ya que, de acuerdo con el manager Dave Roberts, el estelar pelotero japonés de los Dodgers estaría de regreso en la alineación para el juego de este miércoles 23 de septiembre ante los Padres.
Ohtani fue colocado en la lista de lesionados por 15 días con fecha retroactiva al 8 de septiembre debido a las constantes molestias en la rodilla izquierda y su bíceps derecho. Después de otro productivo día bateando, Ohtani sigue en camino para volver como el bateador designado de los Dodgers durante su última serie de la temporada regular en casa.
“Es muy probable que lo veamos en la próxima serie”, dijo Roberts.
El pasado martes 15 de septiembre, Ohtani retomó sus actividades de bateo y el sábado finalmente comenzó a batear con la máquina Trajekt, la cual simula el movimiento de los pitcheos de lanzadores reales. Ohtani se habría sentido bien luego de hacer entre 30 y 40 swings, además de correr las bases.
Ohtani conectó 30 jonrones, cifra máxima para los Dodgers en la temporada, antes de quedar fuera de acción debido a las constantes molestias físicas. En 24 juegos antes de aterrizar en la lista de lesionados, mismo lapso en el que retomó su programa para lanzar, Shohei cayó estrepitosamente bateando .198 (de 96-19) con 34 ponches.
Si todo sale conforme al plan, los Dodgers tendrán a Ohtani para los últimos cinco juegos de la temporada regular, todos ellos de suma importancia antes de comenzar los playoffs. Por ello, el manager Dave Roberts tiene planeado alinearlo en todos los juegos posibles para que Ohtani tome turnos al bate, especialmente porque no tendrá una asignación de rehabilitación en las Ligas Menores.
Aún con su ausencia en 15 de los últimos 16 juegos, los Dodgers se las han arreglado para firmar un gran cierre firmando una marca de 13-3 en sus 16 juegos más recientes.
Si bien los Dodgers saben que Ohtani no volverá al cien por ciento físicamente, el equipo confía que el descanso de algunos días le permita sentirse mejor para iniciar la postemporada. El piloto aseguró que Shohei está libre de dolor, aunque eso no necesariamente significa que se haya aliviado de todas sus molestias.

title: Nationals vs. Tigers Prediction, Odds, Probable Pitchers, Prop Bets for Monday, Sept. 21
author: Ryan Gilbert
body:
The Detroit Tigers return home for the final week of the season, starting with a three-game set against the Washington Nationals.
The Tigers had a solid winning streak going before dropping four of their last five games. The Nationals have been playing well recently, too, winning six of their last eight contests.
DJ Herz and River Ryan are both set to make their season debuts after missing all of last season due to Tommy John surgery.
Here are the odds, probable pitchers, and predictions for Nationals vs. Tigers on Monday, Sept. 21.
Nationals vs. Tigers Odds, Run Line and Total
Run Line
- Nationals +1.5 (-186)
- Tigers -1.5 (+153)
Moneyline
- Nationals +112
- Tigers -135
Total
- 8 (Over -118/Under -102)
Nationals vs. Tigers Probable Pitchers
- Nationals: DJ Herz (4-9, 4.16 ERA in 2024)
- Tigers: River Ryan (1-0, 1.33 ERA in 2024)
DJ Herz made 19 starts in 2024 but missed all of last season and nearly all of this season due to an elbow injury. The southpaw made 10 starts in the minors this season, allowing 10 runs (nine earned) on 19 hits in 25.2 innings.
River Ryan will make his Tigers debut tonight after being acquired in the Tarik Skubal trade. He, too, missed all of last season after making four starts with the Dodgers in 2024. The right-hander allowed 22 runs (20 earned) on 46 hits in 41 innings across 10 minor-league starts this season.
Nationals vs. Tigers How to Watch
- Date: Monday, Sept. 21
- Time: 6:40 p.m. ET
- Venue: Comerica Park
- How to Watch (TV): NATS, DSN
- Nationals record: 73-83
- Tigers record: 73-83
Nationals vs. Tigers Best MLB Prop Bets
Tigers Best MLB Prop Bet
- Riley Greene OVER 1.5 Hits + Runs + RBIs (-109)
Riley Greene is looking to finish the season on a high note in Detroit. He’s currently riding a 10-game hitting streak, going 16 for 40 (.400) with seven runs scored and 10 RBI in that span. He went OVER 1.5 HRR in nine of those 10 contests, including each of the last three.
Going back to Sept. 5, Greene is 25-for-59 (.424) with five home runs, five doubles, and a triple. I’ll take him to stay hot at home tonight.
Nationals vs. Tigers Prediction and Pick
I broke down this pick in SI Betting’s daily MLB best bets column, Walk-Off Wagers:
It’s a feel-good pitching matchup in Detroit tonight with both DJ Herz and River Ryan returning from Tommy John Surgery to make their first starts since 2024. There’s not a ton of analysis that you can have on that matchup, so I’m looking at how these teams have played overall as of late for this pick.
The Nats have won six of their last eight games, including two of three in St. Louis over the weekend, while the Tigers have lost four of five after a winning streak. Detroit scored just one run in each of those four losses, breaking out for 11 runs in its lone win in that span.
The Tigers may have a bit more pep in their step as they return home, but I can’t back them as favorites given their offensive struggles. I’ll take the Nationals as road underdogs given how they’ve played recently.
Pick: Nationals +112

title: Dodgers playoff roster projection: Could Edwin Díaz, Josue De Paula, even Hyeseong Kim surprise?
author: Jack Harris
body:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.

C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*

Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips

The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

title: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts reveals new role for Roki Sasaki
author: Matt Borelli
body:
Roki Sasaki is among the players expected to rejoin the Los Angeles Dodgers this week as they inch closer to full strength ahead of the postseason.
The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since Aug. 27 due to a blister on his right middle finger, but made steady progress throughout his recovery. He has thrown multiple bullpen sessions and live batting practices this month, including 48 pitches over four innings last Wednesday.
Sasaki was originally slated to return as a starting pitcher, but he now appears headed to the bullpen for the remainder of the 2026 season. The 24-year-old is capable of pitching multiple innings as a reliever, but not in the traditional sense of a bulk pitcher.
“I can see multiples, but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings. It won’t be that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s role.
Sasaki won’t be limited to simply providing length out of the bullpen. Roberts also indicated that he would feel comfortable using him in high-leverage situations, but only at the start of a “clean inning.”
As for whether Sasaki could get save opportunities, it’s something that Roberts might consider down the road.
“It won’t be in the ninth the first time, but it potentially could fall out (that way),” the Dodgers skipper said.
Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ primary closer in recent weeks, but Edwin Díaz recently returned from the 15-day IL and is hoping to eventually reclaim the role. Edgardo Henriquez also received save opportunities prior to landing on the IL with lower back discomfort.
Roki Sasaki’s postseason success
Sasaki shined as a reliever during the Dodgers’ World Series run last year, pitching to a minuscule 0.84 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with three saves in nine appearances. His previous success on baseball’s biggest stage played a role in the team’s decision to once again move him to the bullpen.
“Yeah. He’s done it, he’s really good, he’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff,” Roberts said. “You really just need four starters, so we’re in a good spot there for now.”
Along with Sasaki, the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen could include other traditional starters such as Justin Wrobleski and Emmet Sheehan. The club’s starting rotation will feature two of the league’s best arms in Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal.

title: The 2026 Arizona Diamondbacks have (just!) surpassed pre-season expectations
author: Jim McLennan
body:
With just six games to go, the Diamondbacks have a record of 82-74. While not technically eliminated from post-season contention yet, their playoff hopes would require a spectacular confluence of events in the first half of the week, probably followed by a sweep of the Padres in San Diego next weekend. Obviously, that’s disappointing. But on the other hand, the D-backs have, albeit in a small way, actually done better than what most neutral expectations were for team at the beginning of the year. Let’s start off by reviewing what various parties predicted Arizona would do before Opening Day.
The metrics
- Baseball Prospectus (PECOTA): 78.4 wins. Our friends over at Purple Row captured this prediction in their preview of the division. They (and not BP) said, “The D-Backs still have some question marks and might not emerge as one of MLB’s top teams, but they certainly are positioned to push for the playoffs if they see a return to form for Gallen and some improvements to their pitching numbers overall. However, an uptick in pitching could unfortunately pair with a regression in batting, threatening those chances.”
- Fangraphs: 81-81. These came out in late January, once Dan Szymborski had finished running ZIPS for all thirty teams. We’ll get more into those later, as we look at which individuals out- or under-performed their projections. But there isn’t much said about them at the overall level, except for “ZIPS remains unsure of Arizona’s rotation.” However, at the end of spring training, the expected tally was still basically 81-81, with a 31% chance of making the post-season.
The pundits
- George Castillo, ESPN: 81-81. “Will the pitching staff sink Arizona’s playoff chances again? The Diamondbacks can score. Two years ago, they paced the majors in runs scored. Last year, they finished sixth… And yet, the Diamondbacks have not reached the postseason since their surprise run to the World Series in 2023, largely because their pitching staff ranked 27th in ERA in 2024 and 23rd last season.”
- Tim Kelly, Bleacher Report: 82-80. “Lovullo has shown an ability to get the most out of his teams, and with Corbin Caroll, Ketel Marte and Gerlado Perdomo anchoring his lineup, this is going to be a competitive team. They just have too much working against them in terms of pitching injuries.”
- Gabe Lacques, USA Today: 81-81. “In coming weeks, Arizona Diamondbacks (80-82) corner infielders Nolan Arenado and Carlos Santana will turn 35 and 40, respectively. They’ll need some gulps from the fountain of youth to ensure the bottom of the lineup isn’t an arid wasteland.”
- Ryan Phillips, Sports Illustrated: 77-85. “The Diamondbacks signed several late-career veterans, searching for the magic of 2023. But Arizona’s roster doesn’t look anywhere near pennant-worthy. Manager Torey Lovullo has just two playoff appearances in nine seasons.”
- Fred Zinkle, Yahoo! Sports: 82-80. “This figures to be a retooling year in Arizona, while the organization waits to get Burnes back in 2027. Success this season might look like determining which players, particularly among Del Castillo, Lawlar, Pfaadt, Nelson and Thomas, can be part of the next wave of success. There will also be more trade rumors around Marte in July, and the front office will have to decide whether to recoup a package of prospects or keep Marte in hopes of competing in 2027.”
The group exercises
- Sports books: 79.5 wins. This was more or less the consensus across the board, with the line being drawn here by Caesar’s, Draft Kings and BetMGM.
- Arizona Sports roundtable: 81.8 wins. The radio station polled 14 of their staff, with numbers ranging from 75 to 86 wins. They also asked if the team would make the playoffs, and “No” won that vote, ten of the fourteen polled saying there’d be no post-season.
- AZ SnakePit writers: 84.2 wins. The highest prediction and not unexpectedly, the usual optimism prevailing. This is in line with history over the last couple of years, the 2025 prediction being a (now somewhat embarrassing!) 91.3 wins, and the 2024 prediction also being higher than reality could deliver, at 86.7 wins. And that 2024 figure was before we signed Jordan Montgomery, which seemed like a big deal at the time…
- Fan vote: 84 wins. This answer is based off the median - half above, half below - for SnakePit voters in our poll. The most popular category was actually higher, at 86-88 wins. But that only got 21%, barely edging out the 83-85 win group, at 20%. The “tail” below that was also longer, bringing the median down.
A straight average of the eleven predictions above comes in at 81 wins - an expectation of just one more victory than the previous season. As we head into the final week of the season, the Diamondbacks are already above that. There is even a significant chance of reaching 85 wins, which would be better than any of the 11 pre-season projections mentioned above. Taking two of three in Colorado and one in San Diego would get us there. Get one less, and 84 wins is certainly very plausible. That would only be (very narrowly) surpassed by the SnakePit writers’ poll. But what are the individual contributors to the moderate over-performance?
Winners and losers
When it comes to looking at individual players, we are mostly going off the 2026 ZIPS projections for Arizona. [I had to chase down some players not present on that page, no longer with AZ] As with any projection system, these are expectations, not guarantees. Inevitably, reality will differ, and that’s no mark at all against the effort Dan Szymborski puts in to them. Don’t worry about the playing time numbers, especially for those we didn’t see. Cristofer Torin did not quite make 129 appearances. We’re looking only at the fWAR expected tallies, compared to the actual ones. Those are through Saturday night’s game, although with only about 4% of the schedule remaining, I didn’t bother pro-rating.
Hitters: Over- and under-performers
- Gabriel Moreno 4.9 vs. 3.3
- Nolan Arenado 2.7 vs. 1.9
- ———
- Carlos Santana 0.6 vs. -0.5
- Ketel Marte 2.3 vs 4.3
- Lourdes Gurriel 1.3 vs. -1.0
I’ve not listed on either side, players like Jordan Lawlar, whose playing time didn’t come close to the ZIPS figure, for reasons beyond their control. Though technically, Santana and Gurriel’s didn’t either. So yes, I am being very arbitrary about this. No question who the team’s MVP has been, and I’m sure Mike Hazen is regretting not being able to ink Moreno to a long-term contract last winter. The asking price will now be considerably higher, and a significant arbitration bump will be coming down Gaby Lane next year (lockout permitting). Arenado has also been everything we could have wanted, and more.
On the downside, hopes that Santana might be able to play a competent first-base proved wildly optimistic, and the team didn’t really have a Plan B. That’s why we have Ildemaro Vargas getting more at-bats at 1B than anyone else. This was a mistake by Hazen. The discovery Gurriel was now well below replacement level in left was also unpleasant, and Max Kepler wasn’t the answer either. Then there’s the whole Marte situation. Be very interesting to see what happens there over the winter, because if the sharp drop-off in production was not a blip, those four remaining guaranteed years might not be a lot of fun.
Pitchers: Over- and under-performers
- Eduardo Rodriguez: 3.1 vs. 1.5
- Michael Soroka: 2.5 vs. 0.9
- Juan Morillo: 1.5 vs. -0.1
- Brandyn Garcia: 1.3 vs. 0.0
- ———
- Zac Gallen: -0.1 vs. 1.8
- Merrill Kelly: -0.2 vs. 1.9
- Corbin Burnes: 0.0 vs. 2.6
Very much a rotation of two halves. ERod and Soroka have both performed much better than expected, while Gallen and Kelly have been sore disappointments. We should have let Zac just walk, and the lack of suitors for his services in 2026 turned out to be the reddest of red flags. Kelly will be around next year, and there is hope in that he has been better of late. Small sample-size, but over the four games since the spat with the Cubs, where he may have discovered he was pitch-tipping, Merrill has a 2.86 ERA and 3.55 FIP. Anything like those figures in the remaining year of his contract will be a huge improvement. But Burnes’ extremely belated arrival might have hurt most of all.
Previous years have seen mocking of Mike Hazen for his dumpster diving approach to building a bullpen. But it has worked very well. Discounting Gallen, the eight other current members of the bullpen are earning a total of less than $13 million this year. That’s several million less than the Dodgers are paying Edwin Diaz alone this year, for 15.2 innings of work and a 10.34 ERA. Morillo, Garcia and Jonathan Loaisiga have thrown 171.2 combined innings for an ERA of 2.15. That has been worth a total of 3.9 fWAR, while the trio are getting paid only about $3 million between them. After years of quiet desperation, this bullpen has been quite the refreshing change.
Conclusions
Projections are always going to be wrong. If you look at the Fangraphs totals, there are some big misses: most notably under-estimating the Padres, and over-estimating the Mets. But five of the six teams at the top of the NL will indeed (almost certainly, I guess I should caveat) be among the six teams representing the league in the post-season. While it’s obviously disappointing again not to be in the playoffs, I think it’s encouraging to see the team surpassing expectations. The sharp improvement in the pitching, especially the bullpen, is hopefully something which can be sustained. Get some improved offense and if there is a 2027 season, I expect the D-backs again to be playing meaningful baseball into September.

Last year, they finished sixth… And yet, the Diamondbacks have not reached the postseason since their surprise run to the World Series in 2023, largely because their pitching staff ranked 27th in ERA in 2024 and 23rd last season.”
- Tim Kelly, Bleacher Report: 82-80. “Lovullo has shown an ability to get the most out of his teams, and with Corbin Caroll, Ketel Marte and Gerlado Perdomo anchoring his lineup, this is going to be a competitive team. They just have too much working against them in terms of pitching injuries.”
- Gabe Lacques, USA Today: 81-81. “In coming weeks, Arizona Diamondbacks (80-82) corner infielders Nolan Arenado and Carlos Santana will turn 35 and 40, respectively. They’ll need some gulps from the fountain of youth to ensure the bottom of the lineup isn’t an arid wasteland.”
- Ryan Phillips, Sports Illustrated: 77-85. “The Diamondbacks signed several late-career veterans, searching for the magic of 2023. But Arizona’s roster doesn’t look anywhere near pennant-worthy. Manager Torey Lovullo has just two playoff appearances in nine seasons.”
- Fred Zinkle, Yahoo! Sports: 82-80. “This figures to be a retooling year in Arizona, while the organization waits to get Burnes back in 2027. Success this season might look like determining which players, particularly among Del Castillo, Lawlar, Pfaadt, Nelson and Thomas, can be part of the next wave of success. There will also be more trade rumors around Marte in July, and the front office will have to decide whether to recoup a package of prospects or keep Marte in hopes of competing in 2027.”
The group exercises
- Sports books: 79.5 wins. This was more or less the consensus across the board, with the line being drawn here by Caesar’s, Draft Kings and BetMGM.
- Arizona Sports roundtable: 81.8 wins. The radio station polled 14 of their staff, with numbers ranging from 75 to 86 wins. They also asked if the team would make the playoffs, and “No” won that vote, ten of the fourteen polled saying there’d be no post-season.
- AZ SnakePit writers: 84.2 wins. The highest prediction and not unexpectedly, the usual optimism prevailing. This is in line with history over the last couple of years, the 2025 prediction being a (now somewhat embarrassing!) 91.3 wins, and the 2024 prediction also being higher than reality could deliver, at 86.7 wins. And that 2024 figure was before we signed Jordan Montgomery, which seemed like a big deal at the time…
- Fan vote: 84 wins. This answer is based off the median - half above, half below - for SnakePit voters in our poll. The most popular category was actually higher, at 86-88 wins. But that only got 21%, barely edging out the 83-85 win group, at 20%. The “tail” below that was also longer, bringing the median down.
A straight average of the eleven predictions above comes in at 81 wins - an expectation of just one more victory than the previous season. As we head into the final week of the season, the Diamondbacks are already above that. Taking two of three in Colorado and one in San Diego would get us there. Get one less, and 84 wins is certainly very plausible. That would only be (very narrowly) surpassed by the SnakePit writers’ poll. But what are the individual contributors to the moderate over-performance?
Winners and losers
When it comes to looking at individual players, we are mostly going off the 2026 ZIPS projections for Arizona. [I had to chase down some players not present on that page, no longer with AZ] As with any projection system, these are expectations, not guarantees. Inevitably, reality will differ, and that’s no mark at all against the effort Dan Szymborski puts in to them. Don’t worry about the playing time numbers, especially for those we didn’t see. Cristofer Torin did not quite make 129 appearances. We’re looking only at the fWAR expected tallies, compared to the actual ones. Those are through Saturday night’s game, although with only about 4% of the schedule remaining, I didn’t bother pro-rating.
Hitters: Over- and under-performers
- Gabriel Moreno 4.9 vs. 3.3
- Nolan Arenado 2.7 vs. 1.9
- ———
- Carlos Santana 0.6 vs. -0.5
- Ketel Marte 2.3 vs 4.3
- Lourdes Gurriel 1.3 vs. -1.0
I’ve not listed on either side, players like Jordan Lawlar, whose playing time didn’t come close to the ZIPS figure, for reasons beyond their control. Though technically, Santana and Gurriel’s didn’t either. So yes, I am being very arbitrary about this. No question who the team’s MVP has been, and I’m sure Mike Hazen is regretting not being able to ink Moreno to a long-term contract last winter. The asking price will now be considerably higher, and a significant arbitration bump will be coming down Gaby Lane next year (lockout permitting). Arenado has also been everything we could have wanted, and more.
On the downside, hopes that Santana might be able to play a competent first-base proved wildly optimistic, and the team didn’t really have a Plan B. That’s why we have Ildemaro Vargas getting more at-bats at 1B than anyone else. This was a mistake by Hazen. The discovery Gurriel was now well below replacement level in left was also unpleasant, and Max Kepler wasn’t the answer either. Then there’s the whole Marte situation. Be very interesting to see what happens there over the winter, because if the sharp drop-off in production was not a blip, those four remaining guaranteed years might not be a lot of fun.
Pitchers: Over- and under-performers
- Eduardo Rodriguez: 3.1 vs. 1.5
- Michael Soroka: 2.5 vs. 0.9
- Juan Morillo: 1.5 vs. -0.1
- Brandyn Garcia: 1.3 vs. 0.0
- ———
- Zac Gallen: -0.1 vs. 1.8
- Merrill Kelly: -0.2 vs. 1.9
- Corbin Burnes: 0.0 vs. 2.6
Very much a rotation of two halves. ERod and Soroka have both performed much better than expected, while Gallen and Kelly have been sore disappointments. We should have let Zac just walk, and the lack of suitors for his services in 2026 turned out to be the reddest of red flags. Kelly will be around next year, and there is hope in that he has been better of late. Small sample-size, but over the four games since the spat with the Cubs, where he may have discovered he was pitch-tipping, Merrill has a 2.86 ERA and 3.55 FIP. Anything like those figures in the remaining year of his contract will be a huge improvement. But Burnes’ extremely belated arrival might have hurt most of all.
Previous years have seen mocking of Mike Hazen for his dumpster diving approach to building a bullpen. But it has worked very well. Discounting Gallen, the eight other current members of the bullpen are earning a total of less than $13 million this year. That’s several million less than the Dodgers are paying Edwin Diaz alone this year, for 15.2 innings of work and a 10.34 ERA. Morillo, Garcia and Jonathan Loaisiga have thrown 171.2 combined innings for an ERA of 2.15. That has been worth a total of 3.9 fWAR, while the trio are getting paid only about $3 million between them. After years of quiet desperation, this bullpen has been quite the refreshing change.
Conclusions
Projections are always going to be wrong. If you look at the Fangraphs totals, there are some big misses: most notably under-estimating the Padres, and over-estimating the Mets. But five of the six teams at the top of the NL will indeed (almost certainly, I guess I should caveat) be among the six teams representing the league in the post-season. While it’s obviously disappointing again not to be in the playoffs, I think it’s encouraging to see the team surpassing expectations. The sharp improvement in the pitching, especially the bullpen, is hopefully something which can be sustained. Get some improved offense and if there is a 2027 season, I expect the D-backs again to be playing meaningful baseball into September.

title: Dodgers have lineup problem they cannot afford to solve by benching Josue De Paula
author: Miracle Dimwesh
body:
Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore.
De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason.
That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The Dodgers have several established outfielders, but De Paula's bat is making it harder to find room for everyone.
Josue De Paula has been doing this all year
The rookie's hot start is not coming out of nowhere. De Paula dominated Double-A pitching throughout the season before earning his September call-up.
Minor League Baseball named him the 2026 Texas League MVP on Monday. He hit .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs, 31 stolen bases, 152 hits and 104 RBIs in 124 games for Tulsa.
That production earned him a direct jump from Double-A to Los Angeles. He has continued showing the same offensive approach against MLB pitching.
De Paula has gone 8-for-28 with 10 walks, one home run and seven RBIs in his first 10 games. He has also played two games in left field, showing the Dodgers can move him around when necessary.
Dodgers face a difficult Ohtani lineup decision
Feb 24, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Josue De Paula against the Cleveland Guardians during a spring training game at Camelback Ranch-Glendale. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The situation becomes more complicated with Ohtani nearing a return. Manager Dave Roberts said there is a good chance Ohtani will be activated Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. He will return as a hitter, not a pitcher.
That puts Ohtani back at DH and removes the easiest path to keeping De Paula in the lineup.
The Dodgers already have Kyle Tucker in right field, Teoscar Hernández in left and Andy Pages in center. Tucker signed a four-year, $240 million deal before the season, while Hernández and Pages have remained important parts of the club's outfield plans.
De Paula can play the outfield, but moving him there would force another decision. Taking one of the established outfielders out also means changing a group that has helped Los Angeles reach this point.
The Dodgers do not have to solve the entire problem today. But De Paula's performance has made one thing clear: when Ohtani returns, finding enough at-bats for everyone will be one of Dave Roberts' biggest lineup challenges heading into October.
