Kubek played poorly at shortstop and missed a lot of time, but Keane kept Tresh in the outfield, alternating him between relieving Mantle in center and playing left (there was even some right mixed in). To some extent, it paid off, as Tresh finished in the top 10 for AL MVP, won a Gold Glove, and showed no sign of ill-effect at the plate with a 136 wRC+. To another extent, it didn’t, as the team around him was not good; the Yankees fell below .500 for the first time in 40 years.
Despite the increasing effects of a pitching-heavy era, Tresh pulled off a career-high in home runs in ‘66, smacking 27 dingers in 151 games. That was one of the few highlights for the Yankees though, who were abysmal and dropped all the way to last place. Keane was fired and replaced by Houk in May, who moved Tresh to third base since he wanted to give a young Roy White time in the outfield. Tresh ended up splitting time between left and the hot corner. The Yankees appreciated his athleticism and Zobristian ability to handle basically any position, but it still mystified Tresh to a certain degree:
“I win Rookie of the Year as a shortstop and they move me to the outfield. Then I win a Gold Glove Award there in 1965 and they move me to third. I couldn’t figure out what position I was supposed to prove I could play.“
Although Tresh was only 28 entering the 1967 campaign, the second game of spring training was the beginning of the end. He popped his right knee while firing a throw across his body from left field to the cutoff man. Tresh was in serious pain and could barely walk; it was later revealed to be torn cartilage. Inexplicably, the Yankees told him that he should try to play on it rather than undergo surgery.
It was a disaster. Through some miracle, Tresh kept his numbers above league-average with a 106 wRC+, but his OPS dipped below .700 and he was a shadow of the defender he once was in left field. Tresh later recalled that his knee “gave out five more times” that year, undoubtedly affecting his future. He had surgery to repair the damage in the offseason (why he wasn’t simply shut down on a 90-loss team is a mystery), but the damage was done. Tresh was mostly a hobbling shortstop in ‘68 and his play only worsened in ‘69.
By then, the only other position players aside from Tresh remaining from the Yankees’ early ’60s glory were Joe Pepitone and catcher Jake Gibbs. Mantle, Maris, Berra, Kubek, Elston Howard, and Bobby Richardson were all gone. Tresh was miserable. The team was middling at best, and he could barely hit, let alone play shortstop. So he asked if the Yankees would trade him to the Tigers, where he could at least be close to home, not to mention play for the defending World Series champions. The Yankees acquiesced, and Tresh was dealt to Detroit on June 14th. The very next person to wear number 15 for the Yankees was a worthy heir: Thurman Munson.
Tresh remained primarily a shortstop and appeared in 94 games for the Tigers, batting .224/.305/.387 with 13 homers, a .692 OPS that was amusingly still good for a 92 wRC+ in the league-wide offensive malaise. While Detroit was a better team, there was still no competing with the 109-win juggernaut Orioles, who ran away with the AL East in the first year of divisional play.
Tresh had gone through another surgery on his knee in hopes of playing again in 1970. However, the Tigers told him that he would need to rehab in the minors, and Tresh had no intention of living that kind of life again, particularly with a wife and four kids at home. So Tom Tresh retired having played just eight games after his 31st birthday. His story was a warning sign about the dangers of dismissing injuries, but he had no regrets.
Even though Tresh was so talented before his injury that the Red Sox briefly considered a swap of him for Carl Yastrzemski, one can’t blame Tresh for his overall happiness about his career. He was a beloved teammate, a World Series champion, an All-Star, and an MVP candidate for baseball’s greatest franchise. At the time of his retirement, he was even in the Yankees’ all-time top 20 in homers at 140 (the recent offensive spike pushed him back to a tie for 34th as of 2026). Tresh had a fine life post-retirement too, as he did fulfill that college promise to his parents, even after his father’s passing in 1966.
Tresh earned his degree in physical education from Central Michigan in 1969, where he later served as an assistant baseball coach for 15 years and helped innovate a training tool for sliding and diving called the Slide-Rite. His son Mickey inherited the baseball gene, playing at Miami University of Ohio before going through four years in the minors as well with New York and Detroit. The younger Tresh even got a glimpse of the ascendance of one of the great successors to Tresh and Mantle in center: his 1988 Prince William Yankees teammate, 19-year-old Bernie Williams.
The bond between the Mantles and Treshes remained strong—the two Yankees were at a card show in Nashville when Mickey Tresh called to inform his father that he just had a boy of his own, who he named Tommy. Mantle celebrated with Tresh by ordering a $150 bottle of Dom Perignon, raising a toast to the lad, and later writing “Happy birthday Tommy, we had one for you. Mickey Mantle.” on the bottle.
That bottle could have sold for something valuable, as the glove Mantle gave to Tresh in 1962 was enough by itself to put a down payment on a cottage. Tom Tresh never sold it though; it meant too much to him, and he grieved as much as any of his teammates on the day Mantle passed away from liver cancer in 1995. Thirteen years later, Tresh suddenly left the world as well, as he died of a heart attack on October 14, 2008, not even a month after turning 70.
At least Tresh got to see the old Yankee Stadium one last time before it closed for good, as he was in attendance at the final Old-Timers’ Day. As always, the crowd gave him an ovation before he stepped to foul line one last time. Number 15 will always mean Thurman Munson, but it will also always be connected to Tommy Tresh, another fantastic Yankee.
rss_title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Tom Tresh
rss_body:
Although a familiar name to scholars of Yankees history (for lack of a better term), Tom Tresh did not have a long big-league career due to injuries and treatment of the time. Nonetheless, he was among the Bombers’ finest players of the 1960s and one of the last gasps of greatness from their vaunted farm system. As the team around him declined, Tresh continued to perform at a high level at multiple positions, making him a fan favorite and a valued final connection to those terrific teams of old.

Born: September 20, 1938 (Detroit, MI)
Died: October 14, 2008 (Venice, FL)

Tom Tresh spent some time living with his parents in an apartment in Chicago, but he went to school in Michigan, as his father’s career was over by then. At Allen Park High School in Detroit, he lettered in baseball, football, and basketball, and he later went to Central Michigan University in Mount Pleasant. His father’s prestigious job allowed him to gain some first-hand perspective on how clubhouses operated and what big-league living was like. He was even allowed to become a bat boy when his father briefly managed at Daytona Beach and Wausau, Wisconsin in 1951 and 1952, respectively.
MLB teams knew just how talented the younger Tresh was, and they kept a close scouting eye on him growing up. Mike and Doris Tresh wanted their son to go to college, but after a year at shortstop in Central Michigan, Tresh felt that he could not turn down a $30,000 offer from the New York Yankees. It was a lot of money for the time, the Yankees were baseball’s marquee team, and like many boys in the ’50s, Mickey Mantle was his idol. He recalled going to Tiger Stadium when the Yankees came to town and watching him intently from the upper deck in center field. Mike had even taught Tom how to switch-hit like Mantle.

He capably fielded the position in Kubek’s absence while hitting well from both sides of the plate. The Yankees won the pennant and played the San Francisco Giants in the World Series. Tresh had only just turned 24 and yet he didn’t appear to be fazed at all. He hit .321/.345/.464 in the seven-game series, leading the Yankees in hits and average. Mike Tresh was in the stands at Yankee Stadium when Tresh hit that homer to win Game 5, crying tears of joy. His son had definitely made it.

title: Joe Amalfitano and Charlie Hough Win Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award
author: By
body:
Joe Amalfitano and Charlie Hough Win Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award
LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Dodgers today named Charlie Hough and Joe Amalfitano as recipients of the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award, an honor bestowed every year since 2022 to members of the Los Angeles Dodger community who embody the passion, enthusiasm and love for the Dodgers that the Hall of Fame manager possessed. The award will be presented today by Lasorda’s daughter Laura before the Dodgers’ 1:10 p.m. game against the San Francisco Giants, two days before what would have been Lasorda's 99th birthday.
Hough, 78, has spent 46 years in the Dodger organization as a player, coach and special assistant in the Baseball Operations department, dating back to his selection by the franchise in the eighth round of the June 1966 Amateur Draft. Making his MLB debut for Los Angeles in 1970, Hough pitched 799.2 innings in 401 games for Los Angeles with a 3.50 ERA, including 60 saves and a franchise record 204 relief appearances of at least two innings. Retiring from the Majors at age 46 in 1994 with the Marlins, he finished with a 216-216 career record and 2,362 strikeouts across 3,801.1 innings and 858 games, with a 3.75 ERA.
Amalfitano, 92, served 14 seasons as third-base coach on Lasorda’s staff from 1983-96, as well as Dodger senior adviser in baseball operations from 2002-04. Overall, Amalfitano amassed 67 seasons in professional baseball as a Major League player with the New York/San Francisco Giants, Houston Colt .45s and Chicago Cubs (1954-67), manager with the Cubs (1979-81) and front office executive. As a player, Amalfitano collected 418 hits across 10 seasons in the Majors.
The previous winners of the Lasorda award include longtime public relations executive Steve Brener (2025), Hall of Fame broadcaster Jaime Jarrín (2025), former catcher Steve Yeager (2024), longtime Minor League manager John Shoemaker (2023) and former Los Angeles City Councilmember Rosalind Wyman (2022).
The Los Angeles Dodgers franchise, with nine World Series championships and 26 National League pennants since its beginnings in Brooklyn in 1890, is committed to a tradition of pride and excellence. The Dodgers, baseball’s 2024 and 2025 back-to-back World Champions, are the reigning Sports Business Journal Sports Team of the Year, have been recognized as ESPN’s Sports Humanitarian Team of the Year and are dedicated to supporting a culture of winning baseball, providing a first-class, fan-friendly experience, and building a strong partnership with the community. With the highest cumulative fan attendance in Major League Baseball history and a record of breaking barriers, the Dodgers are one of the most cherished sports franchises in the world. Visit the Dodgers online at www.dodgers.com, follow them on Twitter @Dodgers and like them on Facebook at www.facebook.com/Dodgers. For media information, visit www.dodgerspressbox.com.

title: Cam Schlittler Enters MLB History With Sandy Koufax, Bob Gibson During Cy Young Race
author: Justin Binkowski; Unknown
body:
New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler has joined two Hall of Fame pitchers in the record books after what was likely his second-to-last start of the 2026 regular season.
Schlittler tossed six innings against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Saturday, giving up one earned run on three hits and three walks while striking out six. This was the 24th time this season the right-hander hasn't allowed more than one earned run in a start, tying Hall of Famers Bob Gibson and Sandy Koufax for the second-most such starts since 1920, according to MLB.com's Sarah Langs. Koufax is also at the top of that list with 25 starts in which he gave up no more than one earned run, so the Yankees hurler will have a chance to tie the Dodgers legend again in his final regular-season outing of the year.
This stat is just the latest example of how truly dominant Schlittler has been this season. In fact, some fans have been debating whether the hard-throwing righty could be a legitimate contender for the 2026 American League MVP. At the very least, the young pitcher has made a strong case for the 2026 AL Cy Young Award.
Has Cam Schlittler already done enough to claim the AL Cy Young?
With just one week left in the 2026 MLB regular season, the two pitchers with the best chance to win the American League Cy Young Award are Schlittler and Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease. Schlittler now has an AL-leading 1.94 ERA in 32 starts this year, racking up 234 strikeouts in 190 2/3 innings. Meanwhile, Cease leads the American League with 239 strikeouts and has a 2.40 ERA in 169 innings.
In Cease's most recent start on Friday, the 30-year-old threw just 2 2/3 innings and walked six batters. He had an MRI done on his shoulder Saturday night and is no longer expected to make his next scheduled start on Wednesday, according to The Athletic's Mitch Bannon. While the Toronto hurler could pitch again later in the week, this may impact his chances of making a late push for the 2026 AL Cy Young Award.

title: Edwin Díaz shares encouraging update on feel for pitching since returning
author: Matt Borelli
body:
Edwin Díaz hasn’t lived up to expectations in his first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he is hoping to finish the year on a good note and perhaps emerge as a bigger factor during the playoffs.
Since returning from the 15-day injured list over the weekend, the right-hander has thrown two scoreless innings against the San Francisco Giants. In those appearances, he allowed just two baserunners and collected four strikeouts.
“Yeah, 100%,” Díaz said when asked if he feels as good as he has all season. “I’ve been able to throw strikes. That was my problem and concern. I wasn’t throwing my fastball for strike. Now I’m able to command my fastball pretty good. When I command my fastball, my slider plays up. So I feel really good right now.”
Díaz’s success is coming after an uneven rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City that drew some criticism from manager Dave Roberts. The three-time All-Star gave up five runs in his second-to-last appearance and was reminded that he needed to pitch better.
Díaz bounced back with a scoreless effort after working on some adjustments with Comets pitching coaches Ryan Dennick and David Anderson. It’s still early, but Díaz believes the changes have helped him regain command of his fastball, which had been an issue throughout the season.
“I think my mechanics are better,” Díaz said. “After my rough game in Triple-A, I sat down with the Triple-A pitching coach to see what was the problem. We found I wasn’t moving my hips the right way, so we started working on that.
Díaz further noted his slider is back to being the devastating secondary pitch that he has become known for in his career.
“Yeah, right now it’s really good,” Díaz said. “It’s going down and away. I’ve been able to throw my fastball glove side, and if I throw my fastball glove side, [the slider] will play up in the same path.”
Edwin Díaz benefiting from new role
Prior to rejoining the Dodgers, Roberts made it clear that Díaz would not be returning to the closer role anytime soon as a way to ease him back into action. Both of his appearances against the Giants came in low-leverage situations, and Díaz believes that approach has helped him thrive so far.
“Yeah, yeah. I have an open mind. I’m in the situation right now where I need to help this team to win,” Díaz explained. “Whenever Doc puts me in the game, in any situation, I will do my job. And I feel good. I just want to keep climbing the ladder and finish the season strong.”

title: Dodgers could offer Cubs perfectly-timed solution to looming Ian Happ farewell
author: Jordan Campbell
body:
At the very least, it seems likely that the Chicago Cubs will let both Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki test the free-agent waters this offseason. Between the two, Suzuki makes sense for the Cubs to sign to a long-term deal, but he's positioned to be one of the best hitters available.
Even if Suzuki does return to the Cubs next season, there' the question of replacing Happ. Not to mention, as a whole, the offense could be without Carson Kelly, Michael Conforto, and Tyrone Taylor next season. Pitching is going to be the focus for the Cubs during the offseason, but they can't ignore the position-player side of the roster.
If the Cubs are going to make an addition of consequence to their starting lineup this offseason, chances are it will be in the outfield. That is where things get interesting for the Cubs, considering the rise of Josiah Hartshorn and Kane Kepley this season. Hartshorn and Kepley have both finished the 2026 season with Double-A Knoxville, and while it would aggressive for what the Cubs typically do, one of the two could find their way to Wrigley Field by the end of the 2027 season.
Not to mention, Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramirez could be options, and Ethan Conrad still figures to be involved in the long-term outlook in the outfield.
But given that the Cubs are in the middle of a contention window, it makes sense for them to look for a stopgap in the outfield for the 2027 season. While the free-agent market is thin, the trade market could point them in the direction of the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Teoscar Hernández could give Cubs exactly the stopgap they need if they move on from Ian Happ
FanSided's Pat Ragazzo takes an early look at offseason trade candidates, and among the names mentioned is Dodgers outfielder Teoscar Hernández. While the Dodgers doubled down on Hernández's role at the start of September, and he responded a resurgent month, conventional wisdom points to him being someone LA would be willing to move this offseason. Especially since Josue De Paula looks ready for an expanded role next year.
Hernández is owed over $22 next season, and carries a $15 million club option for the 2028 season. The option also includes a $6.5 million buyout. For a team that has a short-term need in the outfield with over $100 million coming off the books after the season, Hernández wouldn't be that crazy of an option for the Cubs.
The concern is that Hernández's resurgence this month could be a blip. Overall, his numbers have trended in the wrong direction over the last two years, and that could position him to be massively overpaid next season. Ultimately, that could be the reason why the Cubs steer clear of the veteran outfielder in trade talks. But if they are willing to take a gamble, this could be a move to watch for during the offseason.

title: Existe ‘buena posibilidad’ de que Ohtani sea activado en la serie Padres-Dodgers
author: Sonja Chen
body:
Existe ‘buena posibilidad’ de que Ohtani sea activado en la serie Padres-Dodgers
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- Podría no pasar tanto tiempo antes de que Shohei Ohtani esté de regreso para encabezar la alineación de los Dodgers.
Tras otro día productivo en su progresión de bateo, Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) se sigue perfilando a ser activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días durante la próxima serie de los Dodgers contra los Padres, informó el dirigente Dave Roberts tras la victoria del sábado por la noche 10-4 sobre los Gigantes en el Dodger Stadium.
"Hay una buena posiblidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie", expresó Roberts.
El paso de Ohtani a la lista de lesionados de 15 días es retroactivo al 8 de septiembre, lo que significa que es elegible para ser activado el miércoles, el segundo encuentro de la última serie en casa de los bicampeones contra los Frailes. Regresará estrictamente como bateador, debido a que está descartado para lanzar.
Luego de comenzar una progresión de bateo el martes, Ohtani ya avanzó a batear frente a la máquina Trajekt, la cual simula enfrentar a verdaderos lanzadores. Salió sintiéndose bien tras realizar entre 30 y 40 swings el sábado, indicó Roberts. Ohtani también corrió las bases mientras la escuadra de Los Ángeles realizaba las prácticas de bateo en el terreno.
Ohtani registró OPS de .902 y encabezó el equipo con 30 jonrones antes de que sus persistentes lesiones en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda lo obligaran a apartarse. En sus 24 encuentros antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados, que coincidió con un intento de intensificar su trabajo en el montículo, Ohtani bateó .198 (de 96-19) con 34 ponches en 96 turnos.
Si Ohtani regresa cuando sea elegible el miércoles, solo contará con cinco partidos de temporada regular para volverse a acoplar a la acción de las Grandes Ligas antes de la postemporada.
Los Dodgers han estado sin Ohtani en el lineup en 15 de sus últimos 16 compromisos, pero han encontrado su ritmo incluso sin su mejor bateador, consiguiendo marca de 13-3 en ese trecho.

title: One stat defines just how dominant Yoshinobu Yamamoto has been for Dodgers
author: Evan Roberts
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers starting rotation is so good collectively when they are healthy that it's sometimes difficult to focus on the individuals' accomplishments.
As a fan, it's easy to just look at the starting unit of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and Shohei Ohtani as one. But Yamamoto's latest feat stands out even relative to this dominant group of pitchers.
Dodgers starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto has been dominant this season
Yamamoto's most recent start came on September 15 against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. It was yet another ho-hum performance by the Dodgers ace. He picked up the win going seven scoreless innings, while allowing just one hit. He only walked two batters while striking out seven. Yamamoto lowered his career WHIP to 0.96, which is officially the best WHIP ever by a pitcher their first 75 career starts.
Yamamoto outpaced 2025 National League Cy Young Award-winner — and perhaps future Dodgers pitcher in Paul Skenes — as well as former member of LA's pitching staff, Walker Buehler. Behind Yamamoto, Skenes, and Buehler are Seattle Mariners All-Star starter Bryan Woo and Tampa Bay Rays right-hander Drew Rasmussen.
Not only does Yamamoto have the best WHIP ever through his first 75 games, but he's allowed the third-fewest runs in MLB history by a pitcher through that same span (trailing only Rasmussen and Skenes).
Opposing hitters are hitting .192/.252/.310 against Yamamoto through those 75 starts -- that is the lowest batting average against of any pitcher since 1974 (when that data became available). It's also the lowest on-base percentage, the fifth-lowest slugging percentage, and the second-lowest OPS.
Below is a list of fewest hits allowed in MLB history by a pitcher in their first 75 starts. There's a lot of familiar names on that list.
| Pitcher | Hits Allowed | 
|---|---|
| 1. Tony Gonsolin (LAD) | 264 | 
| 2. Freddy Peralta (MIL) | 270 | 
| 3. Drew Rasmussen (TB) | 284 | 
| T-4. Cristian Javier (HOU) | 287 | 
| T-4. Edward Cabrera (MIA) | 287 | 
| 6. Triston McKenzie (CLE) | 295 | 
| 7. Jack Flaherty (STL) | 299 | 
| T-8. Yoshinobu Yamamoto (LAD) | 305 | 
| T-8. Shohei Ohtani (LAA) | 305 | 
| 10. Tyler Glasnow (LAD) | 313 | 
Yamamoto has clearly been worth every penny since he signed that mega-deal with the Dodgers. It's nice to be able to point to his historic regular season success as well as his historic postseason success. Yamamoto is slowly building up a Hall of Fame résumé through his first three Major League seasons.

title: This day in Dodgers history: L.A. Coliseum, Sandy Koufax and Clayton Kershaw
author: Staff Writer
body:
This day in Los Angeles Dodgers history saw the end of an era at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, plus Sandy Koufax and Clayton Kershaw reach individual milestones.
On Sept. 20, 1961, the Dodgers came away with a 3-2 walk-off win against the Chicago Cubs in 13 innings. The game was notable in that Koufax not only pitched all 13 innings but it was the Dodgers’ final time playing at the L.A. Coliseum.
It was their home since moving from Brooklyn for the start of the 1958 season and until Dodger Stadium opened on April 10, 1962.
En route to pitching a complete game, Koufax finished with 15 strikeouts to earn his 18th win of the season.
Although that marked the Dodgers’ final time playing at the Coliseum, their 1961 season concluded with a nine-game road trip comprised of series against the St. Louis Cardinals, Pittsburgh Pirates and Cubs.
The Dodgers went 89-65, good for second place in the National League. They finished four games back of the Cincinnati Reds, who lost in the World Series to the New York Yankees.
On Sept. 20, 1966, Koufax was part of another memorable performance as he became the first NL pitcher in 31 years with back-to-back seasons of at least 25 victories.
Koufax reached the milestone with a complete game in the Dodgers 11-1 win over the Philadelphia Phillies at Dodger Stadium. The left-hander had 26 wins in 1965 and 27 in 1966, which wound up being his final season.
On Sept. 20, 2011, Kershaw became the Dodgers’ first 20-game winner since Ramon Martinez accomplished the feat in 1990. Kershaw pitched 7.1 innings against the San Francisco Giants to earn his 20th win.
Dodgers returned to Coliseum
On March 29, 2008, the Dodgers faced defending World Series champion Boston Red Sox in front of 115,300 fans for an exhibition game at the L.A. Memorial Coliseum. It was held to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Dodgers franchise moving from Brooklyn to Los Angeles.
The crowd represented the largest ever for a baseball game, surpassing the approximately 114,000 fans that were in attendance when the Australian national team played an American services team during the 1956 Olympics in Melbourne.

title: Dodgers eye sweep of Giants behind surging Mookie Betts
author: FLM
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will continue getting their house in order when they face the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon to complete the Dodgers' next-to-last home series of the regular season.
Los Angeles will use a bullpen game Sunday when it seeks a three-game series sweep, while the Giants will send left-hander Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 4.58 ERA) to the mound for his first appearance against the Dodgers.
Los Angeles has a lot of uncertainty heading into its 14th consecutive playoff appearance -- including the rotation because Blake Snell is working through groin discomfort -- while the offense has Shohei Ohtani (biceps inflammation, knee soreness) and Andy Pages (left hand fracture) nearing a return from the injured list.
The revival of Mookie Betts, along with the arrival of Josue De Paula from the minor leagues, has brought renewed energy after a mid-summer swoon.
The Dodgers still do not have a return date for Ohtani, with Betts the latest to claim the star's leadoff spot. Betts had two home runs among his three hits as the leadoff hitter Friday, then returned to the top spot Saturday and went 4-for-4 with three doubles and a walk. He has 10 hits over his past three games.
"The main thing is doing it when it counts," Betts said. "So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up (offensively)."
Betts had an RBI single in the second inning and an RBI double in the fourth Saturday as the Dodgers earned a 10-4 victory over the Giants.
"He's not a chase guy anyway, but he's cut that down considerably," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "The quality of contact is considerably higher. And then now you've got that attitude, that confidence, that we're used to seeing with Mookie."
The Dodgers' Will Smith also is rounding into form after missing three months with neck inflammation. Smith returned at the start of September and has three home runs over his past nine games, including one in each of the past two games.
Smith started consecutive games Friday and Saturday for the third time since he returned, although he is expected to be used off the bench, if at all, on Sunday.
The Giants have their own injury concerns. Ace Logan Webb was the latest to see his season end early, due to a blister on his right middle finger.
On Saturday, first baseman Bryce Eldridge missed his second consecutive game with a head laceration. The 6-foot-7 rookie bumped his head on a low overhang at the team hotel.
"He's still feeling the implications of that deal," Giants manager Tony Vitello said Saturday. "It's kind of a weird spot in the hotel. I checked it out. (Friday) it was a little bit more about just his comfort. But now, stemming from last night and this morning, those guys have been monitoring him like crazy. Just some lingering effects."
Giants rookie Victor Bericoto hit a two-run home run Saturday in his second game since returning from the injured list and now has five homers in 35 career games.
With a win Sunday, the Dodgers can earn their first three-game sweep over the Giants since April 2024. Los Angeles leads the season series 5-4, with one game remaining in L.A. and three games at San Francisco to end the regular season.

title: Dave Roberts acknowledges Dodgers still have big need for postseason
author: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 13th National League West title in the last 14 seasons, and now all that remains to do is stay in front of the Atlanta Braves down the stretch to secure a first-round bye.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset. But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts recently said. “We’ve still got to play well to finish out the season to get to that point. There’s a lot of people that could use the break.”
The Dodgers have a four-game lead over the Braves for the second seed in the NL. L.A. needs to finish with a better record than the Braves by virtue of not holding the head-to-head tiebreaker.
The top seed in the NL is within reach for the Dodgers, but they do not control their own destiny due to trailing the Milwaukee Brewers in the standings. Furthermore, the Dodgers also don’t have the tiebreaker over the Brewers.
Securing home-field advantage throughout the postseason would certainly be of value, but finishing as one of the top two division winners in the NL is of greater importance.
Some of the notable injuries the Dodgers are dealing with include Shohei Ohtani, Edgardo Henriquez, Andy Pages, Will Klein and, most recently, Blake Snell.
The Wild Card Series begins Tuesday, Sept. 29, while the NL Division Series starts Saturday, Oct. 3.
Pages and Ohtani are expected to be activated prior to the regular season concluding, and there is optimism Snell will avoid going on the injured list.
Henriquez is eligible to return on the same day the Wild Card round begins. Meanwhile, Klein can’t return until the NLDS starts. It is not a given that the Dodgers would elect to have Klein on their postseason roster given his two-month absence, but they would still prefer to have the option.
Dodgers postseason outlook
Should the Dodgers remain the No. 2 seed in the NL postseason bracket, they would face the Wild Card winner of the matchup between the third division champion and sixth-place team. However, who that could be is still very much in question in part because of a late surge from the San Diego Padres.
The Chicago Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies and Padres are all in a dead heat and mathematically possible of slotting into any order as the three Wild Card teams.

title: Edwin Díaz’s brilliant return should make Dodgers haters very, very nervous
author: Jake Elman
body:
Only the Los Angeles Dodgers could have a $69 million All-Star closer as a potential hidden weapon ahead of the postseason.
Such a thing shouldn’t be possible, but the Dodgers aren’t most teams. Friday night’s blowout win over the Giants presented what’s been a rare sight this year: Edwin Díaz taking the mound in the ninth inning. The 32-year-old has missed much of the season with elbow and neck problems, and the 8-2 rout marked his first outing since Aug. 17.
Díaz pitching a scoreless ninth in September is exactly what Dodgers fans envisioned when they added the three-time All-Star this past offseason. However, manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Díaz, who had recorded an 11.85 ERA and allowed 10 walks in his first 14.2 innings, will not move back into the closer role.
In fact, Roberts admitted he would not have used the veteran reliever on Friday night if not for the team's six-run lead. To his credit, Díaz worked around a two-out single, and his fastball averaged 97.6 mph, which MLB's Sarah Wexler reported was up 1.3 mph from his season average.
“I think we just want to see him throw the baseball the way he's capable of,” Roberts said. “And you’re talking about nine games, so you're talking three or four outings to evaluate, and that should be adequate.”
The story was much the same on Saturday: L.A. calling on Diaz in a six-run game, and Diaz striking out two batters with just one baserunner in a scoreless inning — all while looking much more like the guy the Dodgers thought they were acquiring this offseason.
Could Edwin Díaz actually help the Los Angeles Dodgers in the postseason?
If the postseason began Sunday, the Dodgers would be the NL’s No. 2 seed and have a first-round bye. They’d then host the highest remaining seed in the NLDS, which would either be the NL East-leading Braves or the No. 6 seed (the Phillies held that spot entering Sunday, though they are one game back of the No. 4 Cubs and No. 5 Padres).
Wexler wrote that Díaz is competing for a spot on the playoff roster, which isn’t overly surprising to anyone familiar with Roberts’ mindset. Financial commitments and a player’s Baseball-Reference pages only matter so much, and the Dodgers have three championships in the last six years to prove it.
Roberts, who took over the Dodgers ahead of the 2016 season, has spent the last decade proving he’s not afraid to bench underperforming players or go with the hot hand. If Díaz returns to his earlier form and is dreadful over the team’s final seven games, it's difficult to imagine he’d be a lock to make the 26-man playoff roster.
The reality is that neither Roberts nor the Dodgers know what they’ll get from Díaz, who already has four games where he's given up at least three runs. He’s been worth -1.2 bWAR in 17 games, and he allowed five runs, three walks and a hit by pitch during a recent Triple-A outing during his rehab stint.
Personally, we’re skeptical about Díaz making a significant positive difference if he makes the postseason roster. Two low-stress outings don't make up for an entire season's worth of dysfunction. But the velocity is now creeping back up into the high 90s, and that's an awfully promising sign. We need to see him keep doing it over the final week of the regular season, but if he can, that could answer this team's most pressing question entering October.
Díaz has silenced his critics in the past, most notably after an ugly first season with the Mets in 2019. Hey, we were willing to own our prediction that the Nationals would lose at least 110 games. Prove us wrong, Edwin!

title: Mookie Betts batea de 4-4 con tres triples y dos impulsadas
source: El Nacional — La voz de todos
author: Agencia AP
body:
Dodgers doblegan Giants
Mookie Betts batea de 4-4 con tres triples y dos impulsadas
El novato dominicano Josué De Paula pega sencillo impulsador de 2 carreras, anota dos y recibe dos bases por bolas
LOS ÁNGELES.— Mookie Betts bateó de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith agregó tres hits, incluyendo un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron a los Gigantes de San Francisco 10-4 el sábado por la noche.
El sencillo de dos carreras con dos outs de Tommy Edman ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate a 4 en la quinta entrada. El bateador emergente Miguel Rojas conectó un sencillo productor para poner el marcador 7-4 a favor de su equipo, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para finalizar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto Freddie Freeman, quien tuvo un mal desempeño y se fue de 0 de 5. Betts igualó su mejor marca de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en jonrones, 15-8. El ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana bateaba .249 hace una semana y desde entonces ha elevado su promedio a .261.
Los Dodgers anotaron carreras en seis entradas consecutivas al inicio de un partido por primera vez en 10 años. Han anotado 15 carreras en sus últimas siete entradas ofensivas, incluyendo cuatro jonrones en la octava entrada contra Abner en el primer partido de la serie del viernes.
Los campeones de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional (95-60) ganaron su partido número 95 para colocarse 35 juegos por encima del .500, su mejor marca de la temporada.
El tercer doble de Betts abrió la sexta entrada y anotó con un sencillo productor de Smith ante el relevista Joel Kuhnel. El novato Josue De Paula añadió un sencillo productor de dos carreras, ampliando la ventaja a 10-4.
En tres ocasiones, los Giants remontaron para empatar el partido, solo para ver cómo los Dodgers volvían a tomar la delantera, destacando el jonrón de dos carreras de Victor Bericoto, de 425 pies, que empató el partido en la tercera entrada.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), no estuvo especialmente brillante, permitiendo cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas. El zurdo ponchó a tres y otorgó dos bases por bolas, y los Dodgers ganaron sus últimas seis salidas.
El relevista Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin permitir carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor de los Giants, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas con dos ponches.
El jardinero derecho de los Dodgers, Kyle Tucker, recibió un foul en la rodilla y fue reemplazado por Alex Call en la séptima entrada.

title: Scout's Josue De Paula assessment will excite Dodgers fans
author: Pat Ragazzo
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers might have their next homegrown superstar in outfielder Josue De Paula. That's at least according to one National League scout who spoke with FanSided.
"JDP is the most polished young hitter I have seen in my 17 years of professional baseball," the scout said. "He is never rushed, immensely confident, and has been incredibly consistent since entering pro ball."
De Paula has done nothing but produce in the minor leagues since signing with the Dodgers out of the Dominican Republic as a 16-year-old in 2022. This season, he slashed .303/.401/.547 with a .948 OPS, 27 homers, 104 RBI and 31 stolen bases in 124 games in Double-A. As a result, he replaced Shohei Ohtani, who went on the IL with knee and biceps injuries, on the Dodgers' roster this month.
De Paula, 21, was called up to make his MLB debut on September 11. He proceeded to crush a moonshot of a three-run home run two days later for his first career big league hit. The future is certainly bright for the left-handed hitter. De Paula is the Dodgers' No. 1 ranked prospect and No. 4 in all of baseball, per Baseball America.
Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula was compared to MLB legend Manny Ramirez
The same scout told FanSided that De Paula's natural hitting skills compare to a former Dodger and legendary slugger.
"The only fair comparison to the ease in which hitting comes to (De Paula) is Manny Ramirez," the scout said. "He was born to hit and has done nothing but refine his gift the last four-plus years."
This is good company to be in. Ramirez was a 12-time All-Star and nine-time Silver Slugger Award winner across 18-years in the big leagues. He led the American League in RBI (1999), won a batting title (2002) and led the AL in home runs (2004). Ramirez was also a two-time World Series champion with the Boston Red Sox and won World Series MVP in 2004. Ramirez would be in the Hall of Fame if not for his ties to performance-enhancing drugs.
If De Paula can have similar results in the majors as Ramirez, the youngster will be in pretty good shape, and so will the Dodgers. Los Angeles has center fielder Andy Pages under control through 2030, left fielder Teoscar Hernandez is entering the final year of his deal in 2027, and Kyle Tucker is in year-one of a four-year, $240 million deal that has opt outs after 2027 and 2028. Luckily, De Paula is expected to be a future core piece of the Dodgers' outfield for many years to come.

Los Angeles has center fielder Andy Pages under control through 2030, left fielder Teoscar Hernandez is entering the final year of his deal in 2027, and Kyle Tucker is in year-one of a four-year, $240 million deal that has opt outs after 2027 and 2028. Luckily, De Paula is expected to be a future core piece of the Dodgers' outfield for many years to come.

title: Dodgers Notes: LA Promotes Outfielder, Shohei Ohtani Injury Update, Teoscar Hernandez Trade?
author: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 10-4, on Saturday night and improved to 95-60 on the year.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal had an uncharacteristic start, striking out just three batters over five innings while allowing four earned runs. Fortunately, the bullpen picked him up with four scoreless innings.
Offensively, Mookie Betts had a marvelous four-hit night and Will Smith notched three hits of his own, including a home run. Rookie Josue De Paula continued to impress with two walks and a two-run single with the bases loaded.
After the game, manager Dave Roberts provided an update on Shohei Ohtani, saying he has a "good chance" of being activated during the team's series against the San Diego Padres this week.
While Ohtani is eligible to be activated on Wednesday, it's currently unclear if that's the day he'll be back.
Either way, the Dodgers are expecting Ohtani back soon, and he took a major step on Saturday, hitting off the Trajekt machine and running the bases before the game.
In his stead, De Paula has done an unbelievable job as the everyday designated hitter.
In other news, the Dodgers recently promoted an outfielder who previously thought that his season might be over. The third-round pick in the 2024 MLB Draft was hitting .306 with a .985 OPS across 35 games in High-A and 71 appearances in Double-A this season.
Finally, veteran outfielder Teoscar Hernández was recently labeled as a likely trade candidate by Pat Ragazzo of FanSided. The insider explained that the influx of outfield talent, combined with an expiring contract that was reportedly being shopped around over the offseason, could lead to the team parting ways with "Mr. Seeds."
"The Dodgers have No. 1 prospect Josue De Paula and other young outfielders in their farm system, who could replace Hernandez in left field next season," Ragazzo wrote. "It would make sense for the Dodgers to ship Hernandez out this offseason with one-year remaining on his deal."

title: Is Blake Snell the Dodgers’ Best Pitcher Right Now? | Just Baseball
author: Ryan Murphy
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have done it again.
With the Dodgers’ win on Thursday afternoon, they officially clinched the NL West championship for the fifth consecutive year. This marks the Dodgers’ 13th NL West title out of the past 14 years, with their lone second place finish coming in 2021 behind an otherworldly season from the San Francisco Giants.
It has been an interesting season for this Dodgers team. After a scorching hot 56-30 start through June, the Dodgers slumped to a 26-25 record in July and August. Now hunting for the top seed in the National League for the postseason, the Dodgers have bounced back to an 11-5 record in September (as of Thursday).
A major factor in the Dodgers’ volatility this year has been their susceptibility to injury. This year alone, a whopping 27 players have seen time on the Dodgers’ injured list.
The majority of these players have made their way back from the injured list, to varying degrees of success. Of those who have returned to the active roster, one player stands above them all.
Starter Blake Snell has been on a tear since his return from the injured list. While his status moving forward is now in question following his early exit from his September 16 start against the Cincinnati Reds, his run of dominance has been a sight to behold.
Yet, for Snell, the journey to get to this point has been far from a walk in the park.
Stats as of September 17.
Celebrations and Setbacks
Snell came into the 2026 season as arguably the co-ace of the Dodgers’ starting rotation, alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
The left-hander had been a pivotal part of the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series run, allowing just two runs over his first 21 innings of work. Snell cooled off significantly in the World Series, allowing 10 earned runs over 13 innings, but he was invaluable to the Dodgers nonetheless.
However, Snell’s heavy usage in October had some untoward downstream effects. Left with minimal recovery time between the end of the season and the beginning of spring training, Snell had difficulty getting ramped back up for the year. As a result, his offseason throwing progression suffered unanticipated delays.
Lingering shoulder fatigue kept Snell off of the mound through early May, missing the first 38 games. Finally, nearly a month and a half into the 2026 season, Snell was set to make his season debut. Unfortunately for Snell and the Dodgers, his return was interrupted almost immediately.
After three innings against the Atlanta Braves on May 9, Snell’s season debut was done. He allowed four earned runs, striking out five batters while allowing six hits and two walks. Unbeknownst to Snell, this would be his last start for over three months.
Snell was scratched from his next scheduled start. Just one day later, he underwent surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. As a result, Snell missed another 78 games, finally making his return in early August. Since then, he seems to have unlocked a new level.
Second-Half Hero
Snell has long been known to elevate his game during the second half of each season. For his career, he has posted a 3.96 ERA in the first half and a 2.31 ERA during the latter half. As good as his career second-half numbers may be, he’s been even better in his return to the mound this year.
Over his last seven starts, Snell has pitched to an incredible 1.01 ERA, recording 47 strikeouts and 14 walks over 35.2 innings. Opponents are batting a measly .164/.254/.205 against him, and he has allowed no more than one run in any start during this span.
With a sample this small, it is difficult to quantify just how effective Snell has been compared to his Dodgers teammates. This is especially true given the run their starting rotation has been on in recent weeks.
Both Yamamoto and the Dodgers’ marquee trade deadline pickup, Tarik Skubal, have been dominant in their own right. Since Snell returned to the rotation on August 11, Yamamoto and Skubal have each posted an ERA under 2.10 over 30+ innings apiece.
Still, Snell’s ERA over the same span clears both of theirs by a full run. Though Skubal narrowly edges out Snell in fWAR (1.8 fWAR vs. 1.7 fWAR), Snell’s success is all the more unprecedented given this is his first sustained stretch of play since the 2025 postseason.
Expanding beyond just the Dodgers, Snell’s metrics stack up well among the league’s best. Among all qualified pitchers over the same span, Snell holds the second-best ERA, third-best FIP, second-best fWAR, and third-best K/9 rate. He is the only qualified pitcher to have yet to surrender a home run over this span.
What’s Been Working?
Since returning from the IL, Snell has demonstrated a number of improvements.
For one, his stuff seems to have jumped in effectiveness. Every one of Snell’s pitches has seen either a marginal or significant jump in induced movement.
In particular, his fastball has gained nearly an inch of both induced vertical break and horizontal break. This pairs incredibly well with his improved curveball, which has gained two inches of depth and over an inch of horizontal movement.
Factoring in his slider and changeup, Snell’s arsenal has looked remarkably effective as a whole. As a result, his two best pitches have played up in a big way. Though the sample is small, Snell’s fastball has allowed just a 5.6% hard-hit percentage. While batters hit .309 and slugged .426 against his heater in 2025, those figures have dropped to .179 and .232 so far this year.
The results on his curveball have been even more effective, as batters are batting and slugging .086 against it. In 37 plate appearances, hitters have recorded just three hits against Snell’s curveball compared to 20 strikeouts. He has yet to allow an extra-base hit with his curveball in 2026.
Beyond Snell’s improved arsenal, he has also located the ball well. A pitcher with Snell’s profile traditionally operates best working around the edges of the strike zone. This allows him to induce whiffs and chase swings, leading to a higher strikeout rate and more frequent weak contact, but also more walks.
Snell has leaned into this philosophy, attacking early while working around the edges later in at-bats. He has thrown fewer balls in the zone overall, improving his chase rate, but has also significantly increased his first-pitch strike percentage.
Room for Concern
Snell’s run of dominance has been impressive, to say the least. But, his most recent start brings a sobering point to the conversation around his performance.
Last year, the Dodgers leaned heavily on Snell at the end of the regular season and the postseason. He did not bounce back gracefully, missing over 100 games in the 2026 season.
This year, the Dodgers hope to lean on Snell heavily once again as they approach October baseball. As such, it is reasonable to air concerns around the volatility of his health, with his most recent start as an example.
Snell left after one inning against the Reds, citing a left groin issue. In years past, Snell has missed anywhere from a few weeks to a couple of months battling the same issue.
However, he did frame his decision to exit the game as precautionary, rather than reactive. According to Snell, he felt the area tighten up during his pre-game bullpen, and he felt it was best not to push it. While he still hopes to make his next start, nobody can know for sure what the full impact of this issue will wind up being.
The Dodgers have yet to make any further announcements around the injury. At this time, Snell has not been placed on the injured list either. The first real test will be whether Snell ends up making his next start. Manager Dave Roberts has weighed the idea of delaying it, but any deviation from the norm will have an impact at this stage.
Whether Snell remains healthy through October is anybody’s guess. Regardless, his remarkable performance since coming back from injury is a testament to both his talent and resilience. Hopefully, fans can look forward to Snell making a comeback against the San Diego Padres next week.

title: MLB roundup: D-backs walk off Yankees on World Series anniversary night
body:
Field Level Media
                
20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1

title: With the season winding down, Mookie Betts is heating up
author: Jacob Macofsky
body:
2026 looked to be a lost season for Mookie Betts, as an oblique injury cost him a month’s worth of time. At the All-Star break, the Dodgers shortstop was limping to the tune of a .235/.293/.416 slashline with 11 home runs and 31 RBI over 60 games.
Since the second half of the regular season began, Betts has turned into his 2023 MVP-runner-up self, as he’s slashing .290/.364/.452 with 11 home runs and 36 RBI over his last 56 games. Betts has been on a tear his last three games, as he’s hitting .833 with five extra-base hits and five RBI, highlighted by a four-hit, three-double game on Saturday in the Dodgers’ 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
Betts has hit all around the lineup, going from as high as leadoff to as low as the six hole, but Betts has been certifying himself as a force at the top of the lineup during this final homestand. Betts spoke with David Vassegh of SportsNet LA about his torrid stretch at the plate hitting at the top spot following Saturday’s win, noting that the return of Shohei Ohtani will directly impact where he hits everyday.
“It’s fun. Like you said, I’ve done it for so long, but that man Shohei— he deserves what he gets. We all know where he needs to hit in the lineup.”
Saturday was a rough outing for left-hander Tarik Skubal as he allowed four earned runs while striking out a season-low three hitters over five innings.
Despite the atypical night for Skubal, his offense was able to generate six runs after his final pitch, giving him his fourth win as a Dodger. When speaking with Vassegh following the game, Skubal gave all the credit to the offense and bullpen for carrying the team the rest of the way.
“Obviously, I wasn’t very good today. The offense, defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that’s what good teams do— they pick each other up, and win series and win baseball games. Hats off to them.”
Mirjam Swanson at the Los Angeles Times writes about Tyler Glasnow and the ability to trust himself as the playoffs loom near. Glasnow was solid on Friday against San Francisco, allowing just two runs while striking out 10 hitters.
“Today was a step in the right direction,” said Glasnow, the formerHart High star, before leaving the clubhouse in flip-flops. “I’d rather kind of feel it, work through some stuff, and have a good one right before playoffs.
“I think I’m in a good spot right now.”
Jack Harris of the California Post has a positive update regarding Shohei Ohtani, as the two-way superstar did base running drills and used the Trajekt Ark pitching machine in the cage. Hitting coach Aaron Bates notes that Ohtani has been really good with the machine, and the next test will be how he performs in live batting practice.
“In the cage, in a controlled setting, he’s been really good. It’s 100% intensity,” Bates said. “Once he gets out to the field, if he does a live BP or something like that, and the intensity ramps up, it’ll be a good test to see what happens. But in the cage, in the controlled setting, he’s been really good.”

title: 「真剣に検討すべき」崩れなかった1番固定方針に懸念 大谷翔平が抱える“異変”を米メディアが指摘「リードオフマンにふさわしいレベルじゃない」
body:
「真剣に検討すべき」崩れなかった1番固定方針に懸念 大谷翔平が抱える“異変”を米メディアが指摘「リードオフマンにふさわしいレベルじゃない」
グラウンドに立ち、ベースランニングを軽快にこなす大谷(C)Getty Images
戦線復帰に向けた準備は着々と進んでいる。現地時間9月19日に行われたジャイアンツ戦後、ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は、負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている大谷翔平について「次のシリーズ（パドレスとの3連戦）で復帰する可能性は十分ある」と明言した。
今月11日に右上腕の炎症による15日間のILに入った大谷。今シーズン中の投手断念をせざるを得ない緊急事態に陥った偉才だったが、チームから与えられた休養期間を活かし、満身創痍だった肉体の回復に努めてきた。
19日のジャイアンツ戦前には、グラウンド上でのベースランニングや、高性能打撃マシン「Trajekt Arc」を用いた打撃練習もこなした。その内容についてロバーツ監督も「すごく良かった。バッティング練習も30～40スイングぐらいしたと思うが、終えた後の状態は良かった」と前向きな見解を示した。
となれば、注目を集めるのは、起用法だ。ドジャース入団以来1番打者として固定されてきた大谷だが、多くの打席が回ることで生じる負担の多さは懸念材料となる。怪我を再発させるリスクを考えれば、2番、もしくは3番に打順を下げる可能性もゼロとは言えない。
ドジャースのありとあらゆる情報を発信している米メディア『Dodgers Nation』は、「万全の状態ではないオオタニ、完全なる健康状態である時と同じレベルに達するのは不可能。実際、怪我と疲労が重なってスイングに悪影響を及ぼすにつれ、彼はリードオフマンにふさわしいレベルの活躍ができなくなっていた」と指摘。離脱直前の7試合で打率.077（長打率.077）、出塁率.255とアベレージが極端に低下していた打撃内容を紹介した一方で、直近15試合で打率.356、出塁率.457と好成績を残しているムーキー・ベッツの復調ぶりを強調。「ロバーツとチームはワールドシリーズ3連覇の可能性を高めるために打順の変更を真剣に検討する必要があるだろう」と論じた。

title: Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
author: Doug Padilla
body:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

title: Dodgers outslug Giants 10-4, led by Mookie Betts with four hits
source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
author: ABC News; BETH HARRIS AP sports writer
body:
Dodgers outslug Giants 10-4, led by Mookie Betts with four hits
Mookie Betts had four hits, including three doubles, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4
LOS ANGELES -- Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.
Tommy Edman's two-run, two-out single off reliever Philip Abner snapped a 4-all tie in the fifth. Pinch-hitter Miguel Rojas followed with an RBI single for a 7-4 lead, with Edman thrown out at home to end the inning.
Every Dodger had at least one hit, except for struggling Freddie Freeman who was 0 for 5. Betts tied his season high for hits and the team outslugged the Giants, 15-8. The former AL MVP was hitting .249 a week ago, and has since raised his average to .261.
The Dodgers scored runs in six straight innings to start a game for the first time in 10 years. They've scored 15 runs in their last seven offensive innings, including a four-homer eighth off Abner in Friday's series opener.
The NL West champions (95-60) won their 95th game to move a season-high 35 games above .500.
Betts' third double led off the sixth and he scored on Smith's RBI single off reliever Joel Kuhnel. Rookie Josue De Paula added a two-run RBI single, extending the lead to 10-4.
Three times the Giants rallied to tie the game only to see the Dodgers retake the lead, highlighted by Victor Bericoto's game-tying, 425-foot two-run homer in the third.
Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal (11-7) wasn't particularly sharp, allowing four runs and eight hits in five innings. The left-hander struck out three and walked two, with the Dodgers winning each of his last six outings.
Reliever Edwin Díaz pitched a scoreless eighth in his second straight appearance since coming off the injured list Friday.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings with two strikeouts.
Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker fouled a ball off his knee and was replaced by Alex Call in the seventh.
Neither team had announced their starters for the series finale Sunday.
___

title: Mookie Betts thriving batting first: Should he hit leadoff for Dodgers instead of Shohei Ohtani?
author: Jack Harris
body:
Plan A, as always, is Shohei Ohtani.
But over the last couple nights, Plan B has looked pretty good too.
Whenever Ohtani returns from the injured list, the two-way star will likely reprise his customary role as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter –– one he has held since halfway through his debut 2024 season with the team.
Likely, however, was as far as manager Dave Roberts was willing to describe it on Saturday.
Because in Ohtani’s absence, Mookie Betts has made a case to spearhead the team’s order, too.
Over the last week, a red-hot Betts has served as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter three times. In each of those contests, he delivered a vintage performance.
There was a 2-for-4 display with an RBI and a double in Miami last week.
A 3-for-4 outburst with two home runs (including one to lead off the game) against the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Then, a 4-for-4, three-double, two-RBI, one-walk masterpiece in another 10-4 rout of the Giants on Saturday, a victory that lowered the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round playoff bye down to four with eight days remaining in the season.
“I just think he’s physically in a better spot than he has been,” Roberts said after Saturday’s outburst, which pushed Betts’ season average up to .261 and OPS to .785. “The ball’s coming off the right way.”
Of course, Betts has been crushing the ball regardless of where he’s been in the order lately. Since Aug. 5, he is batting .336 in 39 games with nine home runs, 12 doubles, 31 RBIs and a 1.008 OPS.
It has marked the former MVP’s best extended stretch since early in the 2024 season. It has been a reminder that there’s still plenty of life left in his previously slumping bat.
“I know I’m still capable of it,” the 33-year-old Betts said. “I know it was in there somewhere.”
Added Roberts: “It just doesn’t matter where you hit him, who he’s facing, [what’s] the situation –– he’s taking good at-bats.”
Betts’ impact at the top of the lineup specifically, however, has been impossible to ignore over the last week; especially when juxtaposed with the ongoing uncertainty surrounding Ohtani, who is expected back next week from right arm and left knee injuries but still doesn’t figure to be 100% physically.
That’s why, after writing Betts’ name in at the leadoff spot for a second-straight day Saturday, Roberts was asked if it’s still a certainty that Ohtani will remain in the leadoff spot upon his return.
“Yeah, I mean, I think that’s my first kind of thought,” Roberts said. “But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I’ll kind of potentially read and react.”
Much will obviously depend on how Ohtani looks, which will be the biggest question after a 6-for-52 slump leading up to his IL stint.
Roberts also cited other factors like trying to match up against either right- or left-handed pitching, leaving the door open to some game-by-game tinkering in October.
“I haven’t really thought too much about it [yet],” he insisted.
The way Betts is going, though, it might soon become a critical lineup-construction decision.
Run the risk with a potentially diminished but ever-dangerous Ohtani? Or give the most at-bats as possible to the team’s hottest current hitter?
Granted, Betts hasn’t pushed to take over the leadoff spot, saying Friday that “I’ll hit wherever” and “there’s a guy that’s named Shohei that needs to be up there and to get us going.”
But if the Dodgers need to pivot among Ohtani’s ongoing ailments, he is quickly emerging as their best fallback option –– especially with their initial leadoff replacement, the switch-hitting Tommy Edman, mired in a brutal 2-for-39 slump.
“Going back up there, it is fun,” Betts acknowledged, having played almost 1,100 career games as a leadoff hitter over his 13-year career. “Kind of feels like home.”
“You do got to kind of prepare for whatever,” Roberts added, “and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
For now, the Dodgers’ bigger priority will be making sure Betts keeps swinging the bat well, whether that’s in the No. 1 spot or somewhere else in the heart of the order.
His late-season surge has been one of the biggest reasons the team has survived Ohtani’s absence –– winning 13 of its last 16 despite the superstar slugger playing in just one of those contests.
“It’s good. It’s fun. But the main thing is doing it when it counts,” Betts said of his recent success. “Right now, just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up.”
Still, given how things are trending at the moment, it might not be a surprise if the Dodgers’ first at-bat of the playoffs belonged to their streaking shortstop.
“I couldn’t tell you that I saw this [coming],” Roberts conceded. “But he’s got stronger. He’s worked hard on that … And just for it to come together has been great.”

title: Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants
author: Field Level Media
body:
Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants
(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith hit a home run as the Dodgers (95-60) won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3.
Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings with three strikeouts. The left-hander is now 4-2 with a 2.85 ERA in nine starts for Los Angeles after a trade from the Detroit Tigers on Aug. 2.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants (64-91) while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
San Francisco lost for the sixth time in its past eight games in its next-to-last road game of the season.
Max Muncy had an RBI double in the first inning to score Betts as the Dodgers started a stretch in which they scored in each of the first six innings. Betts had an RBI single in the second.
The Giants tied the score in the third on Bericoto's fifth home run over his first 35 career games.
Los Angeles went back on top 3-2 in the third on Smith's leadoff home run. Both teams scored in the fourth, with San Francisco tying the score 4-4 in the fifth on a double from Jung Hoo Lee.
Edman's two-run single in the fifth gave the Dodgers the lead for good and they added another in the inning for a 7-4 lead on a Miguel Rojas single.
In the sixth, Smith added an RBI single, while rookie Josue De Paula followed with a two-run single for a 10-4 advantage.
Los Angeles has a 5-4 advantage in the season series with four games still remaining between the teams.
Smith went 3-for-5 as the Dodgers collected 15 hits.
Lee went 2-for-4 for the Giants and drove in a run. The Giants had two hits in a dozen at-bats with runners in scoring position.

title: Dodging a loss in a game of Giant momentum swings
author: Jacob Macofsky
body:
The Dodgers and San Francisco Giants kept things neck-and-neck through the first half of Saturday night’s contest, but the Dodgers rattled off six unanswered runs in a 10-4 victory.
After Tarik Skubal allowed a two-out walk to Giants designated hitter Victor Bericoto, Jung Hoo Lee attacked the first pitch he saw into the right-center field gap, but a diving play from Kyle Tucker got Skubal out of the inning with the game remaining scoreless.
Mookie Betts started things off in the bottom of the first inning with a leadoff double, and Max Muncy cashed him in with a two-strike, two-out RBI double to give the Dodgers the first lead of the game. Betts would come through again in the bottom of the second inning, lacing an RBI single the other way to plate Josue De Paula and make it a 2-0 Dodger lead.
Skubal worked his way around two baserunners for a scoreless top of the second inning, but after allowing a one-out single to Turner Hill in the top of the third inning, Bericoto launched a 3-2 fastball deep over the center field wall, tying the game at 2. Will Smith wasted no time giving the Dodgers the lead again, hammering a solo home run to lead off the bottom of the third inning, giving him his second home run in as many games.
The Giants responded with a pair of leadoff singles from Andrew Knizner and Osleivis Basabe to begin the top of the fourth inning. A bunt from Christian Koss moved both men into scoring position, and a squeeze bunt from Jonah Cox plated Knizner to tie the game at 3.
The Dodgers would get another one-run lead thanks to an RBI double from Mookie Betts in the bottom of the fourth inning— his second double and second RBI of the game. The Giants wouldn’t let Skubal settle in for the top of the fifth inning, as Bericoto and Lee both doubled to tie the game at four.
Saturday turned out to be Skubal’s worst outing of the season, let alone as a Dodger. Skubal managed to complete five innings of work but allowed a season-high four earned runs, while his three strikeouts on the night were the fewest in any start since striking out three on August 14 of last season against the Minnesota Twins.
Despite the poor start, the Dodgers put Skubal officially in line for the win as Teoscar Hernández ignited a two-out rally with an opposite-field single. Kyle Tucker and Josue De Paula each followed with a walk, and Tommy Edman snapped out of a 1-37 funk with a go-ahead, two-run single to give the Dodgers their first multi-run lead since the third. Miguel Rojas knocked a pinch-hit single to bring home De Paula, but Edman was thrown out at home attempting to make it a four-run inning.
Evan Phillips recorded the first clean inning of the night in relief of Skubal in the top of the sixth inning, and the Dodgers responded with another three-run inning, capitalized by a two-run single by De Paula and giving the Dodgers a six-run cushion.
After a scoreless inning from Alex Vesia in the seventh inning, Edwin Díaz came in for his second consecutive game since returning from injury, pitching a scoreless top of the eighth inning while picking up a pair of strikeouts.
Mookie Betts finished Saturday going 4-4 with three doubles and two RBI, reaching base five times after a walk in the seventh inning. Betts is now 10-12 (.833 average) over his last three games with three doubles, two home runs and five RBI.
With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintain a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the no. 2 seed in the National League. They still trail the Milwaukee Brewers by two games for the top seed.
Game particulars
- Home runs— Victor Bericoto (5); Will Smith (9)
- WP— Tarik Skubal (11-7): 5 IP, 8 hits, 4 earned runs, 2 walks, 3 strikeouts
- LP— Yunior Marte (0-1): 4 2/3 IP, 8 hits, 6 earned runs, 3 walks, 2 strikeouts
Up next
The Dodgers wrap things up against San Francisco on Sunday (1:10 p.m. PT, SportsNet LA) before hosting the San Diego Padres for their final regular season home series beginning Tuesday. Both teams have yet to announce their starters.

title: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani: 'Good chance' to return vs. SD
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said after Saturday's game that there's a "good chance" Ohtani (knee/biceps) will be activated during next week's series against the Padres, Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic reports.
Ohtani ran the bases on the field prior to Saturday's game and also advanced to taking simulated at-bats against the team's Trajekt machine. It sounds like the Dodgers are pleased with Ohtani's progress, enough so that he's penciled in to return during the homestand. If Ohtani is activated Wednesday when first eligible, he could play in up to five games before the end of the regular season.

title: 大谷翔平、最短24日パドレス戦で復帰か ロバーツ監督が示唆「可能性は高い」
author: Full-Count編集部
body:
大谷翔平、最短24日パドレス戦で復帰か ロバーツ監督が示唆「可能性は高い」
ロバーツ監督「グレートだった。グレートだった」
【MLB】ドジャース 10ー4 ジャイアンツ（日本時間20日・ロサンゼルス）
ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督が19日（日本時間20日）、大谷翔平投手の状態に言及し、順調な回復ぶりと次カードでの復帰可能性を示唆した。ドジャースは、本拠地で行われたジャイアンツ戦に10-4で快勝。ロバーツ監督は試合後の会見で、大谷の最近の調整状況について回答した。
「（試合前の練習は）グレートだった。グレートだった。実際に彼は（走塁練習だけでなく）投手（の映像が映ってる）マシン相手にも打撃を行った。今晩は30、40スイングかな。うまくいった」
さらに、打撃だけでなく走塁面での仕上がりについても高く評価した。
「なので明日も打撃練習をするだろう。彼が走塁をする姿を見て、脚を使えているように見えたし、（実際に）力強い印象だった。なので次の（パドレスとの）シリーズで彼を見られる（出場する）可能性は高い」
右上腕二頭筋の炎症で、11日（同12日）から負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている大谷。復帰できるのは最短で23日（同24日）に行われるパドレスとの2戦目となる。ポストシーズンを見据え、ワールドシリーズ3連覇へ向けた戦いが続くドジャース。主砲の復帰はチームにとって大きな追い風となりそうだ。
（Full-Count編集部）

The catcher had gone 14 games without a multi-RBI game, batting .211 (8-for-38) in that span.
