title: Edwin Díaz brilla en su regreso desde la lista de lesionados y alcanza casi las 99 millas con su recta
author: Por Servicios combinados
body:
En el partido de regreso la recta de Edwin Díaz promedió 97.6 millas por hora, 1.3 millas por arriba de lo que era su promedio en la temporada, pero alcanzó en el juego las 99 mph. (Mark J. Terrill)
Por Servicios combinados
Los Ángeles - Mookie Betts conectó dos jonrones y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles pegaron cuatro cuadrangulares en la octava entrada para imponerse 8-2 a los Giants de San Francisco la noche del viernes, en un partido que marcó el regreso desde la lista de lesionados del relevista puertorriqueño Edwin “Sugar” Díaz.
Max Muncy y Kyle Tucker conectaron jonrones consecutivos en la octava. Betts y Max Muncy añadieron vuelacercas solitarios con dos outs en una entrada de cinco carreras, mientras los campeones del Oeste de la Liga Nacional se impusieron en el primer juego de una serie entre viejos rivales.
Tyler Glasnow (5-1) permitió dos carreras y tres imparables en seis entradas, con un máximo de temporada de 10 ponches.
La lluvia de jonrones ocurrió en el vigésimo aniversario del juego de cuatro-más-uno de los Dodgers. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin y Marlon Anderson conectaron cuatro jonrones consecutivos en la parte baja de la novena entrada, la cuarta vez en la historia de las Grandes Ligas que se lograba esa hazaña.
El relevista de los Giants Philip Abner permitió las cinco carreras en la octava, que comenzó con los Dodgers arriba 3-2. Se convirtió en el segundo relevista en la historia de San Francisco en permitir cuatro jonrones en una misma entrada.
Los Giants (64-90) perdieron su juego número 90, su mayor cantidad desde 2017, cuando cayeron 98 veces.
El boricua Edwin Díaz ponchó a dos en una novena entrada sin carreras en su regreso desde la lista de lesionados.
Los Dodgers lo activaron desde la lista de lesionados de 15 días, donde había ingresado el 18 de agosto por una inflamación en el cuello. Fue su segunda vez en el año en la lista de lesionados, luego de una primera por problemas en el codo derecho.
El equipo no espera usar al relevista en situaciones de aprietos, pero con ventaja de seis carreras fue traído en la novena. De no haber sido por esa ventaja, admitió el dirigente Dave Roberts, no lo hubieran utilizado en la novena.
Provocó un elevado y ponchó a un bateador con un foul tip antes de permitir un sencillo con dos outs. Pero evitó cualquier daño, terminando el juego al hacer que Brett Harris hiciera swing a un slider difícil de batear. La recta de cuatro costuras de Díaz promedió 97.6 millas por hora (1.3 mph más que su promedio de la temporada), alcanzando un máximo de 98.7 millas.
“La recta tenía mucha vida”, dijo Roberts según publicó MLB.com. “Noventa y seis millas por hora es muy diferente a 99. Y parecía que su lanzamiento pasaba por el receptor, y la recta tenía esa potencia. Y luego el slider... una vez que tienes esa recta, el slider es bastante letal”.

Max Muncy y Kyle Tucker conectaron jonrones consecutivos en la octava. Betts y Max Muncy añadieron vuelacercas solitarios con dos outs en una entrada de cinco carreras, mientras los campeones del Oeste de la Liga Nacional se impusieron en el primer juego de una serie entre viejos rivales.
Tyler Glasnow (5-1) permitió dos carreras y tres imparables en seis entradas, con un máximo de temporada de 10 ponches.
La lluvia de jonrones ocurrió en el vigésimo aniversario del juego de cuatro-más-uno de los Dodgers. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin y Marlon Anderson conectaron cuatro jonrones consecutivos en la parte baja de la novena entrada, la cuarta vez en la historia de las Grandes Ligas que se lograba esa hazaña.
El relevista de los Giants Philip Abner permitió las cinco carreras en la octava, que comenzó con los Dodgers arriba 3-2. Se convirtió en el segundo relevista en la historia de San Francisco en permitir cuatro jonrones en una misma entrada.
Los Giants (64-90) perdieron su juego número 90, su mayor cantidad desde 2017, cuando cayeron 98 veces.
El boricua Edwin Díaz ponchó a dos en una novena entrada sin carreras en su regreso desde la lista de lesionados.
Los Dodgers lo activaron desde la lista de lesionados de 15 días, donde había ingresado el 18 de agosto por una inflamación en el cuello. Fue su segunda vez en el año en la lista de lesionados, luego de una primera por problemas en el codo derecho.
El equipo no espera usar al relevista en situaciones de aprietos, pero con ventaja de seis carreras fue traído en la novena. De no haber sido por esa ventaja, admitió el dirigente Dave Roberts, no lo hubieran utilizado en la novena.
Provocó un elevado y ponchó a un bateador con un foul tip antes de permitir un sencillo con dos outs. Pero evitó cualquier daño, terminando el juego al hacer que Brett Harris hiciera swing a un slider difícil de batear. La recta de cuatro costuras de Díaz promedió 97.6 millas por hora (1.3 mph más que su promedio de la temporada), alcanzando un máximo de 98.7 millas.
“La recta tenía mucha vida”, dijo Roberts según publicó MLB.com. “Noventa y seis millas por hora es muy diferente a 99. Y parecía que su lanzamiento pasaba por el receptor, y la recta tenía esa potencia. Y luego el slider... una vez que tienes esa recta, el slider es bastante letal”.

title: Blake Snell bromance may be enough to convince Tarik Skubal to reach to stay with Dodgers
author: Anthony Ranaudo
body:
Whether you believe Tarik Skubal actually has a chance to sign with the Los Angeles Dodgers long-term or not, the relationship blossoming between him and Blake Snell right now is giving fans something to enjoy heading into the postseason.
The two shared a moment in the clubhouse after Thursday's 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, a game that clinched Los Angeles' 13th NL West title in the last 14 seasons and its fifth in a row.
Skubal called it "the first of many," Snell fired back that it's special "because you're playing this postseason with your boy," and Skubal's response, calling Snell his best friend and "little brother," is exactly the kind of dugout chemistry that makes a fanbase fall in love with a roster before any playoff game is played.
Star power gelling like this isn't as easy as it looks from the outside. I've been in enough clubhouses to know that talent alone doesn't guarantee chemistry, and sometimes the best player in the world never quite finds his footing in a new room.
That clearly hasn't been the issue here. Skubal and Snell have started pulling actual pranks on each other, knocking over one another's chairs in the clubhouse, and have leaned into Step Brothers-inspired jokes about becoming new best friends on social media.
Pitching coach Mark Prior summed it up simply: "He's just chill. You can joke around with him. You can talk to him." Those are the intangibles that matter just as much as mound presence, stuff and command once October arrives.
Baseball already has some precedent for this kind of bond becoming part of a team's identity. Kris Bryant and Anthony Rizzo built exactly that in Chicago on their way to breaking a 108-year championship drought in 2016, and a decade later, people are still throwing them reunion podcasts built around that friendship.
Why Scott Boras could still complicate a Tarik Skubal-Blake Snell reunion with Dodgers
Now for the reality check. Scott Boras has made a career out of pushing his best clients toward the open market, with Snell happening to be one of those clients, on his own five-year, $182 million deal signed in 2024 that runs through 2029, with a conditional option for 2030.
If Skubal follows his buddy, annd signs anywhere from three to five years this winter, that puts the two of them together in that rotation for at least three seasons and potentially four, right in the prime of their careers.
However, a meaningful friendship doesn't change Boras's feelings nor his instincts. It's still going to take a team's best offer (plus some likey gaudy contract incentives) to ultimately entice him to sign. What should give Dodgers fans a glimmer of hope is simpler than any friendship storyline, though.
Skubal has been outstanding since the trade, going 3-2 with a 2.52 ERA across eight starts in Dodger blue, looking every bit like a two-time Cy Young winner who's found his rhythm in a new clubhouse. He looks like he's having fun out there, and that has a way of translating into winning, which is ultimately the only thing this fanbase really cares about.
The bromance is funny and keeps things light when the whole world is watching your every move. The Boras conundrum is still the reality. But if the two ever turn this relationship into a marriage, a long-term deal that keeps Skubal in a Dodgers uniform next to his little brother, that's the version of this story Los Angeles fans are actually hoping for.

title: Mookie Betts shares his hope for Dodgers mindset to finish the season
author: Blake Williams
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have been on a hot streak in September, and it starts with their offense getting back on track after an awful month of August.
Their lineup breaking out has coincided with Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts starting to produce at expected levels, and the return of Will Smith from the injured list. However, it has come without Shohei Ohtani as he’s currently on the 15-day injured list, and Freddie Freeman has been in a major slump due to right knee tendinitis.
Even without two of their biggest bats producing, the Dodgers have answered a lot of questions about their offense. They have taken better at-bats, they’re hitting the ball harder, and there is an increased focus and intensity with each pitch.
But with little left to play for after clinching the National League West and currently in a great spot to lock up the number two seed, that could lead to the Dodgers taking their foot off the gas in their final few games.
“We’re just playing good ball right now,” Betts said. “Just got to keep playing good ball and keep going through the end of the season. We don’t want any letups; we don’t want to try turning anything on once the postseason starts. We just want to play good ball and we want that to be our identity.”
The Dodgers are also starting to get healthy at the right time, which further boosts their confidence heading into October.
Andy Pages and Ohtani are both on the verge of returning, and Roki Sasaki should re-join the pitching staff soon as well. In addition, the Dodgers remain optimistic that Edgardo Henriquez will be back for the playoffs.
“It’s been good. We just have to keep playing,” Betts said. “Get guys to come back, like (Edwin) Díaz tonight. Get a couple more guys back and we should be ready to roll.”
What Mookie Betts thinks of Dodgers lineup
With nearly everyone in the lineup hitting well right now, Betts has seen both a positive and a negative effect from it. Betts described it as taking pressure off because you can trust the players behind you, but you’re also coming up to bat in RBI situations and big moments far more often because of the success of the hitters in front of you.
“It’s easier, but it’s also tough,” Betts began. “Because there’s constantly guys on base, so the constant need for that hit. But I think that’s the beauty in it. We just keep giving ourselves opportunities, and eventually something will crack like it did tonight.
“We just have to keep getting guys on base and giving ourselves a chance. The hits will fall.”

title: Dodgers esperan que Snell (ingle) haga una apertura más antes de la postemporada
author: Sarah Wexler
body:
Dodgers esperan que Snell (ingle) haga una apertura más antes de la postemporada
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- Dos días después de salir de su apertura tras apenas una entrada debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda, Blake Snell lanzó desde 90 pies de distancia en el terreno del Dodger Stadium antes del primer juego de la serie del viernes contra los Gigantes. Salió sintiéndose bien, y los Dodgers creen que evitaron lo peor con una lesión que ha sido un problema recurrente a lo largo de la carrera del zurdo.
"Feliz de que lo detectamos a tiempo", indicó el manager Dave Roberts, quien señaló que Snell no fue enviado a hacerse ninguna prueba de imagen.
Los Dodgers se mantienen optimistas de que el dos veces ganador del Premio Cy Young hará otra apertura en la temporada regular en algún momento durante sus nueve juegos restantes. El día específico está por verse -- su turno regular en la rotación caería durante la serie de tres choques de Los Ángeles ante San Diego que comienza el martes -- pero no se espera que lance con ninguna limitación.
"Creo que sería más una apertura normal", aseguró Roberts. "Tal vez no lo exijamos muchísimo, dado que no sabemos cómo se desarrollará la temporada. Pero esta será su última salida de la temporada regular, así que creo que sería más una apertura regular".
This browser does not support the video element.
Snell inició la campaña en la lista de lesionados de 15 días con fatiga en el hombro izquierdo, haciendo su debut de temporada apenas el 9 de mayo. Casi de inmediato volvió a la lista de lesionados debido a cuerpos libres en su codo izquierdo, los cuales fueron removidos mediante el procedimiento NanoNeedle Scope. Desde que regresó el 11 de agosto, Snell ha lucido como si no hubiera perdido el ritmo, registrando efectividad de 1.01 en siete aperturas, con 47 ponches y 14 bases por bolas en 35.2 entradas.
Para un lanzador que comparte la rotación con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tarik Skubal, Snell es una pieza absolutamente vital en los planes de los Dodgers para los playoffs. Si su condición empeora, la profundidad del pitcheo abridor de Los Ángeles de repente luce bastante mermada. Está Tyler Glasnow, quien abrió el viernes contra San Francisco pero que ha lidiado con sus propios problemas de lesiones este año. También se espera que Roki Sasaki (fuera desde el 27 de agosto por una ampolla en el dedo medio derecho) regrese pronto para una última apertura en la temporada regular.
Dada la historia de Snell de lanzar bien luego de largas ausencias de acción en Grandes Ligas, ¿han considerado los Dodgers permitirle saltarse su próxima apertura, que siga descansando y esperar a que vuelva a la loma una vez que comiencen los juegos de postemporada?
"Se ha pensado en eso", reveló Roberts. "Pero todavía estás hablando de unos posibles 17 días, algo así... es mucho tiempo para no estar en competencia. Donde normalmente, con su historial, todavía tienes rehabilitaciones y cosas por el estilo. Así que no es sólo cuestión de conectarlo y ya, que descanse dos semanas y lance en un juego de playoffs".

Dodgers esperan que Snell (ingle) haga una apertura más antes de la postemporada
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- Dos días después de salir de su apertura tras apenas una entrada debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda, Blake Snell lanzó desde 90 pies de distancia en el terreno del Dodger Stadium antes del primer juego de la serie del viernes contra los Gigantes. Salió sintiéndose bien, y los Dodgers creen que evitaron lo peor con una lesión que ha sido un problema recurrente a lo largo de la carrera del zurdo.
"Feliz de que lo detectamos a tiempo", indicó el manager Dave Roberts, quien señaló que Snell no fue enviado a hacerse ninguna prueba de imagen.
Los Dodgers se mantienen optimistas de que el dos veces ganador del Premio Cy Young hará otra apertura en la temporada regular en algún momento durante sus nueve juegos restantes. El día específico está por verse -- su turno regular en la rotación caería durante la serie de tres choques de Los Ángeles ante San Diego que comienza el martes -- pero no se espera que lance con ninguna limitación.
"Creo que sería más una apertura normal", aseguró Roberts. "Tal vez no lo exijamos muchísimo, dado que no sabemos cómo se desarrollará la temporada. Pero esta será su última salida de la temporada regular, así que creo que sería más una apertura regular".
This browser does not support the video element.
Snell inició la campaña en la lista de lesionados de 15 días con fatiga en el hombro izquierdo, haciendo su debut de temporada apenas el 9 de mayo. Casi de inmediato volvió a la lista de lesionados debido a cuerpos libres en su codo izquierdo, los cuales fueron removidos mediante el procedimiento NanoNeedle Scope. Desde que regresó el 11 de agosto, Snell ha lucido como si no hubiera perdido el ritmo, registrando efectividad de 1.01 en siete aperturas, con 47 ponches y 14 bases por bolas en 35.2 entradas.
Para un lanzador que comparte la rotación con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tarik Skubal, Snell es una pieza absolutamente vital en los planes de los Dodgers para los playoffs. Si su condición empeora, la profundidad del pitcheo abridor de Los Ángeles de repente luce bastante mermada. Está Tyler Glasnow, quien abrió el viernes contra San Francisco pero que ha lidiado con sus propios problemas de lesiones este año. También se espera que Roki Sasaki (fuera desde el 27 de agosto por una ampolla en el dedo medio derecho) regrese pronto para una última apertura en la temporada regular.
Dada la historia de Snell de lanzar bien luego de largas ausencias de acción en Grandes Ligas, ¿han considerado los Dodgers permitirle saltarse su próxima apertura, que siga descansando y esperar a que vuelva a la loma una vez que comiencen los juegos de postemporada?
"Se ha pensado en eso", reveló Roberts. "Pero todavía estás hablando de unos posibles 17 días, algo así... es mucho tiempo para no estar en competencia. Donde normalmente, con su historial, todavía tienes rehabilitaciones y cosas por el estilo. Así que no es sólo cuestión de conectarlo y ya, que descanse dos semanas y lance en un juego de playoffs".

title: Josue De Paula Is Giving Dodgers Another Corey Seager-Type Decision
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula has shown a plate approach and swing that have translated directly to the big leagues. He has cemented himself as a postseason-caliber player.
In his Dodger Stadium debut on September 19th against the San Francisco Giants, De Paula went 2-for-3 with a double, an RBI, and a walk.
It was electric, and hitting in the No. 9 spot, he got on base and scored twice.
Since getting called up, De Paula is hitting .238/.448/.476 in eight games, with eight walks and two strikeouts. His OPS is .924, and while the sample size is limited, the results grow more undeniable game after game.
His production isn’t coming from something high-variance like a high batting average on batted balls; rather, he is delivering through a calculated plate approach, taking walks and never pressing the issue through his 29 plate appearances.
The problem with adding De Paula to the playoff roster
De Paula is “potentially” an option for the postseason roster, according to manager Dave Roberts.
For him to play in October, the team has to jump through hoops. The Dodgers would need to file an exemption with the Commissioner’s Office to add him to the postseason roster.
De Paula was not on the 40-man roster by September 1st, making him technically ineligible unless the Dodgers get the exemption.
They would need a player on the injured list as the reason, making outfielder Andy Pages and catcher Dalton Rushing the two possible postseason casualties.
Given Pages’ status on the team, there is no chance he does not get the nod. Rushing, meanwhile, is trying to swing the bat despite elbow irritation, though he is still a ways from returning.
Something worth noting: Andrew Friedman has a history of letting a hot prospect ride in the postseason.
The Corey Seager Parallel
Seager, at 21, the same age as De Paula, got a call-up on September 3rd, 2015, and he was a sensation from the outset.
He played 27 games and was one of baseball’s best hitters for about a month. Seager slashed .337/.425/.561 with 14 walks, 19 strikeouts, four home runs, and 17 RBIs.
His play earned him a postseason roster spot, where he started. He struggled, hitting .188/.250/.485 with eight strikeouts and 1 walk.
That year, the Dodgers were bounced out by the New York Mets in a five-game thriller. Seager played in all five games.
While Seager struggled, there are reasons to believe that De Paula thrived. He has better discipline and chases less than the young shortstop.
Additionally, De Paula has much more talent and experience around him than Seager did.
With Shohei Ohtani returning, DePaula would be a pinch hitter who is tasked with getting on base. DePaula has success against both left- and right-handed pitching, so that he can be a versatile bat off the bench.
If he keeps performing as he has, Friedman will have another clear decision on his hands — give the young guy a chance to show what he can do.

title: Dodgers' Dave Roberts Sends Clear Challenge to Edwin Diaz
author: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts wants to see Edwin Diaz perform up to par.
Roberts spoke to the media on Thursday, a day before the Dodgers activated Diaz, and challenged him to prove he can be the closer they signed to a massive deal this past winter.
“I think, like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said of the team's bullpen. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also have to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Diaz was activated on Friday. In a corresponding move, the Dodgers optioned right-handed pitcher Landon Knack.
The All-Star closer has had a frustrating season. Entering Friday night, the right-hander had appeared in only 16 games this season, recording an abysmal 11.35 ERA, 2.56 WHIP and 19 strikeouts in 13.2 innings.
Los Angeles made Diaz the highest-paid closer by average annual salary, but the investment has yet to pay off.
The 32-year-old has blown four saves out of 11 opportunities, while batters were hitting a staggering .385 against him in Los Angeles heading into Friday night's game.
On Friday night, Diaz entered in the six-run game in the ninth inning, and had a scoreless inning with two strikeouts.
Injuries have certainly played a role in what has been a disappointing season for Diaz. He missed significant time following elbow surgery and has recently been sidelined by neck inflammation.
The combination of inconsistency on the mound, injuries and a lack of results has cast serious doubt over whether Diaz will even make the Dodgers' postseason roster.
Will Edwin Diaz Make the Dodgers’ Postseason Roster?
With a little over a week until the end of the regular season, Roberts and the Dodgers will have to make a tough decision.
Diaz looked good in his first outing, and he'll likely have three or four more to prove he deserves a spot on the postseson roster.
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said in regards to what he hopes to see from Diaz. “That’s probably it. As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it. Quality of strike-throwing, and get guys out.”
The Dodgers skipper said they will use Diaz in low-leverage situations to ramp him up, and he'll have to earn more high-profile assignments.
If Diaz can find his form over the next week or so, the Dodgers could be in a much better position to chase their third straight World Series title this October.

title: Dodgers figuring out how to score runs without Shohei Ohtani
author: Dylan Hernandez
body:
Super Mario ran into a mushroom. Popeye devoured a can of spinach.
The Dodgers are scoring runs in bunches again.
Say what you want to say about the quality of opposition or small sample size, but the numbers are the numbers.
Ninety-seven runs in their first 17 games of September.
Nineteen home runs in their last nine games, including five in their 8-2 win over the Giants on Friday night.
With a little more than a week remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are finally starting to resemble the team they were expected to be.
Even without Shohei Ohtani.
The Dodgers doing this with Ohtani on the 15-day injured list is the most promising aspect of their recent offensive resurgence.
Because they will likely have to do something like this to give themselves a chance to complete their three-peat.
Manager Dave Roberts reported Ohtani was “in a good spot” as a result of “a really productive last three to four to five days,” but the reality is that the Dodgers have no credibility on this subject whatsoever.
Remember when general manager Brandon Gomes said earlier this month that Ohtani might pitch again this season? Or when Gomes said “nothing has indicated” Ohtani would have to be placed on the IL the day after a game in which he was shaking his arm and looking as if he was hitting on one leg?
Knowing Ohtani, he will be in the Dodgers’ lineup when the playoffs start, but his presence will be more a reflection of his willpower than of his health. The Dodgers can’t count on him to produce, at least not with any consistency.
Which is why it was important that Mookie Betts homered twice on Friday night.
Or that Max Muncy, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith also went deep.
Or that Ohtani’s replacement at designated hitter, 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, scored the run that tied the game in the fifth inning and doubled in the go-ahead run in the sixth.
“It’s a high-floor talent level,” Roberts said. “I just like the way we’re taking better team at-bats and making up for not having Shohei in there.”
The Dodgers have scored an average of 5.71 runs per game this month, an improvement from their average of 4.89 through Aug. 31.
They are doing what Betts previously called on them to do, to build momentum in September that can be taken into October.
“We just gotta keep playing good ball and want to keep going through the end of the season,” Betts said. “We don’t want any letups. We don’t want to try and turn anything on once the postseason starts. We just want to play good ball, and we want that to be our identity.”

title: Dodgers’ Mookie Betts Makes Baseball History With Expanded Record
author: Billy Heyen
body:
Mookie Betts appears to be heating up at just the right time for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Dodgers, of course, are going for a three-peat. They've won back-to-back World Series championships. And they have the roster to do it again.
Betts hasn't always been at his best the past couple seasons, but he remains one of the most accomplished players of his generation, so it's never really a surprise when he does something special.
He did something special on Friday night. Betts, batting leadoff for the Dodgers, led off the game with a home run, but he wasn't done.
Later on, Betts left the yard for a second time:
In the process, Betts made some MLB history — really, extended his own history.
Mookie Betts Holds MLB Record
Betts actually already holds the record for most multi-homer games out of the leadoff spot, and now he has added one to that.
MLB's Sarah Langs shared the stat on X, with Betts atop the leaderboard at 27 leadoff games with multiple homers.
The likes of George Springer, Kyle Schwarber, Francisco Lindor, Ronald Acuna Jr. and Joc Pederson are all still active:
Most multi-HR games out of leadoff spot:
Mookie Betts: 27
 George Springer: 24
 Kyle Schwarber: 23
 Alfonso Soriano: 19
 Francisco Lindor: 16
 Ronald Acuña Jr.: 15
 Joc Pederson: 15 https://t.co/epsanHodqf
— Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) September 19, 2026
If Betts were to be worried about this record getting away from him, it'd probably be to Kyle Schwarber — if the Phillies keep leading their slugger off.
But regardless, for now, Betts has an incredible accomplishment.
Leadoff Hitter Power
The irony, of course, is that for so much of baseball history, the leadoff hitter wasn't about power at all.
Teams put their fastest contact hitter atop the order. They wanted him to get on base and create havoc.
Betts is fast, too, but he's part of a generation of speedsters who also have power — even though some of them, like Betts, aren't the biggest guys.
He first arrived with the Boston Red Sox and was a star very quickly, and then he was part of a shocking trade to the Dodgers, where he has continued to be one of the sport's best players.
Betts will turn 34 years old in October, when he'll expect the Dodgers to still be playing baseball.
And even as he has aged, Mookie has remained dangerous. When he steps into the box to lead off a game, he's capable of doing immense damage — and then you better watch out as the game goes on, too. Because if Betts gets one home run, he's got a pretty decent chance of finding his way to another one, too.

title: Shohei Ohtani IL Decision: Dodgers GM Explains
author: Los Royers
body:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers have not seen enough evidence to put Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, general manager Brandon Gomes said Thursday, adding that an extended absence had not been discussed as the club continued evaluating him day to day.
“Nothing has indicated that it should be an IL at this point,” Gomes said.
Gomes said the Dodgers would prefer to avoid losing the four-time MVP from the lineup for roughly 10 days. He also questioned whether a prescribed period of rest would necessarily resolve the physical issues Ohtani has been managing.
“It really hasn’t even, you know, been something that we discussed,” Gomes said of the longer absence.
Why Shohei Ohtani has not gone on the injured list
Asked whether a longer break could help, Gomes acknowledged that it might, but said the team could not be certain of a benefit or identify a set number of days that would solve the problem. His preference was to continue checking how Ohtani felt and consider individual days off as needed.
That explanation came amid visible signs of discomfort at the plate. Gomes acknowledged the arm shaking from the previous night as something the Dodgers needed to monitor closely. He did not announce a new diagnosis or say Ohtani’s symptoms had disappeared.
Gomes said he had not yet seen Ohtani that day at the time of his remarks. The next steps would depend on further conversations and how Ohtani responded physically.
Gomes stops short of tying the slump to physical issues
Gomes was pressed on whether Ohtani’s offensive struggles and lingering symptoms were connected. He said it was difficult to separate physical factors from the normal fluctuations of a baseball season and did not believe the Dodgers could definitively establish that connection.
He described Ohtani as a “victim of his own greatness,” suggesting that the expectations created by his usual production amplify the attention on a difficult stretch. Gomes said Ohtani continued following his routine and putting in the work.
Those comments offered a different emphasis from Dave Roberts’ assessment after Wednesday’s game. Roberts said he saw wincing, arm shaking and compensation in Ohtani’s swing, and subsequently said the symptoms had not been improving.
Roberts’ observations concerned what he was seeing physically. Gomes’ response concerned whether the club could conclusively attribute Ohtani’s offensive results to those issues. Neither assessment amounted to an announcement that Ohtani would go on the injured list.
Pitching innings remain valuable, but not at any cost
Gomes said the Dodgers were also continuing to weigh a possible pitching return against the need to protect Ohtani’s offensive contribution.
“Any Sho innings are really valuable,” Gomes said. “But if it comes at a cost, then you make that decision.”
He said the club still had time to see how Ohtani responded and threw before deciding whether continuing the pitching effort made sense. He did not announce a shutdown or a date for another pitching appearance.
Gomes also described Ohtani as willing to communicate with the organization. He said their interests were aligned around putting Ohtani, and in turn the team, in the best position to succeed.
For now, the Dodgers’ stated approach remained day-to-day evaluation, not a commitment to uninterrupted playing time or a scheduled extended break.

title: Secret to success? Josue De Paula raves about Dodgers teammates
author: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
body:
Josue De Paula has made his presence felt since being called up to the Los Angeles Dodgers roster on Sept. 11.
The 21-year-old plays an exciting brand of baseball and has shown a real command of the strike zone so far with eight walks in 29 plate appearances. De Paula has felt prepared to meet the challenge of playing in the Majors head on and credits his Dodgers teammates for creating an environment conducive to letting him play freely.
“Probably the biggest is takeaway is it’s basically the same game, just around different people,” he said on SportsNet LA. “But one thing I didn’t expect was this team to be so cool. Like, all the players, the way they accepted me, the way they greeted me, making me feel comfortable. It put me in a better position to be me.”
De Paula is the first position-player Dodgers prospect to be promoted directly from Double-A to the Majors during Andrew Friedman’s tenure as president of baseball operations. Most impressively, he has not looked overwhelmed at the plate despite the jump in competition.
The 21-year-old reached an important milestone last Sunday with the first two hits of his Major League career. The first was a three-run homer. It left De Paula’s bat with a 108.2 mph exit velocity and traveled 416 feet. De Paula flipped his bat in excitement and took a moment to admire the majestic blast.
The reaction from his teammates was an early indication of how open the clubhouse was to the young left-hander.
“It was sick to see all them react that way,” De Paula said. “They were all rooting for me, so they’ve been great and accepted me basically into the team. So it’s awesome.”
Aside from the display of power, De Paula’s plate vision has drawn comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto. His keen eye was on full display in Monday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds, complete with his own version of the “Soto shuffle.”
While De Paula still has work to do on defense, he has shown the potential to be a foundational building block in the outfield.
Josue De Paula impresses at Dodger Stadium
After beginning his MLB career on the road, De Paula received his first chance to play in front of hometown fans on Friday night and he did not disappoint. He delivered a go-ahead RBI double in the sixth inning and celebrated accordingly upon arriving at second base.
“It felt amazing. To do that for the team, to give us a lead, I’m just celebrating with the boys. I just want to see us win,” he said after the game.
De Paula also reiterated how much he’s been able to learn from teammates and attributed some of his success to the welcoming environment.

original_title: Secret to success? Josue De Paula raves about Dodgers teammates
original_body:
Josue De Paula has made his presence felt since being called up to the Los Angeles Dodgers roster on Sept. 11.
The 21-year-old plays an exciting brand of baseball and has shown a real command of the strike zone so far with eight walks in 29 plate appearances. De Paula has felt prepared to meet the challenge of playing in the Majors head on and credits his Dodgers teammates for creating an environment conducive to letting him play freely.
“Probably the biggest is takeaway is it’s basically the same game, just around different people,” he said on SportsNet LA. “But one thing I didn’t expect was this team to be so cool. Like, all the players, the way they accepted me, the way they greeted me, making me feel comfortable. It put me in a better position to be me.”
De Paula is the first position-player Dodgers prospect to be promoted directly from Double-A to the Majors during Andrew Friedman’s tenure as president of baseball operations. Most impressively, he has not looked overwhelmed at the plate despite the jump in competition.
The 21-year-old reached an important milestone last Sunday with the first two hits of his Major League career. The first was a three-run homer. It left De Paula’s bat with a 108.2 mph exit velocity and traveled 416 feet. De Paula flipped his bat in excitement and took a moment to admire the majestic blast.
The reaction from his teammates was an early indication of how open the clubhouse was to the young left-hander.
“It was sick to see all them react that way,” De Paula said. “They were all rooting for me, so they’ve been great and accepted me basically into the team. So it’s awesome.”
Aside from the display of power, De Paula’s plate vision has drawn comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto. His keen eye was on full display in Monday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds, complete with his own version of the “Soto shuffle.”
While De Paula still has work to do on defense, he has shown the potential to be a foundational building block in the outfield.

After beginning his MLB career on the road, De Paula received his first chance to play in front of hometown fans on Friday night and he did not disappoint. He delivered a go-ahead RBI double in the sixth inning and celebrated accordingly upon arriving at second base.
“It felt amazing. To do that for the team, to give us a lead, I’m just celebrating with the boys. I just want to see us win,” he said after the game.

title: Dodgers aplastan a Giants con cuatro jonrones en la octava
author: Luizangel Valdez
body:
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 8-2 a los Giants de San Francisco, impulsados por cinco jonrones y una gran actuación de Mookie Betts.
Los Dodgers comenzaron el encuentro con ventaja gracias a un jonrón solitario de Mookie Betts en la primera entrada.
San Francisco respondió en los siguientes episodios. Jung Hoo Lee conectó cuadrangular en la segunda entrada y posteriormente Jonah Cox produjo otra carrera con un sencillo, colocando a los Giants arriba 2-1.
Los locales lograron empatar en la quinta entrada mediante un sencillo productor de Teoscar Hernández. En el sexto episodio, un doblete de Josué De Paula permitió que Kyle Tucker anotara la carrera que puso nuevamente a Los Ángeles al frente.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tyler Glasnow, tuvo una actuación destacada al lanzar seis entradas, permitir tres imparables y dos carreras, además de registrar 10 ponches.
Dodgers explotan con cinco carreras en la octava entrada
El partido se definió en la octava entrada, cuando Los Ángeles fabricó un rally de cinco carreras.
Max Muncy abrió la ofensiva con un cuadrangular solitario y Kyle Tucker siguió con otro jonrón para ampliar la ventaja.
Posteriormente, Mookie Betts conectó su segundo cuadrangular de la noche, esta vez con un corredor en circulación, para colocar el marcador 7-2.
La fiesta ofensiva terminó con un jonrón solitario de Will Smith, que puso el 8-2 definitivo. Los Dodgers conectaron cuatro cuadrangulares en esa entrada.
Betts terminó como una de las figuras del encuentro al conectar dos jonrones y producir tres carreras. Por su parte, Glasnow consiguió la victoria y elevó su registro de la temporada a 5-1.
Con el triunfo, los Dodgers mejoraron su marca a 94-60 y se mantienen en el primer lugar del Oeste de la Liga Nacional, mientras que San Francisco quedó con registro de 64-90.

title: Dave Roberts Updates on Shohei Ohtani's Progress Toward Dodgers Return
author: Miracle Dimwesh
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting closer to having Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup.
Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani took a full round of batting practice from a coach during the Dodgers' series against the San Francisco Giants. The next major step will be facing live pitching as the team continues to monitor his recovery.
Ohtani has been sidelined since the Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list with right biceps inflammation and left knee swelling.
Dave Roberts said Shohei Ohtani continues to progress in the right direction taking BP from a coach in the cage today.
Live BP would be a greater sign he is close to returning. #Dodgers
The IL stint was backdated to Sept. 8, making Ohtani eligible to return on Sept. 23. For now, the Dodgers are keeping his work focused on hitting.
The team had already stopped his throwing program after an Aug. 28 bullpen session. Ohtani has since progressed through dry swings and tee work before taking batting practice from a coach.
A live batting-practice session will give the Dodgers another important checkpoint. It should also provide a better indication of whether his knee can handle the movement involved in hitting against actual pitching.
Ohtani has been one of Los Angeles' most productive hitters when healthy. He is batting .277 with 25 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 80 RBI and 89 runs in 130 games.
He also owns a .380 on-base percentage and .522 slugging percentage while going 11-for-14 on stolen-base attempts.
Ohtani's abbreviated pitching work has been just as impressive. He is 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 95 strikeouts and a .180 opponent batting average across 14 starts and 85.2 innings.
The Dodgers have already clinched the NL West, giving them some flexibility with Ohtani's return. The priority now is getting him enough hitting work without creating another setback.
Los Angeles entered Saturday at 94-60 with eight regular-season games remaining. Ohtani's progression will remain one of the team's biggest storylines as the Dodgers prepare for October.

title: Josué De Paula, tres canciones de entrada y un gran doble marcan su memorable debut en el Dodger Stadium
source: El Nacional — La voz de todos
author: Agencia AP
body:
Grandes Ligas
Josué De Paula, tres canciones de entrada y un gran doble marcan su memorable debut en el Dodger Stadium
En ocho partidos, el joven dominicano de 21 años suma cinco hits —el primero fue un jonrón de tres carreras contra Eury Pérez de los Marlins—, cinco carreras impulsadas y cuatro anotadas
LOS ÁNGELES.— Josué De Paula dio mucho de qué hablar durante su primera semana en las Grandes Ligas con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, y eso sin contar el uso de tres canciones de entrada en el mismo partido.
“Fue increíble”, dijo, mostrando una sonrisa deslumbrante.
En su debut en el Dodger Stadium el viernes por la noche, De Paula, que bateó en novena posición como bateador designado, conectó dos hits en tres turnos al bate, anotando dos carreras y produciendo una carrera impulsada. En la victoria por 8-2 sobre los Gigantes de San Francisco, el equipo contrario.
“Tengo muchísima confianza en mí mismo y en mis capacidades”, dijo, “así que sé que cuando llegue el momento, voy a estar a la altura”.
De Paula debutó en las Grandes Ligas el viernes pasado en Miami. En ocho partidos, el joven de 21 años suma cinco hits —el primero fue un jonrón de tres carreras contra Eury Pérez de los Marlins—, cinco carreras impulsadas y cuatro anotadas. Ha recibido ocho bases por bolas y se ha ponchado solo dos veces. Su promedio de bateo es de .238 con un OPS de .924.
“Sabíamos que al llegar a las Grandes Ligas no se iba a sentir abrumado”, dijo el mánager Dave Roberts.
De Paula fue convocado después de que Shohei Ohtani, cuatro veces MVP, entrara en la lista de lesionados y se está ganando un puesto en la plantilla para la postemporada.
“Necesitamos a alguien que salga del banquillo. Él está entre los candidatos”, dijo Roberts. “Sin duda, está haciendo muchas cosas bien”.
De Paula nació y creció en Brooklyn, pero se mudó a la República Dominicana, país natal de su padre, cuando la pandemia de COVID-19 paralizó los deportes en Nueva York, para poder jugar béisbol durante todo el año. Vivió con sus tíos y se matriculó en una academia de béisbol.
Obtuvo la ciudadanía dominicana, lo que le permitió firmar con los Dodgers como agente libre internacional en 2022. Fue ascendido rápidamente a la Clase A al año siguiente, a los 18 años. En 2024, fue ascendido a la Clase A Avanzada.
El año pasado, representó a los Dodgers en el Juego de las Futuras Estrellas , donde conectó un jonrón de tres carreras y obtuvo el premio al Jugador Más Valioso.
De Paula es el primer jugador en ser ascendido directamente desde Doble-A durante los 12 años de Andrew Friedman como presidente de operaciones de béisbol. También es el primer jugador en la historia de los Dodgers en usar el número 95.
Extraoficialmente, podría ser el primer jugador del equipo en usar tres canciones diferentes de entrada al bate en el mismo partido. Como un guiño a sus raíces en Brooklyn —también el distrito neoyorquino donde se originaron los Dodgers— salió al plato en la segunda entrada con la canción "Notorious" de The Notorious BIG, otro nativo de Brooklyn.
“No esperaba que los aficionados me apoyaran tanto, ¡fueron increíbles!”, dijo.
De Paula abrió la quinta entrada con la canción "Ima a Boss" del rapero Meek Mill, en homenaje a su padre, y rápidamente conectó un sencillo para su primer hit en casa. Recibió la pelota y planeaba regalarle el recuerdo a sus padres. Su tercera canción de entrada fue para su madre.
Su doblete con dos outs en la sexta entrada rompió el empate a 2.
“Me encantan sus turnos al bate”, dijo Roberts. “Aprovecha las bases por bolas. Cuando la pelota está en la zona de bateo, puede conectar un jonrón, pero también sabe cómo conseguir un sencillo. Ha sido muy profesional”.
De Paula incluso ganó su desafío utilizando el sistema automatizado de lanzamiento y strike durante un turno al bate.
“Siento la adrenalina, pero creo que sé cómo controlarla y enfocarla”, dijo. “Estoy totalmente concentrado, pero sé cómo tranquilizarme”.
De Paula demuestra un swing sólido y un buen instinto para seleccionar los lanzamientos. En defensa, sabe que necesita mejorar en los jardines.
“Muy pronto voy a callar a mucha gente que se está defendiendo”, dijo.
De Paula ya ha impresionado a su compañero de equipo en los Dodgers y ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana, Mookie Betts, quien dijo que era "realmente genial" ver a un jugador joven que puede enfrentarse a cualquier lanzador contrario.
“Le encanta jugar”, dijo Betts. “Cuando está en el campo, se concentra en silencio, pero fuera del campo le gusta bromear y reír. Es un buen chico”.

En su debut en el Dodger Stadium el viernes por la noche, De Paula, que bateó en novena posición como bateador designado, conectó dos hits en tres turnos al bate, anotando dos carreras y produciendo una carrera impulsada. En la victoria por 8-2 sobre los Gigantes de San Francisco, el equipo contrario.
“Tengo muchísima confianza en mí mismo y en mis capacidades”, dijo, “así que sé que cuando llegue el momento, voy a estar a la altura”.
De Paula debutó en las Grandes Ligas el viernes pasado en Miami. En ocho partidos, el joven de 21 años suma cinco hits —el primero fue un jonrón de tres carreras contra Eury Pérez de los Marlins—, cinco carreras impulsadas y cuatro anotadas. Ha recibido ocho bases por bolas y se ha ponchado solo dos veces. Su promedio de bateo es de .238 con un OPS de .924.
“Sabíamos que al llegar a las Grandes Ligas no se iba a sentir abrumado”, dijo el mánager Dave Roberts.
De Paula fue convocado después de que Shohei Ohtani, cuatro veces MVP, entrara en la lista de lesionados y se está ganando un puesto en la plantilla para la postemporada.
“Necesitamos a alguien que salga del banquillo. Él está entre los candidatos”, dijo Roberts. “Sin duda, está haciendo muchas cosas bien”.
De Paula nació y creció en Brooklyn, pero se mudó a la República Dominicana, país natal de su padre, cuando la pandemia de COVID-19 paralizó los deportes en Nueva York, para poder jugar béisbol durante todo el año. Vivió con sus tíos y se matriculó en una academia de béisbol.
Obtuvo la ciudadanía dominicana, lo que le permitió firmar con los Dodgers como agente libre internacional en 2022. Fue ascendido rápidamente a la Clase A al año siguiente, a los 18 años. En 2024, fue ascendido a la Clase A Avanzada.
El año pasado, representó a los Dodgers en el Juego de las Futuras Estrellas , donde conectó un jonrón de tres carreras y obtuvo el premio al Jugador Más Valioso.
De Paula es el primer jugador en ser ascendido directamente desde Doble-A durante los 12 años de Andrew Friedman como presidente de operaciones de béisbol. También es el primer jugador en la historia de los Dodgers en usar el número 95.
Extraoficialmente, podría ser el primer jugador del equipo en usar tres canciones diferentes de entrada al bate en el mismo partido. Como un guiño a sus raíces en Brooklyn —también el distrito neoyorquino donde se originaron los Dodgers— salió al plato en la segunda entrada con la canción "Notorious" de The Notorious BIG, otro nativo de Brooklyn.
“No esperaba que los aficionados me apoyaran tanto, ¡fueron increíbles!”, dijo.
De Paula abrió la quinta entrada con la canción "Ima a Boss" del rapero Meek Mill, en homenaje a su padre, y rápidamente conectó un sencillo para su primer hit en casa. Recibió la pelota y planeaba regalarle el recuerdo a sus padres. Su tercera canción de entrada fue para su madre.
Su doblete con dos outs en la sexta entrada rompió el empate a 2.
“Me encantan sus turnos al bate”, dijo Roberts. “Aprovecha las bases por bolas. Cuando la pelota está en la zona de bateo, puede conectar un jonrón, pero también sabe cómo conseguir un sencillo. Ha sido muy profesional”.
De Paula incluso ganó su desafío utilizando el sistema automatizado de lanzamiento y strike durante un turno al bate.
“Siento la adrenalina, pero creo que sé cómo controlarla y enfocarla”, dijo. “Estoy totalmente concentrado, pero sé cómo tranquilizarme”.
De Paula demuestra un swing sólido y un buen instinto para seleccionar los lanzamientos. En defensa, sabe que necesita mejorar en los jardines.
“Muy pronto voy a callar a mucha gente que se está defendiendo”, dijo.
De Paula ya ha impresionado a su compañero de equipo en los Dodgers y ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana, Mookie Betts, quien dijo que era "realmente genial" ver a un jugador joven que puede enfrentarse a cualquier lanzador contrario.
“Le encanta jugar”, dijo Betts. “Cuando está en el campo, se concentra en silencio, pero fuera del campo le gusta bromear y reír. Es un buen chico”.

title: Dalton Rushing's treatment, Dodgers optimistic with Pages, Snell & Ohtani
author: Matthew Moreno
body:
With just over one week left in the regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are still looking to secure the No. 2 seed in the National League postseason bracket and perhaps more importantly, get to a better state of health.
Edwin Díaz returned from the injured list on Friday, but the Dodgers are still waiting on the likes of Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani. Fortunately for L.A., there is optimism with that group, and Blake Snell as well after he came out his most recent start due to left groin tightness.
Dodgers updates
Blake Snell
Snell played catch from flat ground on Friday, getting out to 90 feet as signs point to avoiding the 15-day injured list.
“I’m very hopeful that he’ll make a start before the end of the season,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Snell has a history of missing roughly one month because of adductor/groin strains, but he and the team believe the latest issue did not advance to being that significant.
“Don’t know the answer exactly,” Roberts said when asked what may have caused the tightness, “but happy that we caught it early.”
If — or when — Snell does pitch again, Roberts indicated it would be a normal start rather than an abbreviated final tuneup before the postseason begins.
Andy Pages
After previously sharing the expectation is for Pages to return during the homestand, Roberts offered a slightly more concrete timeline by saying that should come during the Dodgers’ series against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing
According to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic, Rushing received a PRP injection in his right forearm.
Dalton Rushing got a PRP injection a week ago to address his flexor in his right arm. Still holding out hope he can be an option as a bat going forward — will hit off a machine in the coming days to test it out.
Surgery still doesn’t appear on the table yet.
— Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) September 18, 2026
Rushing had a brief return at the start of September after going on the 10-day injured list last month because of a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow. The Dodgers have suggested a best-case scenario is to have Rushing available as a pinch-hit option off the bench in the playoffs.
Shohei Ohtani
Ohtani took swings against a coach pitching in the batting cage and “came out of it well,” per Roberts. Although the superstar talent is making progress, Roberts said more clarity won’t come until Ohtani faces live pitching or hits off the Trajekt machine.
“But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days. He’s in a good spot,” Roberts added.
Roki Sasaki
Roberts further confirmed Sasaki is nearing a return and will start despite the prior plan being to shift him into a bullpen role. Some of the change is due to the uncertainty that arose from Snell’s groin trouble.
However, Sasaki still figures to be utilized as a reliever in the postseason if the Dodgers rotation remains healthy.

title: Edwin Diaz Gives Dodgers Something to Believe in After Rocky Rehab
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers got to see Edwin Diaz in action for the first time since a tumultuous stint in Triple-A, and his outing inspired confidence.
Diaz, who was activated on Friday, returned to the majors the same day, ending a month on the sidelines.
He didn’t warm up until the Dodgers lit up the San Francisco Giants for five runs in the eighth inning, creating an 8-2 gap and a low-leverage chance for the Puerto Rican.
Then, Diaz got up, and eventually, the trumpets sounded at the top of the ninth inning.
He came in and had a good outing, allowing just one hit, no walks, and two punchouts.
More importantly than anything, there were no hard-hit balls for Diaz, something that he has struggled with, while avoiding walks.
Diaz’s fastball was the star of the show. It improved compared to earlier in the season, with 1.3 mph more on the pitch and an extra inch of horizontal and vertical break, according to Baseball Savant.
Not only did the pitch move well, but he controlled it well too. Diaz’s slider delivered well in terms of results, getting a 50% chase rate.
The slider had less drop and horizontal break by an inch each, something to monitor going forward, but based on just the game, it was good enough to complement the fastball.
Why Edwin Diaz needed a good outing
Diaz had two different stints on the injured list, one for his elbow surgery and another for neck inflammation, and has been bad at pretty much every turn.
In the major leagues, Diaz was riding an 11.85 ERA through 13.2 innings with a 5.81 FIP, signaling consistent struggles, per Baseball-Reference.
During his latest minor league stint, things were ugly again. He pitched 4.1 innings in Triple-A and posted an 11.00 ERA.
Given how things looked all year for Diaz, with more bad outings than good, the fanbase feared giving him another chance, and even Dave Roberts, who seemingly loves Diaz based on their interactions, challenged Diaz to produce good outings.
After Friday’s return, Roberts was quite happy.
“I think getting strike one, I think the fastball had that life, 96 is a lot different than 99, and it just seemed like his delivery was through the catcher, and the slider, once you have that fastball, the slider is pretty lethal,” Roberts said.
“He’ll be available tomorrow and we are trying to get him four or five start or outings before the end of the season.”
During those next outings, Diaz’s slider and results will remain under a microscope.

title: Dodgers' Dalton Rushing Provides Injury Update Ahead of MLB Playoffs
author: Miracle Dimwesh
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still hoping Dalton Rushing can return as a hitter before the postseason despite his latest right arm issue.
Rushing received a platelet-rich plasma injection for a flexor problem in his right arm, according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya. The Dodgers are now preparing to test the rookie by having him hit off a pitching machine.
The evaluation will give Los Angeles a better idea of whether Rushing can contribute offensively when the playoffs begin.
Dalton Rushing got a PRP injection a week ago to address his flexor in his right arm. Still holding out hope he can be an option as a bat going forward — will hit off a machine in the coming days to test it out. 
Surgery still doesn’t appear on the table yet.
Rushing has already dealt with multiple setbacks in his right arm this season. He was diagnosed with a slight UCL tear in August, which ended his catching duties for the remainder of the season.
The Dodgers then used him primarily as a designated hitter before another setback while he was playing catch on Sept. 5. That issue involved his right elbow and flexor and eventually led to a stint on the 10-day injured list.
The PRP injection gives Rushing another path toward returning without undergoing immediate surgery. His defensive role behind the plate remains off the table, but a successful hitting test could allow him to contribute as a DH or pinch-hitter.
Rushing has provided meaningful offensive production during his rookie season. He has appeared in 78 games, batting .249 with 12 doubles, 12 home runs and 36 RBI in 221 at-bats.
The 25-year-old also owns a .332 on-base percentage and .466 slugging percentage for a .798 OPS.
The Dodgers have already secured the NL West, giving them some flexibility with Rushing's recovery. Rather than rushing him back, the club can evaluate his arm through controlled hitting work before making a decision.
For now, the pitching-machine session represents another step in Rushing's attempt to get back on the field. If he responds well, the Dodgers could have another left-handed offensive option available when October arrives.

title: Mookie Betts comanda con dos jonrones noche de cinco vuelacercas
author: Diego Torres Contreras
body:
Mookie Betts estuvo intratable con el madero para liderar la exhibición de poder de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, quienes se impusieron con un contundente 8-2 sobre los Gigantes de San Francisco. La ofensiva californiana se descargó con un total de cinco cuadrangulares en una velada especial para la franquicia.
El estelar bateador abrió la cuenta desde el primer episodio al conectar su bambinazo número 21 del año por el callejón del jardín izquierdo-central. Más adelante, en el octavo tramo, volvió a conectar un batazo de cuatro esquinas con un corredor a bordo para registrar su cuadrangular 22 de la temporada y redondear una noche importante a la ofensiva.
El despliegue de fuerza sirvió como conmemoración de los 20 años del emblemático juego del “4+1”, una de las remontadas más recordadas en la historia de la organización. Los bateadores de los Dodgers emularon aquel hecho desatando un vendaval de batazos para asegurar la victoria.
Leer también: Martín Pérez afina el brazo para cuarta postemporada
En lo individual, Betts terminó la jornada de 4-3 con dos cuadrangulares, tres carreras impulsadas y una base por bolas recibida, méritos suficientes para ser nombrado el Jugador del Partido. Desde la lomita, Tyler Glasnow se adjudicó el triunfo tras una buena labor, mientras que la derrota recayó en Jason Foley.
Con esta victoria de local, los Dodgers alcanzaron las 94 victorias en la campaña para mantenerse firmes en la cima de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional, poniéndose a tono cara a los playoffs.

title: Commentary: Dodgers have no choice. They must hope Tyler Glasnow can trust himself in the playoffs
author: Mirjam Swanson
body:
-    Click here to listen to this article
-   
- The oft-injured Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
- Glasnow fought through early struggles to throw six innings and strike out 10 in an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants, but can he replicate that in the playoffs?
- The veteran right-hander played a key role in the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series, and the team will need him to do the same this October.
The Dodgers are all in, going for a three-peat.
And they might not have an extra ace up their sleeve anymore, but when the postseason begins, they’ll still hope to play their quad of aces — four of a kind that will beat almost every other hand.
But do the Dodgers have four aces? Or three? Or just a pair, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal?
Could the left groin tightness that chased Blake Snell from his last start after an inning linger into the postseason? Snell isn’t the sturdiest of starters, having missed most of the season because of shoulder fatigue and loose bodies in his left elbow. But the Dodgers suggest he’s going to be OK; Snell is slated for one last regular-season start.
And what about Tyler Glasnow?
Tyler Glasnow gives up just three hits and strikes out 10, and Mookie Betts hits two home runs in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
Can the Dodgers trust the 6-foot-8 right-hander who missed three months because of back spasms?
Should they put their belief in the 11th-year pitcher who likely would be the odd man out in the postseason if Shohei Ohtani still were available to deal on the mound?
They’re going to have to trust Glasnow. And he’s going to have to trust himself.
“He’s a guy that you can’t put too much thought into him, or it starts getting in his own head,” said catcher Dalton Rushing, who is injured but enjoyed watching Glasnow find his footing in Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
“It was a lot of fun to watch tonight,” Rushing said. “Looked like himself.”
After three suboptimal innings, Glasnow settled down in a trust-building exercise of an outing against the Giants and their triple A-caliber lineup.
He wasn’t the most efficient, the most pristine, the sharpest — but he was fit to throw 98 pitches and six innings.
To fight through after laboring with 59 pitches in the first three innings, to earn his second win since April and to help the Dodgers maintain their four-game buffer over the Atlanta Braves as they play to secure a first-round bye with eight games left.
There was no champagne hangover for Glasnow on Friday — he flew directly back to L.A. from Miami, skipping Thursday’s clubhouse party in Cincinnati, where the Dodgers celebrated clinching the National League West Division for the 13th time in 14 years — but how about a toast to good health?
Cheers to giving up just two runs, one each in the second and third innings. To walking only two batters and striking out 10. To giving up only three hard hits and producing 15 whiffs.
To feeling and pitching better.
“After that third inning, I just stopped trying to be quick,” Glasnow said. “Just go out and be athletic, and I think it started to feel a little bit more timed up.”
Glasnow came into Friday’s game — one of his final two regular-season starts — having given up eight runs on 11 hits and seven walks in his previous two starts, looking less than comfortable in both. Out of rhythm, out of sync.
“This is an important start, and he knows it,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s certainly not do or die, but ... just to kind of get back feeling good.”
Afterward, Roberts wasn’t thrilled with how Glasnow started, but liked how he finished.
“You could see him fighting himself a little bit,” Roberts said. “The fastball command wasn’t great early. Got a lot of strikeouts. Curveball wasn’t sharp. But I thought he did a good job of making pitches when he needed to. The slider got better, fastball command got better as the game went on. Good to see him get through six innings.”
It’ll be better yet for the Dodgers’ odds if Glasnow can carry Friday’s progress into his next start — and then into the playoffs, where he proved himself as a Dodger last season after an elbow sprain sidelined him for the 2024 postseason.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
In the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series run, Glasnow made six appearances, three of them starts. He had a 1.69 ERA and averaged 10.5 strikeouts per nine innings. The stuff of aces.
“Today was a step in the right direction,” said Glasnow, the formerHart High School star, before leaving the clubhouse in flip-flops. “I’d rather kind of feel it, work through some stuff, and have a good one right before playoffs.
“I think I’m in a good spot right now.”

title: Column: Sandy Koufax dominated opponents during his time in the game
author: Lamar Garrard Special
body:
“Sandy would strike me out two or three times a game. I knew every pitch he was going to throw, and I still could not hit him.” — Willie Mays, Hall of Fame outfielder
Short versions of the meaning of the word dominator would be someone of importance who has authority or control, or who rules over a situation.
The list is long and too many to name, but the major league pitchers who were in complete control during a game would have to include the Dodgers’ crafty left-handed Hall of Famer, Sandy Koufax.
Koufax is the youngest man ever inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame, at the age of 36 in 1972. He was only the second Jewish player ever to be inducted.
Not the official list, but my first reaction would be to place Nolan Ryan and Randy Johnson right at the top, and Bob Gibson would be in my threesome. Can you imagine how hard it was to hit any of those three guys? Where would you place Tom Seaver, Steve Carlton and Don Sutton? Maybe put them in your lineup with Justin Verlander, Max Scherzer and Gaylord Perry. What about Walter Johnson, Clayton Kershaw, Cy Young, Jim Bunning and Greg Maddux? Can’t leave them off. There are others, and I am reminded of the World War II era patriots, Bob Feller and Warren Spahn.
The Dodgers franchise officials would have been smiling if they had known that on Dec. 30th, 1935, not far from Ebbets Field in Brooklyn, a future phenom pitcher was born. A Brooklyn native he was, and destiny saw to it that Mr. Koufax would become a name associated with Dodger successes, feted as one of the greatest pitchers of all time.
He was born with the name Sanford Braun, with the last name Koufax being added as he was named after his stepfather. Sandy is the name he used and is recorded in most written accounts of this great icon.
Sandy Koufax never played in the minor leagues, as he started with the Brooklyn Dodgers at age 19 in 1955. Fate was with him from the start, as this was the storybook team that beat the Yankees in the World Series. There were a few other names that never played in the lower leagues. Consider Mel Ott, Al Kaline, Ernie Banks, Catfish Hunter and Dick Groat. There are others.
Koufax teamed up with Don Drysdale, and they became an unbeatable team on and off the field. By that I mean working together on TV, doing commercials, special events and Dodger promotions, magazine and newspaper articles; they were household names. They even teamed up as a pair of holdouts one year to try to get the Dodgers to raise their salaries. My guess is that before the players’ union, they were very limited as to how much leverage they could muster against the dictatorial management of Major League Baseball.
Sandy attended Columbia University after high school and later the University of Cincinnati with the intention of becoming an architect. Ironically, his path led him to baseball, and now his choice to play “America’s Game’ was good for baseball and especially the fans. He started playing in local leagues around New York City. While in school playing basketball for the University of Cincinnati, he was recruited by the baseball team. Boy, if that baseball coach had only known how his choosing Sandy to play for him would affect Major League Baseball history.
Koufax only pitched 12 seasons in the big leagues, all with the Dodgers, and retired because of arm trouble. With sports medicine as it is today, he may have been able to pitch longer with modern arm treatments and protocols.
Starting in Brooklyn in 1955, he pitched through 1966, ending the majority of his years with the L.A. Dodgers. In 397 games, he posted a record of 165 wins and 87 losses, logging an amazing .655 winning percentage. He fanned 2,396 batters and only walked 817.
Sandy made the All-Star team seven times and was the National League MVP in 1963. He captured the Cy Young Award three times and was a two-time World Series MVP. He was on four World Championship Dodgers teams: 1955, ’59, ’63, and ’65. He was the National League strikeout leader four times. He had four no-hitters and one perfect game. On Sept. 9, 1965, at Dodger Stadium, he pitched a perfect game against the Chicago Cubs. Incidentally, the losing pitcher for the Cubs was Bob Hendley, a native of Macon, Ga., and a standout hurler for Lanier High School in Macon back in the 1950s.
Sandy Koufax’s jersey No. 32 is retired by the Dodgers. He is recognized as a member of Major League Baseball's All-Time Team, the All-Century Team, and, of course, the Hall of Fame. Sandy is soon to be 91 years old and is active as a supporter and a goodwill ambassador for the Dodgers and baseball in general. He was the best of the best.

title: 「肩が大木すぎ」大谷翔平じゃない…日本人の肉体に反響 ニヤリ笑顔「とってもハンサム」
author: Full-Count編集部
body:
「肩が大木すぎ」大谷翔平じゃない…日本人の肉体に反響 ニヤリ笑顔「とってもハンサム」
MLB公式Xの投稿が話題
MLB公式X（旧ツイッター）が18日（日本時間19日）、突如として日本人メジャーリーガーの写真を投稿した。タンクトップ越しに伝わる肉体と笑顔にファンから熱い視線が注がれている。
筋肉の絵文字とともに「豪快なアーチを叩き込む準備ができているなら、笑顔を見せてくれ」と綴ってMLB公式Xが写真を公開したのは、練習中と思われるホワイトソックス・村上宗隆内野手だ。タンクトップ姿でバットを持ってカメラに笑顔を向けている。
日本人選手で、頻繁に肉体が話題となるのはドジャース・大谷翔平投手だ。トレーニング風景なども関心の的で、鍛え抜かれた肉体には日本ファン以外も注目している。そしてメジャー1年目から本塁打を量産している村上も、パワーを生み出す筋肉にファンの目が奪われたようだ。
MLB公式Xの投稿には「パワー」「ハンサムだ」「とってもハンサム」「腕というか肩が大木過ぎるwww」「メジャー顔になってるよね」などと反響が広がった。
村上はこの日のタイガース戦では4打数無安打1四球に終わり、2戦連発とはならなかった。チームもまさかの逆転負けを喫し、地区首位から後退している。

title: Dodgers’ Tyler Glasnow quiets concerns in bounce-back start, after unusual travel plan helped him reset
author: Jack Harris
body:
A week ago, Tyler Glasnow was beginning to turn back into a question mark.
So, the Dodgers sent him home and hoped he would reset.
Last Saturday, the All-Star pitcher looked all out of sorts in a four-inning, four-run and frankly foreboding start during the team’s visit to Miami.
He was battling his mechanics. He was stretching out his long-bothersome back. And, most concerningly, he was losing the confident demeanor the Dodgers had seen when he first returned from his latest extended stint on the injured list last month.
Thus, instead of accompanying the team on the second leg of its road trip this week in Cincinnati, Glasnow traveled immediately back to Los Angeles the day after his clunker against the Marlins.
No extra flight. No added time on the road. Just a week where he could focus on his delivery and try to keep his season from once again slipping off track.
“He got back on Pacific Standard Time, in his own bed, one leg of travel versus the two,” manager Dave Roberts said Friday afternoon. “He threw his bullpen a few days ago. That went great. So he’s dialed in.”
In a six-inning, two-run, 10-strikeout start in Friday’s 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants, there was still more dialing in left for Glasnow to do.
He hung a curveball in the second inning that Jung Hoo Lee belted for a home run.
He lost his feel pitching from the stretch after a leadoff single in the third, giving up another run that briefly put the Dodgers behind before they stormed back with five home runs –– including four in the eighth inning alone –– from their recently resurgent offense.
The important thing, though, was that Glasnow felt better.
With his health. With his throw. With his ability to get completely synced up in time for the playoffs.
“I think I feel relatively consistent. It’s just a matter of, sometimes I’m not going to feel good, sometimes I will,” Glasnow said. “Today, I think it was a step in the right direction. I think it’s better than feeling really good for a long time before [the playoffs]. I’d rather kind of feel it, work through some stuff and have a good one right before playoffs. So I think I’m in a good spot right now.”
That might sound counter-intuitive for a pitcher who could be crucial to the Dodgers’ postseason plans. It might be rationalization from an 11-year veteran who has never made it through a full regular season healthy.
Then again, it’s a blueprint that worked well enough for Glasnow last year, when he only felt his mechanics click in the last few weeks before the start of the playoffs yet went on to post a 1.69 ERA in six October outings.
“It is just making sure he’s feeling good, he’s healthy, which he is,” Roberts said. “So now it’s just letting him go do what he does and bet on the talent to perform. That’s where I think we all feel good, especially Tyler right now, just knowing the health and where the head’s at, all that stuff. We’re in a good spot.”
Roberts struck a decidedly different tone after Glasnow’s start last week, saying then that the right-hander “didn’t feel great coming into the game as far as kind of overall body.”
That revelation raised alarm bells regarding the oft-injured 33-year-old –– who had already missed more than three months this season with a back spasms problem that lasted far longer than initially anticipated.
His absence in Cincinnati was also conspicuous, turning Friday’s outing into something of a late-season litmus test.
“This is an important start,” Roberts said beforehand. “He knows it.”
The manager’s evaluation afterward?
“I thought he did a good job of making pitches when he needed to,” Roberts said, encouraged by Glasnow’s ability to get swing-and-miss, as well as the way he retired 10 of his final 11 batters in a 98-pitch performance.
For his part, Glasnow downplayed whatever concerns had been lingering about his health of late.
He acknowledged he felt “not great” last week. He cited the cross-country flight as perhaps getting him out of whack. But he also noted that, “in the course of a season, you’re not always going to feel good.”
“It wasn’t anything crazy,” he added. “But I definitely feel better now than I did then.”
At this point, that will have to be enough for the Dodgers. Come the start of the postseason, they will be counting on him to be an effective member of their rotation.
“Right now, I feel pretty good,” Glasnow said. “We worked on some stuff after that last start. Just tried to keep for this start, take it in the next start. And then hopefully everything is feeling good for playoffs.”

title: Josue De Paula’s 3 walk-up songs and a big double mark his memorable Dodger Stadium debut
author: BETH HARRIS
body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Josue De Paula made plenty of noise during his first week in the major leagues with the Los Angeles Dodgers, and that's not even counting his use of three walk-up songs in the same game.
“It was awesome,” he said, flashing a dazzling smile.
Batting ninth as the designated hitter, De Paula went 2 for 3 with two runs and an RBI in his Dodger Stadium debut Friday night, an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
"I have the utmost confidence in myself and belief,” he said, “so I know when the moment is up for it, I know I’m going to come through.”
De Paula debuted in the major leagues last Friday at Miami. In eight games, the 21-year-old has five hits — his first being a three-run homer off Eury Pérez of the Marlins — five RBIs and four runs. He’s drawn eight walks and struck out just twice. He’s hitting .238 with an OPS of .924.
“We knew that coming up to the big leagues he wasn’t going to get overwhelmed,” manager Dave Roberts said.
De Paula got called up after four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani went on the injured list and is playing his way into a shot at making the postseason roster.
“We need to have somebody coming off the bench. He’s in the mix,” Roberts said. “He’s certainly doing a lot of things well.”
De Paula was born and raised in Brooklyn, but relocated to his father's native Dominican Republic when the COVID-19 pandemic shut down sports in New York so he could play baseball year-round. He lived with his uncles and enrolled in a baseball academy.
He gained Dominican citizenship, which allowed him to sign with the Dodgers as an international free agent in 2022. He was quickly promoted to Class A the following year at age 18. In 2024, he was promoted to High-A.
Last year, he represented the Dodgers in the All-Star Futures Game, hitting a three-run homer and earning MVP honors.
De Paula is the first player to be called up directly from Double-A during Andrew Friedman's 12-year tenure as president of baseball operations. He's also the first player in Dodgers history to wear No. 95.
Unofficially, he may be the first player on the team to use three different walk-up songs in the same game. In a nod to his Brooklyn roots — also the New York borough where the Dodgers originated — he came to the plate in the second inning to “Notorious” by The Notorious B.I.G., another Brooklyn native.
“I didn’t expect the fans to be so supportive and they were awesome,” he said.
De Paula led off the fifth to “Ima a Boss” by rapper Meek Mill in a nod to his father and promptly singled for his first hit at home. He got the ball and planned to give the keepsake to his parents. His third walk-up song was for his mother.
His two-out double in the sixth snapped a 2-all tie.
“I just love his at-bats,” Roberts said. “He takes his walks. When the ball’s in the hitting zone, he can slug you — but he also knows how to get a base hit. It’s been very professional.”
De Paula even won his challenge using the Automated Ball-Strike system during one at-bat.
“I feel the adrenaline, but I just feel like I know how to pinpoint it and focus it,” he said. “I’m so locked in, but I know how to calm myself down.”
De Paula displays a solid swing and an instinct for good pitch selection. Defensively, he knows he needs some work in the outfield.
“I’m going to shut a lot of people up on my defense very soon,” he said.
De Paula has already impressed Dodgers teammate and former AL MVP Mookie Betts, who called it “really neat” to see a young player who can handle any opposing pitcher.
“He loves playing the game,” Betts said. “When he gets on the field, it’s like a quiet focus, but when he’s off the field, he likes joking and laughing. He’s a good kid.”

“I just love his at-bats,” Roberts said. “He takes his walks. When the ball’s in the hitting zone, he can slug you — but he also knows how to get a base hit. It’s been very professional.”
De Paula even won his challenge using the Automated Ball-Strike system during one at-bat.
“I feel the adrenaline, but I just feel like I know how to pinpoint it and focus it,” he said. “I’m so locked in, but I know how to calm myself down.”
De Paula displays a solid swing and an instinct for good pitch selection. Defensively, he knows he needs some work in the outfield.
“I’m going to shut a lot of people up on my defense very soon,” he said.
De Paula has already impressed Dodgers teammate and former AL MVP Mookie Betts, who called it “really neat” to see a young player who can handle any opposing pitcher.
“He loves playing the game,” Betts said. “When he gets on the field, it’s like a quiet focus, but when he’s off the field, he likes joking and laughing. He’s a good kid.”
