title: Josue De Paula says he'll "shut a lot of people up" with his defense
author: Fredo Cervantes
body:
LOS ANGELES — There was no hangover at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium.
Not after clinching the National League West. Not with the champagne still fresh in the Dodgers’ minds. And certainly not with Josue De Paula getting his first real taste of the big stage in Chavez Ravine.
Instead, the Dodgers looked very much like a team preparing for October. And De Paula looked like a player who wants to be part of it.
The 21-year-old came through with the go-ahead RBI double in the sixth inning Friday night, turning a tie game into a Dodgers lead and helping spark what eventually became an 8-2 victory over the Giants.
“It felt amazing,” De Paula said. “To do that for the team, give us the lead. I’m just celebrating with the boys. I just want to see us win.”
That last part might have been the most telling.
De Paula isn't approaching his first week in the major leagues like a player trying to prove he belongs with a franchise full of veterans and established stars. At least publicly, he's approaching it like a kid soaking in every moment.
But his performance is making it increasingly difficult for the Dodgers to ignore what he might bring when the calendar flips to October.
Dave Roberts acknowledged as much after the game.
“He’s certainly doing a lot of things well,” Roberts said when asked about De Paula potentially being part of the Dodgers’ postseason roster mix.
For now, De Paula says he's trying not to look too far ahead.
“Yeah, it’s crossed my mind,” he said of making the postseason roster. “Like I said, I try to focus on the now, right here. I’m enjoying every moment with these veteran players.”
The now, on Friday, was pretty impressive.
De Paula came to the plate in the fifth inning with the Dodgers trailing 2-1 and opened the frame with a single, his first hit at Dodger Stadium.
Mookie Betts followed with a single of his own, and Teoscar Hernández brought De Paula home with an RBI single to tie the game.
One inning later, De Paula was back in the middle of it.
This time, he delivered the biggest swing of the night to that point, lining an RBI double to put the Dodgers ahead.
A player who had spent years dreaming about moments like this had just created one.
“It was awesome,” De Paula said of his first week in the majors. “Like I said, everybody, the manager, all the teammates have been amazing and accepting me.”
There is, however, one part of his game De Paula knows still needs work.
His defense. And he's not shying away from it.
“I know that's a big area and improvement for me,” De Paula said. “I know I got a lot of hate on it. So I'm that type: if I get hate on it, I'm gonna focus on it more. So I'm gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon.”
That confidence is unmistakable.
So is the willingness to accept criticism and use it as motivation.
The Dodgers don't need De Paula to become a finished product overnight. They need to determine whether his offensive impact, approach and overall upside give them enough reason to keep him around as they prepare for a postseason run.
And his teammates are already noticing what he does at the plate.
Betts, who knows something about making an impression in a Dodgers uniform, spoke highly of De Paula's at-bats.
“He's swinging at strikes, taking balls, impacting the ball,” Betts said. “There's no matchup that is really a bad matchup, which is really neat to see someone so young that can handle it…. He's been awesome.”
That might be the most encouraging part of De Paula's arrival.
The results are one thing. The at-bats are another.
He's not simply getting by on raw talent. He's showing an ability to recognize strikes, lay off pitches outside the zone and impact the baseball against major-league pitching.
And on a night when the Dodgers needed a spark, he provided it.
Of course, De Paula wasn't the only Dodger putting on a show.
Betts got the night started with a leadoff home run in the first inning, crushing the second pitch he saw from Giants left-hander Cesar Perdomo, a 93 mph fastball, into the left-field pavilion.
It was the 33rd leadoff home run of Betts' career.
Later, after the Giants briefly took control, Betts came back with another home run in the eighth inning, his second of the night and his 22nd of the season.
That's two more home runs than he hit last season, with eight games remaining.
Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker then went back-to-back, before Will Smith joined the party.
Four Dodgers, Muncy, Tucker, Betts and Smith, homered in the eighth inning.
What began as a competitive game suddenly became a rout. Muncy's home run gave him 29 for the season, while Tucker continued to show signs of heating up at precisely the time the Dodgers want their lineup clicking.
But none of that changes what made Friday night particularly interesting.
The Dodgers already know what Betts, Muncy, Tucker and Smith can do. They are still learning what De Paula can become.
And on his first night in the big-league spotlight at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium, he gave them another reason to keep watching.
Tyler Glasnow did his part, too.
After Betts gave the Dodgers an early 1-0 lead, Glasnow surrendered a solo home run to Jung Hoo Lee in the second inning before Jonah Cox's RBI single put San Francisco ahead in the third.
From there, Glasnow settled down.
He finished with six innings, allowing three hits and two runs while walking two and striking out 10 on 98 pitches, 63 of them for strikes.
The bullpen took it from there, while the Dodgers' offense eventually turned a close game into another comfortable victory.
They are now 94-60 on the season and remain two games behind Milwaukee for the top seed in the National League, while building a four-game cushion over Atlanta for third place.
The division has already been won. The real work is beginning now.
De Paula says he's focused on the present.
The Dodgers, meanwhile, have to be thinking about the future.
Because if Friday was any indication, Josue De Paula isn't simply here to experience the major leagues.
He's here to make it increasingly difficult to send him anywhere else.

title: 【MLB】山本由伸は“過小評価”されているのか？ 「向けられる注目度は十分ではない」米記者が指摘、その理由とは…… | SPREAD
author: SPREAD編集部
body:
シーズンを通して先発ローテーションを守り抜き、ドジャースのナ・リーグ地区優勝に貢献した山本由伸投手。鉄腕エースを巡り、米メディア『CLUTCH POINTS』は18日（日本時間19日）、「もっと注目されるべき」と訴えた。なぜ、過小評価されているのか。同メディアはその理由に言及した。
■「活躍が見過ごされている」
今季のドジャース先発投手陣は、ブレイク・スネル投手、タイラー・グラスノー投手が序盤から戦列を離れ、終盤を迎えて大谷翔平投手も負傷者リスト（IL）に入った。
エース格が不在となる中、ひとり先発ローテーションを守ったのが山本だった。今季27試合に先発登板し、14勝8敗。防御率2.51はメジャー全体5位、WHIP（1イニングあたりの被安打と与四球）は0.87で同2位、被打率.180は同3位につけている。
堂々たる成績だが、ナ・リーグのサイ・ヤング賞争いはジェイコブ・ミジオロウスキー投手（ブルワーズ）が先行。これにクリス・セール投手（ブレーブス）やクリストファー・サンチェス投手（フィリーズ）らの名前が続く。
この状況を歯がゆく感じているのが、『CLUTCH POINTS』のジョーイ・ミストレッタ記者。「ミジオロウスキーらの傑出したパフォーマンスにより、山本の活躍が見過ごされている」と指摘。その上で「過小評価されているとまでは言わないが、一番問題なのは（ロサンゼルスという）巨大市場を本拠地とするチームでプレーしているにもかかわらず、彼に向けられる注目が十分ではないということだ」と憤った。
■全体17位の奪三振数が影響か
同記者は注目度が高まらない理由について、「目を見張るような三振を奪っているわけではないからかもしれない」と推察。「山本はここまで178奪三振を記録しており、この時期としては立派な数字。しかし、リーグ全体では17位にとどまっている」と紹介した。
現在は最速104マイル（約167キロ）の剛速球を投げるミジオロウスキーが243奪三振でリーグトップに立ち、ブルージェイズのディラン・シース投手（236奪三振）、ガーディアンズのギャビン・ウィリアムズ投手（235奪三振）が全体の2、3位につけている。
同記者としては、山本が剛腕タイプではなく、制球力重視のスタイルであることが、成績に見合うだけの注目を得られない一因かもしれないと指摘した形だ。
また、同記者は「ドジャースには大谷をはじめ多くのスター選手が在籍しており、たとえ山本のような優秀な選手であっても見過ごされる傾向にある」とも主張した。
その上で、最後に「山本がサイ・ヤング賞を受賞することは難しいかもしれない。しかし、彼は現在受けている評価以上に注目されるべき存在であることは確かだ」と説いた。

この状況を歯がゆく感じているのが、『CLUTCH POINTS』のジョーイ・ミストレッタ記者。「ミジオロウスキーらの傑出したパフォーマンスにより、山本の活躍が見過ごされている」と指摘。その上で「過小評価されているとまでは言わないが、一番問題なのは（ロサンゼルスという）巨大市場を本拠地とするチームでプレーしているにもかかわらず、彼に向けられる注目が十分ではないということだ」と憤った。
■全体17位の奪三振数が影響か
同記者は注目度が高まらない理由について、「目を見張るような三振を奪っているわけではないからかもしれない」と推察。「山本はここまで178奪三振を記録しており、この時期としては立派な数字。しかし、リーグ全体では17位にとどまっている」と紹介した。
現在は最速104マイル（約167キロ）の剛速球を投げるミジオロウスキーが243奪三振でリーグトップに立ち、ブルージェイズのディラン・シース投手（236奪三振）、ガーディアンズのギャビン・ウィリアムズ投手（235奪三振）が全体の2、3位につけている。
同記者としては、山本が剛腕タイプではなく、制球力重視のスタイルであることが、成績に見合うだけの注目を得られない一因かもしれないと指摘した形だ。
また、同記者は「ドジャースには大谷をはじめ多くのスター選手が在籍しており、たとえ山本のような優秀な選手であっても見過ごされる傾向にある」とも主張した。
その上で、最後に「山本がサイ・ヤング賞を受賞することは難しいかもしれない。しかし、彼は現在受けている評価以上に注目されるべき存在であることは確かだ」と説いた。

title: Edwin Díaz makes successful return, rookie Josue De Paula strong for Dodgers in win
author: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY
body:
That's one way to start off the last homestand of the regular season.
Forget the fact that it was against the lowly San Francisco Giants and their lineup featuring a who's who of ... "Who?" Forget the fact that five of the Los Angeles Dodgers' runs in their dominant 8-2 win on Friday night came off the relatively unknown Philip Abner. The Dodgers' lineup, without Shohei Ohtani, showed exactly what they're capable of offensively.
This is the version of the team Andrew Friedman envisioned when he signed Kyle Tucker to a four-year, $240 million contract and Edwin Díaz to a three-year, $69 million deal last winter.
"The talent," manager Dave Roberts said. "It's a high-floor talent level. I just like the way we're taking better team at-bats and making up for not having Shohei in there. Obviously, we're a better team with him, but it is nice to see there hasn't been a drop-off with him not in the lineup."
Here's a look at three winners from the Dodgers' victory over the Giants:
The Dodgers lineup is just fine
Mookie Betts started things off when he jumped on a low-90s fastball that San Francisco starter Cesar Perdomo left middle-middle and sent it over the fence in left center field for his 33rd leadoff home run as a Dodger. The bats went quiet briefly from there until the bottom of the fifth when Teoscar Hernández singled home Josue De Paula from third on a sharp liner to right field to tie the game at 2-2.
The rookie De Paula later drove in the go-ahead run on an RBI double in the sixth before a monster five-run eighth inning in which Max Muncy, Tucker, Betts and Will Smith all went yard to put the game out of reach.
"I think that's the beauty in it," Betts said. "We just keep giving ourselves opportunities and eventually, something will crack. It did tonight, so we just have to keep getting guys on base and giving ourselves the chances and the hits will follow."
Edwin Díaz looked good in return from IL
That set the stage for the trumpets to once again blare over the Dodger Stadium loudspeakers. Roberts said he wouldn't have put Díaz in if it wasn't for the six-run lead as he wanted to give Díaz some leeway in his first outing back from an IL stint after health and poor performance have plagued his season.
But Díaz took the opportunity and ran with it. In his first big league appearance since Aug. 17, he got two quick outs before giving up a base hit up the middle. Rather than let that snowball like it has many times in 2026, however, Díaz was able to buckle down and strike out Brett Harris on three pitches to seal a Dodgers win.
"I liked everything," Roberts said. "I liked his intensity; I liked the fastball velocity. The slider was good. It was just really good to get him back in the mix and that's something to build on."
Josue De Paula is different
The through line for the offense on Friday night was the 21-year-old De Paula. The No. 6 prospect in baseball according to MLB Pipeline finished the night 2-for-3 with a walk, two runs and an RBI, but it was the timing of each of those that made his Dodger Stadium debut so special.
De Paula led off the bottom of the fifth with a base hit, which Betts followed up with one of his own before he eventually scored the tying run on Hernández's RBI single. Two innings later, De Paula scored Tucker from first on a double that he put on a rope at 107 mph deep into the right field gap. As he reached second, De Paula pounded his chest and flexed.
Then, in that huge eighth inning, it was De Paula who kept it alive by working a four-pitch walk with two outs, his seventh in a week in the big leagues. Five pitches later, Betts blew the game open with a two-run homer.
"I just love his at-bats," Roberts said. "It's one of those things that we knew coming up to the big leagues, he wasn't going to get overwhelmed, and it just helps when you control the strike zone. He takes his walks, when the ball is in the hitting zone, he can slug you but he also knows how to get a base hit. It's been very professional."

title: Dodgers' Tyler Glasnow: Strikes out 10 in win
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Glasnow (5-1) allowed two runs on three hits and two walks while striking out 10 over six innings to earn the win over the Giants on Friday.
Glasnow had given up eight runs over 10 innings in his first two starts of September, so this was a positive return to form. The right-hander also set a season high with the 10 strikeouts after racking up nine three times earlier in the campaign. He's at a 3.46 ERA, 0.96 WHIP and 87:23 K:BB across 67.2 innings through 12 starts this season. Glasnow's last regular-season outing is projected to be a road rematch versus the Giants, assuming the Dodgers can cobble together enough arms to stay with a six-man rotation to close out the regular season.

title: Mookie Betts pega 2 jonrones y Dodgers conectan 4 en la 8va en triunfo ante Gigantes
author: BETH HARRIS
body:
Mookie Betts pega 2 jonrones y Dodgers conectan 4 en la 8va en triunfo ante Gigantes
LOS ÁNGELES — Mookie Betts conectó dos jonrones y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles pegaron cuatro cuadrangulares en la octava entrada para imponerse 8-2 a los Gigantes de San Francisco la noche del viernes.
Max Muncy y Kyle Tucker conectaron jonrones consecutivos en la octava. Betts y Max Muncy añadieron vuelacercas solitarios con dos outs en una entrada de cinco carreras, mientras los campeones del Oeste de la Liga Nacional se impusieron en el primer juego de una serie entre viejos rivales.
Tyler Glasnow (5-1) permitió dos carreras y tres imparables en seis entradas, con un máximo de temporada de 10 ponches.
La lluvia de jonrones ocurrió en el 20mo aniversario del juego de cuatro-más-uno de los Dodgers. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin y Marlon Anderson conectaron cuatro jonrones consecutivos en la parte baja de la novena entrada, la cuarta vez en la historia de las Grandes Ligas que se lograba esa hazaña.
El relevista de los Gigantes Philip Abner permitió las cinco carreras en la octava, que comenzó con los Dodgers arriba 3-2. Se convirtió en el segundo relevista en la historia de San Francisco en permitir cuatro jonrones en una misma entrada.
Los Gigantes (64-90) perdieron su juego número 90, su mayor cantidad desde 2017, cuando cayeron 98 veces.
El boricua Edwin Díaz ponchó a dos en una novena entrada sin carreras en su regreso desde la lista de lesionados.
El abridor de los Gigantes Cesar Perdomo permitió dos carreras y seis hits en 4 2/3 entradas, con un ponche. Jason Foley (3-2) cargó con la derrota como relevista. ___

title: Mookie Betts homers twice and Dodgers hit 4 in 8th inning of 8-2 win over Giants
author: BETH HARRIS
body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Mookie Betts homered twice and the Los Angeles Dodgers went deep four times in the eighth inning of an 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker connected back-to-back in the eighth. Betts and Max Muncy added two-out solo shots in a five-run inning as the NL West champions rolled in a series opener between old rivals.
Tyler Glasnow (5-1) allowed two runs and three hits in six innings with a season-high 10 strikeouts.
The home run barrage occurred on the 20th anniversary of the Dodgers' four-plus-one game. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin and Marlon Anderson hit four consecutive homers in the bottom of the ninth inning — the fourth time in major league history the feat had been accomplished.
Giants reliever Philip Abner gave up all five runs in the eighth, which began with the Dodgers leading 3-2. He became the second reliever in Giants history to give up four homers in one inning.
The Giants (64-90) lost their 90th game, their most since 2017 when they dropped 98.
Muncy’s shot traveled 420 feet and Tucker’s went 403 feet, both to right-center. Betts also homered leading off the game.
Josue De Paula, a 21-year-old Dodgers rookie finishing his first week in the major leagues, lined a two-out double to right field for the go-ahead run in the sixth. He also singled and scored the tying run on Teoscar Hernández’s RBI single in the fifth.
Edwin Díaz struck out two in a scoreless ninth in his return from the injured list.
The Giants tied the game at 1 on Jung Hoo Lee's leadoff homer in the second and went ahead 2-1 on Jonah Cox's RBI single with two outs in the third.

title: Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
author: Kevin Baxter
body:
Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
-    Click here to listen to this article
-   
- Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
- The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs.
With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important boxes on their postseason to-do list.
They clinched a playoff berth for a record-tying 14th straight season and won the division title for the fifth time in a row. And with Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers (94-60) also have an outside shot at their fourth 100-win season in six years.
But that doesn’t mean they don’t have a lot of work to do between now and the start of the playoffs — the most important task being determining exactly where and when they’ll open the postseason.
With Friday’s win and the Milwaukee Brewers’ victory in Baltimore, the Dodgers trail the Brewers by two games in the race for the league’s best record and the home-field advantage in the postseason that goes with it. They also lead the Atlanta Braves by four games for the league’s second-best record, which would give them a first-round playoff bye and an extra five days to get their sizable contingent of walking wounded healthy.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
“To get one of these top two seeds is important. And our guys understand that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Winning the division is great, but I still think our best baseball is ahead of us.”
Achieving that, however, will require emptying an injury list that is almost as long as the team’s starting lineup. If the season ended today, the Dodgers would have at least seven players who wouldn’t be ready to play.
The Dodgers are also hopeful left-hander Blake Snell, who came out of Wednesday’s game after an inning with groin tightness, will be healthy enough to return for one more regular-season start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who shares the team lead in RBIs with Shohei Ohtani despite missing a month with a fracture in his left hand, is expected to be activated for the series against the San Diego Padres, which begins Tuesday, while backup catcher Dalton Rushing is swinging a bat and will hit against a pitching machine this weekend.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in a bullpen session Wednesday and could come off the IL next week but right-hander Edgardo Henriquez, second among Dodger relievers in innings and strikeouts, will miss the rest of the regular season with a back strain. He could join the team for the playoffs.
Then there’s Ohtani, the four-time MVP. He’s dealing with injuries to his left knee and right biceps. He has resumed taking batting practice and is eligible to come off the IL Wednesday. Roberts said he hopes to get Ohtani 10-12 at-bats before the playoffs.
“I’m just really waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field, let alone take live BP,” Roberts said. “He’s not there yet. But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
One player who did return was closer Edwin Díaz. Limited by multiple injuries to just 16 appearances this season, he was activated off the injured list Friday and threw 17 pitches in the ninth, giving up a single and striking out two batters.
For Roberts, the last month has looked like an episode of “The Pitt,” with medical crises piling up, one atop the other. Yet that’s hardly slowed the Dodgers, who opened their final homestand of the season having won 11 of their past 14 games.
Now the focus becomes continuing that momentum while getting as close to full strength as possible.
“They can go hand in hand,” Roberts said. “We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games, at the same time making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts.”
The Dodgers got a big lift Friday from rookie Josue De Paula, a player who didn’t figure in their postseason plans until a week ago, when he was called up to take Ohtani’s place. In his Dodger Stadium debut, De Paula singled and scored on a Teoscar Hernández single in the fifth, then roped a double to the wall in right-center an inning later, scoring Kyle Tucker to put the Dodgers ahead to stay.
Tucker, Max Muncy, Mookie Betts and Will Smith all homered in a five-run eighth inning, turning a nail-biter into a comfortable win.
Dodgers owner Mark Walter and multiple insurance companies he owns are being sued for allegedly failing to disclose an ongoing federal probe to customers.
That gave right-hander Tyler Glasnow (5-1) his second win since April 23. Glasnow gave up just three hits in six innings, striking out a season-high 10 batters.
Hernández, who had two hits, is batting .368 with 17 RBIs in September; Tucker, who also had two hits, is hitting .424 with five home runs and 13 runs scored in his past 10 games; while Betts, with two homers Friday, has six hits in his past eight at-bats, lifting his average to a season-high .254.
That’s helped make up for Freddie Freeman’s struggles. Freeman, who went hitless in four at-bats Friday, striking out twice, has just six hits — and 13 strikeouts — in his last 48 at-bats.
“We still have a lot of work to do,” Roberts said before the game.
They have just over a week left to get it done.

title: Dodgers Closer Edwin Diaz Returns After Missing Month With Neck Injury
body:
Dodgers Closer Edwin Diaz Returns After Missing Month With Neck Injury
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz came off the injured list Friday after missing a month with a neck injury.
The 32-year-old right-hander was available out of the bullpen for the series opener against San Francisco.
Díaz is 2-2 with an 11.85 ERA in 16 games with the Dodgers. He signed with the team as a free agent last offseason.
He made five rehab appearances during his second IL stint of the season. Díaz allowed six runs and had four strikeouts in 4 1/3 innings.
Right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a day after throwing four scoreless innings in a victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
Reporting by The Associated Press.

title: Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani making swing progress on IL
author: Janis Carr
body:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani casually strolled into the clubhouse on Friday, having received a positive report from his latest batting practice session that has progressed to taking pitches off coaches.
“He’s in a good spot,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said before Friday’s opener against the San Francisco Giants. “He hit today and came out of it well. I’m just waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field or take live BP or Trajekt.
“He’s not there yet, but from everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
Ohtani reunited with the team after their seven-game trip culminated with the Dodgers clinching the NL West title for the 13th time in 14 years with a win in Cincinnati on Thursday.
Ohtani, who went on the 15-day injured list just before the trip with right biceps and left knee issues, remained in Los Angeles to receive treatment. The four-time league MVP had been taking swings off a tee for several days before Friday.
He is eligible for activation as soon as Wednesday during the team’s final home series against the San Diego Padres, but when he rejoins the lineup will depend on his progress. Roberts is counting on Ohtani getting a few regular-season games before the postseason begins.
Before that happens, Roberts said he would like to see Ohtani take somewhere between 10 and 12 at-bats before putting him in the lineup.
“I think no matter what I say, it really doesn’t matter in the sense of it’s what he feels good with, what gets him ready,” Roberts said. “So, I could say 10, but it could be 12. But I think for me, if I’m just kind of spit balling and I think that 10 to 12 would be great.”
DIAZ IS ACTIVATED
Relief pitcher Edwin Diaz returned to the bullpen for Friday’s series opener. Roberts has said the 32-year-old right-hander will be used in low-leverage situations after missing a month because of neck inflammation.
Diaz has struggled with injuries (elbow surgery) and underperformance in his first season with the team, going 2-2 with an 11.85 ERA in 16 games with 19 strikeouts and 10 walks over 13⅔ innings. He made five rehab appearances with Triple-A Oklahoma City during his second IL stint of the season, allowing six runs with four strikeouts in 4⅓ innings.
Roberts said he just wants to see Diaz have success on the mound during the nine remaining regular-season games.

title: Edwin Díaz será operado y es baja de los Dodgers hasta más allá de mitad de la temporada - AGP Noticias
author: AGP Noticias
body:
Denver, Colorado.- El cerrador de los Dodgers, Edwin Díaz, será operado el miércoles en la Clínica Ortopédica Kerlan-Jobe para extraer fragmentos óseos de su codo, según anunció el club antes del partido del lunes contra los Rockies. Díaz, cuyo regreso se espera para la segunda mitad de la temporada, fue colocado en la lista de lesionados el lunes. Como medida complementaria, el club llamó al lanzador zurdo Jake Eder.
Díaz, de 32 años, permitió tres carreras sin conseguir ningún out el domingo contra los Rockies. En lo que va de temporada, tiene marca de 1-0 con una efectividad de 10.50 en siete juegos. El veterano de 10 años tiene una marca de 29-36 en su carrera con una efectividad de 2.91 en 527 juegos. El tres veces All-Star acumula 257 salvamentos en 300 oportunidades con 849 ponches.
“Hoy fue una evaluación difícil”, dijo Roberts después del partido contra Colorado . “Sé cómo debería verse, y cuando no se ve así, me preocupa un poco. Así que hablaré con él”.
La recta de cuatro costuras de Díaz ha promediado entre 97.2 y 99.1 mph en las últimas cuatro temporadas, pero en lo que va de esta temporada solo promedia 95.7 mph, y el domingo en Coors Field llegó a tan solo 92.8 mph. Solo ha lanzado seis rectas más lentas en toda su carrera.
Eder, de 27 años, fue adquirido de los Nationals el 1 de abril a cambio de dinero. Ha participado en tres juegos con el equipo de Triple-A Oklahoma City esta temporada, lanzando 5.1 entradas y permitiendo dos carreras. Lanzó para los Los Angeles Angels en 2025, haciendo ocho apariciones, con un récord de 0-1 y una efectividad de 4.91 en 18.1 entradas.
Hizo su debut en las Grandes Ligas el 17 de septiembre de 2024 como miembro de los Chicago White Sox, permitiendo una carrera en dos entradas. El exjugador de Vanderbilt Commodore fue seleccionado en la cuarta ronda del Draft de Jugadores de Primer Año de 2020 por los Miami Marlins y ha lanzado en 72 juegos de Ligas Menores, con un récord de 10-29, una efectividad de 5.35 y 356 ponches en 312.2 entradas.
Información: MLB.

title: El 'superéxito' Lee Jung-hoo finalmente alcanzó los 10 jonrones; y todo eso ante el lanzador estrella de los Dodgers, Glasnow. | STARNEWS
author: 박수진
body:
Este contenido ha sido traducido por IA.
Lee Jung-hoo, conocido como el 'nieto del viento' (28 años, San Francisco Giants), conectó un valioso jonrón número 10 de la temporada ante su rival de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional, los Los Angeles Dodgers. Fue un golpe decisivo que logró tumbar al ace especial de los Dodgers, Tyler Glasnow (33 años).
Lee Jung-hoo se presentó como el primer bateador en la parte baja de la segunda entrada, cuando su equipo iba perdiendo 0-1, en el encuentro disputado fuera de casa contra los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, celebrado el día 19 (hora coreana) en el Dodger Stadium de Los Ángeles, California, Estados Unidos.
En el montículo del pitcher se mantenía el abridor número uno de los Dodgers, Glasnow. Glasnow alternaba su potente lanzamiento de 96 millas por hora con una curva de nudillo afilada para presionar a Lee Jung-hoo en un conteo de bolas y strikes de 2-2.
Sin embargo, el solucionador fue Lee Jung-hoo. Al entrar en la quinta entrada, un curva de nudillo de 81,5 millas por hora (aproximadamente 131,2 km/h) que se dirigió al centro del plato fue golpeado sin vacilación. En el momento del impacto, la pelota cruzó rápidamente la valla derecha y se clavó directamente en las gradas de los espectadores del jardín derecho. Fue un jonrón solitario que igualó el marcador y sumió instantáneamente el Dodger Stadium en silencio.
Con esto, Lee Jung-hoo logró finalmente su décimo jonrón de la temporada en el escenario de las Grandes Ligas, alcanzando así la cota de dos dígitos. En un enfrentamiento directo contra su archienemigo, los Dodgers, conectó un jonrón perfecto contra el lanzador estrella rival, logrando un empate 1-1 con una acción altamente valiosa.

title: Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch
author: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY
body:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip.
They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed with just nine games to go before October.
But perhaps taking priority over chasing playoff positioning, Roberts expressed confidence that the Dodgers could finish the season relatively healthy with both Shohei Ohtani and Blake Snell progressing well in the final two weeks of the regular season.
"I think it's about winning games, all the while ... getting our players back to health. But I think they can go hand in hand," Roberts said. "We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games and at the same time, making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts."
Ohtani, who has been rehabbing at home while the Dodgers were on the road, swung a bat for the second time since landing on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 8. The two-way superstar took another step forward in his hitting progression as he took batting practice off of coach pitch and came away feeling good, per Roberts. While the Dodgers' skipper acknowledged "he's not there yet" as far as facing live pitching, that would be the next hurdle for Ohtani to clear before returning to the lineup.
In an ideal world, Roberts said he'd like for Ohtani to take somewhere around 10-12 at-bats in live batting practice before he gets activated, but acknowledged that it's really dependent on Ohtani himself.
"It's been a really productive three-to-four-to-five days. He's in a good spot," Roberts said. "No matter what I say, it really doesn't matter in the sense of it's what he feels good with, what gets him ready."
Snell, who exited his last start in Cincinnati after pitching just one inning with left groin tightness, continues to feel good and the overall sense is that he avoided a serious injury. Snell threw 90 feet on Friday while wearing a wrap around his left groin area, and Roberts is "very hopeful" that the former Cy Young winner can make one more regular season start.
Roberts is not sure when exactly that would be but did say that it would be a full start to ramp Snell up for the postseason rather than an abbreviated one.
"It'd be more of a normal start, maybe not pushing him a ton given we don't know how the season's going to play out," Roberts said. "But this will be his last regular season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start."
The Dodgers' depleted bullpen does get some reinforcements back with closer Edwin Díaz being activated from the IL. He's available to pitch on Friday night if needed, and Roberts didn't rule out using him in low leverage situations to try and get him into a rhythm ahead of October.
Roberts also said that he expects outfielder Andy Pages to be activated at some point in the final home series against the San Diego Padres and catcher Dalton Rushing has also been progressing well, though there's no timeline on his return just yet.

"We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games and at the same time, making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts."
Ohtani, who has been rehabbing at home while the Dodgers were on the road, swung a bat for the second time since landing on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 8. The two-way superstar took another step forward in his hitting progression as he took batting practice off of coach pitch and came away feeling good, per Roberts. While the Dodgers' skipper acknowledged "he's not there yet" as far as facing live pitching, that would be the next hurdle for Ohtani to clear before returning to the lineup.
In an ideal world, Roberts said he'd like for Ohtani to take somewhere around 10-12 at-bats in live batting practice before he gets activated, but acknowledged that it's really dependent on Ohtani himself.
"It's been a really productive three-to-four-to-five days. He's in a good spot," Roberts said. "No matter what I say, it really doesn't matter in the sense of it's what he feels good with, what gets him ready."
Snell, who exited his last start in Cincinnati after pitching just one inning with left groin tightness, continues to feel good and the overall sense is that he avoided a serious injury. Snell threw 90 feet on Friday while wearing a wrap around his left groin area, and Roberts is "very hopeful" that the former Cy Young winner can make one more regular season start.
Roberts is not sure when exactly that would be but did say that it would be a full start to ramp Snell up for the postseason rather than an abbreviated one.
"It'd be more of a normal start, maybe not pushing him a ton given we don't know how the season's going to play out," Roberts said. "But this will be his last regular season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start."
The Dodgers' depleted bullpen does get some reinforcements back with closer Edwin Díaz being activated from the IL. He's available to pitch on Friday night if needed, and Roberts didn't rule out using him in low leverage situations to try and get him into a rhythm ahead of October.
Roberts also said that he expects outfielder Andy Pages to be activated at some point in the final home series against the San Diego Padres and catcher Dalton Rushing has also been progressing well, though there's no timeline on his return just yet.

title: Snell (groin) expected to start again for Dodgers before postseason
author: Sarah Wexler
body:
LOS ANGELES -- Two days after he exited a start following just one inning due to left groin tightness, Blake Snell threw from 90 feet on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants. He emerged feeling good, with the Dodgers believing they avoided the worst with an injury that’s been a recurring issue throughout the left-hander’s career.
“Happy that we caught it early,” said manager Dave Roberts, who noted that Snell was not sent to receive any imaging.
The Dodgers remain optimistic that the two-time Cy Young Award winner will make another regular-season start sometime during their remaining nine games. The specific day is to be determined -- his regular spot in the rotation would come up during L.A.’s three-game series vs. San Diego that begins on Tuesday -- but he is not expected to pitch with any limitations.
“I think it'd be more of a normal start,” said Roberts. “Maybe not pushing him a ton, given that we don't know how the season's going to play out. But this will be his last regular-season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start.”
Snell began the season on the 15-day injured list with left shoulder fatigue, not making his season debut until May 9. He almost immediately went back on the IL due to loose bodies in his left elbow, which were removed using the NanoNeedle Scope procedure. Since returning on Aug. 11, Snell has looked like he hasn’t missed a beat, pitching to a 1.01 ERA over seven starts, with 47 strikeouts and 14 walks in 35 2/3 innings.
For a pitcher who shares a rotation with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal, Snell is an absolutely vital part of the Dodgers’ postseason rotation plans. Should his condition worsen, the Dodgers’ starting pitching depth suddenly looks pretty thin. There’s Tyler Glasnow, who started on Friday against San Francisco but has dealt with injury issues of his own this year. Roki Sasaki (out since Aug. 27 with a right middle finger blister) is also expected to return soon for one final regular-season start.
Given Snell’s history of pitching well following long layoffs from Major League action, have the Dodgers given any consideration to letting him skip his next start, continuing to rest and waiting to have him pitch again once postseason games get underway?
“There is a thought,” said Roberts. “But you're still talking about a potential 17 days, something like that -- that's a long time to not be in competition. Where typically, with his history, you still have rehabs and things like that. So it's just not kind of a plug-and-play, sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game.”

title: Ohtani sigue dando pasos para regresar antes del final de la temporada regular
author: Sarah Wexler
body:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Mientras Shohei Ohtani avanza en su recuperación de lesiones en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho, los Dodgers reafirmaron que sigue encaminado a regresar antes de que termine la temporada regular. El viernes dio el siguiente paso hacia ese objetivo, cuando tomó práctica de bateo ante lanzamientos de un coach.
“Salió bien de la sesión”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Creo que, por mi parte, simplemente estoy esperando saber cuándo va a salir al terreno, ni hablar de tomar práctica de bateo en vivo o enfrentar a Trajekt. Y todavía no ha llegado a ese punto. Pero por todo lo que he escuchado, han sido tres, cuatro o cinco días realmente productivos. Está en un buen momento”.
Ohtani está aumentando su carga de trabajo exclusivamente como bateador, ya que no se espera que vuelva a lanzar esta temporada, luego de su última presentación en la lomita el 3 de julio. Su estadía en la lista de lesionados de 15 días es retroactiva al 8 de septiembre, por lo que podría ser activado, como muy pronto, el miércoles. Eso le daría un máximo de cinco juegos para recuperar el ritmo ante pitcheo de Grandes Ligas antes del inicio de la postemporada.
A los Dodgers les ha ido bastante bien sin Ohtani, con marca de 6-3 y 48 carreras anotadas, para un promedio de 5.3 por juego, aunque todos esos encuentros fueron contra equipos fuera de la contienda. Por supuesto, su alineación está en su mejor versión con el cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso como primer bate... siempre y cuando esté saludable.
Durante buena parte de la temporada, Ohtani volvió a registrar números dignos del JMV, incluso mientras lidiaba con una serie de lesiones. Bateó .296 con 26 jonrones y OPS de .952 en sus primeros 110 juegos. Pero en los siguientes 24 encuentros antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados, bateó .198 (de 96-19), con OPS de .690 y 34 ponches, un tramo que coincidió con un intento de aumentar progresivamente su carga de trabajo como lanzador.
Finalmente, los Dodgers decidieron que su estrella de dos vías no sólo necesitaba concentrarse exclusivamente en batear, sino que lo mejor para todos los involucrados era que Ohtani se tomara un tiempo para permitir que su cuerpo descansara y se recuperara, en lugar de intentar seguir jugando pese a las molestias.
Como Ohtani permaneció en Los Ángeles trabajando en su recuperación durante la gira más reciente de los Dodgers, no pudo celebrar con sus compañeros el jueves después de que aseguraran su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas. Eso significa que tendrá que esperar hasta que el equipo asegure otro objetivo para poder descorchar la champaña.
“Ya hicimos eso, así que vamos a ganar hoy y volveremos a brindar con ellos más adelante”, dijo Roberts. “Pero no, no voy a hacer un brindis especial, porque también hay muchos otros jugadores que fueron parte de esto”.

title: Ohtani continues hitting progression as regular-season return remains in play
author: Sarah Wexler
body:
LOS ANGELES -- As Shohei Ohtani works his way back from left knee and right biceps injuries, the Dodgers affirmed that he remains on pace to return before the regular season ends. His next step toward that goal came on Friday, when Ohtani hit coach-pitch batting practice.
“He came out of it well,” said manager Dave Roberts. “I think for me, I'm just really waiting to hear when he's going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt. And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it's been a really productive last three to four to five days. He's in a good spot.”
Ohtani is building up exclusively as a hitter, as he is not expected to pitch again this season, having last appeared on the mound on July 3. His 15-day injured list stint is backdated to Sept. 8, so the earliest he can be activated is Wednesday -- giving him, at most, five games to find his footing against Major League pitching before the postseason gets underway.
The Dodgers have fared well enough with Ohtani out, going 6-3 while scoring 48 runs, good for 5.3 runs per game (albeit exclusively against non-contending teams). Of course, their lineup is at its best with the four-time MVP hitting leadoff … provided that he’s healthy.
For most of the season, Ohtani was once again putting up MVP-caliber numbers, even as he battled a spate of injuries, batting .296 with 26 homers and a .952 OPS through his first 110 games. But over the next 24 games ahead of landing on the IL, he hit .198 (19-for-96) with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts, a stretch coinciding with an attempted pitching ramp-up.
Ultimately, the Dodgers decided that their two-way star needed not only to focus exclusively on hitting, but that the best thing for everyone involved was Ohtani taking some time to let his body rest and recover rather than trying to continue to play through it.
Since Ohtani remained in L.A. to work on his recovery during the Dodgers’ most recent road trip, he missed out on celebrating with his teammates on Thursday after they clinched their 13th NL West title in the past 14 seasons. That means he’ll have to wait for another clinch in order to pop some champagne.
“We already did that, so we're gonna win today, and we'll re-toast with them going forward,” said Roberts. “But no, I'm not going to do a special toast, because there's a lot of other players that were part of this, too.”

title: Grand slam de Kyle Tucker ayuda a Dodgers a vencer a Marlins por 6-2 para 8ª victoria seguida
author: Por ALANIS THAMES
body:
MARLINS (AP) — Kyle Tucker conectó el sexto grand slam de su carrera y se quedó a un doble de completar el ciclo por los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, quienes vencieron el viernes 6-2 a los Marlins de Miami para ampliar a ocho triunfos su mejor racha de la temporada.
Tucker conectó un sweeper en cuenta de 1-1 del relevista Cade Gibson para poner la pizarra 6-1 en el séptimo inning. Pegó un sencillo en el primero y un triple en el sexto.
Max Muncy totalizó tres hits y una base por bolas, y Will Smith añadió un sencillo impulsor de carrera por los Dodgers, líderes de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Blake Snell (4-1) permitió una carrera y ponchó a ocho durante cinco innings y dos tercios, en los que toleró cuatro inatrapables.
Después de que los Dodgers tomaron una ventaja de 2-0 con el sencillo impulsor de Smith, el dominicano Agustín Ramírez conectó un doble impulsor que recortó la diferencia a 2-1. Victor Vodnik abrió el séptimo retirando rápidamente a Alex Freeland y al boricua Kiké Hernández, pero dio bases por bolas a Tommy Edman y Mookie Betts y permitió un sencillo de Muncy para llenar las bases, preparando el batazo de Tucker entre el jardín derecho y el central ante Gibson.
El dominicano Otto López conectó cuatro hits y el venezolano Javier Sanoja conectó un triple y un sencillo por los Marlins, que han perdido siete de ocho y cuatro seguidos. El abridor Ryan Gusto (1-5) permitió dos carreras con cinco hits.
El derecho otorgó tres bases por bolas y ponchó a tres.

title: Dodgers hopeful to avoid worst-case scenario with injured star pitcher
author: Jack Harris
body:
So far, so good in Blake Snell's bid to make another start before the end of the regular season.
Despite leaving his last outing on Wednesday in Cincinnati after just one inning due to tightness in his left groin, Snell arrived at Dodger Stadium on Friday already feeling better, saying his groin was back up to an "8 out of 10" before heading out for a session of flat-ground catch play in the outfield.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts also offered an optimistic outlook on Snell's status, saying he was "very hopeful" in the left-hander's chances to get back on the mound before the beginning of the playoffs.
"Happy that we caught it early," Roberts said of Snell's injury.
Indeed, when Snell exited Wednesday's game after 19 pitches, it raised immediate concerns about the state of the Dodgers' rotation.
Given the injuries the team is dealing with in its bullpen and its offense's inconsistent form through the second half of the season, the Dodgers will almost certainly need to lean on their starters during the playoffs — similar to the way they did last year, when a rotation of Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tyler Glasnow and Shohei Ohtani (who will effectively be replaced by Tarik Skubal this year) carried the pitching staff to a second consecutive World Series title.
Losing Snell — who was already sidelined for three months earlier this season following an elbow procedure and has a history of left groin injuries throughout his career — would have dealt a massive blow to those plans.
However, the Dodgers are at least initially optimistic they've avoided anything close to a worst-case scenario.
While Roberts acknowledged that there is still "a little bit of uncertainty" regarding Snell, and no exact date for when he might pitch again, the skipper also noted that the two-time Cy Young Award winner didn't require medical imaging; another sign of the team's confidence that his injury was not more severe.
It's possible that, even if Snell continues to feel better, the Dodgers could elect to rest him for the remainder of the regular season to ensure he doesn't suffer any further setbacks before the playoffs.
But, they are also wary of giving Snell too long of a layoff entering the postseason.
"It's not just kind of plug-and-play," Roberts said, "[to] sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game."
Thus, the team will continue to monitor Snell's progress in the coming days, hopeful that a potential pitching crisis has been averted.
"We feel confident," Roberts said.

title: Edwin Díaz regresa al bullpen de los Dodgers tras un mes de baja por lesión en el cuello
author: El Nuevo Diario
body:
RESUMEN
EL NUEVO DIARIO, LOS ÁNGELES.- El cerrador de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Edwin Díaz, salió el viernes de la lista de lesionados tras perderse un mes de actividad debido a una lesión en el cuello, según un reporte de MLB.com.
El lanzador derecho de 32 años estuvo disponible en el bullpen para el inicio de la serie contra San Francisco.
Díaz registra una marca de 2-2 y una efectividad de 11.85 en 16 partidos con los Dodgers. Firmó con el equipo como agente libre durante la pasada temporada baja.
Realizó cinco apariciones de rehabilitación durante su segunda estancia en la lista de lesionados esta temporada. Díaz permitió seis carreras y logró cuatro ponches en 4 entradas y un tercio.
El lanzador derecho Landon Knack fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City, un día después de lanzar cuatro entradas en blanco en una victoria sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati.

title: Díaz podría lanzar entradas de baja presión mientras lucha por un puesto en playoffs
author: Sarah Wexler
body:
Díaz podría lanzar entradas de baja presión mientras lucha por un puesto en playoffs
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES - Los Dodgers firmaron al puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz la temporada baja pasada con la firme intención de que fuera su cerrador para el 2026 y más allá. Ahora que regresa tras su segunda estancia en la lista de lesionados esta temporada, se ve obligado a luchar por un puesto en el bullpen de L.A. para la postemporada.
Antes del inicio de la serie del viernes contra los Gigantes en el Dodger Stadium, los Dodgers activaron a Díaz de la lista de lesionados de 15 días, a la que había ingresado el 18 de agosto debido a una inflamación en el cuello. Como movimiento correspondiente, el lanzador derecho Landon Knack fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Ha sido un año turbulento para Díaz, quien el 12 de diciembre firmó un contrato de tres años y $US69 millones con los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial. Huelga decir que las cosas no han salido según lo previsto para el tres veces seleccionado al Juego de Estrellas. En sus primeras siete presentaciones, permitió siete carreras limpias en seis entradas, con 10 ponches y cinco bases por bolas; posteriormente, ingresó a la lista de lesionados debido a cuerpos libres en el codo derecho que requirieron cirugía.
Tras su regreso el 29 de julio, Díaz retomó el rol de cerrador, aunque esta vez registró tres oportunidades de salvamento desperdiciadas en nueve partidos y acumuló una efectividad de 12.91, con nueve ponches, cinco bases por bolas y dos bateadores golpeados en 7 entradas y 2/3 de labor.
La asignación de rehabilitación más reciente de Díaz no generó mucha confianza. Aunque los resultados eran menos importantes que sus sensaciones físicas, tuvo problemas de control: otorgó siete bases por bolas y golpeó a un bateador en cuatro entradas y 1/3 repartidas en cinco salidas con Oklahoma City, logrando además muy pocos swings fallidos.
Entonces, ¿qué debe hacer Díaz para demostrar que merece formar parte de los planes de L.A. para la postemporada?
"Creo que simplemente lanzar bien", dijo el manager Dave Roberts. "Para mí, el rol no importa. Creo que solo queremos verlo lanzar como él es capaz de hacerlo. Y estamos hablando de nueve partidos [restantes en la temporada regular], así que hablamos de tres o cuatro salidas para evaluar, y eso debería ser suficiente".
En este momento, ese rol no será el de "cerrador". Cabe esperar que Díaz sea utilizado en situaciones de menor presión. Tras asegurar su 13er título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas —y mientras luchan por obtener el pase directo a la segunda ronda de los playoffs—, los Dodgers tienen el lujo de aprovechar el resto del calendario de la temporada regular para que varios jugadores se ganen, en la práctica, un puesto en el roster de octubre.
Díaz podría ser la figura más destacada de ese grupo. Este tres veces ganador del premio al Relevista del Año podría convertirse en un factor clave en el bullpen de Los Ángeles en su búsqueda de un tercer título consecutivo, siempre y cuando demuestre ser una opción viable.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Reveal Potential Andy Pages Return Date Before Giants Series
author: Michael McDermott
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers could be getting one of their All-Stars back from injury. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told Dodger Insider that Andy Pages will return when the club hosts the San Diego Padres.
It had been previously reported that Pages would return on the Dodgers’ final homestand of the 2026 season. This update gives a firmer timeline for when the 2026 All-Star will return to the lineup.
Pages has been a huge boost to the Dodgers’ lineup. The 25-year-old has slashed .272/.358/.458 with 21 home runs and a 119 wRC+ in 127 games this season. He also provides elite center field defense, rated at +18 Defensive Runs Saved and +9 Outs Above Average.
Dodgers Provide Andy Pages Return Timeline
With a return date set for Andy Pages, that means he’ll get roughly six games of action to prepare for the postseason. Ideally, the Dodgers center fielder can shake off a month’s worth of rust, since he won’t have the luxury of a rehab assignment.
Pages suffered a fracture of his left hand when he got hit by a 100 MPH fastball from the Pirates‘ Bubba Chandler. The club has turned to Alek Thomas and Tommy Edman in center field in his absence.
Edman is currently penciled in as the everyday center fielder after Thomas struggled in a short stint. The former Diamondback was later DFA’d, then outrighted to Triple-A after seven games in the lineup.

title: MLB 佐々木朗希、実戦復帰間近か 指揮官が示唆「再び先発として投げることに…」 PSも不測の事態に備え、先発でスタンバイの方針（SANSPO）｜ｄメニューニュース
body:
ドジャースージャイアンツ（18日、ロサンゼルス）「右手中指のまめ」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている米大リーグ、ドジャースの佐々木朗希投手（24）が先発として実戦復帰間近であることが明らかとなった。試合前に取材に応じたデーブ・ロバーツ監督（54）が右腕の状態について語った。
「朗希は良い状態にあるし、投げたがっている。近いうちに復帰できると思う。日付は未定だけど、再び先発として投げることになるでしょう」
16日（日本時間17日）にIL入り後2度目となるライブBP（実戦形式の打撃練習）に登板し、4回を投げて50球を消化するなど復帰に向けて順調にステップを踏んでいる。
一方でチームの先発陣はポストシーズンに向け、不安要素を抱えている。16日のレッズ戦に先発したスネルが左股関節の張りを訴え、1回19球で緊急降板。万全な状態でポストシーズンを迎えることができるか不透明な中、復帰間近の佐々木が重要な存在になりそうだ。
指揮官は「防げるのであれば、先発陣の枚数が不足する事態は避けたい。だからこそ、朗希には4、5イニング程度を投げられるスタミナを維持させておく必要がある」と期待を寄せ、「状況に応じて役割を移行できる選択肢を残しておきたい」と先発でも救援でも起用が可能な24歳を〝ジョーカー〟としてスタンバイさせていく考えを示した。

title: Díaz likely to pitch low-leverage innings as he vies for postseason spot
author: Sarah Wexler
body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers signed Edwin Díaz last offseason with every intention of him being their closer, for 2026 and beyond. As he returns from his second injured list stint this season, he finds himself needing to fight for a role in L.A.’s postseason bullpen.
Prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers activated Díaz from the 15-day IL, where he’d landed on Aug. 18 with neck inflammation. Right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City as the corresponding move.
It’s been a tumultuous year for Díaz, who on Dec. 12 signed a three-year, $69 million contract with the two-time reigning World Series champs. Needless to say, things have not gone as expected for the three-time All-Star. Across his first seven appearances, he allowed seven earned runs in six innings with 10 strikeouts and five walks, after which he landed on the IL with loose bodies in his right elbow that necessitated surgery.
Upon his return on July 29, Díaz slotted back into the closer role, this time recording three blown saves over nine games and pitching to a 12.91 ERA, with nine strikeouts, five walks and two hit batters in 7 2/3 innings pitched.
Díaz’s most recent rehab assignment didn’t do much to inspire confidence. Although the results were less important than how he came out feeling, he struggled with his command, issuing seven walks and hitting a batter in 4 1/3 innings across five appearances with Oklahoma City while recording very few swings and misses.
So what does Díaz have to do to prove he deserves to be part of L.A.’s postseason plans?
“I think just pitch well,” said manager Dave Roberts. “For me, it's regardless of the role. I think we just want to see him throw the baseball the way he's capable of. And you're talking about nine games [remaining in the regular season], so you're talking three or four outings to evaluate, and that should be adequate.”
At this point, that role will not be “closer.” Expect to see Díaz used in lower-leverage spots. With their 13th National League West title in the last 14 seasons now clinched -- even as they vie for a first-round bye -- the Dodgers have the luxury of being able to use their remaining regular-season slate to let a handful of guys essentially try out for October roster spots.
Díaz might just be the headliner of that group, as the three-time Reliever of the Year could prove to be an X-factor out of L.A.’s ’pen as it seeks a three-peat -- so long as he shows he’s a viable option.

title: Dodgers Injury Updates: Shohei Ohtani, Blake Snell, Andy Pages and More
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are beginning their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have just nine more games in the regular season. After clinching the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years, they're still battling for playoff positioning with the Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves.
If the Dodgers clinch one of the top two seeds, they'll secure a first-round bye. That is especially crucial this season as the team deals with injuries to a handful of key players.
Here's the latest updates on six of those players.
Shohei Ohtani Injury Update
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Friday that Ohtani is continuing to progress in his swinging progression.
“Everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three, four, five days," Roberts said. "He’s in a good spot.”
Ohtani has not yet progressed to hitting in live batting practice or off the Trajekt machine. Thus, a return doesn't appear to be imminent.
Ohtani is eligible to return on Wednesday, just five days before the final day of the regular season.
Blake Snell Injury Update
Snell gave the Dodgers a major scare when he exited his Wednesday start after one inning with left groin tightness.
Fortunately, Snell said the exit was more precautionary than anything, as he didn't want to make it worse by staying in the game.
Snell expressed optimism he'd be able to make another start before the end of the regular season. On Friday, Roberts struck a similar tone, saying he was "more confident" the left-hander would be able to make a normal start sometime next week in his regular season finale.
Snell didn't undergo imaging on his groin.
Andy Pages Injury Update
Pages has been out since Aug. 21 when he suffered a fractured hand that forced him to undergo surgery.
However, he rejoined the team at home on Friday, and is expected to be activated at some point during the homestand that goes through Thursday.
Pages told David Vassegh of AM570 that he's hoping to be activated by Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing Injury Update
Rushing told Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic that he had a PRP injection to address his elbow injury that forced him to go back on the IL in early September.
The catcher remains hopeful he'll be able to return as a pinch-hit option off the bench for the postseason, but will know more after hitting off a machine in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki Injury Update
Sasaki threw four simulated innings this week and is expected to start "soon," per Roberts.
The team initially planned to move Sasaki to the bullpen, but will instead keep him stretched out as a starter as an insurance option.
Edgardo Henriquez Injury Update
Henriquez surprisingly went on the IL with a low-grade back strain this past week, ending his regular season.
The Dodgers remain "hopeful" he'll be able to return in the postseason, per Roberts.

He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. Noah is the publisher of Dodgers on SI after contributing as a writer and editor over the last three years.

Ohtani is eligible to return on Wednesday, just five days before the final day of the regular season.
Blake Snell Injury Update
Snell gave the Dodgers a major scare when he exited his Wednesday start after one inning with left groin tightness.
Fortunately, Snell said the exit was more precautionary than anything, as he didn't want to make it worse by staying in the game.
Snell expressed optimism he'd be able to make another start before the end of the regular season. On Friday, Roberts struck a similar tone, saying he was "more confident" the left-hander would be able to make a normal start sometime next week in his regular season finale.
Snell didn't undergo imaging on his groin.
Andy Pages Injury Update
Pages has been out since Aug. 21 when he suffered a fractured hand that forced him to undergo surgery.
However, he rejoined the team at home on Friday, and is expected to be activated at some point during the homestand that goes through Thursday.
Pages told David Vassegh of AM570 that he's hoping to be activated by Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing Injury Update
Rushing told Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic that he had a PRP injection to address his elbow injury that forced him to go back on the IL in early September.
The catcher remains hopeful he'll be able to return as a pinch-hit option off the bench for the postseason, but will know more after hitting off a machine in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki Injury Update
Sasaki threw four simulated innings this week and is expected to start "soon," per Roberts.
The team initially planned to move Sasaki to the bullpen, but will instead keep him stretched out as a starter as an insurance option.
Edgardo Henriquez Injury Update
Henriquez surprisingly went on the IL with a low-grade back strain this past week, ending his regular season.
The Dodgers remain "hopeful" he'll be able to return in the postseason, per Roberts.

title: Andy Pages Sets Dodgers Return Date After Month-Long Injury Absence
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages is set to return on Tuesday against the San Diego Padres after missing a month with a hand fracture.
Pages suffered a fracture in his left hand on August 22nd in a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates. A pitch hit his hand, causing the injury.
The Cuban had surgery on his broken hand shortly after, and he has since steadily increased his baseball activity.
When will Andy Pages return?
On Friday, September 18th, before the Dodgers’ home game against the Giants, Pages told AM 570’s David Vassegh he hopes to return for Tuesday’s game against the Padres.
Manager Dave Roberts has already told the media, including Dodgers Nation, that Pages would be activated at some point during the homestand.
The Dodgers will be home from Friday to Wednesday, before ending their regular season against the Giants in San Francisco.
If Pages does return on Tuesday, that would give him five games to get up to MLB game speed.
Assuming he rests one of those, Pages would have only four games to get everything clicking.
Why the Dodgers need Andy Pages back
Pages is an elite defender, with a 9.5 defensive rating, according to FanGraphs.
Tommy Edman, who has taken on the center field responsibilities, has -1 outs above average. While Pages has 8 outs above average at center field, according to Baseball Savant.
For a team that prides itself on defense, Pages presents the glove and range needed to help keep runs down and help the starting pitching stay in the game.
Pages has a 3.9 fWAR and a 119 wRC+ this season, and as a hitter, he brings a good bat-on-ball skill set.
On both ends of the field, Pages is invaluable to the Dodgers, and they will need him for the postseason.

title: Dodgers activate Edwin Díaz from 15-day IL
author: David Shovein; Edwin Díaz
body:
Dodgers activated RHP Edwin Díaz from the 15-day injured list.
            
                As anticipated, Díaz returns to the Dodgers’ bullpen for Friday night’s battle against the Giants. The expectation is that the Dodgers will ease him back into high-leverage situations, so fantasy managers shouldn’t expect him to be a viable option for saves over the final 10 days of the regular season. Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City in a corresponding move on Friday.

title: Dodgers Lineup vs. Giants: Tyler Glasnow, Josue De Paula Face Big Test
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are aiming to get over their National League West celebration hangover by beating rival San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers clinched the division on Thursday, and there were a ton of celebrations, alcoholic bottles popped after the game, including a long flight to Los Angeles for the start of their six-game homestand.
Dodgers’ Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Will Smith, C
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Freddie Freeman, 1B
5. Miguel Rojas, 2B
6. Kyle Tucker, RF
7. Kike Hernandez, 3B
8. Alex Call, CF
9. Josue De Paula, DH
The Dodgers are facing a southpaw and are promoting some of their best hitters up the order. Betts, Hernandez, Smith, and Rojas are all putting together their best work at the plate against lefties.
Additionally, Alex Call gets a turn at center field, replacing Tommy Edman.
Josue De Paula gets a chance to prove himself against a lefty, which could help set up Betts and Smith at the top of the order with a baserunner to cash in.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers are rolling out Tyler Glasnow, who has looked shaky compared to his usual standard. While there will be understandable rust for someone out months on the injured list.
He has a 4.91 ERA though 22 innings since return from the injured list with back spasms. In his most recent outing, the tall righty allowed four runs off five hits and four walks, with seven strikeouts.
Glasnow only provided four inning as well.
Heading into such a key stretch with the postseason around the corner, Glasnow has the chance to ease any doubts over his ability to deliver a quality playoff start.
With Blake Snell injured and facing an uncertain timeline, there is more riding on Glasnow than ever.

title: Here’s where to watch Giants vs. Dodgers for free tonight: Time, livestream
author: Angela Tricarico; Matt Levy
body:
One of baseball’s oldest rivalries is getting a Friday Night Baseball spotlight.
The San Francisco Giants and Los Angeles Dodgers open a weekend series tonight, Sept. 18; the game is set to air exclusively on Apple TV.
As NL West teams, the Giants and Dodgers play each other 13 times every season, and going into this evening’s contest, only seven have gone down thus far. In exactly one week, the teams will meet again in San Francisco for their final three game stand of the season.
Watch Giants vs. Dodgers for free
- When: Sept. 18, 7:15 p.m. PT / 10:15 p.m. ET
- Where: Dodger Stadium (Los Angeles, California)
- How to watch for free: Apple TV (seven-day free trial)
- Channel: Streaming exclusive
In April, the Giants won two of three against the Dodgers at home. One month later, they split a four-game series at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of this NorCal/SoCal showdown, Dave Roberts’ boys in blue clinched the NL West after taking three of four from the Reds. With this playoff berth, the Dodgers tied the 1991-2005 Atlanta Braves for most consecutive years — 14 to be exact — advancing to the postseason.
San Francisco’s 64-89 season hasn’t been as successful under first-time MLB skipper Tony Vitello but they did take two of three from the Cardinals in their most recent series.
Tonight’s Friday Night Baseball is exclusively streaming on Apple TV, but fear not: subscribing is easy and you’ll be able to tune in in just minutes — and it’s completely free if you’ve never tried Apple TV before.
Giants vs. Dodgers start time
Tonight’s (Sept. 18) Giants versus Dodgers game is scheduled to begin at 7:15 p.m. PT / 10:15 p.m. ET.
How to watch Giants vs. Dodgers for free
Tonight’s Giants versus Dodgers game is airing exclusively on Apple TV‘s Friday Night Baseball, so you’ll need a subscription to watch the game.
Apple TV offers a seven-day free trial for users, so you’ll be able to watch two weeks of doubleheaders before the $14.99/month payments kick in.
Amazon Prime members can also subscribe to Apple TV directly through Prime Video. It costs the same monthly price and also includes a seven-day free trial, but allows you to stream Apple’s content inside the Prime Video app.
Giants vs. Dodgers pitching matchup
Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.68 ERA) starts for the Giants. Tyler Glasnow (4-1, 3.50 ERA) will be on the mound for the Dodgers.

title: Dodgers Announce Starting Lineup vs Giants on Friday Without Max Muncy, Tommy Edman
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers begin their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the rival San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers (93-60) clinched the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years on Thursday. The Giants (64-89) are a whopping 29 games behind LA in the division.
“It’s a big deal. It’s not easy,” manager Dave Roberts said of his team winning another NL West title. “I think a lot of people think it’s easy, it’s a rite of passage. But it’s not easy to win a division when everyone is gunning for you, to keep everyone motivated to play over the course of 162. It’s something we’re all really proud of. But that’s not the end goal.”
The Dodgers and Giants play six times over the next 10 days to close out the season. The Dodgers are just 3-4 against the Giants this season.
Dodgers vs Giants Pitching Matchup on Friday
Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the ball for the Dodgers on Friday night amid a concerning stretch of play.
The right-hander has allowed four runs in each of his last two starts. After his most recent one, manager Dave Roberts somewhat ominously said Glasnow "didn’t feel great" going into it.
Glasnow has made four starts since coming off the IL after a four-month absence due to a back injury. He left the team to go home early this week instead of traveling with them to Cincinnati as the staff wanted to have him avoid going on two flights.
The Dodgers will hope for better results from him on Friday, especially after Blake Snell left his Wednesday start with a groin injury.
For what it's worth, Glasnow's best start of the season came against the Giants in April, when he allowed one hit over eight shutout innings with nine strikeouts.
Opposite Glasnow will be left-hander Cesar Perdomo, who owns a 3.68 ERA over 14.2 career innings at the MLB level.
He made his debut on Sept. 1 as a reliever before starting each of his last two games.
Dodgers Lineup vs Giants
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Will Smith, C
- Teoscar Hernández, LF
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Miguel Rojas, 2B
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Kiké Hernández, 3B
- Alex Call, CF
- Josue De Paula, DH
Max Muncy and Alex Freeland are out of the lineup with the left-handed pitcher on the mound. Tommy Edman is also out.
How to Watch Dodgers vs Giants on Friday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. San Francisco Giants on Friday, Sept. 18 is 7:15 p.m. PT/10:15 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on Apple TV+.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).

rss_body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers begin their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the rival San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers (93-60) clinched the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years on Thursday. The Giants (64-89) are a whopping 29 games behind LA in the division.
“It’s a big deal. It’s not easy,” manager Dave Roberts said of his team winning another NL West title. “I think a lot of people think it’s easy, it’s a rite of passage. But it’s not easy to win a division when everyone is gunning for you, to keep everyone motivated to play over the course of 162. It’s something we’re all really proud of. But that’s not the end goal.”
The Dodgers and Giants play six times over the next 10 days to close out the season. The Dodgers are just 3-4 against the Giants this season.

Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the ball for the Dodgers on Friday night amid a concerning stretch of play.

title: Edwin Diaz Gets Final Chance to Earn Dodgers Postseason Roster Spot
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have officially activated Edwin Diaz from the injured list and optioned reliever Landon Knack back down to the minor leagues.
Diaz has been rehabilitating down in Triple-A with the Oklahoma City Comets as he tries to recover from neck inflammation.
In 4.1 innings of work in the minors during his latest assignment, he has a 12.46 ERA.
With the season winding down for the Comets and Diaz still needing to pitch and prove that he can get outs, the Dodgers are giving him a shot on the major league roster.
Manager Dave Roberts has made it clear that Diaz needs to show tangible results in the regular season to get any standing in the bullpen trust tree.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said.
“So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
This story will be updated.

title: Dodgers activate Edwin Díaz, option Landon Knack
author: Eric Stephen
body:
The Dodgers on Friday activated Edwin Díaz off the injured list, with a week and a half remaining in the regular season to see if his slim chance of pitching his way onto the postseason roster comes to fruition.
Díaz, who signed a three-year contract with the Dodgers in December, struggled to open the season before undergoing arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow in April, which cost him three and a half months.
In 16 appearances with the Dodgers this season, Díaz has allowed runs in nine of them, with an 11.85 ERA, 6.37 xERA, 19 strikeouts and 10 walks in 13 2/3 innings. In nine games after returning from elbow surgery, Díaz had a 19.6-percent strikeout rate, down from 30.3 percent in seven games before surgery, and well below his 39.9-percent career strikeout rate through 2025.
The latest malady for Díaz was neck inflammation, sidelined since August 18. His rehab assignment with Oklahoma City didn't go well at all, throwing more balls than strikes in three of his five appearances, with six runs allowed in 4 1/3 innings, seven walks, and four strikeouts. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Thursday in Cincinnati that Díaz will need to throw more strikes, and quality ones at that, in order to be considered to pitch in October.
"Like anything, it should be a meritocracy. You have to earn the right of opportunities, and you've also got to perform. Eddie understands that," Roberts said, as shown on SportsNet LA. "Where we're at now, we need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That's what he's about."
Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, after fulfilling his role with aplomb on Thursday. Called up for a day, Knack tossed four scoreless innings in relief and earned the win in the Dodgers' division clincher in Cincinnati.
In Knack's three stints in the majors this year, he pitched in four of the eight games for which he was active, with a 3.86 ERA and 4.09 xERA in build relief, with eight strikeouts and two walks in his 11 2/3 innings, plus one save of 2 2/3 innings, the Dodgers' longest save of the season.

title: Dodgers' Edwin Diaz: Officially reinstated from IL
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
The Dodgers activated Diaz (neck) from the 15-day injured list Friday.
Diaz has been officially cleared to return from a nearly one month absence due to a neck injury. The veteran reliever will serve in low-leverage situations upon his return and is unlikely to see many save opportunities unless favored closer Tanner Scott is unavailable. Across five rehab outings, Diaz allowed six runs on four hits and seven walks while striking out four across 4.1 innings.

title: Dodgers Demote Pitcher, Officially Activate Edwin Diaz Amid Disastrous Season
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are giving Edwin Díaz one final chance to prove he belongs on the postseason roster.
On Friday, ahead of their series opener against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers have officially activated Díaz off the 15-day injured list. In order to make room on the active roster, right-hander Landon Knack was optioned.
Díaz joined the Dodgers this offseason on a three-year, $69 million deal to be the team's closer. He had a 10.50 ERA over six innings before going on the injured list and undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
Díaz made his long-awaited return in late July, and the Dodgers were hoping his early-season issues would be behind him.
Unfortunately, that wasn't the case.
The three-time All-Star had an even worse 12.91 ERA over 7.2 innings. He then went back on the IL — this time with a neck injury — and has been out for the last month.
Díaz struggled on his rehab assignment, and there were questions about whether the team would even give him another chance this season.
“He needs to pitch better. It hasn’t been good,” manager Dave Roberts said on Monday. “He’s going to pitch on Wednesday, and I guess we’ll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well."
He had a better rehab outing on Wednesday, pitching one scoreless inning. That was enough for the Dodgers to give him one more opportunity at the big league level.
It won't be as the team's closer, though.
What Will Edwin Diaz's Role Be For Dodgers?
The Dodgers will be using Díaz in low-leverage spots at first as they see if he can be an option for the postseason roster.
“I think like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also got to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now, we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Across Díaz's 16 appearances this season, he has a disastrous 11.85 ERA and four blown saves in 11 chances.
However, if he returns to form in time for the playoffs, all will be forgotten from his disappointing first season in LA.
