title: Es hora de que Shohei Ohtani renuncie al pitcheo de manera definitiva
author: Ryan Phillips
body:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. El pitcheo de Ohtani es un lujo del que Los Angeles puede darse el lujo de prescindir.

original_title: Es hora de que Shohei Ohtani renuncie al pitcheo de manera definitiva
original_body:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. title: Kyle Tucker's recent Dodgers surge is smokescreen fans shouldn't fall for
author: Katrina Stebbins
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West for the 14th time in their last 15 seasons with an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday. Justin Wrobleski pitched three perfect innings, Freddie Freeman continued to heat up, Miguel Rojas hit just his fourth homer of the year, but the Dodgers' top performer, not just in the series finale, but over the Dodgers' last 10 games was Kyle Tucker.
He homered in his first at-bat on Thursday to give the Dodgers an early 2-0 lead. By the end of the game, he'd gone 4-for-5 with the homer, two doubles, three RBI, and ended up a triple shy of the cycle.
After a long season of struggles and fans and writers alike wondering aloud if the Dodgers made a huge mistake signing him to his absurd four-year, $240 million contract, Tucker seems to have turned back into his old self at just the right time.
The Dodgers, while still heavy favorites to win the World Series, have a whole host of weaknesses their upcoming postseason opponents can (and will) identify and exploit. But Tucker earning back his old King Tuck moniker in LA would add an extra bite the lineup expected but hasn't seen most of this season.
However, there's a caveat to all of this that Dodgers fans shouldn't ignore. LA has played seven of their last 10 games against the Reds, one of the worst teams in the National League.
Kyle Tucker's newfound success for the Dodgers has to be tempered by one unavoidable fact
Before coming into this nine-game stretch, Tucker hit .143 with a .628 OPS against the Detroit Tigers, St. Louis Cardinals, and Washington Nationals. All are inferior opponents to the Dodgers and some even had worse records than the Reds by the time they saw the Dodgers. But none had the NL or AL's second-worst run differential like Cincinnati.
Going into this series, Cincinnati had a staggering -148 run differential. Their pitching staff's collective ERA is 4.87 and WHIP is 1.45, the third-worst in baseball in both categories. Of the four starters the Dodgers faced during this series, only Andrew Abbott had an ERA under 5.00 (4.78).
The Dodgers' last nine games should be a greater test of Tucker's mettle, and will prove whether or not this hot streak was purely incidental. Six inter-division games against the San Francisco Giants and three against the San Diego Padres are surely going to give the Dodgers more grief, as games against those teams often do, and may expose this recent surge as being nothing more than a flash in the pan.

title: When is Shohei Ohtani coming back? Dodgers reveal injury update
author: Gabe Lacques; USA TODAY
body:
Andrew Friedman, the Los Angeles Dodgers' president of baseball operations, told reporters in Cincinnati that he expects Shohei Ohtani will return during the club's final nine games of the regular season.
Speaking after the champagne celebration that followed the club's 8-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds that clinched the National League West, Friedman said of Ohtani, "I expect him back in the regular season."
The four-time MVP and two-way superstar will not pitch this season due to right biceps and left knee injuries, and he has not been in the Dodgers lineup since Sept. 7, after which he was placed on the 15-day injured list. Ohtani sat out five games before giving that one a go, and he had just six hits in 49 at-bats (.122) with no home runs in his final 61 plate appearances.
Much of that span was spent trying to also return as a pitcher, before a bullpen session on Aug. 28 was cut short. The club is hoping his focus on playing one side of the ball enables his body not only to heal, but hold up as the Dodgers aim for a third consecutive World Series title.
For the season, Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs and a .902 OPS, and will likely cede his two-year reign as NL MVP to the Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong.

title: 大谷翔平、ド軍地区5連覇を祝福 自身は欠場も…SNSで称えた史上4番目のスピード記録（Full-Count）｜ｄメニューニュース
body:
インスタグラムを更新

title: Edwin Díaz regresará el viernes, pero deberá ganarse su lugar
author: Líder en Deportes
body:
La tambaleante asignación de rehabilitación del puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz ha llegado a su fin.
Se espera que Díaz sea activado de la lista de lesionados el viernes en Los Ángeles, informó el manager Dave Roberts antes del juego del jueves en Cincinnati. Completó un inning en blanco en su quinta salida de rehabilitación con Triple-A Oklahoma City el miércoles, un paso hacia adelante luego de permitir cinco carreras limpias en dos tercios de entrada en su presentación anterior el domingo.
La primera temporada del contrato de tres años y US$69 millones de Díaz con los Dodgers ha estado llena de adversidades. Dos pasantías por la lista de lesionados — primero debido a una cirugía para remover cuerpos libres de su codo derecho en abril, y actualmente una inflamación en el cuello que lo marginó en agosto — lo han mantenido alejado de la lomita de Grandes Ligas durante la mayor parte de la campaña. Cuando ha estado sano, no ha rendido, registrando efectividad de 11.85 con cuatro salvamentos desperdiciados en 11 oportunidades.
Lee también: Miguel Rojas castigó a Cincinnati
Los Dodgers inicialmente esperaban que la asignación de rehabilitación de Díaz fuera breve, pero necesitaban ver más de él antes de activarlo de la lista de lesionados. En cinco oportunidades con Oklahoma City, Díaz permitió seis carreras en 4.1 entradas (efectividad de 12.46). Sus problemas de control han continuado, ya que otorgó más boletos (siete) que ponches (cuatro).
Tal como estaban las cosas, Díaz ya estaba destinado a ser utilizado en situaciones de menor apremio al regresar de la lista de lesionados. Pero también es posible que tenga que ganarse su lugar en el bullpen para la postemporada, ya que Roberts reconoció el lunes que podría quedar fuera del roster si no muestra avances.
“Creo que, como todo, debería ser una meritocracia”, señaló Roberts. “Tienes que ganarte el derecho a las oportunidades, pero luego también tienes que rendir, ¿verdad? Eddie entiende eso. Creo que en el punto en el que estamos ahora, necesitamos que los muchachos se comprometan, rindan y a partir de ahí veremos”.
Aquí tienes todo lo que debes saber sobre la última salida de rehabilitación de Díaz:
¿Cómo le fue?
Díaz realizó 15 pitcheos (11 strikes) para completar la novena entrada en blanco, sorteando un doblete con dos outs que salió del bate del dominicano Miguel Andújar, quien también se está rehabilitando, a 104.3 millas por hora. No indujo ningún swing en blanco en los ocho swings que hicieron en su contra (seis ante su slider y dos frente a su recta de cuatro costuras).
¿Qué están diciendo?
A pesar de que los números subyacentes detrás del inning en blanco de Díaz no fueron ideales, pudo trabajar con lo que tenía para conseguir tres outs — lo cual era lo que los Dodgers necesitaban ver de él.
“Calidad a la hora de lanzar strikes. Sacar outs. Probablemente sea eso”, indicó Roberts. “A medida que entras a la postemporada, cada entrada es de alto apremio”.
¿Qué sigue?
Los Dodgers vieron lo suficiente el miércoles como para traer de vuelta a Díaz para sus últimos nueve juegos de la temporada regular. Comenzará lanzando en situaciones de bajo apremio, pero podría ganarse oportunidades de mayor responsabilidad si rinde.
¿Qué más?
- Los Dodgers recibieron un refuerzo para el bullpen el miércoles, activando a Kris Bubic, adquisición de la Fecha Límite de Cambios, de la lista de lesionados de 60 días. El zurdo tiró un inning en blanco en su debut con el equipo para comenzar a presentar sus argumentos de cara al bullpen de postemporada de Los Ángeles.
- El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez mantiene las esperanzas de regresar para la postemporada luego de que unas imágenes de su espalda revelaran una distensión de bajo grado, informó Roberts. En medio de la incertidumbre con Díaz, Henríquez sería una opción para cerrar juegos en octubre si está sano.
- El cerrador de la postemporada del año pasado, Roki Sasaki, podría asumir un rol de similar este año una vez que sea activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días debido a una ampolla en el dedo medio derecho. Sin embargo, los Dodgers lo mantendrán como abridor por ahora mientras evalúan sus necesidades.
MLB.com.

title: Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
author: JEFF WALLNER
body:
Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Rojos de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.

title: Dodgers exec Andrew Friedman expects Shohei Ohtani to return from IL in the regular season: 'He's progressing well'
author: Kari Anderson
body:
Although the Los Angeles Dodgers are playing without star Shohei Ohtani for the near future, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman thinks it won't be too long before Ohtani is able to make his return.
Ohtani landed on the injured list for the first time in his Dodgers tenure last week, going on the 15-day IL due to right biceps inflammation. But while speaking to reporters Thursday after the Dodgers clinched their fifth straight NL West title, Friedman said Ohtani is on the mend.
"He's doing well," Friedman said, via Jack Harris of the California Post. "He's progressing well."
When asked if Ohtani would be back in time to join the Dodgers in the playoffs, Friedman pointed to the two-way player returning even sooner: "I expect him back in the regular season," he said.
However, Friedman did not provide an answer when asked how many at-bats Ohtani is expected to take, via the Orange County Register's Bill Plunkett.
Because Ohtani's IL stint was backdated to Sept. 8, the earliest he's able to return to the Dodgers' lineup is Sept. 23. Los Angeles will have five games left in the regular season at that point.
Earlier this week, Ohtani took a few hits off a tee in his first swings since going on the IL. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, like Friedman, said at the time that Ohtani was feeling "good" but that the team planned to give him a "consistent build-up."
Roberts did not have a specific return timetable in mind but, like Friedman, said he was hopeful that Ohtani could return before the postseason.
"Whether it happens or not is to be determined, but I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games," Roberts said. "I don't know how many."
With an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday, Los Angeles won the NL West for the 13th time in a 14-year span. The Dodgers had clinched a postseason berth earlier this week, marking the team's 14th consecutive year in the playoffs.

title: Don't Look Now, but Dodgers' Kyle Tucker is Heating Up Just in Time for October
author: Cameron Kiszla
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are rounding into shape as the playoffs are just a couple of weeks away, and perhaps the most important part of that resurgence is Kyle Tucker.
The right fielder has been the subject of complaints and jeers for much of the year after he underperformed his $240 million contract, the largest average annual value in baseball.
Over the past eight games, though, Tucker has been among the best hitters in the sport, and there’s hope he can continue to rake.
Division-clinching game solidifies Tucker’s turnaround
Tucker has notably struggled at home this year, but his coming out party actually began on Sept. 9 at Dodger Stadium.
In that 14-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds, Tucker hit 3-for-5 with a double and a home run, scoring twice in the process.
Two days later, he went 3-for-3 with another homer — a grand slam, his first in three years — and a triple, scoring twice and driving in five runs.
In the seven-game span that ended Wednesday, Baseball Reference shows that Tucker is hitting .333/.433/.833/1.267 — unreal numbers given his yearly stats of.226/.327/.373/.700.
In those seven games, he also hit three homers, a double and a triple, driving in seven runs and scoring nine times.
Thursday, though, was Tucker’s best game yet as a Dodger.
He hit 4-for-5 with a homer and two doubles, driving in three runs and scoring twice.
He very nearly hit for the cycle, with many wanting him to try to stretch that second double into a triple to achieve the feat.
Tucker, however, pushed back on that notion, telling David Vassegh postgame that he “tried my best.”
“I didn’t think I was going to get there. I probably would have been thrown out halfway, but it’s all good,” he said.
Tucker said all that through a Champagne-soaked smile, but it’s clear to see that he was happy about more than just his team clinching the division.
Tucker seems to have found his groove, something surely helped, at least in part, by mechanical changes he’s made with the coaching staff.
What October heroics can do for Kyle Tucker
It’s crazy to think that just a few weeks ago, fans were debating if Tucker should be given a standing ovation at home to help build his confidence.
Whether it was the ovation, those mechanical tweaks or a combination of those and other factors, Tucker’s confidence is clearly back.
He’s again a threat in the batter’s box, and that bodes well for the team’s three-peat chances.
It will be interesting to see if Tucker’s renewed performance continues in the upcoming series at home, but given that this hot streak started at Dodger Stadium, there’s hope he can keep it up.
He has experience with winning playoff baseball, and the Dodgers hope he can be part of another title run next month.

title: Roki Sasaki Watch Takes Another Turn for Dodgers
author: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki has been sidelined for the last three weeks due to a lingering blister.
After dealing with the blister during a late-August start, Sasaki was removed from the game and later added to the injured list.
"When I was facing the first hitter in the fourth inning, I actually didn't feel anything coming beforehand," Sasaki said through an interpreter after that game. "My skin just ripped off, and then after that, it got worse. ... I thought I was able to manage at first because the skin was still there, but after that, it kept getting worse, and I think it affected my slider afterwards."
As he has continued to recover and trend back towards the mound, Sasaki threw a simulated game on Wednesday, in which he completed four innings.
The Dodgers were thinking about having Sasaki pitch in Thursday's series finale against the Cincinnati Reds, but instead elected for the sim game, and to have him set up to return next week.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said on Wednesday. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. ... So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
At first, the Dodgers weren't sure if Sasaki would be back in the rotation — where he appeared for 23 starts this season — or if he would head to the bullpen.
However, after Blake Snell exited Wednesday's start after one inning, Roberts confirmed Sasaki would rejoin the rotation for the time being.
Sasaki had a 4.72 ERA across the first eight starts of his MLB career last season before he was placed on the injured list with a shoulder impingement for over four months. Upon his late-September return, he was not placed back into the rotation, but rather into a bullpen role that saw plenty of success.
In his first two innings of work, Sasaki struck out four and allowed just one hit and zero runs. His next appearance came in the postseason.
For the remainder of the postseason — one that included the first three saves of his MLB career, the pivotal 8th through 10th innings of an NLDS thriller and even 2.2 innings in the World Series — Sasaki established a 0.84 ERA across 10.2 innings of work.
Sasaki will likely return to the bullpen for the postseason this year, especially with the question marks surrounding Edwin Díaz. However, for now, he appears set to make one more start, and improve upon his 4.60 ERA over 119.1 innings this season.

He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

As he has continued to recover and trend back towards the mound, Sasaki threw a simulated game on Wednesday, in which he completed four innings.
The Dodgers were thinking about having Sasaki pitch in Thursday's series finale against the Cincinnati Reds, but instead elected for the sim game, and to have him set up to return next week.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said on Wednesday. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. ... So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
At first, the Dodgers weren't sure if Sasaki would be back in the rotation — where he appeared for 23 starts this season — or if he would head to the bullpen.
However, after Blake Snell exited Wednesday's start after one inning, Roberts confirmed Sasaki would rejoin the rotation for the time being.
Sasaki had a 4.72 ERA across the first eight starts of his MLB career last season before he was placed on the injured list with a shoulder impingement for over four months. Upon his late-September return, he was not placed back into the rotation, but rather into a bullpen role that saw plenty of success.
In his first two innings of work, Sasaki struck out four and allowed just one hit and zero runs. His next appearance came in the postseason.
For the remainder of the postseason — one that included the first three saves of his MLB career, the pivotal 8th through 10th innings of an NLDS thriller and even 2.2 innings in the World Series — Sasaki established a 0.84 ERA across 10.2 innings of work.
Sasaki will likely return to the bullpen for the postseason this year, especially with the question marks surrounding Edwin Díaz. However, for now, he appears set to make one more start, and improve upon his 4.60 ERA over 119.1 innings this season.

title: Sin Shohei Ohtani, los Dodgers amarraron su quinto título divisional
author: FOX Deportes
body:
Redacción FOX Deportes
Sin Shohei Ohtani, los Dodgers amarraron su quinto título divisional
El equipo angelino derrotó a los Cincinnati Reds y se colocó en una posición privilegiada
Los Angeles volvió a teñirse de fiesta al vencer 8-2 a los Cincinnati Reds. Con este triunfo, los Dodgers aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. La ofensiva brilló gracias a Kyle Tucker, quien pegó home run y produjo tres carreras, junto a cuadrangulares de Miguel Rojas y producciones de Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy y Josué De Paula.
La hazaña cobra un valor aún más especial por las complejas circunstancias que rodeaban al equipo en el terreno. La superestrella japonesa Shohei Ohtani tuvo que ver la celebración desde la banca, marginado del line up tras ingresar a la lista de lesionados por molestias físicas. Sin la imponente presencia de su bateador designado titular, la alineación angelina tuvo que reinventarse y responder con contundencia en el momento exacto.
Ante la ausencia del fenómeno japonés, la profundidad del plantel asumió la responsabilidad de dar la cara por el proyecto. Bateadores de experiencia y jugadores de rol enlazaron turnos de alta calidad para sostener a la ofensiva en los momentos más tensos de la jornada. Paralelamente, el pitcheo dictó cátedra desde la loma para silenciar los bates rivales y mantener el control del encuentro de principio a fin.
Al caer el último out de la tarde, el vestidor estalló en júbilo para dar inicio al ya tradicional baño de champán. Este quinto banderín divisional al hilo confirma la jerarquía de una organización construida para sobreponerse a cualquier adversidad. Con el billete a octubre garantizado, Los Angeles envía un mensaje contundente a toda la liga de cara a la postemporada.
LO MÁS VISTO

title: Mookie Betts Thanks Dodgers Fans for Support After Clinching NL West Title - AOL
author: Xavier Constantino
body:
Mookie Betts has a message for Los Angeles Dodgers fans following Thursday’s win over the Cincinnati Reds, which clinched the Dodgers’ fifth straight National League West title after a tumultuous season for the 33-year-old shortstop.
Betts entered Thursday’s game batting .250 with a .316 on-base percentage and a 103 OPS+, well off his career norms. He had 20 home runs with 62 RBIs in 114 games this season, missing time with an oblique strain and facing criticism from parts of the fan base during his early slump, which even led him to step away from social media in May.
“Thank you for sticking with me. I know it was hard,” Betts said in an interview with David Vassegh of SportsNet LA. “I make it hard sometimes, but thank you for sticking by my side. By our side. We’ve got something special coming.” (h/t Dodger Blue on X.com)
Advertisement
Betts has been part of the Dodgers’ last five division titles, and has built a reputation as one of the club’s biggest stars since joining the team in 2020.
A player who has been part of multiple World Series-winning teams, Betts has learned from experience what it takes to win championships, leaning on his teammates and coaches to help guide him through the process.
With the division locked up, the Dodgers now have roughly a week and a half to set their postseason rotation and lineup. The veteran is preparing to lead the Dodgers back to October baseball, chasing the club’s third straight World Series title.

title: Dodgers exec sets definitive expectation for Shohei Ohtani’s return
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI — Amid a champagne-spraying, speaker-blaring, beer-soaked clubhouse scene on Thursday afternoon, there was one matter of on-field business for Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman to address.
How was Shohei Ohtani doing in his recovery from right arm and left knee injuries?
“He’s doing well,” Friedman said, as the team celebrated another National League West title around him at Great American Ball Park. “He’s progressing well.”
Well enough for the two-way star — who was rehabbing back in Los Angeles during the club’s division-clinching road trip — to return before the beginning of the playoffs?
“I expect him back in the regular season,” Friedman declared.
Indeed, by all accounts from team officials over the last couple days, Ohtani has been taking encouraging steps forward as he aims to return from the injured list when eligible next Wednesday.
On Tuesday, Ohtani took his first swings since being removed from the active roster, beginning a hitting ramp-up with reps off a batting tee.
And after a day off from activities Wednesday, manager Dave Roberts said before Thursday’s game that the four-time MVP will advance to coach-pitch batting practice later this week.
“There’s no pain. He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when [the] time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Roberts described Ohtani as feeling “normal-ish” so far in his recovery work. He noted that the slugger has reported no recurrence of discomfort in his arm as he has begun building back up to a return to the field.
That doesn’t mean Ohtani will get back to 100% in time for October.
The ship on that likely sailed after he tried playing through his injuries, at least as a hitter, during the second half of the season — until it reached the point where he was showing visible signs of pain in multiple games earlier this month.
The Dodgers already know Ohtani won’t be able to pitch in the playoffs, after he endured repeated setbacks in his pitching progression despite not making an actual start since July 3.
They know he might still have to battle through his ailments at the plate in the playoffs, as the team attempts to complete a World Series three-peat.
Still, even having a relatively healthy version of Ohtani could weigh heavily in the team’s championship ambitions.
Not until he returns to action will they know exactly where he is at healthwise, after he suffered a 6-for-52 slump leading up to his IL placement.
But for now, they remain hopeful — of not only having Ohtani back by the start of the playoffs but increasingly likely even before then.

title: Los Dodgers reconquistan el Oeste de la Liga Nacional y sellan su 14ª postemporada consecutiva
author: Noroeste; Redacción
body:
Los Dodgers reconquistan el Oeste de la Liga Nacional y sellan su 14ª postemporada consecutiva
CINCINNATI._ Por más que intenten ver el 2026 como una temporada independiente, todo lo que los Dodgers han hecho este año es imposible de separar del contexto más amplio de lo que han logrado en más de una década de excelencia.
Catorce clasificaciones consecutivas a la postemporada. Cinco títulos divisionales seguidos. La inusual oportunidad de luchar por un tricampeonato de la Serie Mundial.
Los Dodgers alcanzaron otro hito importante en la defensa de su título al recuperar la corona del Oeste de la Liga Nacional con una victoria de 8-2 sobre los Rojos la tarde del jueves en el Great American Ball Park. Tres días después de su tradicional brindis con champaña para celebrar que aseguraron un lugar en la postemporada, conquistar el Oeste desató una eufórica celebración en el clubhouse, que esperan sea la primera de muchas durante las próximas semanas.
En sus 14 participaciones consecutivas en la postemporada, igualando un récord, los Dodgers han conquistado 13 títulos divisionales. El único equipo que logró destronarlos fueron los Gigantes del 2021, que los superaron por estrecho margen en una de las luchas por el Oeste de la Liga Nacional más reñidas de los últimos tiempos.
La ofensiva de los Dodgers, cuya inconsistencia ha sido una preocupación constante a lo largo de la temporada, brindó bastante respaldo desde temprano para apoyar un juego de bullpen programado. Kyle Tucker encabezó el ataque con cuatro hits y tres carreras impulsadas, quedándose a un triple de conseguir el primer ciclo de los Dodgers desde el 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, el dominicano Josué De Paula y el venezolano Miguel Rojas también remolcaron anotaciones.
Justin Wrobleski abrió el juego de bullpen con tres innings perfectos, y aunque Blake Treinen permitió un jonrón solitario en el cuarto episodio, Landon Knack lanzó cuatro entradas en blanco antes de que Seth Halvorsen concediera una rayita en el noveno acto.
Con nueve juegos restantes en la temporada regular, los Dodgers están lejos de contar con todo su plantel. Su mejor bateador, Shohei Ohtani, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días, al igual que el cubano Andy Pagés, llamado por primera vez al Juego de Estrellas. La rotación de seis abridores que utilizaron durante gran parte de la temporada se ha reducido a cuatro abridores completamente acondicionados en el róster activo, lo que hizo necesario recurrir a un juego de bullpen el jueves.
Los Dodgers esperan recuperar refuerzos antes de la postemporada y se beneficiarían enormemente de asegurar el descanso en la primera ronda para avanzar directamente a la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, lo que les daría cinco días libres después del final de la temporada regular. Tienen una ventaja de 4.0 juegos sobre los Bravos por el segundo puesto de la Liga Nacional.
Esta versión de los Dodgers no está exenta de defectos, pero tampoco lo estuvieron los equipos campeones consecutivos del 2024 y 2025. Después de convertirse el año pasado en el primer equipo en un cuarto de siglo en defender con éxito su título, buscarán el primer tricampeonato de Grandes Ligas desde los Yanquis de 1998 al 2000.
“Tenemos tanta hambre como en el 2024 y 2025”, dijo el piloto Dave Roberts. “Esta es una temporada aparte. Nuestros muchachos lo entienden”.
(Con información de MLB)

La ofensiva de los Dodgers, cuya inconsistencia ha sido una preocupación constante a lo largo de la temporada, brindó bastante respaldo desde temprano para apoyar un juego de bullpen programado. Kyle Tucker encabezó el ataque con cuatro hits y tres carreras impulsadas, quedándose a un triple de conseguir el primer ciclo de los Dodgers desde el 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, el dominicano Josué De Paula y el venezolano Miguel Rojas también remolcaron anotaciones.
Justin Wrobleski abrió el juego de bullpen con tres innings perfectos, y aunque Blake Treinen permitió un jonrón solitario en el cuarto episodio, Landon Knack lanzó cuatro entradas en blanco antes de que Seth Halvorsen concediera una rayita en el noveno acto.
Con nueve juegos restantes en la temporada regular, los Dodgers están lejos de contar con todo su plantel. Su mejor bateador, Shohei Ohtani, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días, al igual que el cubano Andy Pagés, llamado por primera vez al Juego de Estrellas. La rotación de seis abridores que utilizaron durante gran parte de la temporada se ha reducido a cuatro abridores completamente acondicionados en el róster activo, lo que hizo necesario recurrir a un juego de bullpen el jueves.
Los Dodgers esperan recuperar refuerzos antes de la postemporada y se beneficiarían enormemente de asegurar el descanso en la primera ronda para avanzar directamente a la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, lo que les daría cinco días libres después del final de la temporada regular. Tienen una ventaja de 4.0 juegos sobre los Bravos por el segundo puesto de la Liga Nacional.
Esta versión de los Dodgers no está exenta de defectos, pero tampoco lo estuvieron los equipos campeones consecutivos del 2024 y 2025. Después de convertirse el año pasado en el primer equipo en un cuarto de siglo en defender con éxito su título, buscarán el primer tricampeonato de Grandes Ligas desde los Yanquis de 1998 al 2000.
“Tenemos tanta hambre como en el 2024 y 2025”, dijo el piloto Dave Roberts. “Esta es una temporada aparte. Nuestros muchachos lo entienden”.

title: Tarik Skubal Sends Hilarious Message to Blake Snell After Reds Win
author: TJ French
body:
After their win on Thursday afternoon, the Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West for the 13th time in the past 14 seasons.
LA has a dominant team once again, which is no surprise, especially with two frontline aces on their staff in Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell. While Skubal and Snell haven’t played long together, as Snell was activated off the IL semi-recently and Skubal was traded to LA in August, you can tell the two have formed a close bond while talking shop about pitching.
After the Reds game on Thursday, the Dodgers celebrated in the visiting clubhouse, and Skubal and Sale had a hilarious moment together.
More MLB on Heavy: Mookie Betts Drops Heartfelt Message After Dodgers-Reds Game
Tarik Skubal ‘Little Bros’ Blake Snell
After the game, Tarik Skubal sent this message to Blake Snell:
“This is my best friend. He’s my little brother.”
Tarik Skubal is 29 years old.
Blake Snell is 33 years old.
Perhaps they are best friends, but to say someone four years older than you is hilarious.
However, the joke works because both Skubal and Snell are among the two best starters in all of MLB.
Here was the full exchange:
Skubal: “It’s gonna be special. It’s gonna be the first of many.”
Snell: “Tell em it’s gonna be special because you’re playing this postseason with your boy.”
Skubal: “This is my best friend; he’s my little brother.”
Blake Snell has been known as a locker room clown since joining the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Former Los Angeles Dodgers Pitcher Suddenly Released by New MLB Team
How Do Blake Snell and Tarik Skubal Impact Dodgers’ Postseason Chances?
The Los Angeles Dodgers will likely capture a top-2 seed in the NL, which grants them a bye into the NLDS.
Who their opponent will be remains TBD, but what is determined is that Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell will be the focal point of the Dodgers’ rotation (along with Yamamoto).
So LA needs the dominant southpaws to be at their best in each start they make.
Easier said than done, yes, but both Skubal and Snell were flat-out unhittable in last season’s postseason, so there’s reason to believe they both carry some October mojo.

title: Dodgers clinch 5th straight NL West title, 13th in 14 years, Tucker has 4 hits in 8-2 win over Reds
source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
author: ABC News; JEFF WALLNER Associated Press
body:
Dodgers clinch 5th straight NL West title, 13th in 14 years, Tucker has 4 hits in 8-2 win over Reds
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons, sparked by four hits from Kyle Tucker that included a first-inning home run in an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, The two-time World Series ch...
CINCINNATI -- The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their fifth consecutive NL West division title and 13th in the 14 seasons, sparked by four hits from Kyle Tucker that included a first-inning home run in an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday,
The two-time World Series champions already were assured of their 14th straight postseason appearance, trying the record Atlanta set from 1991 to 2005. Los Angeles (93-60) had clinched no worse than a wild-card berth on Monday.
Los Angeles opened a 9 1/2-game lead over second-place San Diego and has the second-best record in the NL as they try to overtake Milwaukee (95-57 entering Thursday) for the top NL seed. The division clinching was the fourth earliest for the Dodgers after Sept. 10 in 2019, Sept. 13 in 2022 and Sept. 16 in 2023.
Tucker fell a triple short of the cycle and had three RBIs, hitting a single and a pair of doubles. He hit his 16th homer, a two-run drive in the first off Brady Singer, who allowed seven runs, nine hits and four walks in 3 1/3 innings.
Freddie Freeman's sacrifice fly and Tucker's RBI double boosted the lead in the second, and the Dodgers opened a 7-0 lead in the fourth on Max Muncy's two-run double and Josue De Paula's RBI single.
Dodger left-hander Justin Wrobleski, making his 22nd start this season and first since Sept. 6, did not allow a baserunner in three innings while striking out three.
Wrobleski and Blake Treinen combined to retire their first 11 batters before Sal Stewart's 32nd homer.
Landon Knack (1-0) allowed four hits over four scoreless innings for his first big league win since May 31 last year.
Miguel Rojas homered off Brandon Williamson in the ninth.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said reliever Edwin Díaz (neck inflammation) finished his minor league injury rehabilitation assignment and will be activated this weekend.
Dodgers: RHP Tyler Glasnow (4-1, 3.50) starts Friday against San Francisco, who send LHP Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.68) to the mound,
Reds: RHP Chase Burns (15-3, 2.80) starts Friday against the Chicago Cubs.
___

title: Mookie Betts Sends Emotional Message to Dodgers Fans After Difficult Season
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts thanked fans for their support as he battled a hitting slump and injuries again this year.
After the Dodgers clinched the National League West on Thursday, September 17th, Betts reflected on his regular season thus far, which has featured a bumpy ride.
“Thank you for sticking with me. I know it was hard. I make it hard sometimes, but thank you for sticking by my side. By our side. We’ve got something special coming,” Betts said as champagne poured on his face.
This season, Betts battled an oblique injury that sidelined him for about a month, and he started the season poorly at the plate.
In the first month of late March and April, Betts had a 95 wRC+ and a .710 OPS. Then, things got worse until May, with a 75 wRC+ and a .650 OPS.
Things picked up in June, with a 122 wRC+, but July and the first half of August were rough again.
Now, Betts is helping to give the team a last-minute spark.
Mookie Betts’ recent turnaround
Betts has really turned it on offensively over the last month, hitting .280/.366/.466 with five home runs and 23 RBIs.
Along with his standout defense at such a highly valuable position at shortstop, Betts has not been a superstar this year, but instead has been a very good player.
He has a 2.8 fWAR, with a 1.4 offensive rating and a 10.5 defensive rating, both above average, per FanGraphs.
More than the results, he is hitting the ball hard and commanding the strike zone well.
The arrow is pointing up for Mookie Betts at the right time.

title: Dodgers' Kyle Tucker: Powers Dodgers in win
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
Tucker went 4-for-5 with a two-run homer, two doubles, three total RBI and an additional run scored in Thursday's 8-2 win over the Reds.
Tucker got the Dodgers started early with a two-run shot off Brady Singer in the first inning, his 16th homer this season and his first of three extra-base hits in the victory. While it's been a tough year overall for Tucker, the outfielder seems to have turned a corner down the stretch -- he's now 12-for-29 (.414) with four homers and eight extra-base hits in his last eight games. Tucker's boosted his slash line to .232/.331/.387 across 593 plate appearances with 69 RBI, 85 runs scored and 11 stolen bases.

title: Dodgers Clinch NL West Behind Kyle Tucker’s Best Game Yet
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, September 17th, to clinch the National League West.
Kyle Tucker’s big day
Tucker has been fantastic lately, and Thursday’s game was a true cherry on top. He went 4-for-5 with two doubles, a home run, and a single, and drove in three runs.
Over the last seven games, Tucker has put up a .375/.467/.917 slash line with three home runs, nine RBIs, five walks, and three strikeouts.
Even over the last 15 games, Tucker is hitting .280/.383/.680 with five home runs and 11 RBIs.
Tucker nearly had a cycle, but when he gapped a ball in the eighth inning, he didn’t push for a triple and held up instead.
Still, this was Tucker’s game and a promising sign of things to come.
It was not just Tucker who played well, though; Freddie Freeman went 2-for-3 with an RBI and a walk, while Max Muncy went 2-for-4 with two RBIs.
Additionally, Miguel Rojas added the eighth run with a solo home run in the top of the ninth.
Considering the Dodgers went 0-for-11 with runners in scoring position on Wednesday, Thursday’s game was a welcome development.
Bullpen bounce-back
Justin Wrobleski looked great for three innings, allowing no hits and pitching them all perfect, with three strikeouts.
He was only at 32 pitches, and if Roberts wanted to stretch him out, he could have, but the Dodgers want to save his best stuff for the postseason.
Additionally, Landon Knack handled the bulk of the relief, allowing just four hits and recording two punchouts over four innings of clean work.
Blake Treinen and Seth Halvorsen each allowed a run, but thanks to Knack and Wrobleski, it was more than enough to finally clinch the division.

title: Dodgers roll to division-clinching victory behind 4-hit game from Kyle Tucker
author: Bill Plunkett
body:
CINCINNATI — There is the road less traveled. And there is what the Dodgers do every year.
For the 13th time in the past 14 years, they are the National League West division champions. They clinched it with an 8-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds Thursday afternoon.
The Dodgers scored seven times in the first four innings, leaving little doubt about the outcome.
There was little doubt about this year’s division title either.
The Dodgers spent a total of six days out of first place this season – two in April, four in May. They took over first place for good after beating the San Diego Padres on May 19. They had a double-digit lead for the first time on June 28 and have led by no less than seven games every day since.
Any drama is quickly draining from the playoff seeding race as well. Thursday’s win put the Dodgers four games up on the Atlanta Braves (off on Thursday) with a magic number of six to clinch one of the top two seeds and a first-round bye.
Clinching a postseason berth for the 14th consecutive season (tying the Braves’ MLB record) on Monday required only a champagne toast and a short speech from Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Reveal Edwin Diaz Plans Amid Looming Return
author: TJ French
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers, like all other 29 MLB teams, have around 10 games left on the schedule.
LA already knows it will be headed to October, but the Dodgers are still aiming to clinch the NL West, which could happen on Thursday afternoon.
As the Dodgers gear up for October, one of the biggest storylines surrounding the team is who will close games out.
Edwin Diaz was signed to be the team's closer, but he's had inconsistency problems. On Thursday, during their series with the Reds, LA revealed its plans with Edwin Diaz.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Dealt Positive Shohei Ohtani News During Reds Series
Edwin Diaz to be Activated Off IL on Friday
According to multiple reporters who follow the Los Angeles Dodgers, Edwin Diaz will be activated from the Injured List on Friday.
"Dave Roberts said Edwin Diaz will meet team in Los Angeles. When he is activated it will be "low leverage" situations and will have to earn higher leverage spots."
So, that basically rules out the possibility that Edwin Diaz will be a closer for the Dodgers, which is a good call by Dave Roberts. Despite a few solid outings on paper, it feels like every time Diaz has pitched for the Dodgers this season, there's always been added nerves to the situation.
More MLB on Heavy: Blake Snell's Latest Injury Comments Should Not Faze Los Angeles Dodgers Fans
More on Edwin Diaz Injury….
Edwin Diaz has been sidelined since mid-August with a neck injury.
He will be eased into the bullpen fold, and the good news for LA is that they may have already wrapped up the NL West when Diaz joins the team in LA on Friday.
"Díaz signed a three-year, $69MM contract over the winter, but it's been a lost season for the All-Star closer. He's pitched in just 13 2/3 big league innings due to injury and hasn't looked anywhere close to his usual self when healthy enough to take the mound. He's been rocked for 18 runs on 25 hits and 10 walks, leading to an awful 11.85 earned run average. Díaz entered the season with a career 39.9% strikeout rate and 8.6% walk rate. Those marks have plummeted to 24.1% and 12.7% this season, and his average fastball has dropped from 97.2 mph in 2025 to 96.3 mph in 2026."
In other Dodgers news, Andy Pages could be nearing a return as well, and manager Dave Roberts did not rule out a return for Shohei Ohtani during the regular season, which has just a week and a half left.

title: 【MLB】山本由伸、3年目も右肩上がり 勝利、イニング数キャリアハイ更新 ワールドシリーズMVP→WBC→開幕投手→ローテ死守→シーズン完遂
author: 横山尚杜
body:
レッズ2－8ドジャース（17日、シンシナティ）米大リーグ、ドジャースがレッズ戦に勝利し、ナ・リーグ西地区で5年連続の地区優勝を決めた。93勝60敗で、シーズン9試合を残して独走。5月19日（日本時間20日）以降、一度も首位を譲らなかった。球団は直近10年で9度、2016年に就任したロバーツ監督は11年で10度地区Vに輝いた。
昨季、ワールドシリーズ第6戦に先発後、第7戦に〝中0日〟で救援登板し、シリーズMVPを受賞した山本由伸投手（28）は昨季を上回る成績を残した。3月のワールド・ベースボール・クラシック（WBC）にも出場し、シーズンでは2年連続の開幕投手。2年連続ドジャースでただ一人、先発ローテを守り14勝8敗、防御率2.51、178奪三振。シーズン残り1試合の先発を残す状況で、勝利数、イニング数（179回）はキャリアハイを更新。2年連続でオールスターにも選出された。
サイ・ヤング賞（最優秀投手賞）2度を誇るスクバル、スネルと並んでも、その存在感は別格。移籍3年目で、誰からも認められる存在となり、ドジャース投手陣を支えるエースに君臨する。
ワールドシリーズ3連覇を狙うポストシーズンでも欠かせない存在。「終わりだなという気持ちにならないで、引き締めて過ごしていきたいのと調子はいいので自信を持っていきたい」と山本。無双のエースは、ここからが本領発揮の場となる。

title: 【MLB】大谷翔平、MVP獲得絶望的…昨季まで3年連続4度 歓喜のVに〝不在〟 移籍後初のILでリハビリ 3年ぶり開幕二刀流も苦闘の1年
author: 横山尚杜
body:
レッズ2－8ドジャース（17日、シンシナティ）米大リーグ、ドジャースがレッズ戦に勝利し、ナ・リーグ西地区で5年連続の地区優勝を飾った。「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りする大谷翔平投手（32）は遠征地のシンシナティに帯同せず、優勝の瞬間に不在だった。
2023年以来、3年ぶりに開幕二刀流で迎えたが、苦難のシーズンだった。春先は圧巻の内容で投球を続けたが、6月に左膝、7月に右上腕を負傷。例年、夏場に状態が上がる打撃も成績は伸びず、7月10日の登板を回避し、オールスター辞退を発表。12日に左膝潤滑剤注射を受けた。
後半戦は投手復帰のリハビリを進めながら、打者専念で出場するも患部の状態は一進一退で、計3度の投球中断を経た。8月30日の復帰に向け、28日に敵地デトロイトでブルペン入りしたが、患部の状態は思わしくなく復帰を断念。シーズン最終盤で打者専念の決断を下すも、スイングする際に右上腕の違和感も拭えず、9月9日にドジャース移籍後初となる負傷者リスト（IL）入りとなった。
15日に打撃練習を再開するも、依然復帰時期は不透明で、ポストシーズンの出場も危ぶまれている。今季は投手として8勝2敗、防御率1.79、95奪三振。打者として打率・277、30本塁打、80打点、11盗塁の成績。昨季まで3年連続4度受賞していたMVPの獲得は絶望的。ワールドシリーズ3連覇に照準を定める。

2023年以来、3年ぶりに開幕二刀流で迎えたが、苦難のシーズンだった。春先は圧巻の内容で投球を続けたが、6月に左膝、7月に右上腕を負傷。例年、夏場に状態が上がる打撃も成績は伸びず、7月10日の登板を回避し、オールスター辞退を発表。12日に左膝潤滑剤注射を受けた。
後半戦は投手復帰のリハビリを進めながら、打者専念で出場するも患部の状態は一進一退で、計3度の投球中断を経た。8月30日の復帰に向け、28日に敵地デトロイトでブルペン入りしたが、患部の状態は思わしくなく復帰を断念。シーズン最終盤で打者専念の決断を下すも、スイングする際に右上腕の違和感も拭えず、9月9日にドジャース移籍後初となる負傷者リスト（IL）入りとなった。
15日に打撃練習を再開するも、依然復帰時期は不透明で、ポストシーズンの出場も危ぶまれている。今季は投手として8勝2敗、防御率1.79、95奪三振。打者として打率・277、30本塁打、80打点、11盗塁の成績。昨季まで3年連続4度受賞していたMVPの獲得は絶望的。ワールドシリーズ3連覇に照準を定める。

alternate_sources.title: MLB 大谷翔平、MVP獲得絶望的…昨季まで3年連続4度 歓喜のVに〝不在〟 移籍後初のILでリハビリ 3年ぶり開幕二刀流も苦闘の1年（SANSPO）｜ｄメニューニュース

title: Commentary: No more bubbly — NL West champion Dodgers appear headed for early fall
author: Bill Plaschke
body:
-    Click here to listen to this article
-   
They hit their magic number, but minus the magic.
The Dodgers trudged toward October by clinching their 13th National League West title in 14 years on Thursday, their customary march mired in a quicksand of questions.
Has any Dodger team during this golden era entered the playoffs with more injuries, more uncertainty, and a greater fear of underachievement?
Will the party in Cincinnati be the last time they celebrate this season?
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
The Three-Peat looks like a no-go.
Despite the best efforts from baseball’s best braintrust, their latest creation simply doesn’t have the appearance of a championship team.
They’re aging, they’re hurting and, with only a couple of weeks left until the beginning of their annual autumnal angst, they look tired and taut and unprepared for this monumental tussle with history.
“I think for me, the message was, ‘We haven’t come close to playing our best baseball yet.’” manager Dave Roberts told reporters when relaying his speech to the team earlier this week upon clinching a record-tying 14th consecutive playoff berth.
He added, “The message was, we’ve accomplished a lot up to this point, all the while not playing our best baseball. So let’s get some of these guys healthy.”
Haven’t come close to playing our best baseball… Let’s get some of these guys healthy.
Not exactly “Win one for the Gipper” stuff, but completely accurate. These postseason’s themes are more realistic than inspirational, and for good reason.
No, they haven’t come close to playing their best baseball. Forget what you see in these season-ending games against some of the worst teams. Remember, instead, what they’ve done against some of baseball’s best.
Since the All-Star break, they are 4-12 against the five National League playoff contenders. The Atlanta Braves swept them. The Chicago Cubs swept them. The Milwaukee Brewers dominated them.
These teams will be waiting for them in October, and even baseball’s richest roster might not be enough to carry this staggered bunch through their toughest stretch. They’ve played a lot of games in three years, all under baseball’s brightest spotlight, every night, scores of media, millions of fans, a worldwide whirl for 28 regular dudes, and it’s finally taken its toll.
They’ve hit the wall… and the wall is about to hit back.
“It’s not easy, I think it’s a lot harder than people think it is,” said Roberts. “Human nature alone, when you’re hungry, when you’re chasing something, it’s a lot more easy to be motivated, versus, having been there, done that, it gets a little trite, a little old.”
He added: “To keep guys enthusiastic, focused, hungry, that’s harder. But to their credit, they stayed the course. And for me, we’re just as hungry as we were in ‘24 and ‘25. This is a separate season. Our guys understand.”
The 1988-89 Lakers understood, too. And they still got burned in ways that Dodger fans will find painfully familiar. Showtime was chasing the original “three-peat” trademarked by Pat Riley when the Lakers were swept by the Detroit Pistons in a Finals that seemed cursed,
Byron Scott missed the series with a hamstring injury and Magic Johnson essentially missed the final two games with a hamstring injury and they couldn’t survive.
This looks like the Dodgers today. Their injuries feel too major, and the impact too deep.
Start with Shohei Ohtani. The Dodgers haven’t won a full-season championship in 38 years without him at the top of the lineup. He’ll be there again, but his body has been breaking down for the last couple of months, and, before being recently placed on the injured list — finally! — he was only a shadow of himself.
He hasn’t hit a home run or driven in a run outside of Coors Field in more than a month. In his last 24 games before going on the IL with biceps and knee issues, he was batting .198. The Dodgers can’t admit it, and Ohtani would never acknowledge it, but this is a man in serious need of an extended rest.
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
Also on the injured list in these final days is Andy Pages, who was having a career year before breaking his hand. He’ll return without much time to get ready for October, and this is a man who will need some time, as he has a career .114 average in the postseason and was even benched last year before he redeemed himself with that picturesque catch over Kiké Hernández.
Speaking of last October’s heroes, the biggest savior has also spent the summer in pain, Will Smith battling neck issues until recently returning to the lineup. But the comeback has been bumpy. In his initial games since returning at the start of September, Smith was batting .171. Last October he set a major league record by catching 73 innings in the World Series. He is still paying the price.
Then there’s Freddie Freeman, whose bat doesn’t have the same pop, who’s step doesn’t have the same spring, and who has his worst OPS in 14 years. Add an inconsistent Mookie Betts and an incredibly streaky Teoscar Hernández to an already-shaky lineup.
It’s been such an unsteady year, Andrew Friedman’s two big offseason acquisitions have been busts. Edwin Díaz has been terrible, and then injured, then terrible again. Kyle Tucker has been terrible, then worse, then mostly invisible.
Even the Dodgers two role-playing heroes have seemingly disappeared. Kiké Hernández, at age 35, has his lowest home-run total — three — in 12 years. Miguel Rojas, at age 37, has his lowest home run and RBI totals in nine years.
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
As if they didn’t have enough problems on the field and at the plate, check out the mound. No, don’t.
Even what should be their strength is now being threatened. Blake Snell left Wednesday’s game early with groin issues and Tyler Glasnow recently complained of general discomfort. This leaves a proven playoff rotation of two, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal, and if you think Yamamoto threw a lot of innings last October, this time he won’t be able to leave the mound for a month.
In all, this is a Dodger team facing its toughest challenge yet, their quest for an historic three-peat much tougher than the last two journeys, one that will require arguably the greatest stretch of baseball in franchise history to complete.
This division title is a nice beginning.
It could also be the end.

title: ドジャース５連覇 大谷翔平不在も24度目地区優勝 2013年以降は14年間で13度目と圧倒 - ＭＬＢ : 日刊スポーツ
body:
ドジャースが敵地でレッズに快勝し、5年連続の地区優勝を決めた。通算24度目で、2013年以降は14年間で13度目と圧倒している。16年に就任したデーブ・ロバーツ監督は11年で10度目の優勝となった。
1回、タッカーの16号2ランで先制。2回はフリーマンの犠飛、タッカーの適時二塁打で2点を追加。4回には無死満塁からマンシーの2点適時二塁打、デパウラの適時打で3点を奪い7－0とリードを広げた。9回には今季限りでの引退を表明しているロハスが4号ソロを放ちダメを押した。
守っては先発のロブレスキが3回を無安打無失点の好投。4回から継投に入りトライネン、ナック、ハルボーセンとつなぎ2失点に抑え快勝した。右上腕二頭筋の炎症で負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている大谷翔平投手（32）はロサンゼルスに残留しており不在だった。
大谷と山本由伸投手（28）は3年連続、佐々木朗希投手（24）にとっては2年連続の栄誉。24年は9月26日、昨年は9月25日に優勝が決まっており、ここ3年で最も早い優勝決定となった。
ドジャースは14日のレッズとのカード初戦に勝利し、メジャータイ記録となる14年連続のポストシーズン進出を決めた。マジック「1」で迎えた前日は左腕スネルの緊急降板もあり2－6で敗戦。その後に行われた試合で2位パドレスが勝利したため優勝決定はならなかったが、一夜明けてきっちり自軍の勝利で優勝を決めた。
ポストシーズンはワイルドカードシリーズが29日（同30日）、地区シリーズが10月3日（同4日）に開幕。第2シード（地区優勝チームの中で勝率2位）までに入れば地区シリーズからのスタートになるため、今後もシード争いは続く。

ドジャースは14日のレッズとのカード初戦に勝利し、メジャータイ記録となる14年連続のポストシーズン進出を決めた。マジック「1」で迎えた前日は左腕スネルの緊急降板もあり2－6で敗戦。その後に行われた試合で2位パドレスが勝利したため優勝決定はならなかったが、一夜明けてきっちり自軍の勝利で優勝を決めた。
ポストシーズンはワイルドカードシリーズが29日（同30日）、地区シリーズが10月3日（同4日）に開幕。第2シード（地区優勝チームの中で勝率2位）までに入れば地区シリーズからのスタートになるため、今後もシード争いは続く。

title: Pages (fractured hand) will return within the week
author: Eric Samulski; Andy Pages
body:
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said that the team’s plan is “to activate Andy Pages (fractured hand) this homestand without a rehab assignment.”
            
                The Dodgers are home from Friday through next Wednesday, so Pages could be activated at any time during that stretch. The season ends for Triple-A Oklahoma City on Sunday, so if Pages is coming back without playing in rehab games, our best guess is that he returns early next week. Considering the 25-year-old fractured his hand on August 21st and will not have any rehab games before returning, it’s going to be tough to trust him in fantasy leagues for the final week of the season.

title: Edmunds and Dodgers’ Tommy ‘Tanks’ Edman Fuel LA Fans with $25,000 Gas Giveaway on Sept. 25
author: Edmunds
body:
SANTA MONICA, Calif., Sept. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Los Angeles-based car shopping site Edmunds today announced it is fueling Los Angeles Dodgers fans for October baseball with $25,000 in free gas on Friday, September 25.
Edmunds is joining forces with Dodgers fan-favorite #25 Tommy ‘Tanks’ Edman for the Tommy Tanks Gas Giveaway at Longo Lexus in El Monte, CA. Fans must arrive by car to participate and are encouraged to wear Dodger blue attire. A total of 333 $75 gas gift cards from 76® will be distributed while supplies last, limited to one per vehicle.
With Edman and the team away for their final regular season series in San Francisco, Dodgers fans are invited to root on the Boys in Blue as they gear up for October baseball.
Taking ‘Tommy Tanks’ Beyond the Ballpark with $25K in Free Gas
Playing off Edman’s No. 25, Edmunds will give away $25,000 in gas on September 25, bringing his ‘Tommy Tanks’ moniker beyond the ballpark and to the pump for LA drivers.
- Date: Friday, September 25
- Time: 6 - 8 PM
- Location: Longo Lexus in El Monte, CA (3530 Peck Rd, El Monte, CA 91731)
- How to Participate: Fans must arrive by car and enter Longo Lexus through the main entrance on Peck Road; walk-up entry is not permitted. One person per vehicle will receive a wristband before parking and heading to the Longo Lexus showroom to complete a quick form, engage with the Tommy Tanks Gas Calculator, and receive the gift card. Dodgers gear is encouraged! A total of 333 $75 gas gift cards from 76® will be available while supplies last, limited to one per vehicle.
- More Information: Full event details and giveaway rules can be found at edmunds.com/freegas.
VIDEO: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/r6zzAd3Iqtk
Dodgers Fans Said They’d Turn Down $1 Gas for Another Championship. Edmunds is Fueling Their Dedication.
The Tommy Tanks Gas Giveaway was inspired by a survey of more than 2,000 Dodgers fans conducted by Edmunds earlier this season1 that revealed just how far fans are willing to go for the Boys in Blue. When asked to choose between the Dodgers winning a third consecutive World Championship or gas prices falling to $1 per gallon, 80% chose another ring. And they’re willing to brave some serious LA traffic for their team, too: Nearly one-third (32%) said they’d spend five hours or more traveling to and from a Dodgers home game in October.
“Between driving in LA traffic and keeping up with high fuel costs, local drivers could use a win,” said Tommy Edman. “Teaming with Edmunds to fuel up the best fanbase in baseball for another October run is an awesome way to thank LA for showing up for us night in and night out.”
High Gas Prices Add to Affordability Pressures for LA Drivers 
The giveaway comes as LA drivers continue to face stubbornly high prices at the pump, adding to the persistent affordability challenges facing vehicle owners. According to AAA, the average price for regular fuel in the Los Angeles/Long Beach metro area was $6.09 yesterday, September 16. 
The pressure at the pump comes as consumers are already navigating record-high vehicle expenses: Edmunds recently reported that the average monthly payment on new-vehicle purchases hit a new record of $777 in Q2, and the average price for a 3-year-old used vehicle rose to $32,461 last quarter, a new second-quarter record.
“We know how much Southern Californians rely on their cars and how quickly the costs of driving can add up,” said Alison Steinlauf Anziska, senior vice president of marketing at Edmunds. “Dodgers fans have shown us just how far they’ll go to support their team, and Tommy’s been showing them exactly why they call him ‘Tommy Tanks.’ We thought it would be fun to take that nickname beyond the ballpark and give fans a little relief at the pump as they cheer on the Dodgers into October.”
More Dodgers Fan Survey Findings Highlight Serious Dedication
Beyond their willingness to choose another Dodgers championship over $1 gas and spend long hours on the road traveling to October home games, Edmunds’ survey of more than 2,000 Dodgers fans from earlier this season revealed a few other ways their fandom shows up on and off the road:
- Many fans are susceptible to catching a case of the ‘Dodger blues’: Two-thirds (66%) of fans said they have skipped work, school or another major obligation to attend a Dodger game.
- Dodgers passion extends to the driveway: 13% of Dodger fans drive a blue car, well above the California state average of 7% of new vehicles sold in 2025.
- Fuel economy matters to Dodgers fans: When considering the car-shopping priorities that mattered most to fans, fuel economy ranked among the top three factors, along with price and reliability.
Edmunds, Edman and the Dodgers Go ‘Back-to-Back’
The gas giveaway and fan survey are the latest elements of Edmunds’ ‘Back to Back’ brand campaign in collaboration with the Dodgers and Edman. As part of the campaign, Edmunds is also transforming its Gas Savings Calculator into the ‘Tommy Tanks Gas Calculator,’ helping consumers estimate how much they could save on fuel by switching to a more fuel-efficient vehicle or different powertrain.
Earlier this season, Edmunds executed a sweepstakes offering fans a chance at the ultimate VIP gameday experience and a free vehicle appraisal. Edmunds also launched ‘The Challenge,’ the brand’s second consecutive hero digital ad campaign starring Edman as he helps fans make the right call in their next car shopping decision with the help of Edmunds.
For more information and official rules, check out the Tommy Tanks Gas Giveaway event page at edmunds.com/freegas.
1 *Source: Edmunds survey of Dodgers fans, n=2,071, April 2026
About Longo Lexus
Longo Lexus, located in El Monte, California, is a premier Lexus dealership dedicated to delivering exceptional guest experiences throughout every stage of the vehicle ownership journey. Part of Penske Motor Group, Longo Lexus has been recognized as the #1 Lexus dealership for new vehicle sales in the Western United States since opening in 1990. The dealership offers an extensive selection of new, L/Certified, and pre-owned vehicles, supported by state-of-the-art service, parts, collision repair, and in-house customization facilities. Built on a longstanding commitment to integrity, excellence, and putting guests first, Longo Lexus continues to set the standard for luxury automotive retail and ownership. For more information, visit longolexus.com or follow Longo Lexus on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and LinkedIn.

Edmunds guides car shoppers online from research to purchase. With in-depth reviews of every new vehicle, shopping tips from an in-house team of experts, plus a wealth of consumer and automotive market insights, Edmunds helps millions of shoppers each month select, price and buy a car with confidence. Regarded as one of America's best workplaces by Newsweek, Fortune, Great Place to Work and Built In, Edmunds is based in Santa Monica, California. title: Blake Snell’s Latest Injury Comments Should Not Faze Los Angeles Dodgers Fans
author: TJ French
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers endured a bit of an injury scare regarding starter Blake Snell in their recent game against the Cincinnati Reds.
Snell, who made the start for LA, was pulled after just one inning with groin tightness.
During the game, reports surfaced that the Snell injury was not thought to be serious, and that Snell should still be in line to make his start.
Well, after the end of the game, Snell spoke with the media, and his comments about the injury should give Dodgers fans some assurance.
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to George Lombard Jr. Blunder in Yankees-Twins Game
What Did Blake Snell Say About His Groin Injury?
Per @SportsNetLA, here is some of what Blake Snell had to say about his early exit:
"I was gonna try to get through five, but I just knew I didn't have a good shot of doing that and remaining healthy."
He also added that he's "day-to-day", and "should be good" to make his next start.
So while many Dodgers fans may have been panicking after he was pulled from the game, it's expected to be a precautionary measure.
The Dodgers' October rotation would still look very formidable without Blake Snell in it, but considering Snell's additions last October, LA is likely going to be as careful as possible when it comes to him being at a full bill of health in a few weeks.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Critical Roki Sasaki Update During Reds Series
