title: ‘I just want to feel saucy’: Inside Josue De Paula’s fearless Dodgers debut
author: Fabian Ardaya
body:
CINCINNATI — Josue De Paula is in his element in the batter’s box. He carries himself like a guy who knows his importance to the Los Angeles Dodgers depends on how well he can command himself within those 24 square feet of chalk lines. De Paula asserts himself with a confident shake of the head after each pitch outside the strike zone.
Advertisement
Some head shakes are more exaggerated than others. Each demonstrates the same message: De Paula is not going to give in.
“I just want to feel saucy when I’m up there, you know what I’m saying?” De Paula told The Athletic this week. “I feel like I’m in control, not you. … I want my pitch. Come in the zone. Let’s go.”
This is who De Paula wants to be. He describes hitting as “aggressive patience,” an approach that puts him on the attack.
“It’s almost like a war for me in my head,” De Paula said. “I look confident. I look saucy. I feel saucy when I’m in the box, so it’s like, ‘Hey bro, let’s keep it rocking.’”
It took four games for De Paula to inspire fascination within the Dodgers dynasty, where his every at-bat feels like a must-watch example of how to command a zone. Of the first 37 big-league pitches De Paula saw outside of the strike zone, he swung at just five. He made it 17 plate appearances without striking out before going down swinging in the seventh inning and looking in the ninth in the Dodgers’ 4-0 win over the Reds on Tuesday. De Paula does not seem fazed that he is just 2 for 14 (.143) since being called up, including five hitless at-bats in his first game in the leadoff spot.
That’s because he believes in his process. A day earlier, De Paula battled back from down in the count against Reds lefty Nick Lodolo, a former All-Star. The left-handed batter took a 2-2 fastball just below the knees, crouched and shook his head. A pitch later, De Paula walked for the fifth time in his short career.
The clip of the head shake drew a chuckle from the proprietor of the “Soto Shuffle” himself, Juan Soto, who, like De Paula, once honed his craft at the El Niche Baseball Academy in the Dominican city of Santo Domingo.
Josue De Paula live reaction to you trying to get him to chase. https://t.co/CrmRSnDVgO pic.twitter.com/dbXGz8WYL0
— Chad Moriyama (@ChadMoriyama) September 14, 2026
“El loco mío,” Soto shared to his Instagram story in Spanish, stamping his approval with a laughing emoji. My guy.
Advertisement
“I swear I wasn’t trying to do like the whole thing,” De Paula said with a laugh. “I just got into my legs, and I was shaking my head … but I’m not mad. That’s not a bad player to look like.”
De Paula, 21, feels like an injection of youthful exuberance for baseball’s oldest lineup. The Brooklyn-born son of a Dominican father (and relative of NBA veterans Stephon Marbury and Sebastian Telfair) speaks with a thick New York accent and oozes the confidence of a player who carries that swagger into the box.
De Paula is the crown jewel of a Dodgers farm system that is expected to prolong this run of excellence. Last week, he became the first position player ever to be called up directly from Double A by this Andrew Friedman-led front office group.
De Paula is here because he can hit, has always hit, and the Dodgers need him to hit. De Paula is here to serve as the Dodgers’ designated hitter, at least until Shohei Ohtani returns from the injured list. No one with the Dodgers, however, is ruling out the possibility that De Paula could help them in October as they seek a third consecutive World Series title.
“I hope he makes our decision hard,” manager Dave Roberts said.
Through De Paula’s torrid run through the Dodgers’ farm system, officials raved about his keen ability to pick up the baseball, make proper swing decisions and recognize spin.
“He doesn’t give away any pitches, which I love, let alone give away any at-bats,” Roberts said.
Pair that with a preternatural ability to make contact, and De Paula entered this season as one of the highly-regarded young hitters in the league. The Dodgers implemented a change to De Paula’s swing this year, lowering his hands and opening up his resulting bat path to keep the barrel in the zone longer. That has allowed him to access more power by pulling more fly balls and has made him a lethal producer at Double A.
Advertisement
De Paula slugged 27 home runs this season in Double A, more than double what he had in any of his first four professional seasons. His first hit Sunday in Miami was a mammoth upper-deck shot to right field on the kind of awe-inspiring swing that has come much more easily for De Paula than in years past.
“When all those things are kind of clicking, it’s tough for any pitcher to compete with,” hitting coach Robert Van Scoyoc said. “So it’s been very impressive so far.”
De Paula became a Dodger partially as a byproduct of the COVID-19 pandemic, which shut down the New York baseball season and prompted De Paula’s father, Josue Sr., to send him to the Dominican Republic to work at El Niche under Cristian “Niche” Batista.
“It was like stepping into a whole other world,” De Paula said.
It was there, during an offseason workout, that De Paula met Soto, who broke into the big leagues at 19 years old with the kind of swaggering command of the batter’s box that De Paula hopes to replicate. Some head shakes are more exaggerated than others. Each demonstrates the same message: De Paula is not going to give in.
“I just want to feel saucy when I’m up there, you know what I’m saying?” De Paula told The Athletic this week. “I feel like I’m in control, not you. … I want my pitch. Come in the zone. Let’s go.”
This is who De Paula wants to be. He describes hitting as “aggressive patience,” an approach that puts him on the attack.
“It’s almost like a war for me in my head,” De Paula said. “I look confident. I look saucy. I feel saucy when I’m in the box, so it’s like, ‘Hey bro, let’s keep it rocking.’”
It took four games for De Paula to inspire fascination within the Dodgers dynasty, where his every at-bat feels like a must-watch example of how to command a zone. Of the first 37 big-league pitches De Paula saw outside of the strike zone, he swung at just five. He made it 17 plate appearances without striking out before going down swinging in the seventh inning and looking in the ninth in the Dodgers’ 4-0 win over the Reds on Tuesday. De Paula does not seem fazed that he is just 2 for 14 (.143) since being called up, including five hitless at-bats in his first game in the leadoff spot.

The left-handed batter took a 2-2 fastball just below the knees, crouched and shook his head. A pitch later, De Paula walked for the fifth time in his short career.

title: Dodgers notes: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Teoscar Hernández, Shohei Ohtani
author: Jacob Macofsky
body:
The Dodgers’ winning ways in September were briefly interrupted for two games against the Miami Marlins, but they have picked back up against the Cincinnati Reds, taking the first two games of a four-game set.
After Tarik Skubal shut down Cincinnati over seven innings on Monday, Yoshinobu Yamamoto continued the trend of marvelous results from the rotation with a seven-inning scoreless gem on Tuesday, working through a pair of lead-off walks while allowing just one hit while striking out seven. Yamamoto has amazed in his two most recent starts— both against the Reds— allowing just one run over 14 innings while racking up 17 strikeouts compared to just three walks.
Yamamoto held the Reds to just a 1-21 clip after walking his first two hitters of the game on Tuesday, and the right-hander managed to take a page out of Skubal’s playbook for his dominating efforts, notes Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
Yamamoto was able to learn from how the Reds approached Skubal the night before, and Snell was no doubt gathering similar information on Tuesday.
“That kind of encouraged me to be aggressive and attack the hitters,” Yamamoto said through interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda.
The pitching has managed to hold their end of the bargain against Cincinnati this week, and Blake Snell looks to keep that trajectory in motion. On the offensive side of the ball, Teoscar Hernández has fortified the offense at Great American Ball Park, as the right-hander has crushed a pair of two-run home runs that put both games out of reach.
Hernández has once again found his stride that fans saw during spring training this year, and the Dodger outfielder’s recent success is the brainchild of hitting coach Aaron Bates, allowing Hernández to have a “twister tap” in his stride to the ball, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“It was a great meeting we had,” Bates said. “We all talked about it, and then he felt comfortable enough to do it, and then the rest is to his credit. He’s just been who he is.”
“When Teo’s hips are loose that way, and his front leg looks like an Elvis knee, it’s a good sign for us,” Bates said. “Because that means that he can open and close it without his upper body going with it.”
Update on Shohei Ohtani
It’s an unusual feeling watching the Dodgers without Shohei Ohtani in the everyday lineup. So far, rookie Josue De Paula has filled in at DH to a small degree of success in limited time (.143/.368/.429, 19 PA) while the reigning two-time NL MVP recovers from multiple nagging issues.
Jack Harris of the California Post notes that Ohtani was able to take batting practice on Monday, and the team is optimistic that he can potentially return from the injured list before the end of the regular season.
“Today was positive,” Roberts said, “and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”

title: MLB News: Roberto Clemente Day, Shohei Ohtani, Pete Alonso, Aaron Judge, Arizona Fall League, Gerrit Cole
author: Ashley MacLennan
body:
Tuesday was Roberto Clemente Day in MLB, celebrating one of the most outstanding humans to ever play baseball, and annually it is used as an opportunity to honor both Latin players and also the humanitarian and charitable efforts of players on every team by nominating a candidate for the season’s Roberto Clemente Award. It’s a good day to remember all the good that Clemente did, but also all the good he continues to inspire.
We will also look at some more controversial topics, like whether or not it’s time for the Braves to consider selling the team, or if it’s time for Shohei Ohtani to give up pitching for good. Plus, is Gerrit Cole putting too much blame on the ABS system for his pitching woes?
There’s all that and more below, so let’s get right into it!
- Dan Szymborski wonders if Gavin Williams is a legit ace.
- Arizona Fall League rosters have been revealed. (MLB)
- A look at some other players who have managed to have a 10 WAR season. (MLB)
- Ryan Phillips thinks it’s time that Shohei Ohtani give up pitching for good.
- Evan Drellich explains why one Braves’ investor thinks now is the time to sell the team. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- On Roberto Clemente Day, Jorge Castillo takes a deep dive into the declining numbers of Puerto Rican players in MLB.
- Aaron Judge got his first home run after his return from the IL, and helped the Yankees clinch a postseason berth. (AP)
- Jim Bowden assesses what is and isn’t fair in the CBA negotiations from the perspective of a former exec. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- This is a crazy at-bat.
- David Laurila talks to the delightful Sean Doolittle about pitching.
- Does height really matter? In baseball it sure does, and Davy Andrews explains why.
- With 14 straight, the Dodgers have tied the record for consecutive playoff clinches. Story by Sonja Chen.
- Andy Demetra shares the story of a banned minor leaguer who changed his name to sneak back into the majors.
- Terry Francona seemed relieved by reports that there would be no major changes in the Reds’ front office. (AP)
- Tom Verducci explains why Gerrit Cole can’t blame the ABS for his pitching woes.
- Pete Alonso was touched by the crowd’s welcome in his return to Citi Field. (AP)
- Tyler Kepner bemoans the Mets’ loss of Alonso and their inability to replace him. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- Your 2026 Roberto Clemente Award nominees.
- Jay Jaffe checks in on the Cy Young races and the leading candidates for both leagues.
- Jared Greenspan also checks in on the likely (and possibly unanimous) Cy Young winners.
- Ben Clemens talks to Noah Cameron about how his worst pitch actually made him better.
- Kiri Oler checks in on how the San Francisco Firebells are dominating the WPBL postseason.
- Ian Browne looks at what the return of Garrett Crochet could mean for the Red Sox.
- Karl Rasmussen rounds up some milestones that could be set in the final weeks of the season.

title: Robert De Niro ya negocia su próximo proyecto: un biopic sobre una leyenda del béisbol
author: Europa Press
body:
Robert De Niro en la película Fanático - TRISTAR PICTURES
 
 
   MADRID, 16 Sep. (CulturaOcio) - 
   Robert De Niro se encuentra en negociaciones para dar vida a Tommy Lasorda, el entrenador de los Dodgers fallecido en 2021, en un biopic sobre su vida que prepara Skydance Sports. Lasorda, una de las figuras más destacadas de la historia reciente del béisbol, estuvo más de 70 años vinculado a los Dodgers, primero como jugador y, posteriormente, como entrenador.
   Según informa Deadline citando fuentes cercanas a la producción, su título provisional es Tommy & Me. Reid Carolin (Magic Mike, Dog. Un viaje salvaje) será el encargado de dirigir la cinta, cuyo guion firman George Gallo, Cambron Clark y el propio Carolin. Por el momento, se desconocen detalles sobre el enfoque que adoptará el filme para narrar la historia de Lasorda.
   Carolin también produce la película a través de Free Association, sello del que es socio junto a Channing Tatum. Entre sus próximos proyectos, el cineasta tiene previsto dirigir Isle of Man, drama deportivo centrado en las carreras de motos.
   En cuanto a De Niro, que acaba de estrenar en Netflix el thriller Susurran tu nombre, el dos veces ganador del Oscar tiene pendiente el estreno de Ahora los suegros son ellos, la nueva entrega de la saga de comedia que protagoniza junto a Ben Stiller, el próximo 27 de septiembre. Tommy & Me sería el segundo biopic de su carrera tras Toro salvaje, que le valió la estatuilla a mejor actor principal en 1981. 
   Además, De Niro ya se adentró en el mundo del béisbol en Fanático, el filme de Tony Scott en el que daba vida a un inquietante aficionado obsesionado con los San Francisco Giants y con su nuevo fichaje, el antaño mejor jugador al que dio vida Wesley Snipes. La película se estreno en 1996 y se presentó en el Festival de cine de San Sebastián.
TOMMY LASORDA, LA LEYENDA DE LOS DODGERS
   Nacido en Pensilvania e hijo de inmigrantes italianos, Lasorda dio sus primeros pasos en el béisbol profesional cuando fichó por los Philadelphia Phillies como agente libre amateur en 1945. Cuatro años más tarde, debutó en las ligas menores con los Brooklyn Dodgers, aunque solo jugó como titular en un partido.
   Su carrera como jugador estuvo llena de dificultades, y su legado verdadero legado comenzó comenzó a forjarse una vez colgó los guantes. En 1960, los recién creados Dodgers de Los Ángeles lo contrataron como ojeador, y en 1973, el entrenador del equipo, Walter Alston, lo fichó como entrenador de tercera base, con vistas a que acabara convirtiéndose en su sucesor. Efectivamente, cuatro años más tarde, una vez que Alston se jubiló, Lasorda asumió el cargo al frente del equipo.
   Durante sus veinte años como entrenador, Lasorda conquistó cuatro títulos de la Liga Nacional y dos campeonatos de la Serie Mundial. En los últimos años de su vida, ejerció como asesor del equipo, colaborando en la búsqueda de talentos y en los entrenamientos. También era habitual verlo en el Dodger Stadium, en un asiento situado cerca del banquillo que ocupó como entrenador.
   En total, Lasorda estuvo vinculado a los Dodgers durante 71 años de su vida, la relación más longeva que alguien ha mantenido con el equipo.

title: Dodgers beat Reds 4-0
author: Associated Press
body:
CINCINNATI — Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed one hit through seven innings as the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 4-0 on Tuesday night to edge closer to an NL West division title.
The Dodgers reduced the magic number to clinch their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons to two. Los Angeles wrapped up a playoff spot on Monday and still is vying for the top seed in the NL.
Cincinnati is assured of a non-winning season after its 81st loss.
Yamamoto (14-8) made his team-high 27th start and allowed only a third-inning double to Elly De La Cruz, after which he retired 10 straight. He walked two and struck out seven. It was the second straight game a Dodgers starter went seven scoreless after Tarik Skubal on Monday.
Dodgers pitching recorded its 12th shutout of the season. The Reds were blanked for the 17th time.
Freddie Freeman returned to the Dodgers lineup after missing three of the past five games with right knee soreness and had three singles in five at-bats. Freeman was 3 for 30 coming into Tuesday.
Josue De Paula batted leadoff for the first time in just his fifth career game for the Dodgers and went 0 for 5 with a strikeout. He's 2 for 14 since his callup.
Teoscar Hernandez's 15th homer of the season off right-hander Rhett Lowder followed a walk to Kyle Tucker and made the score 3-0 in the third. Lowder (6-11) allowed three earned runs on five hits in five innings.
Alex Freeland made the score 4-0 in the seventh with a solo homer off Pierce Johnson.
De La Cruz extended his on-base streak to 22 games dating to Aug. 22, going 2 for 3 with a double, walk, and stolen base.
Cincinnati had runners on first and third in the ninth against Tanner Scott who struck out the next three batters to seal the Dodgers' ninth straight win over the Reds.
Dodgers LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.91) will oppose Reds LHP Andrew Abbott (6-11, 4.84) on Wednesday.

title: Se acercan los Dodgers al título del Oeste
author: AP
body:
Se acercan los Dodgers al título del Oeste
Blanquean a Rojos de Cincinnati con excelente labor de pitcheo del japonés Yoshinobu Yamamoto
Destacados
Preguntas y respuestas
CINCINNATI.- Yoshinobu Yamamoto permitió un hit en siete entradas y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron el martes 4-0 a los Rojos de Cincinnati para acercarse al título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Los Dodgers redujeron a dos el número mágico para asegurar su 13er título divisional en las últimas 14 temporadas. Los Ángeles aseguró un puesto en los playoffs el lunes y todavía compite por el primer puesto de preclasificación en la Liga Nacional.
Cincinnati, por su parte, tiene garantizada una temporada sin récord ganador tras su 81ra derrota.
Yamamoto (14-8) realizó la 27ma apertura de su equipo, la mayor cantidad, y permitió únicamente un doble en la tercera entrada al dominicano Elly De La Cruz, tras lo cual retiró a 10 bateadores consecutivos. Dio dos bases por bolas y ponchó a siete. Fue el segundo juego seguido en el que un abridor de los Dodgers lanzó siete entradas sin permitir carreras, después de Tarik Skubal el lunes.
¡Sigue nuestro canal de WhatsApp para más noticias! Únete aquí
Los Dodgers registraron su 12da blanqueada de la temporada. Los Rojos se fueron en blanco por 17ma vez.
Freddie Freeman regresó a la alineación de los Dodgers después de perderse tres de los últimos cinco juegos por molestias en la rodilla derecha y conectó tres sencillos en cinco turnos. Freeman llegaba al martes con 3 hits en 30 turnos.
Josue De Paula bateó como primer bate por primera vez, apenas en su quinto juego en Grandes Ligas con los Dodgers, y se fue de 0-5 con un ponche. Tiene 2 hits en 14 turnos desde su llamado.
El 15to jonrón de la temporada del dominicano Teoscar Hernández, ante el derecho Rhett Lowder, llegó después de una base por bolas a Kyle Tucker y puso el marcador 3-0 en la tercera entrada. Lowder (6-11) permitió tres carreras limpias.

title: 「投手を続ける価値が本当にあるのか…」米誌が大谷翔平に“勧告” 二刀流継続で「度重なる代償を払い続けている」
body:
「投手を続ける価値が本当にあるのか…」米誌が大谷翔平に“勧告” 二刀流継続で「度重なる代償を払い続けている」
大谷は二刀流を終える時なのか。米誌が見解を示した(C)Getty Images
ドジャースの大谷翔平は二刀流を終える時なのか。右上腕二頭筋と左膝の不調を抱えて負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている大谷について、米誌『Sports Illustrated』の電子版『Dodgers ON SI』が見解を示した。
同誌は「かつてないほどに打席でもマウンドでも圧倒的な存在感を放つオオタニだが、投球を続けることが彼の身体に及ぼしてきた負担を考えれば、投手を続ける価値が本当にあるのかを決断すべき時がきている」と伝えた。
さらに「率直に言って、私たちは2度と彼がピッチャーマウンドに立つ姿を見るべきではないのかもしれない」と、厳しい言葉を投げかけた。
今季の大谷は投手として8勝2敗、防御率1.79、95奪三振の好成績を収めており「球界初の本格的な二刀流スターとなった彼の凄まじい才能を、私たちは改めて見せつけられた。しかし残念ながら、その才能を維持することで、度重なる代償を払い続けている」と主張した。
続けて「フルタイムの先発投手と毎試合出場する打者を両立させようとする中で、オオタニは長年にわたり数々のケガに見舞われてきた。これまでの取り組みが打席での能力に影を落とすことはなかったが、32歳となった今、ついにその影響が出始めているように見受けられる」と、二刀流による弊害を指摘した。

title: How Teoscar Hernández fixed his swing to help power Dodgers over the Reds
author: Maddie Lee
body:
How Teoscar Hernández fixed his swing to help power Dodgers over the Reds
-    Click here to listen to this article
-   
CINCINNATI — A simple change opened a dramatic offensive turnaround for Dodgers left fielder Teoscar Hernández.
Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday, in the Dodgers’ 4-0 win against the Reds, was his second home run in as many nights, as the team trimmed its magic number to clinch the division to one behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s seven innings of one-hit ball. And, significantly, this one was against a right-handed pitcher.
“It’s been very helpful,” manager Dave Roberts said after the game. “As certain guys are not seeing the ball as well, it’s nice to kind of backfill with guys like Teo swinging the bat. And when you can slug like he can, you can win baseball games, and he can carry us for a while. And the last 10 days, something like that, it’s been really good from him.”
Through the end of August, Hernández had just a .668 OPS against right-handed pitchers this season. So, when Roberts was asked in Detroit whether the Dodgers would consider setting up a left-field platoon with the team’s September call-ups, he said yes.
Hernández homered off Tigers left-hander Framber Valdez on the last day of the series. And before the Dodgers opened a three-game set against the Cardinals at Dodger Stadium, Hernández met with the hitting coaches.
Against Valdez, Hernández was in a closed stance, to delay his front hip from opening, according to Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates. But the team’s hitting group thought a return to a familiar setup could be a long-term solution.
“It was a great meeting we had,” Bates said. “We all talked about it, and then he felt comfortable enough to do it, and then the rest is to his credit. He’s just been who he is.”
Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” before putting him on the playoff roster.
In the past, Hernández had used a “twister tap” as his stride. He started in a more open stance, tapped his toe in line with the pitcher, and then set his foot down. But lower-body injuries the last couple of years — a left groin strain last season and a left hamstring strain earlier this season — forced him away from it.
His improved health and hip flexibility opened the avenue for him to return to that timing mechanism.
“When Teo’s hips are loose that way, and his front leg looks like an Elvis knee, it’s a good sign for us,” Bates said. “Because that means that he can open and close it without his upper body going with it.”
The advantage of the twister tap, as Hernández explained it, is how repeatable it is. A more traditional stride can be sped up or slowed down.
“Just being able to control my body and being in a good position,” Hernández said earlier this month. “I can see the pitch a little sooner and identify what kind of pitch it is and if it’s going to be a strike or a ball.”
With that change, he’s rewarded the Dodgers for deciding against platooning left field. Hernández entered Tuesday with a .777 OPS against right-handed pitchers — a sample size of just 28 plate appearances but still a significant jump.
“The biggest thing is his plate coverage away,” Bates said. “Because now he can spoil pitches, and he’s staying in at-bats longer.”
Hernández’s dramatic offensive turnaround, along with fellow corner outfielder Kyle Tucker’s improvement, have helped steady a Dodgers offense that’s missing Shohei Ohtani (on the IL with right biceps and left knee injuries) and includes a hobbled Freddie Freeman (right knee soreness).
Rookie Josue De Paula, mostly filling in for Ohtani at designated hitter, has already shown he can take mature at-bats and provide some pop. But he’s still finding his footing in a new league.
It lengthens the Dodgers lineup for Hernández, after a slow start to his year, to return to being a veteran power threat — just in time to, ideally, carry the momentum into the postseason.
On Monday, he launched his two-run shot off left-hander Nick Lodolo. On Tuesday, he replicated the feat off right-hander Rhett Lowder.
On the second pitch of the at-bat, Hernández recognized a hung slider, and he roped it over the left-field fence at 109.3 mph, according to Statcast. The blast put the Dodgers up 3-0 in the third inning, with Dodgers starter Yamamoto settling into a groove on the other side.
Yamamoto had walked the first two batters he faced, but he reined in his control to pitch seven scoreless innings and allow just one more baserunner — a double by Reds star shortstop Elly De La Cruz.
The Dodgers also scored on Hunter Feduccia’s second-inning single and Alex Freeland’s seventh-inning homer. And the Dodgers bullpen completed the shutout.
Freeman staying in the lineup
Freeman was all smiles after his three-hit game Tuesday — after going hitless for his last four games.
“I was supposed to be off tomorrow, but I played myself in there,” he said. “So I’m very excited.”
Roberts explained: “He was joking, saying, ‘If I get three hits, then can I be in there tomorrow?’”
Sure enough, the mechanical adjustments he made in the batting cage — focusing on getting his foot down early and making contact out in front — got him there.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results,” Freeman said. “We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago, I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable.”
Though Roberts has been trying to find opportunities to rest Freeman, he saw promising signs Tuesday beyond the results.
“Just my eyes, just watching him move, I feel good about him going tomorrow,” Roberts said.
De Paula, Freeland and third baseman Max Muncy will be out of the lineup Wednesday, Roberts said.

title: Dodgers news: Freddie Freeman reveals all he's 'trying to do' before MLB playoffs
author: Rexwell Villas; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Freddie Freeman reveals all he's 'trying to do' before MLB playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Freddie Freeman returned to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup on Tuesday for the second game of their series against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park in Cincinnati.
The former National League Most Valuable Player missed three of the previous five Los Angeles games because of ongoing right knee soreness, but he managed to make an impact on the Dodgers' 4-0 victory over the Reds.
Freeman looked great with the bat in his return. He didn't score a run or drive one in, but he went 3-for-5. For now, the 37-year-old first baseman is looking to build momentum and reach his top form once the postseason rolls around.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"It was good. I've been kind of working, did a new thing in the cage the last couple of days, so gotta go for results-based things right now. We gotta get hot with two weeks to go, and looking to be hot for a few weeks. That's all I'm trying to do," the 10-time All-Star said in a postgame interview (via SportsNet LA)
Freeman is an undeniably integral part of the Dodgers' success in recent years, and he's expected to play a major role in the postseason, as Los Angeles takes aim at winning a World Series for the third year in a row.
That said, he's hitting just .100/.270/.200 with just a home run and three RBIs in nine games played so far in September. There is still a lot of time for him to get back to his usual form, with the Dodgers already assured of a spot in the playoffs.
Related: Dodgers' Dave Roberts gives props to Yoshinobu Yamamoto for savvy game vs. Reds
Related: Bobby Miller gets brutally honest on returning to Dodgers

title: Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 4-pitch leadoff walk was a red flag, but the Dodgers' ace proved it was a fluke
author: Jake Mintz
body:
CINCINNATI — Before each start, Yoshinobu Yamamoto does something remarkable.
Many pitchers long toss as part of their pregame routine. It's common practice at the high school level and above to warm up the arm, boot up the body, rev up the engine. Throwing a ball far is mighty similar, biomechanically, to throwing a ball fast.
But Yamamoto takes things to another level. After subjecting his muscles and ligaments to an elaborate stretching program, the Dodgers righty begins playing catch, gradually working his way toward the outer reaches of a big-league park's center-field grasslands. First 200 feet, then 250, 275, up to around 300. But instead of winding himself up with a few hop-steps like most long-tossers do, Yamamoto lets it fly from the relative standstill of his usual in-game windup.
It's a mesmerizing thing to witness — this 5-foot-10, 176-pound speck of cerulean catapulting a baseball 100 yards without the help of any real momentum. For a few seconds after release, Yamamoto stands frozen, balancing on his left leg with his right leg dangling in the air. The whole thing looks fake, like a lazy AI generation. How could a dude that small throw a ball that far that easily?
Such is the magic of Yamamoto: balance, intention, mechanical precision.
All those qualities and more were on display Tuesday in Cincinnati as the undersized hurler tore the Reds asunder. He worked seven scoreless innings, struck out seven and allowed just one hit.
After walking the first two hitters of the game, Yamamoto settled in. Following Elly De La Cruz's double in the third, the Dodgers starter retired the final 13 hitters he faced.
"He's able to reset on the fly. He's able to bear down and make pitches when he needs to," manager Dave Roberts explained after L.A.'s 4-0 win.
Yamamoto needed that adjustability Tuesday after an uncharacteristically poor start to the outing. He walked Cincinnati leadoff man Carlos Jorge, making just the fifth start of his MLB career, on four wayward offerings. It was the first time in Yamamoto's stateside tenure that he walked the first batter of the game on four pitches. He was similarly over-careful with the following hitter, walking De La Cruz on a 3-1 count. Jorge reached third base on a sac fly but got no further, as Yamamoto escaped the frame with no damage.
"At the beginning, because I [didn't] have my usual stuff mechanically, so mentally I was very calm, and then still kept composed, so I was able to make an adjustment on time," Yamamoto said afterward.
From there, it was business as usual, with Yamamoto deploying his typical barrage of splitters, curves and heaters. It was metronomical, almost humdrum, the way Yamamoto eased through the outing with little trouble. You blinked, and he was in the seventh with a zero on the board.
His entire season has carried a similar energy. The National League's overabundance of headline hurlers has been one of this campaign's main storylines. Jacob Misiorowski looks primed to win his first Cy Young behind a historic, bat-missing stat line. Chris Sale, Cristopher Sánchez, Jesús Luzardo and Chase Burns have all been excellent as well. Those characters, to a certain extent, have overshadowed Yamamoto's contributions.
This tumultuous Dodgers season, too, has stolen some of the shine. So much attention has been paid to the health and exploits of Shohei Ohtani and his quest to reestablish himself as a two-way dynamo over a full season. L.A.'s acquisition of Tarik Skubal overtook the trade deadline. Through it all, Yamamoto has remained magnificently consistent.
And with October just around the corner, the 2025 World Series hero is looking primed to carry the torch for the Dodgers once again.

title: Tarik Skubal Says Will Smith Is Key to Unlocking His Best for Dodgers
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers newest star pitcher Tarik Skubal reveals the impact of Will Smith calling his pitches.
Smith has come back from his neck injury and made an immediate impression on the pitching staff.
Skubal, who joined the team at the trade deadline, hasn’t been able to work much with Smith since Smith’s injury.
However, since coming back to the Dodgers on September 1st, Smith has caught three games for Skubal and left the two-time Cy Young winner quite impressed.
In those three starts, he has a 1.80 ERA over 20 innings with four walks and 20 strikeouts.
Most notably, in his last start, Skubal went seven innings, allowing no runs, one walk, and nine strikeouts in what became the best start of his Dodgers career.
After the game, Skubal told reporters that Smith called every pitch, never shaking him off once during the outing.
“Yeah, I think it’s just kind of reading, reacting to what situations, or reading swings,” Skubal said.
“And honestly, a lot of that’s Will. Like, I trust him with calling every pitch. I think I shook one time tonight, so we’re in pretty good rhythm.”
How Smith is helping Skubal settle in with the Dodgers
Skubal has said he’s been thinking too much about pitch selection rather than focusing on execution, leading to inconsistent results.
Since joining the Dodgers, Skubal has felt he underestimated how much familiarity with the catchers and other members of the pitching staff matters.
Now, he is working hard to focus on that line of communication.
“I think just trying to get on the same page with everybody here, you know, catching department, pitching department, constantly learning each other and developing those relationships,” Skubal explained.
“And I probably underestimated that a little bit, but just communicating, having open dialogue with all these guys on what I like to do, what I’m comfortable with.
“And then, honestly, some things I’m uncomfortable with, working on those things because it’s gonna be important.
“I think we’re developing a really good relationship and rhythm, just with me and everybody else, the catchers and the pitching department.”
With Skubal settling in and starting to make the most out of a pitching operation that has succeeded over the last several years, this bodes very well for the postseason outlook.

これまでにも定期的に行われてきた今季サイ・ヤング賞の模擬投票。30名を超える審査員によって投票が行われ、各リーグ上位5名が、受賞候補者として選出されます。

title: Dodgers finally get positive injury updates on Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI — For the first time in what’s felt like a while, the Dodgers’ usually foreboding daily injury updates came with some needed signs of optimism on Tuesday.
Before the game, manager Dave Roberts said two-way star Shohei Ohtani “felt good” after resuming hitting activities on Monday, when he took swings off a tee back in Los Angeles. And while Roberts didn’t guarantee Ohtani would return from the injured list before the end of the regular season, that at least remains the team’s expectation for now.
“Today was positive,” Roberts said, “and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”
Then, in an even bigger development, first baseman Freddie Freeman not only returned to the lineup in Tuesday night’s win over the Cincinnati Reds, but put together a three-hit performance that “played myself in” to Wednesday’s lineup, he proudly noted with a grin.
Initially, Roberts was planning to rest Freeman on Wednesday amid his ongoing battle with a right knee injury. That would have marked the 37-year-old’s fourth missed game out of the last seven for the team.
Early in the night, however, Freeman struck a deal with his manager.
“He was joking, saying, ‘If I get three hits, then can I be in there tomorrow?’” Roberts recounted.
Right on cue, Freeman lined singles in the first, fifth and seventh innings — snapping out of his troubling 3-for-30 slump previously.
“It looked good,” Roberts said. “It looked more like Freddie.”
Not only did the veteran slugger feel no pain in his knee — where he has been battling a patellar tendinitis problem — but he also revealed a fruitful adjustment he had made before the game with his swing.
Amid his recent knee problems, Freeman felt he had started letting the ball travel too far in his stance before beginning his swing, causing him to “slide” in the box, especially with a compromised front leg.
Thus, he made a temporary change he hopes will spark him ahead of the playoffs, focusing on getting his front leg down sooner and catching the ball further out at the front of his swing.
“I feel like my faults are I try to hit the ball to the opposite field too much, and I let the ball get too deep,” he said. “So today was [get the] foot down early, catch the ball out front a little bit, and it kind of worked. I wasn’t squaring the ball up in the game, but I’ll take those three hits and keep that work going tomorrow, and hopefully we’ll get hot.”
It’s not a permanent solution, Freeman noted. But at this point in the year, “I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable,” he said. “I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
Indeed, between that and Ohtani’s progress — which has the Dodgers remaining cautiously optimistic about his chances to make an impact in the playoffs — it was enough for the team to finally feel some optimism about the way they are trending toward October, getting a couple of positive updates on two of their superstar hitters.

title: How did Josue De Paula do for Dodgers vs. Reds on Sept. 15?
author: James H Williams
body:
How did Josue De Paula do for Dodgers vs. Reds on Sept. 15?
Josue De Paula made his first start as the Los Angeles Dodgers' leadoff hitter on Tuesday, Sept. 15.
He went 0-for-5 at the plate in the Dodgers' 4-0 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
The 21-year-old designated hitter jumped up into the leadoff spot in place of Tommy Edman, who was originally in the role after Shohei Ohtani's injury woes.
De Paula added to the Dodgers' offense in a game against the Miami Marlins, hitting a three-run home run for his first career homer on Sept. 13.
The 21-year-old De Paula made his major-league debut for the team at LoanDepot Park on Friday, Sept. 11, becoming the youngest Dodgers player since Alex Verdugo on Sept. 2, 2017.
De Paula has been viewed as the organization's top prospect and recently became the first Dodgers position player called up from AA, while skipping AAA, since Steve Sax in 1981.

title: 【MLB】大谷翔平がBOSS公式インスタに登場「あなたの考え方、あなたの力、あなたのスタイルを見せて」…世界のスーパースターと共演
author: SANKEI DIGITAL INC
body:
アパレルブランド「BOSS」の公式インスタグラムが16日までに更新され、米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）が登場した。
「BOSS」の公式インスタには「BOSS」の秋の新作に身を包んだ大谷が登場。シックなデザインの秋らしい装いの写真を複数アップし「洗練されたBOSSの最新スタイルに身を包んだ大谷翔平から秋の装いを見直そう」と呼びかけた。
また大谷が出演する動画も公開され、ボールやバットを手に力強い視線を投げかけており、「あなたの考え方、あなたの力、あなたのスタイルを見せて」とつづっている。
この他にもインスタには、陸上女子の中距離走で活躍するアリカ・シュミット（27）＝ドイツ＝や、自動車F1のドライバー、フェルナンド・アロンソ（45）＝スペイン＝、NFLの若手スターQBジャクソン・ダート（23）＝米国＝が登場しており、世界のスーパースターの豪華共演となっている。
大谷は「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りしており、15日から打撃活動を再開。IL明けは23日（同24日）となっている。実戦復帰までこなす過程は多く、レギュラーシーズン中の復帰は不透明となっている。

title: Dodgers Legend Tommy Lasorda Getting Hollywood Treatment With A-List Star
author: Cameron Kiszla
body:
An all-time Los Angeles Dodger great is the subject of a new Hollywood production.
Tommy Lasorda, the longtime Dodgers manager, will be the titular character of the new biopic “Tommy & Me,” report Matt Grobar and Justin Kroll of Deadline.
Lasorda, who pitched briefly for the Dodgers back in Brooklyn, is perhaps best remembered as the team’s manager from 1976 to 1996.
In that time, he won four National League pennants and a pair of World Series titles, eventually earning a spot in the National Baseball Hall of Fame.
“His reputation as one of baseball’s most beloved and recognizable figures only grew with age. A passionate ambassador for both the Dodgers and the city of Los Angeles, he died in 2021 at 93,” Grobar and Kroll wrote.
So who else could portray this Dodgers legend besides a legend of the silver screen?
Who will play Tommy Lasorda in the new movie?
Tommy Lasagna will be played by another Italian-American legend: Robert De Niro.
The “Godfather Part II” and “Goodfellas” actor is in talks to play Lasorda, Deadline reports.
And he’s not the only established Hollywood name involved in the production.
The Skydance Sports production is to be directed by Reid Carolin, best known for his work with producing partner Channing Tatum, and the script is being written by Carolin, George Gallo and Cambron Clark.
What will the movie be about?
Given De Niro’s age of 83, it seems likely that he’ll play an older adult Lasorda.
The 1988 World Series, the Dodgers’ final championship before this recent spate of three titles in six years, would certainly make an interesting setting.
Orel Hershiser in his prime, Kirk Gibson’s World Series homer, it all seems readymade for the big screen.
That said, De Niro has done some de-aging work, like in “The Irishman,” so perhaps the film will include earlier moments from Lasorda’s life as well and use AI to make De Niro appear younger.
In any case, it’s the kind of project that’s surely to get baseball fans excited and lead to theaters packed full of Dodgers fans in Southern California.
There’s no telling how long this movie will take to come to fruition, but do you plan on catching it once it comes out?

title: VIDEO | Teoscar Hernández y Yoshinobu Yamamoto brillan, Dodgers a 2 triunfos de ganar la división
author: Diario Libre
body:
Teoscar Hernández volvió a demostrar que atraviesa un momento ofensivo importante y encabezó la ofensiva de los Dodgers en la victoria 4-0 sobre los Reds este martes en el Great American Ball Park.
El dominicano conectó un cuadrangular de dos carreras en la tercera entrada, su segundo vuelacercas en igual cantidad de partidos, para ampliar una ventaja que Los Ángeles ya no perdería.
Hernández terminó de 3-1 y produjo dos carreras, mientras los Dodgers se acercaron a solo dos victorias de asegurar el título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
El jonrón tuvo además un significado particular para Hernández, quien había tenido dificultades frente a los lanzadores derechos durante buena parte de la temporada. Hasta finales de agosto, registraba apenas .668 de OPS contra derechos, situación que incluso llevó al manager Dave Roberts a considerar un posible pelotón en el jardín izquierdo con jugadores recién ascendidos.
Después de conectar un jonrón ante el zurdo Framber Valdez en Detroit, Hernández trabajó con los coaches de bateo antes de la serie contra los Cardinals, y desde entonces su producción ha comenzado a cambiar.
Yamamoto intransitable
La actuación del dominicano sirvió como complemento perfecto para otra extraordinaria presentación de Yoshinobu Yamamoto. El japonés tuvo un comienzo poco habitual, al fallar ocho de sus primeros nueve lanzamientos y conceder boletos consecutivos a los dos primeros bateadores de Cincinnati. Fue apenas la cuarta ocasión esta temporada en que otorgó múltiples boletos en una entrada y la primera vez en su carrera de Grandes Ligas que abrió una salida con dos bases por bolas consecutivas.
Pero aquel descontrol inicial quedó rápidamente en el pasado. Después de poner a dos corredores en las bases en el primer episodio, Yamamoto solo permitió que otro bateador de Cincinnati llegara a salvo durante el resto de su actuación. Retiró a 21 de los últimos 22 bateadores que enfrentó y completó siete entradas en blanco, con apenas un hit permitido, un doble de Elly De La Cruz en el tercer inning, además de siete ponches.
La ofensiva angelina había tomado ventaja desde el segundo episodio, cuando Hunter Feduccia produjo una carrera con un sencillo. En el tercero llegó el batazo de Hernández para colocar el marcador 3-0 y, posteriormente, Alex Freeland agregó otro cuadrangular solitario para completar las cuatro carreras de Los Ángeles. El ataque de los Dodgers no fue especialmente abundante, pero produjo lo suficiente para respaldar a Yamamoto y convertir su actuación en una nueva joya monticular.
Para Yamamoto, fue además su tercera apertura consecutiva completando siete entradas y la quinta salida seguida en la que alcanzó al menos el séptimo episodio. Desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas, el derecho japonés ha mantenido un ritmo dominante, con efectividad de 1.98 en 68? entradas, 72 ponches y solo 16 boletos en 10 aperturas, una producción que lo coloca como una de las principales piezas de la rotación de Los Ángeles de cara a octubre.
La victoria dejó a los Dodgers con el número mágico en dos para conquistar su decimotercer título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas.
- Después de haber asegurado ya su boleto a la postemporada, Los Ángeles continúa ahora en busca de la corona divisional y de una posición privilegiada para octubre.
Blake Snell será el encargado de subir al montículo en el próximo encuentro de la serie, mientras los Dodgers siguen construyendo una rotación que, con Yamamoto al frente, vuelve a tomar protagonismo en su búsqueda de un tercer campeonato consecutivo.

title: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers’ bullpen combine on 3-hit shutout to beat Reds
author: Bill Plunkett
body:
CINCINNATI — The Dodgers can only hope it looks this good in October.
One night after Tarik Skubal went seven innings in his first scoreless outing as a Dodger, Yoshinobu Yamamoto matched him, allowing only one hit in his seven scoreless innings as the Dodgers shut out the Cincinnati Reds, 4-0, on Tuesday night.
“When you’re writing in the lineup and you see those guys, and one trying to up the other guy, and then now you got Snell going tomorrow – you feel good about preventing runs,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
“A team like the Reds right now, where they’re scuffling a little bit, it’s daunting when you see a starter like those guys that we’re running out there.”
The win moved the Dodgers (92-59) within one day of clinching their 13th NL West division title in the past 14 seasons. Their magic number is one after the second-place San Diego Padres (82-69) lost to the Colorado Rockies later Tuesday night.
The Dodgers’ lead over the Atlanta Braves (89-63) for the No. 2 seed in the National League remains 3½ games. Their magic number to clinch a first-round bye is eight.
All of that makes the final two weeks of the regular season a chance for the Dodgers to get things right for October and their three-peat pursuit. The starting rotation appears to be there already.
Skubal has a 1.73 ERA over his past four starts. With Tuesday’s outing, Yamamoto’s ERA is 1.79 over his past seven starts. Blake Snell starts on Wednesday – and he has given up a total of only four runs in six starts since returning from elbow surgery. Only fourth starter Tyler Glasnow (eight runs in 10 innings over his past two starts) seems to have some work to do before being October-ready.
“Yeah, pretty good,” first baseman Freddie Freeman said after his first three-hit game since Aug. 17. “You have Blake Snell going tomorrow. Tyler on the back end of that too. Roki’s on his way back.
“It’s a special pitching staff. It really is. So as an offense, we just need to score a few runs for them, just like we did last year.”
Yamamoto started Tuesday by giving the Reds hope – he walked the first two batters he faced – then he took it away, retiring 21 of the next 22 batters he faced.
“They took a little moment for me,” Yamamoto said through his interpreter of the mound visit from catcher Hunter Feduccia and pitching coach Mark Prior that followed the walks. “They came up to me and, ‘Hey, how you doing?’ and just checked in on me. And then I was able to get back to my normal rhythm.”
Elly De La Cruz had the only hit off Yamamoto, a double into the left-field corner with two outs in the third inning.
But even that was a victory – Yamamoto kept him in the ballpark after De La Cruz had hit a home run in each of the previous four games between the Dodgers and Reds. He then retired the next 13 batters in order, getting six of his seven strikeouts.
“After the first two hitters, it was vintage Yama,” Roberts said. “Just attacking, not trying to be too fine. Not giving these guys too much credit. And yeah, at first, it didn’t look promising as far as pitch count, the two walks. But then he kind of dialed things in, like he’s been known to do.”
The Dodgers gave him a lead in the second inning when Max Muncy was hit by a pitch and Tommy Edman and Hunter Feduccia followed with singles. They added to it in the third inning with a two-run home run from Teoscar Hernandez, who remains hot – 24 for 63 (.381) in his past 18 games.
“It’s been very helpful,” Roberts said of Hernandez’s late-season renaissance. “As certain guys are not seeing the ball as well, it’s nice to kind of backfill with guys like Teo swinging the bat. And when you can slug like he can, you can win baseball games, and he can carry us for a while. The last 10 days, something like that, it’s been really good from him. The defense ticked up. The at-bat quality, the taking walks, all of it. I can’t say enough about what he’s done the last 10 days.”
De La Cruz had another hit, a single in the ninth inning that put runners on the corners for the Reds with no outs. Tanner Scott struck out Sal Stewart, Jose Trevino and Eugenio Suarez to close out the shutout.

title: Yoshinobu Yamamoto rounds into playoff form as Dodgers move to cusp of NL West title
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI –– There’s not much the Dodgers can do, manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday afternoon, to get their all-important rotation ready for the added workload that will come in the postseason.
Over the final couple weeks of the regular season, they have to just keep running their starters out there, and counting on them to round into elevated October form.
That’s what appeared to happen with Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Tuesday night at Great American Ball Park, in what was the right-hander’s most dominant performance of at least the last couple months.
In the Dodgers’ 4-0 win over the Cincinnati Reds, Yamamoto threw a one-hit masterpiece over seven scoreless innings, flashing the kind of ruthless efficiency that defined his heroics during last year’s playoffs.
After walking his first two batters in the first inning, he retired 21 of the 22 after with seven strikeouts and virtually no stress.
“After the first two hitters, it was vintage Yama,” Roberts said. “Just attacking, not trying to be too fine.”
The reigning World Series MVP hadn’t exactly been struggling lately, of course. Just last week, he held the Reds to one run over seven innings with 10 strikeouts back in Los Angeles.
But what Yamamoto did on Tuesday was different, keyed by quick and easy outs on soft and harmless contact.
It’s what he did as the ace of last year’s postseason staff, and what he will need to do again as the Dodgers go for a World Series three-peat this fall.
“I’d like to carry this,” Yamamoto said through an interpreter of his renewed stuff, “into October.”
The Dodgers are hoping they won’t have to ask as much out of Yamamoto this time around; that they need him to pitch back-to-back complete games (like he did in Game 2 of the NLCS and Game 2 of the World Series) or provide back-to-back nights of season-saving heroics (following up a victorious Game 6 start in the Fall Classic with a winning three-inning appearance out of the bullpen in Game 7).
But in a postseason environment, it’s impossible to know what exactly will be required.
“You can’t just try to create that during the regular season because you want these guys as strong and healthy for the October run [as possible],” Roberts said pregame. “But it’s one of those things that, once we get to the postseason, all bets are off and everyone is going to do what they can to contribute.”
It would help, of course, if the Dodgers’ currently Shohei Ohtani-less offense can keep turning a corner, with Tuesday bringing more positive –– albeit subtle –– signs.

title: 【MLB】山本由伸が7回1安打無失点の快投で14勝目 ドジャースは完封勝利で地区優勝へマジック2（MLB公式日本語サイト） - Yahoo!ニュース
body:
【ドジャース4-0レッズ】シンシナティ／グレートアメリカンボールパーク、9月15日（日本時間16日）
前日の勝利で14年連続のポストシーズン進出を決めたドジャースは敵地でのレッズ4連戦の2戦目。地区優勝が目前に迫る中、山本由伸が今季27度目の先発マウンドに上がった。前回登板でもレッズを相手に7回3安打1失点、10三振の好投を披露した右腕が、この日も相手打線を寄せつけない投球を見せ、4-0で勝利。山本は7回91球を投げて1安打無失点、7三振の内容で自己最多をさらに更新する14勝目（8敗、防御率2.51）を挙げた。 山本は初回、先頭から2者連続四球で得点圏に走者を背負ったものの、後続を抑えて無失点でスタート。すると打線は二回、1死からマックス・マンシーの死球とトミー・エドマンのヒットでチャンスを作り、ハンター・フェデューシアがセンターへのタイムリーを放って1点を先制した。 三回は1死からカイル・タッカーが四球で出塁し、続くテオスカー・ヘルナンデスがレフトスタンドへ2試合連発となる15号2ラン。リードを3点に広げ、山本を援護した。 援護を受けた山本は、三回2死からエリー・デラクルーズに初安打となる二塁打を許したが、新人王候補のサル・スチュワートを空振り三振に仕留めて無失点。その後はレッズ打線につけ入る隙を与えず、スコアボードにゼロを並べ続けた。 ドジャースは七回1死からアレックス・フリーランドの4号ソロで1点を追加。山本は七回も三者凡退に抑え、7回1安打無失点と前回登板に続いてレッズ打線を圧倒した。 ドジャースは八回を2番手のブロック・スチュワートが無失点に抑えると、最終回は3番手のタナー・スコットがマウンドへ。ところが、先頭の代打デーン・マイヤーズに四球を与えると、続くデラクルーズにはセンター前に運ばれ、無死一、三塁のピンチとなった。しかし、後続を3者連続三振に抑えて4-0で試合終了。この試合が終了した時点で地区優勝へのマジックナンバーを「2」とした。

title: Robert De Niro expected to play Dodgers legend Tommy Lasorda in upcoming Hollywood blockbuster
author: Thomas L Murray
body:
The legacy of Tommy Lasorda is expected to hit theaters in the near future, and it’s believed to have one of Hollywood’s finest playing the Hall of Fame Los Angeles Dodgers manager.
Robert De Niro is in talks to play Lasorda in the upcoming film “Tommy & Me,” according to Deadline,
Details have yet to emerge as to what approach the film will take in telling Lasorda’s story, but the script will be led by George Gallo, Cambron Clark and Reid Carolin. Skydance Sports is expected to help produce the movie that will highlight one of baseball’s most iconic figures.
Lasorda, known for his fiery spirit and larger-than-life personality, is one of the most iconic managers in Dodgers history, as he helped coach and manage the team from 1973 through 1996, leading them to two World Series titles in 1981 and 1988, and being crowned National League Manager of the Year in 1983 and 1988.
In 1997, the Dodgers retired his No. 2 jersey, the same year he was immortalized in the National Baseball Hall of Fame.
After his managing career came to an end, Lasorda became an impactful member of the Dodgers front office, serving as a vice president, senior vice president, and special advisor from 1998 to 2021, where he is credited with making a large impact, such as helping scout and sign Mike Piazza.
In 2021, the Dodgers announced that Lasorda had passed away at a hospital near his home in Fullerton.
Before working as a coach and in front offices, Lasorda’s start in baseball began in 1954 as a player with the Dodgers, when they were still located in Brooklyn.
His playing career didn’t last too long, as he spent his first two seasons with the Dodgers and was later sold to the Kansas City Athletics in 1956.
Lasorda spent the next four years in the Minor Leagues and would retire from playing following the 1960 season.
De Niro, who is known for being able to play characters that have a fiery passion like Lasorda, has been in many notable films during his acting career, including Taxi Driver, The Godfather Part II, and Goodfellas.

title: Dodgers news: Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages get big injury updates before playoffs
author: Matty Breisch; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages get big injury updates before playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
With a spot in the MLB playoff locked up, the Los Angeles Dodgers have one major goal for the rest of September: get healthy.
Sure, there are sub-storylines to follow, from Josue De Paula filling in at DH, which bullpen arms are getting hot at the right time, and Kyle Tucker figuring it out down the stretch, but for the most part, the Dodgers simply want to take the field in October with their best guys all available for Dave Roberts to call upon.
Fortunately, on Tuesday, Roberts provided fans with some positive updates on that very front, noting that Shohei Ohtani and Andy Pages are trending in the right direction, as reported by The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.

title: Edwin Díaz deberá ganarse la confianza de Dave Roberts para lanzar con los Dodgers en la postemporada
author: Joseph Reboyras
body:
Edwin Díaz deberá ganarse la confianza de Dave Roberts para lanzar con los Dodgers en la postemporada
El dirigente de Los Ángeles puso en duda la participación del relevista tras un primer año complicado con los bicampeones.
PUBLICIDAD
El cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin “Sugar” Díaz deberá ganarse su espacio en el roster de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para poder treparse al montículo durante la postemporada, informó el mánager Dave Roberts en un aparte con la prensa estadounidense.
Díaz ha tenido un primer año complicado tras firmar un contrato de tres campañas y $69 millones con los Dodgers en la temporada muerta. Posee marca de 2-2, siete salvamentos, una errática efectividad de 11.85 en 13.2 entradas lanzadas durante 16 apariciones y ha desperdiciado cuatro de sus 11 oportunidades de salvamento.
También ha permitido 18 carreras, tres de ellas en el noveno inning de su última presentación frente a los Rockies de Colorado el pasado 17 de agosto. Al día siguiente entró a la lista de lesionados por una inflamación en el cuello.
Actualmente se encuentra en una asignación de rehabilitación con los Comets de Oklahoma City, filial de los Dodgers en Triple A. Sin embargo, lo que apuntaba a ser una corta estadía en las Menores para recuperar su nivel ha generado aún más interrogantes sobre el naguabeño, quien hace unos años era considerado uno de los mejores relevistas de las Mayores.
Díaz cargó el domingo con la más reciente derrota de Oklahoma City al permitir cinco carreras y conceder tres bases por bolas ante los Space Cowboys, filial de los Astros de Houston. El derecho pudo retirar a un solo bateador.
Por actuaciones como esas, Roberts entiende que el boricua aún no ha recuperado su nivel y evitó comprometerse cuando la prensa le preguntó si estará entre los lanzadores seleccionados para la postemporada.
Dave Roberts on Edwin Diaz's rehab assignment, via @SonjaMChen:
"He needs to pitch better. It hasn't been good."
Diaz rehab assignment so far:
3.1 IP, 6 ER, 4 K, 3 H, 7 BB pic.twitter.com/304XoBbDsU
“Necesita lanzar mejor. No lo ha hecho bien. Lanzará el miércoles y supongo que lo evaluaremos entonces”, dijo el dirigente de los Dodgers.
“Lo tengo en muy alta estima, pero en esta situación tiene que haber algo que nos dé motivos para estar seguros y él lo sabe. Quiere lanzar bien. Así que, por mi parte, el miércoles lo observaremos con atención”, abundó.
Díaz subirá a la loma el miércoles contra los Chihuahuas de El Paso, filial de los Padres de San Diego en las Menores. La llegada del tres veces seleccionado al Juego de Estrellas a Los Ángeles generó grandes expectativas, ya que era visto como el relevista que le daría a Roberts la seguridad que no tuvo su bullpen en campañas anteriores.
En cambio, el primer año del naguabeño vistiendo el uniforme de Los Ángeles ha estado marcado por lesiones, incluida una en el codo derecho que requirió una intervención quirúrgica y que lo mantuvo fuera por más de tres meses. Aun así, el piloto de los bicampeones continúa apostando en Díaz.
“Tenemos que ir con nuestros mejores lanzadores en términos de rendimiento, talento y todo eso”, indicó Roberts.
“Mi apuesta es que (Díaz) estará (incluido en el roster), pero, nuevamente, tiene que haber algún tipo de evidencia o algo que nos permita confiar en él. Mi apuesta es que sí, pero todavía tenemos que ver algo”, continuó.
Los Dodgers clasificaron el lunes a la postemporada con una victoria sobre los Reds de Cincinnati. Será su decimocuarta aparición consecutiva en los playoffs, empatando así el récord de las Grandes Ligas que los Braves de Atlanta establecieron entre 1991 y 2005. Además, lideran la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional con marca de 91-59.

title: How Tarik Skubal found ‘who I know I am’ in Dodgers adjustment process
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI –– Every day, Tarik Skubal learns something new about playing for the Dodgers.
Monday's lesson: Clinching a playoff spot warrants only subtle celebrations.
"It's different than anything I've experienced, for sure," Skubal chuckled on Monday night, after the Dodgers recognized their 14th consecutive postseason berth with only a subdued postgame champagne toast and brief speech from manager Dave Roberts.
"But," the club's new star pitcher added, "I think it just speaks to the people in this room and what they expect out of this team. That was cool. A little toast and move on. Forget it happened. We've got more to accomplish this season."
Consider it the latest step in Skubal's acclimation process with the Dodgers –– another little moment that made him feel more at home with his new team.
He's now six weeks on from his emotional trade from the Detroit Tigers at the deadline.
And he's starting to find a comfort level that, after an uneven start to his Dodgers tenure, is helping him look more like the star pitcher he is accustomed to being.
"Constantly learning each other and developing relationships –– a lot of that stuff you don't realize, no one writes about that kind of relationship –– but I think it matters, it matters a lot. I probably underestimated that a little bit," said Skubal, who had spent the entirety of his career in Detroit before his marquee move to the Dodgers.
"But just communicating, having an open dialogue with everyone, all these guys, on what I like to do, what I'm comfortable with and honestly what I'm uncomfortable with … I think we're developing a real good relationship," he added.
And as a result, as manager Dave Roberts noted, "I think the last couple [outings he has made] have been his best."
That was certainly true on Monday, when Skubal spun a gem with the Dodgers' postseason berth in the balance.
He delivered his first scoreless start with the team by blanking the Reds over seven innings at Great American Ball Park. He gave up just three hits and one walk while striking out nine batters in a 90-pitch domination.
"To take the mound on the night that we had a chance to clinch, and we did it," Roberts said, "I think that's something he should be proud of."
More important to Skubal was the way it reflected his growing familiarity with the Dodgers' catchers and pitching department.
He noted he only shook Will Smith off one time all night. He praised the rhythm he has developed with pitching coaches in pre-game prep meetings. And he credited it all with helping him eliminate some perfectionist tendencies that hampered his first month with the team (when he gave up nine runs in 24 innings while lacking the ruthless efficiency that made him a reigning back-to-back Cy Young Award winner).
"I think a lot of the struggles have been 'me vs. me,' thinking too much out there and not competing the way I know how to compete," Skubal said. "Sometimes I try to be too perfect with things instead of just attacking guys over the middle of the plate and letting my stuff play, especially early in games, behind in the count, just not trying to be too fine."
To put it more simply, Skubal added, it was a process of "trying to find the rhythm of who I know I am."
And to people around the team, it's no coincidence that has happened as he's carved out a place in his new clubhouse, as well.
"He's just chill," pitching coach Mark Prior said. "You can joke around with him. You can talk to him."
Few players have grown closer with Skubal than Blake Snell to this point. They've sat side-by-side in the dugout during games, locked in constant conversation. They were pulling practical jokes on one another Tuesday, knocking over each other's chairs in the clubhouse. They've even begun making Step Brothers-inspired jokes about being new best friends on social media.
"I think we're best friends," Snell deadpanned. "Some days, he agrees."
Snell told the California Post that their relationship blossomed naturally, with Snell immediately being struck by how Skubal was "very confident and very secure with who he is" even amid new surroundings.
Two other observations:
"I didn't think he was that funny," Snell joked, describing a side of Skubal that came out Monday night when he razzed backup catcher Hunter Feduccia about a snazzy short-sleeve dress shirt and matching pair of brown slacks ("Outfit of the day!" Skubal declared).
"And," Snell added, "I like how competitive he is. Because it just makes both of us so much better."
That latter dynamic could fuel the Dodgers' entire rotation moving forward, especially entering a postseason in which the group will likely have to carry the team.
"Every time one of our boys go, we want them to dominate, and then the next man up wants to do even better," Snell said. "I think that's very important, to know that we're supporting each other and we're pushing each other to be great, and that we're not focused on just our own achievements. We're focused on our group of starting pitchers all succeeding."
Prior echoed those sentiments, noting that with Skubal specifically: "He wants to have fun. And he wants to win."
Lately, Skubal has been, now on a four-start stretch with only five runs allowed in his last 26 innings.
For the Dodgers, it's a sign of his growth process since being acquired by the club; one that could prove crucial in their three-peat ambitions.
"It's hard to get in that rhythm [and develop] that trust," Roberts said. "But for me, I see just more of the trust in whatever is called, and then you can just go out there [be himself]."

That was certainly true on Monday, when Skubal spun a gem with the Dodgers' postseason berth in the balance.
He delivered his first scoreless start with the team by blanking the Reds over seven innings at Great American Ball Park. He gave up just three hits and one walk while striking out nine batters in a 90-pitch domination.
"To take the mound on the night that we had a chance to clinch, and we did it," Roberts said, "I think that's something he should be proud of."
More important to Skubal was the way it reflected his growing familiarity with the Dodgers' catchers and pitching department.
He noted he only shook Will Smith off one time all night. He praised the rhythm he has developed with pitching coaches in pre-game prep meetings. And he credited it all with helping him eliminate some perfectionist tendencies that hampered his first month with the team (when he gave up nine runs in 24 innings while lacking the ruthless efficiency that made him a reigning back-to-back Cy Young Award winner).
"I think a lot of the struggles have been 'me vs. me,' thinking too much out there and not competing the way I know how to compete," Skubal said. "Sometimes I try to be too perfect with things instead of just attacking guys over the middle of the plate and letting my stuff play, especially early in games, behind in the count, just not trying to be too fine."
To put it more simply, Skubal added, it was a process of "trying to find the rhythm of who I know I am."
And to people around the team, it's no coincidence that has happened as he's carved out a place in his new clubhouse, as well.
"He's just chill," pitching coach Mark Prior said. "You can joke around with him. You can talk to him."
Few players have grown closer with Skubal than Blake Snell to this point. They've sat side-by-side in the dugout during games, locked in constant conversation. They were pulling practical jokes on one another Tuesday, knocking over each other's chairs in the clubhouse. They've even begun making Step Brothers-inspired jokes about being new best friends on social media.
"I think we're best friends," Snell deadpanned. "Some days, he agrees."
Snell told the California Post that their relationship blossomed naturally, with Snell immediately being struck by how Skubal was "very confident and very secure with who he is" even amid new surroundings.
Two other observations:
"I didn't think he was that funny," Snell joked, describing a side of Skubal that came out Monday night when he razzed backup catcher Hunter Feduccia about a snazzy short-sleeve dress shirt and matching pair of brown slacks ("Outfit of the day!" Skubal declared).
"And," Snell added, "I like how competitive he is. Because it just makes both of us so much better."
That latter dynamic could fuel the Dodgers' entire rotation moving forward, especially entering a postseason in which the group will likely have to carry the team.
"Every time one of our boys go, we want them to dominate, and then the next man up wants to do even better," Snell said. "I think that's very important, to know that we're supporting each other and we're pushing each other to be great, and that we're not focused on just our own achievements. We're focused on our group of starting pitchers all succeeding."
Prior echoed those sentiments, noting that with Skubal specifically: "He wants to have fun. And he wants to win."
Lately, Skubal has been, now on a four-start stretch with only five runs allowed in his last 26 innings.
For the Dodgers, it's a sign of his growth process since being acquired by the club; one that could prove crucial in their three-peat ambitions.
"It's hard to get in that rhythm [and develop] that trust," Roberts said. "But for me, I see just more of the trust in whatever is called, and then you can just go out there [be himself]."

title: Los Dodgers enfrentan una pesadilla con Edwin Díaz rumbo a los playoffs
author: Jose Rodriguez
body:
- MLB. Reaparecen viejos 'fantasmas' para Oneil Cruz por el accidente de tráfico en el que mató a tres personas
- MLB. Drama en Yankee Stadium: Aaron Boone saca a Aaron Judge antes de tiempo en su regreso ante los Rockies
Edwin Díaz pasó de ser una de las grandes apuestas de los Los Angeles Dodgers a convertirse en una de las mayores incógnitas del equipo rumbo a la postemporada. A pesar de firmar un contrato de 69 millones de dólares antes de la temporada 2026, el veterano cerrador podría quedar fuera del roster de playoffs, lo que sería mucho más que una simple decepción.
La prioridad de la organización es clara: llegar a octubre con sus 26 mejores jugadores disponibles, sin importar el salario o la reputación. Y el panorama actual de Díaz no es alentador. Las lesiones lo han limitado a apenas 16 apariciones, mientras que registra una preocupante efectividad de 11.85, muy lejos del nivel que los Dodgers esperaban tras otorgarle uno de los contratos más importantes para un relevista.
Dodgers no garantizan un lugar para Edwin Díaz en playoffs
El reconocido analista de MLB Ken Rosenthal reveló que los Dodgers están considerando seriamente dejar fuera al relevista puertorriqueño del roster de postemporada si no demuestra que puede ser una de sus mejores opciones en el bullpen.
“Si eres los Dodgers, vas a llevar a tus 26 mejores jugadores. Han hablado en distintos momentos sobre cómo sienten que este año su cuerpo de lanzadores, del uno al 13 o del uno al 12 en la postemporada, podría ser el más fuerte que hayan llevado a octubre”, explicó Rosenthal durante una aparición en Foul Territory.
El periodista resumió todavía más la filosofía de la organización angelina:
“Esta es una industria donde se gana a cualquier costo”.
La posibilidad de que un cerrador tres veces All-Star y uno de los relevistas mejor pagados de las Grandes Ligas quede fuera del roster de playoffs habría parecido impensable hace apenas unos meses. Sin embargo, las lesiones y su bajo rendimiento han cambiado por completo el panorama.
Aun así, la puerta no está cerrada. Rosenthal considera que Díaz todavía tiene tiempo para recuperar su mejor versión y convencer a los Dodgers de que merece un lugar en el roster de octubre.
Por ahora, Los Ángeles mantiene abiertas todas sus opciones en una decisión que podría convertirse en una de las historias más sorprendentes de la recta final de la temporada.

title: Ohtani begins hitting progression, as regular-season return remains in sight
author: Sonja Chen
body:
CINCINNATI -- Shohei Ohtani resumed swinging on Tuesday for the first time since landing on the 15-day injured list last week, manager Dave Roberts said before the Dodgers' game against the Reds at Great American Ball Park.
Ohtani is not on the road with the Dodgers, but he hit off a tee in L.A. and came away feeling good afterward, Roberts said. It was Ohtani's first time swinging since his lingering right biceps and left knee injuries led him to be shut down starting last Wednesday.
"I don't know what's in store for tomorrow, but I know that there's going to be a consistent buildup," Roberts said. "Don't know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive, and hopefully we can just keep building towards that."
Ohtani's 15-day IL placement is backdated to Sept. 8, meaning that the earliest he can be activated is Sept. 23, with five regular-season games remaining for the Dodgers. Roberts believes that Ohtani will be back in action before the end of the regular season.
"Whether it happens or not is to be determined, but I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games," Roberts said. "Don't know how many of them."
In his last 24 games, a span that coincided with an attempt to ramp up as a pitcher, Ohtani hit .198 (19-for-96) with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts. Toward the end of that stretch, he began to look physically compromised at the plate, leading the Dodgers to leave him out of the lineup for four straight games. He returned to the lineup on Sept. 7 but did not come away from that game feeling good.
At that point, the Dodgers opted to place Ohtani on the IL with the aim of getting him right for the postseason. He will return only as a hitter, with his two-way duties shelved until 2027.
The Dodgers have fared well without their best hitter, entering Tuesday having won nine of the 11 games they played since Ohtani was first held out of the lineup on Sept. 3. They clinched their record-tying 14th consecutive postseason berth on Monday and are close to winning their 13th NL West title in that span, all while remaining in position to secure a first-round bye.
The understanding is that Ohtani will probably not feel 100 percent in the postseason, but he'll use the weeks ahead to feel as good as he can, both physically and with his swing. While the Dodgers have gotten by without him, they know they'll need whatever they can get from him as they bid for a three-peat.

title: Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki plan ahead of postseason remains uncertain
author: Joey Mistretta; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki plan ahead of postseason remains uncertain appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are preparing for the MLB postseason. Roki Sasaki has been recovering from a blister on his right middle finger. While he has been trending in the right direction, will Sasaki be ready for the postseason? Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic provided the latest update on Sasaki.
"Roki Sasaki will throw a simulated game tomorrow and will not start this week, Dave Roberts said. The Dodgers are still figuring out if he will start a game before the end of the regular season or if he will come back as a reliever," Ardaya reported.
It previously seemed as if Sasaki was close to returning. In all reality, Sasaki may still return fairly soon — it just won't be this week.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Dodgers fans will remember that Sasaki spent last postseason in the bullpen. While his first two regular seasons in MLB as a starter have been underwhelming, the right-handed pitcher performed well out of the bullpen last October. He recorded a stellar 0.84 ERA across nine outings to go along with three saves.
The Dodgers certainly wouldn't mind a similar postseason performance from Sasaki in 2026. One has to imagine that having him work out of the bullpen in the playoffs makes the most sense for LA, but it seems as if the ball club is still at least open to the idea of him starting again this year.
Updates on Roki Sasaki will continue to be monitored and provided as they are made available. Meanwhile, the Dodgers will play the Reds in Cincinnati on Tuesday night at 6:40 PM ET.

title: Roki Sasaki Could Be Thrown Straight Into Dodgers Postseason Bullpen
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki’s regular-season status is unclear, according to Dave Roberts.
The Dodgers are trying to determine whether Sasaki will pitch again before the regular season wraps up or if his next outing will come in the postseason as a reliever.
Sasaki has been battling a blister, and he has thrown some bullpen sessions, but he is not ready to return yet, Roberts said.
Per the skipper, he will throw in a simulated game on Wednesday, September 16th, before the team decides whether he can pitch this season.
Originally, the Dodgers were hopeful Sasaki would pitch as early as Thursday, according to The Athletic’s Katie Woo, but that is no longer the case under Dave Roberts’ new timeline.
Only a handful of games remain in the regular season, and if he doesn’t pitch this week, he has only one other week left to pitch.
It seems there may not be a soft landing for the young Japanese pitcher, and he will be asked to jump headfirst into a role he is familiar with.
Why Sasaki’s setback may not be a big deal
This season, Roki Sasaki has pitched 119.1 innings in 23 games, so he will not be battling much rust.
Additionally, he hasn’t been totally shut down for long; he got treatment for the blister and has diligently ramped up his recovery.
Sasaki will not enter the postseason cold, and he has pitched out of the bullpen before, notably in the 2025 postseason when he was the closer.
While he may be asked to be the setup man rather than the closer, he should still have plenty of experience to draw on before the playoffs begin.
